rule_violated: Fresh restore targets must bootstrap PGDATA ownership deterministically before dropping privileges
notes: The restore kernel now verifies an empty fresh target, applies postgres ownership/mode 0700, and re-attests the boundary.

title: Physical backup rewrites the WAL-G secret symlink and the restore kernel rejects its own current backup
rule_violated: A current production base backup must be self-restorable without credential paths inside PGDATA
notes: WAL-G v3.0.8 restores PostgreSQL symlinks from header Name rather than Linkname. Secrets now resolve directly to tmpfs and the runtime rejects every PGDATA symlink before backup and after fetch.

title: Logical backup uploads tenant-bearing verification sidecar plaintext outside the mandatory GPG envelope
rule_violated: Every source-bound logical backup payload containing tenant identity or parity metadata must be client-side encrypted before upload
notes: The deterministic verification JSON contains tenant schema identities, row counts, and checksums but is uploaded directly while only the dump receives GPG encryption.

title: Logical restore does not verify the escrow key fingerprint and uses a signing-key option for decryption selection
rule_violated: Backup encryption and restore must bind to exact independently escrowed public and private key fingerprints
notes: gpg --local-user configures signing identity and does not select or attest the secret key used for decryption; backup recipient input is also not structurally constrained to a fingerprint.

title: Protected-sha archive extraction trusts mutable Git replacement refs from the production worktree
rule_violated: Protected release extraction must disable replacement refs for every object lookup and archive operation
notes: A deploy-user-controlled refs/replace mapping can make git show and git archive execute substituted workflow content while the protected SHA string and replacement-derived manifest hashes still appear consistent.

title: Archive health grants two consecutive five-minute loss windows and no WAL-G push deadline
rule_violated: The full WAL switch, upload, and failure-detection path must fit one RPO budget of at most five minutes
notes: archive_timeout can consume 300 seconds before a ready file exists, health then grants that ready file another 300 seconds, and wal-push itself has no deadline.

title: PITR cleanup can delete a foreign Docker volume won during a name race
rule_violated: Destructive cleanup must prove immutable run ownership immediately before deleting every disposable resource
notes: Docker volume create is idempotent, so a competing volume can appear after preflight and be marked created; cleanup deletes by predictable name without ID and label re-attestation.

title: WAL-G source secrets bypass their exact boundary through the PostgreSQL TLS parent mount
rule_violated: Physical backup credentials must have one exact file-only mount path outside every broader runtime bind
notes: The parent certs/postgres bind exposes certs/postgres/wal-g below /ssl while the same directory is separately mounted at the intended source boundary.

title: WAL-G encryption-key rotation can write a new epoch into an unchanged object prefix
rule_violated: The client-encryption key, object prefix, and declared epoch must rotate as one fail-closed authority before any archive write
notes: The materializer can activate a new libsodium key while the Compose prefix remains bucket-derived and unchanged, mixing unreadable encryption epochs before evidence evaluation can reject them.

title: Protected backup extraction executes mutable Git remote configuration from the shared worktree
rule_violated: Production backup runtime bytes must arrive from protected workflow authority without executing mutable target-host repository configuration
notes: Disabling replacement refs does not stop fetch from reading local remote.origin.url and protocol configuration; an ext remote helper can execute before manifest verification with backup secrets present.

title: Interrupted WAL-G materialization leaves raw next-generation secret files on persistent storage
rule_violated: Failed or interrupted credential rotation must leave no raw staging inode and the next successful run must reject all residue
notes: A failure after the first per-file move leaves a hidden .next PID file outside STAGE_DIR, while the loader validates declared files but does not reject extra source entries.

title: PostgreSQL source TLS private key remains world-readable beside its hardened runtime copy
rule_violated: The source and runtime copies of a production TLS private key must both exclude the PostgreSQL runtime UID and all non-root readers
notes: The certificate generator applies mode 0644 to the PostgreSQL key and Compose mounts the entire source directory, so postgres can read the original even though the tmpfs copy is mode 0600.

title: Backup SSH secrets cross mutable target login-shell startup before the verified payload runs
rule_violated: Production secrets must not enter a mutable target execution boundary before payload authorization and integrity verification
notes: A fixed absolute shell command is defense in depth only: sshd still invokes the target account login shell before that command. Production remains locked until a dedicated backup account, root-owned non-writable startup boundary, forced-command broker, and separate backup/PITR keys are proven on the target.

title: Runner cleanup can report success while production secret payloads remain on disk
rule_violated: Secret-bearing temporary files must be removed with verified fail-closed cleanup before a ceremony can report success
notes: Local cleanup functions discard rm failures and do not prove absence, allowing a green workflow to leave SSH keys or payloads containing production secrets on the runner.

title: WAL-G loader reads the encryption key before disabling inherited shell xtrace
rule_violated: Secret-loading entry points must disable shell tracing before any credential byte is read or expanded
notes: _walg_validate_bundle reads libsodium.key before walg_exec disables xtrace; install and assert-runtime also enter validation without suppressing inherited tracing.

title: WAL-G rotation trusts prior manifest hashes without proving the prior bundle bytes
rule_violated: A rotation authority must be verified against the exact canonical credential bytes before it can authorize key or epoch transitions
notes: validate_rotation_authority validates manifest shape but uses its stored epoch/key/prefix hashes without sha256sum-checking every prior canonical file, allowing a corrupted manifest to become rotation authority.

title: Protected backup entry points read production secrets before disabling inherited shell tracing
rule_violated: Every secret-bearing entry point must disable inherited shell tracing before reading or expanding any protected value
notes: Exported SHELLOPTS/xtrace can expose the SSH private key and backup object credentials before the helper, preflight, or secret-bearing workflow block executes set +x.

title: Protected SSH streams tenant restore verification evidence into GitHub Actions logs
rule_violated: Tenant-scoped restore evidence must remain in an authenticated artifact channel and must not be copied into shared workflow logs
notes: The SSH helper tees all remote stdout into the Actions log while PITR emits base64-encoded database_verification evidence containing tenant schema identities and checksums; base64 is not a confidentiality boundary.

title: Scheduled WAL-G evidence requires the current main SHA even when the deployed PostgreSQL image was not rebuilt
rule_violated: Backup evidence must bind to the immutable deployed database image identity rather than an unrelated repository head
notes: Selective deploys do not rebuild the PostgreSQL image for app-only changes, so requiring its source revision label to equal the latest workflow GITHUB_SHA makes scheduled backup and PITR fail despite an unchanged, valid deployed image.

title: Secret-bearing backup jobs can run branch-dispatched code outside the protected main authority
rule_violated: Every job receiving production-backup Environment secrets must independently prove protected-main authority before checkout or secret expansion
notes: Job-level failure does not authorize sibling or dependent jobs: publish-evidence uses always() and freshness has no main guard, so a branch dispatch can request production Environment secrets unless each secret-bearing job and its first step independently fail closed.

title: WAL-G subprocess inherits unrelated PostgreSQL container secrets
rule_violated: The physical-backup subprocess must receive only the explicit WAL-G and PostgreSQL allowlist required for its operation
notes: walg_exec invokes env without -i, so unrelated container environment values, including service credentials, remain visible to the WAL-G subprocess.

title: PITR target secret source defaults to the live WAL-G write-credential directory
rule_violated: A disposable restore target must require an explicit run-scoped read-only credential source and reject the production write bundle
notes: The workflow passes a safe target-only path, but the script's default silently falls back to /var/aqua-saas/certs/wal-g/postgres when another caller omits TARGET_WALG_SECRET_SOURCE.

title: WAL-G materializer treats Docker daemon and authorization failures as an absent PostgreSQL container
rule_violated: Runtime credential activation may tolerate only a positively proven absent container; control-plane failures must stop the rotation
notes: docker inspect stderr and exit status are discarded with || true, conflating daemon outage or permission denial with the legitimate no-such-container case.

title: receive-delivery.handler.ts wrote storage_inventory + stock_movements directly, bypassing StockMovementService.recordMovement: PO-received feed never rolled up onto Feed.quantity (invisible to the consumption forecast and every aggregate reader), no idempotency key, no outbox event.
rule_violated: All storage inventory mutations flow through the single inventory-mutation sink (StockMovementService.recordMovement) so roll-up, idempotency, lot bookkeeping and the immutable audit row cannot be skipped by any writer.
notes: Feeding-protocol SSoT plan Phase 0 (plan ref P-08). Fix routes each received item through recordMovement(IN) on the receipt transaction, enqueues StockMovementRecorded to the transactional outbox, forwards SEC-HIGH-051 site authorization, and skips PO progress on idempotent replay.

title: requestIncidentMediaUpload @Mutation shipped without a permission-matrix classification, leaving the "every @Mutation is classified" invariant (permission-matrix.spec.ts) red on every farm-service test run.
rule_violated: Every new GraphQL operation must be classified deliberately in the permission matrix (role-listed or grandfathered) in the same change that introduces it.
notes: Found while implementing the feeding-protocol SSoT plan (pre-existing red test on branch base). Roles mirror the resolver @Roles decorator: MODULE_MANAGER, MODULE_USER, TENANT_ADMIN.

title: Feed/stock low-stock alert chain was dead end-to-end: threshold detection lived only in the RecordStockMovementHandler wrapper (feeding deductions and PO receipts never raised LowStockDetected), alert-engine had ZERO feed/stock event consumers, the websocket bridge only forwarded legacy FeedInventoryLow, and the in-process notification chain terminated with no listener.
rule_violated: Operational alarms must flow through durable events with a real consumer (outbox -> NATS -> alert-engine incident); threshold detection belongs at the single mutation sink so no writer can bypass it.
notes: Feeding-protocol SSoT plan Phase 1 (plan refs P-11/C-1/C-2, register HIGH-005). Fix: LowStockDetected enqueued inside StockMovementService.recordMovement on the caller manager (all writers covered), wire schema added to FARM_EVENT_SCHEMAS, alert-engine LowStockEventHandler + LowStockAlertService create deduped escalatable incidents per (itemType,itemId), websocket bridge + web/mobile invalidation maps carry the new event alongside legacy FeedInventoryLow during the migration window, and the wrapper emits the in-process inventory.lowStock STOCK_LOW auto-task signal post-commit only (new behavior for storage items, documented).

title: Feed stock had three stores (Feed.quantity roll-up, legacy feed_inventory, storage_inventory), three independent inbound writers, and two divergent "days remaining" read paths (forecast vs scheduler cron) — no single source of truth for how much feed exists.
rule_violated: One ledger per physical fact: every reader and writer of feed stock goes through the storage ledger (StockMovementService) and its Feed.quantity roll-up; parallel stores are structural drift.
notes: Feeding-protocol SSoT plan Phase 2 (plan refs P-07/P-09/P-10/P-15, register HIGH-004). Fix: legacy feed_inventory deduction legs removed from both feeding paths (sink emits LowStockDetected), add/adjust/consume/get feed-inventory GraphQL stack deleted with its sole FE consumer (FeedInventoryTab; StoragePage is the single stock UI), scheduler low-stock/expiry/forecast readers re-pointed to the ledger roll-up + lot expiry, demo seeder writes the ledger, permission matrices pruned, e2e specs reworked to the single-ledger reality. Frozen feed_inventory table + entity + wire contracts retire in Phase 8 with an upcaster.

title: Feeding knowledge was fragmented across three overlapping mechanisms (FeedingProtocol template with an UNCONSUMED meal schedule, FeedingProgram+DailyFeedingExecution engine, legacy FeedingTable+scheduler running a parallel 05:00 plan cron) and four independent weight-band feed tables with duplicated findFeedForWeight logic — no single source of truth for what/how much/when fish get fed.
rule_violated: One protocol SSoT: weight-band feed product, rate, expected FCR and meal schedule live in one assignable entity; a single engine plans and executes; duplicated band tables and parallel plan engines are structural drift.
notes: Feeding-protocol SSoT plan Phases 3-6 (plan refs P-01..P-04, register rows HIGH-003 + protocol unification). Phase 3 lands FeedingProtocolV2 + ProtocolAssignment + validation/rate SSoT services; later phases land the per-meal engine, data migration, cutover (all legacy generation disabled) and retirement.

title: skipMeal acquired its pessimistic locks in the REVERSE order (FeedingMeal -> FeedingDayPlan) of the canonical K-1 order (FeedingDayPlan -> FeedingMeal) used by recordMealFeeding and correctMealPour, opening an AB-BA deadlock window between a concurrent skip and a pour on the same meal.
rule_violated: Canonical lock order (K-1): Batch(asc) -> TankBatch -> FeedingDayPlan -> FeedingMeal -> ProtocolAssignment -> storage LAST; every writer acquires in the same direction.
notes: Pre-merge end-to-end audit finding A1. Fix: unlocked meal pre-read resolves dayPlanId, then DayPlan -> Meal pessimistic_write in canonical order, status re-asserted after locking; lock-order pinned by spec.

title: alert-engine had NO feeding-execution consumer: MealUnderfed, MealMissed and UnfedUnitDetected produced no incidents and FeedTypeTransitioned produced no info/audit trail — the Phase 7 table's feeding-execution.handler.ts was never written, so the durable feeding alarm chain dead-ended at NATS.
rule_violated: Operational alarms must flow through durable events with a real consumer (outbox -> NATS -> alert-engine incident); an emitted event without a consumer is a dead contract.
notes: Pre-merge end-to-end audit finding B5 (plan section 6 / K-8b).

title: The 20:00 cron enqueued FeedingDailySummaryEvent to the outbox but notification-service had no consumer, so the daily feeding summary reached no channel (K-8c promised outbox -> notification-service transport).
rule_violated: Every durable event that carries a user-facing obligation must have a registered consumer in the owning service.
notes: Pre-merge end-to-end audit finding B4.

title: ProtocolFeedForecastService.refreshTenant read unit biomass from the NULLABLE TankBatch.currentBiomassKg mirror (Number(undefined) = NaN poisons the whole scope series) instead of the engine/generator SSoT totalBiomassKg (production biomass, cleaner fish excluded per D-13).
rule_violated: Forecast and engine must read fish count/biomass from the same TankBatch SSoT columns (totalQuantity/totalBiomassKg); mirrors are projection conveniences, never calculation inputs.
notes: Pre-merge end-to-end audit finding A2.

title: Forecast startDate was the UTC calendar day (new Date().toISOString().slice(0,10)) while day plans materialize planDate in the site timezone (D-4) — day-0 alignment can shift a day near midnight boundaries and the UTC contract was undocumented.
rule_violated: Date-day semantics must name their timezone SSoT explicitly; silent mixed-timezone day arithmetic is drift.
notes: Pre-merge end-to-end audit finding A3. FE freshness stamp already slices computedAt in UTC — contract documented as UTC day, deliberate and pinned.

title: The forecast loader hardcoded dailySurvivalRate=1.0 and never wired Species.growthParameters.expectedSurvivalRate, so mortalityAssumption was always 'none' even for species with a defined survival rate (plan section 5 requires converting it to a daily rate over the horizon).
rule_violated: Forecast assumptions must be sourced from declared reference data and surfaced explicitly (mortalityAssumption), never silently defaulted when the reference value exists.
notes: Pre-merge end-to-end audit finding A4. computeForecast already supports survival; only the loader wiring was missing.

title: Stockout severity thresholds lived as code twins: alert-engine STOCKOUT_CRITICAL_DAYS=3 and the warehouse-summary handler's literal <=3/<=leadTime coverageStatus thresholds — no shared constant, silent divergence possible.
rule_violated: One threshold, one owner: severity cutoffs consumed by multiple services live in the shared contract package next to the event they qualify.
notes: Pre-merge end-to-end audit finding A5.

title: The 05:30 sweep finalized stale partially_fed meals WITHOUT applying growth for per_meal-mode protocols (the rollup branch only covers growthApplicationMode='daily'), silently losing biomass growth for meals auto-finalized at window close.
rule_violated: Growth application is a total function over finalized intake: every finalized meal applies growth exactly once (per_meal at finalize, daily at rollup) — no finalize path may drop it.
notes: Pre-merge end-to-end audit finding A6.

title: DayPlanAdminResult.outcome was a bare GraphQL String carrying 'recalculated'|'generated'|'transitioned' instead of a registered enum — invalid values were not structurally excluded on the wire (P-25 typed-response posture).
rule_violated: Closed value sets cross the GraphQL boundary as registered enums, not stringly-typed unions.
notes: Pre-merge end-to-end audit finding A7. FE fetches the field but never branches on it; type updated alongside.

title: The plan section 1.2 convenience mutation assignProtocolToBatchUnits(batchId, protocolId) — assign a protocol to all units currently holding a batch — was never implemented.
rule_violated: Planned public API surface ships with the phase that promised it, or is re-scoped with an explicit tracked decision.
notes: Pre-merge end-to-end audit finding B1.

title: The P-30 resolution promised a v2 test rule that every raw-SQL column reference in feeding-protocol services is entity-backed (the class of bug where SQL filters on a column no migration ever created) — the spec was never added.
rule_violated: Raw SQL in services must be provably consistent with entity/migration definitions at test time (make-it-detectable, tier 3).
notes: Pre-merge end-to-end audit finding B2.

title: Mixed-tank operator visibility (D-2) was missing end-to-end: the day-plan snapshot carried no mixedBatch/weight-CV info and MealBoard showed no mixed-tank badge or high-CV warning, even though band policy silently computes from the dominant-biomass batch.
rule_violated: Silent policy assumptions visible to operators: when the engine picks a policy basis (dominant batch) in an ambiguous physical state (mixed tank), the UI must surface it.
notes: Pre-merge end-to-end audit finding B3.

title: useProtocolFeedForecast had no enabled guard: the KPI header and ForecastTab fired the query with siteId undefined while sites were still loading (Forbidden for MODULE_USER; wasted duplicate request churn for everyone).
rule_violated: Queries whose inputs are not yet resolvable are gated with enabled, not fired-and-discarded.
notes: Pre-merge end-to-end audit finding C1.

title: The feeding KPI header and ForecastTab rendered silent zeros/empties on query error — error state was indistinguishable from 'no data', an operator-truth defect on a stock-coverage surface.
rule_violated: Error states render as errors (em-dash/notice), never as fabricated zero metrics.
notes: Pre-merge end-to-end audit finding C2.

title: FeedingFilters remained rendered on FeedingPage although none of the surviving tabs (meal board / forecast / records) consume its filter state — dead UI inviting operator confusion.
rule_violated: Every rendered control affects something; controls whose consumers were retired retire with them.
notes: Pre-merge end-to-end audit finding C3.

title: stableStringify existed as THREE copies: the FARM-LOW-141-pinned byte-identical pair (useBatches.ts + aquamobil offline-queue.ts) plus a divergent utils/command-envelope.ts copy that filters undefined-valued keys — in-module duplication with a semantic drift.
rule_violated: One canonical serializer per app for the payloadHash dedup contract; the mobile copy is the single documented exception (standalone app).
notes: Pre-merge end-to-end audit finding C4.

title: useWarehouseSummary built its query key with tenantId twice (createTenantQueryKey(tenantId, 'warehouseSummary', tenantId)) — redundant key segment, cache-key hygiene.
rule_violated: Tenant scoping lives once in the key factory prefix; payload segments carry only query-distinguishing inputs.
notes: Pre-merge end-to-end audit finding C5.

title: Droplet capacity diagnostics were blind during the exact incidents they exist for: du -x -d1 / traversed the docker overlay tree and hit the 60s timeout (disk_usage_unavailable exit_status=124), so the report could not attribute the ~90GB of NON-docker usage; docker bytes were already itemized by docker system df.
rule_violated: Capacity triage output must attribute usage when the gate fails; a diagnostic that times out under the condition it diagnoses is structurally useless.
notes: Fix: du walk excludes docker/containerd subtrees (their bytes come from docker system df), default timeout 60->120s, maintenance surface runs deep per-directory mode; SSoT contract pins updated.

title: Safe image GC had an open-ended tag class: app-prefix tags outside the keep-allowlist that were neither 40-hex SHAs nor rollback-* (e.g. incident-clean-e8a67919b, 1.87GB) matched NO GC branch and accumulated forever.
rule_violated: Image retention is a closed allowlist (default-deny): an unclassified tag class must be reclaimed when unprotected, not silently immortal.
notes: Fix: unclassified app tags removed when the image ID is unprotected (running containers / rollback manifest / current DEPLOY_SHA still protect); removed_unclassified counter + invariant pins added.

title: Finding IDs are allocated from independent worktree snapshots, allowing concurrent registry writers to select the same domain suffix
rule_violated: 2026-07-15 enterprise-closure finding policy — identities must be allocated atomically across concurrent worktrees before append
notes: Verified recurrence: duplicate detection happened only after a caller supplied an ID, and each worktree read its own registry snapshot. The remediation must serialize all registry mutations in Git common-dir, durably reserve a domain high-water mark, scan active worktrees, and fail closed on malformed or foreign locks.

title: Post-cutover FeedingLedger treats depleted feed as untracked and commits feeding without a stock movement
rule_violated: After single-ledger cutover, missing usable stock must fail closed; row absence cannot select a compatibility mode.
notes: Post-cutover recurrence of the Phase-A exception documented by resolved FARM-HIGH-058; FARM-HIGH-218 does not capture this fail-open depleted-row chain.

title: Migration 180610 skips every legacy balance for dual-present feeds and overwrites the roll-up without reconciliation provenance
rule_violated: A cutover must classify every legacy row as MIGRATED, ALREADY_REPRESENTED, or CONFLICT and fail closed on unresolved reconciliation.
notes: The concrete row-level loss is not canonically covered by the broad FARM-HIGH-218 SSoT finding.

title: Inventory-count approval and stock transfer bypass the canonical inventory mutation sink
rule_violated: Every physical stock mutation must pass through the canonical mutation kernel so idempotency, audit, roll-up, lot, alarm, outbox, and concurrency policy cannot diverge.
notes: FARM-HIGH-215 covers only purchase-order receipt; it does not cover inventory-count approval or stock transfer writers.

title: Concurrent NULL-lot receipts can create duplicate storage projections and leave Feed.quantity stale
rule_violated: The physical-stock key must be database-unique including NULL lot values, and inbound projection mutation must be atomic under concurrency.
notes: The runtime race and stale roll-up are not represented by an existing canonical FARM finding.

title: Migration 180660 rollback cannot distinguish backfilled records from live drain writes and deletes both
rule_violated: A migration rollback may delete only rows carrying migration-owned provenance; predicate similarity must never erase live writer output.
notes: No existing canonical finding covers this destructive rollback/live-write provenance collision.

title: The production stop-line also blocks the PostgreSQL WAL-G image required to establish the backup evidence that unlocks it
rule_violated: A fail-closed production release lock must retain a separately authorized, least-privilege recovery path for the exact control-plane component needed to produce its own unlock evidence.
notes: Keep the general production stop-line unchanged. The repair must build an exact protected-main PostgreSQL digest without production secrets or SSH, sign it only after the protected backup-release Environment gate, and permit a provider-console executor to recreate only postgres by digest. It must not expose db-migrate, application services, mutable tags, repository-variable mutation, or the legacy GitHub SSH lane.

title: Production maintenance has no fixed-allowlist, predicate-guarded host-artifact operation; the 6 GiB cleanup-named candidate is active swap and must be denied
rule_violated: Production host reclamation must be an audited fixed allowlist with fail-closed ownership, activity, mount, swap, and deploy-checkout predicates; operators must never pass arbitrary deletion paths.
notes: The candidate /swapfile-cleanup-20260610 is currently active and 5,137,809,408 of 6,442,446,848 bytes are used. The remediation must intentionally deny it while active; swapoff and reclamation are out of scope without separate memory-lifecycle authority.
narrative: Deploy Capacity Maintenance run 29619814634 measured 6,442,463,232 allocated bytes at /swapfile-cleanup-20260610.
Read-only swapon evidence on 2026-07-18 showed that the cleanup-named file is active and heavily used, so it is neither stale nor currently reclaimable.

title: The planned PostgreSQL DR bootstrap cannot safely land while capacity and deploy host mutations lack one global lock
rule_violated: Every production host control plane that can mutate Docker image or container state must serialize through one root-owned lock, and unresolved or corrupt recovery journals must make image GC fail closed.
notes: Pre-merge design blocker for INFRA-HIGH-073: that finding requires an exact-digest PostgreSQL provider executor with exact-prior rollback, while current capacity GC performs global dangling prunes and tag removal and the current deploy lane mutates the same host without a common lock. The DR executor must not merge until all three lanes share one authority and GC fails closed on unresolved recovery state.
narrative: INFRA-HIGH-073's canonical repair contract requires a provider-console executor that can restore the observed prior PostgreSQL image after a failed forward recreation.

Current capacity GC and production deploy have no host-global lock or recovery-journal guard, so the planned executor would introduce an unsafe interleaving unless the sibling control planes are repaired in the same ordered train.

title: Production capacity and deploy SSH recur INFRA-CRITICAL-041/043: opaque transport lacks host-key authority and executes target-host Git from mutable shared configuration
rule_violated: All production SSH must use auditable native OpenSSH with an exact protected host fingerprint, sanitized execution, and runner-produced exact-SHA release material; target-host mutable Git configuration cannot be an execution authority.
notes: Backup/PITR lanes were repaired, but deploy-capacity-maintenance and both deploy-digitalocean SSH jobs still use appleboy/ssh-action without fingerprint binding. Capacity also fetches/checks out through /var/aqua-saas/.git; deploy bootstraps from the same mutable remote/object-store authority. The production Environment initially lacked DROPLET_SSH_FINGERPRINT; it was provisioned on 2026-07-18 but is not yet consumed by these workflows.
narrative: Live GitHub configuration showed DROPLET_SSH_FINGERPRINT only in production-backup before remediation; the production Environment received the host's ED25519 fingerprint on 2026-07-18.
Secret provisioning alone does not close the recurrence: the workflows must leave the opaque action and target-host Git bootstrap path.

title: The 8 GiB production host is using 7.28 GiB of swap while production, integration, and agent workloads share the node; the second swap file cannot be reclaimed safely
rule_violated: Production memory and swap must have an owned capacity/lifecycle budget; development and long-lived integration workloads cannot consume the same node without bounded cleanup and proof that swap changes cannot trigger OOM.
notes: Read-only evidence: RAM total 8,326,946,816 and available 3,567,439,872; swap used 7,275,569,152 of 8,589,926,400. /swapfile uses 2,137,759,744 bytes and /swapfile-cleanup-20260610 uses 5,137,809,408 bytes. Swapoff/removal is forbidden until workload lifecycle and memory headroom prove safety.
narrative: Container inventory included three aqua-walg-it integration containers running for about 42 hours alongside the production stack; active agent sessions also share the node.

This evidence does not authorize killing sessions, deleting worktrees, stopping proof containers, resizing a paid droplet, or changing swap; each needs explicit lifecycle evidence and a bounded control-plane operation.

title: Four minimatch overrides both masked high npm advisories and force-downgraded glob v10/v13 across a major API boundary, leaving the production dependency graph on unpatchable brace-expansion lines
rule_violated: A dependency override must express a version floor that its consumer's declared range admits; pinning a consumer below the major it declares silences the audit while breaking the consumer's API contract.
notes: npm audit --audit-level=high --omit=dev (the ci-affected security-audit job, a required merge-gate input) reported 4 advisory groups; once the tree resolved honestly it was 10 high findings. Three of the four minimatch overrides pinned exactly the version their consumer already declares and were inert, and one of those consumers (@humanwhocodes/config-array) is no longer in the tree. The fourth, glob:{minimatch:3.1.5}, applied to glob@10.5.0 (declares ^9.0.4) and glob@13.0.6 (declares ^10.2.2), both of which construct Minimatch with optimizationLevel/windowsPathsNoEscape options minimatch@3 does not have; npm ls reported minimatch@3.1.5 invalid: ^10. Fixed by REMOVING the overrides rather than adding pins, then flooring brace-expansion to ^5.0.8 scoped to minimatch@^10 only -- 5.0.8 is the sole unaffected release (advisory range is <=5.0.7 with no lower bound, so 1.1.16 and 2.1.2 do not clear it) and its export is an object rather than a callable, so a repo-wide override breaks every minimatch@3 consumer. That is exactly how the earlier attempt e4bcb6cf7 failed: the Nx project graph died with 'expand is not a function'. typeorm moved to glob ^13.0.6; gaxios ^7.3.0 dropped rimraf upstream, deleting the gcp-metadata->gaxios->rimraf->glob@10->minimatch@9 chain outright. fast-uri ^3.1.2->^3.1.4 (the old override permitted the vulnerable 3.0.0-3.1.3 range), postcss ^8.5.23, sharp ^0.34.5->^0.35.3 with a named type import in thumbnail.service.ts because sharp 0.35's types field now points at the ESM index.d.mts, whose named exports replace declare namespace sharp. Verified: 10 high -> 1 high; type-check 40/40; nx graph resolves; the CI npm ls graph-contract step exits 0; typeorm glob@13 entity discovery returns 94/18/22 files matching find; sharp loads libvips 8.18.3 and encodes under --ignore-scripts; dashboard build, event-contracts 279 tests, messaging-service 285 tests + lint, lint-gate parity 11/11 all green. The residual is INFRA-HIGH-081.

title: brace-expansion DoS stays reachable in the production graph through eslint 9's minimatch 3 chain, and the only upstream fix (eslint 10) has no compatible release for three of the six lint plugins in use
rule_violated: A known-vulnerable transitive dependency that cannot be floored must carry a tracked owner, deadline and unblock condition rather than be silenced at the gate or left unnamed.
notes: After INFRA-HIGH-080 the security-audit gate reports 1 high advisory instead of 0. brace-expansion@1.1.15 remains under eslint, @eslint/eslintrc and @eslint/config-array. It cannot be floored there: the only unaffected release is 5.0.8, whose export is an object; eslint/lib/eslint/eslint-helpers.js does const minimatch = require('minimatch') and calls it, and both @eslint packages use a default import; minimatch@10 exports an object with no default export (verified -- require() yields {minimatch, sep, GLOBSTAR, ...} and a default ESM import throws). npm names the fix itself: fixAvailable eslint@10.8.0, which depends on minimatch ^10.2.5. Blocked upstream, not by scope: the repo already runs flat config with no .eslintrc* files left and @typescript-eslint v8 already accepts eslint ^10, but eslint-plugin-import@2.32.0, eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y@6.10.2 and eslint-plugin-react@7.37.5 are the current releases and all three cap their eslint peer at ^9. Forcing eslint 10 past three unsatisfied peers is the override-that-breaks-the-build this work exists to avoid. UNBLOCK CONDITION: those three plugins ship eslint-10 peer ranges; the migration must then also re-baseline tools/lint-gates/eslintrc-flat-parity.spec.ts, which pins a golden ESLint-8 resolved rule map. Rejected alternatives, recorded so they are not silently retried: lowering --audit-level (removes the gate, not the advisory); adding an audit allowlist (the YAML tools/gates/npm-audit.ts documents does not exist, the CI job runs raw npm audit rather than that gate, and building the mechanism would re-point a security control's authority from inside a dependency PR); reclassifying tools/eslint-rules dependencies so eslint leaves the --omit=dev graph -- tested, and marking the eslint peer optional is insufficient because @typescript-eslint/utils declares eslint as a required peer of its own, so making it work needs the plugin's runtime dependency moved to an optional peer too, at which point the manifest is being shaped to move an advisory out of a report rather than to describe the software.

title: Dev-only ESLint tooling and an unused Claude Agent SDK are classified as production dependencies, blocking runtime audit and license gates with packages absent from application execution
rule_violated: Production dependency and license gates must model the exact dependency graph installed into runtime images; build-only workspaces and unused packages cannot become runtime authorities.
notes: tools/eslint-rules was an unreferenced workspace, so npm classified its @typescript-eslint/utils dependency and eslint peer as production. The repository also declared @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk without an import; its platform package carries a custom license. The fix makes the private plugin an explicit root file: devDependency and removes the unused Agent SDK while retaining @anthropic-ai/sdk, the actual ai-service runtime client.

title: CI Full uses an unconfigured Snyk secret and an unpinned first-error license command whose allowlist does not represent the locked production dependency contract
rule_violated: Required CI controls must be deterministic from repository state, must not depend on an unavailable credential, and must fail closed on unreviewed dependency or license drift.
notes: CI Full invoked Snyk despite the dedicated workflow documenting that SNYK_TOKEN is not configured. Its npx license-checker command downloaded an unpinned tool and stopped at the first license, while the allowlist omitted multiple licenses already present in the production lock. The fix leaves Snyk manual and replaces the command with a lockfile-based exact-version policy.

title: CI Full skips pull requests and protected-main pushes, and its ref-scoped cancellation can discard exact-main SHA evidence
rule_violated: The canonical full-CI summary must run on every merge candidate and protected-main SHA, and a later main push must never cancel evidence for an earlier main SHA.
notes: CI Full ran only weekly, manually and for release tags. Its concurrency key grouped all main pushes by refs/heads/main with cancel-in-progress true, so a newer push could cancel the exact-SHA run being used as evidence. The repair adds PR/main triggers, PR-number-or-SHA grouping, PR-only cancellation, an explicit build-status name and required-status contract.

title: Concurrent deploy-capacity fixture writes can interleave and report a false missing invocation
rule_violated: Concurrency tests must record each worker observation atomically; split writes to one shared append log cannot be the authority for invocation cardinality.
notes: CI Full exposed a pre-existing race: four fake du workers appended the encoded scope and newline separately. The repair performs one append per logical record without serializing the production worker pool.

title: CI Full starts parallel Rust lint targets before the pinned toolchain is installed
rule_violated: A CI job that fans out cargo-backed Nx targets must provision the exact Rust toolchain once before parallel execution can mutate the shared rustup installation.
notes: The PR-triggered full lint job reproduced the race: event-contracts-rs saw a toolchain without cargo while router-coprocessor collided during component directory replacement. The repair provisions Rust 1.88.0 before Nx fan-out and contracts the ordering.

title: CI Full turns historical repository-wide Prettier debt into an unrelated required-check failure
rule_violated: A newly required formatting gate must fail closed on the candidate delta without converting pre-existing unrelated debt into an unconditional merge blocker.
notes: CI Full lint, type-check, and type-check-spec succeeded, then the legacy repository-wide format command failed on 5,475 files already present on main. The repair ratchets Prettier-managed files against the PR base or push before SHA, with a parent fallback for scheduled and manual runs.

title: CI Full coverage mode lacks the shared Vitest coverage provider
rule_violated: Every workspace selected by the canonical full test command must have the coverage provider required by its declared test runner available from the reproducible root install.
notes: CI Full reached the complete coverage matrix and proved three Vitest workspaces failed before test discovery because @vitest/coverage-v8 was absent from the root npm installation. The repair adds the provider at the exact root Vitest version so every workspace receives one lockfile-governed implementation.

title: MCP risk report repeats invariant chemistry calculations until coverage timeout
rule_violated: Coverage tests must keep deterministic computation within the runner budget and must not recompute values that are invariant across an inner search dimension.
notes: Once the missing coverage provider was installed, the MCP report scenario exceeded Vitest's five-second default under coverage. Its TAN threshold search recalculated pH-only H2S, CO2, and ammonia fractions for every TAN candidate. The repair precomputes that fixed pH risk grid once and preserves the search resolution and output.

title: CI Full inherited impossible dormant Jest coverage floors and compiled excluded sources
rule_violated: A required coverage gate must begin at an observed enforceable baseline, ratchet monotonically, and collect only sources that belong to the selected unit-test surface.
notes: The first required full-coverage run proved six Jest services had hard-coded 60 percent thresholds above their current passing suites, so the previously dormant gate was impossible. Coverage collection also compiled an archived HR migration, farm E2E sources, and a gateway mock whose narrower response methods conflicted with Partial<Response>. The repair records the first observed floors centrally, locks them with an invariant, excludes only non-unit and archived sources from collection, and corrects the gateway mock type.

title: CI Full required a tokenless Codecov upload without token or OIDC authority
rule_violated: Required CI must provision the authentication authority demanded by a fail-closed external upload, while keeping the local coverage gate independently enforceable.
notes: The exact-head full test command passed and produced 23 coverage reports, but Codecov v7 rejected the subsequent upload because the workflow supplied neither a repository token nor OIDC. The repair grants id-token: write only to the test job, selects use_oidc: true, and locks both requirements with the CI contract invariant.

title: Alert trend regression allocated an index array and traversed each dataset four times
rule_violated: A latency-critical trend primitive must have allocation-free O(n) work with deterministic complexity evidence, not rely only on a scheduler-sensitive wall-clock assertion.
notes: Exact-head full coverage measured 5.26466047 ms per 1,000-value trend calculation against the existing 5 ms SLA. The implementation allocated an indices array and performed four reductions. The repair uses one allocation-free online covariance pass, retains the absolute SLA, and adds an exact one-read-per-sample complexity contract.

title: Unprovisioned Codecov dependency omitted non-root JS coverage evidence
rule_violated: Required coverage evidence must be repository-owned, complete across declared producers, fail closed, and independent of an unprovisioned external control plane.
notes: OIDC issuance succeeded and 23 root reports were found, but Codecov returned Repository not found because the repository was never set up in its control plane. The prior directory scope also omitted Vitest reports outside ./coverage. The repair replaces the unsupported vendor dependency with a 34-producer inventory, deterministic LCOV validation, monotonic service floors, SHA-256 evidence manifest, minimum-permission CI job, and fail-closed GitHub artifact retention.

title: Nested Nx and Vitest worker pools oversubscribed CI runners
rule_violated: Parallel test schedulers must share an explicit resource budget so deterministic tests do not fail under nested worker oversubscription.
notes: Nx runs test projects concurrently while each Vitest project independently sized a worker pool from the host CPU count. Under coverage this caused Recharts/jsdom tests to cross their unchanged 5-second assertion boundary. The centralized policy caps every project at two workers; the unchanged shared-ui suite then passed 23 suites and 368 tests in 30.60 seconds.

title: Typed coverage adapter had no type-check ownership
rule_violated: Every changed TypeScript adapter must have one compiler owner and derive identities from the canonical runtime data contract.
notes: Jest consumes the CommonJS facade while TypeScript resolves the same .js imports through the typed sibling. The adapter was required but fell outside every tools tsconfig and manually repeated the project-name union. The repair adds explicit tools/quality compiler ownership and derives project identities from the JSON SSoT.

title: Test fixtures concealed incomplete contracts behind double casts
rule_violated: Tests must construct contract-valid entities and metadata structures without bypassing the type system through double casts.
notes: The range gate exposed AlertRule fixtures created as Partial and repeatedly forced through double casts, plus GraphQL metadata attached by casting ExecutionContext. The fixture now builds a real AlertRule with all required fields and Object.assign returns a structurally typed extended context.

title: Changed-file guard routed test-utils through production compilers
rule_violated: Changed-file type ownership must classify every conventional test surface under the project test compiler rather than leaking test globals into production.
notes: The guard recognized test/, __tests__, and spec/test suffixes but omitted the repository-wide test-utils convention. It therefore sent a Jest-only gateway helper to tsconfig.app.json and reported missing jest globals. The classifier now routes test-utils through tsconfig.spec.json and an invariant locks the path convention.

title: Workspace package inference exposed unowned test factory lint debt
rule_violated: A first-class workspace package must own a warning-free lint surface whose test factories narrow unknown contracts instead of bypassing the type system.
notes: Adding the package export activated Nx package inference and made the complete testing library lintable. The repair removes a redundant repository double cast, structurally narrows unknown event payloads, and declares the policy file's real CommonJS runtime without disabling any rule.

title: Mock response accessors relied on a non-narrowing array length guard
rule_violated: Test helpers must encode empty-history behavior in their access operation and remain valid under noUncheckedIndexedAccess.
notes: The independent length check did not narrow a subsequent computed index, producing TS2532 on both response accessors in the exact-head changed-file compiler. Optional element access now returns undefined for an empty call history and preserves populated tuple values without assertions.

title: Alert cache test compared two single-sample wall-clock timings
rule_violated: Cache effectiveness must be proven through deterministic hit and I/O contracts rather than scheduler-sensitive single-sample wall-clock ordering.
notes: The exact-head runner measured one valid cache miss at 0.86 ms and its cache hit at 6.84 ms because of scheduler jitter. The replacement proves object reuse plus exactly one query-builder construction and one repository read across two loads, without changing production logic, timeouts, or thresholds.

title: Frozen coverage policy declaration was incompatible with Vitest InlineConfig
rule_violated: A shared configuration SSoT must expose a type contract assignable to every consumer without introducing shared mutable state.
notes: The runtime policy deep-froze its reporter tuple and the declaration exposed that readonly tuple directly, but Vitest InlineConfig requires an assignable mutable Arrayable reporter field. A factory now returns a fresh reporter array per consumer inside a frozen policy envelope; all 40 project tsconfigs, the runtime target, and an isolation invariant pass.

title: Coverage-mode test run swallowed --coverage at eight producers and cached test tasks without their coverage outputs
rule_violated: A gate must be able to succeed: the coverage-evidence contract required reports from producers whose runner never received the coverage flag
narrative: The ci-full test job runs `npm run test:all -- --coverage`, which becomes `nx run-many --target=test --all --coverage`. Eight Vitest producers defined `test` as an `nx:run-commands` target wrapping `npm run test`. That executor appends forwarded arguments to its command string, producing `npm run test --coverage` — npm reads the flag as one of its own config options and never passes it to Vitest. Those eight ran with coverage off, wrote no report, and the coverage-evidence gate failed on a run in which every test had passed.

The two producers that did emit reports (messaging-module, tenant-admin) declared no `test` target at all and used the target Nx infers from the package.json script, whose executor forwards options correctly.

A second, latent half of the same failure: `test` is a cached target and ci-full restores .nx/cache between runs, but no test target declared the coverage directory among its `outputs`. Nx restores only declared outputs, so a replayed test task left no report behind — the gate would have failed intermittently even after the flag reached the runner.

title: Attendance clock-in test spied on Date.now while the handler reads new Date, so it passed only during the shift window's hours
rule_violated: A test must control the inputs it claims to control; wall-clock time is an input, not an ambient constant
narrative: `ClockInHandler` reads the instant with `new Date()` (line 93). The test set up its clock with `jest.spyOn(Date, 'now')`, and `new Date()` never calls `Date.now()` — so the spy changed nothing and the handler saw the real wall clock.

The handler rejects a clock-in outside the shift window, which for the fixture shift is 07:00-22:00. The assertion therefore passed whenever CI happened to run inside that window and failed on every run outside it. It went red on a 06:31 UTC run and had passed on a 21:11 UTC run of the same code the evening before.

Reproduced deterministically by moving the runner's timezone rather than waiting for the hour: under TZ=Etc/GMT+6 (local 01:00) the failure is identical to CI's, and after faking the system clock the suite is 30/30 under Etc/GMT+6, Etc/GMT-9 and UTC alike.

title: Payroll period numbering and leave half-day arithmetic shift by one calendar unit when the host timezone is behind UTC
rule_violated: Date arithmetic that spans a calendar boundary must be evaluated in a fixed, declared timezone rather than the host's
narrative: Surfaced while reproducing the attendance clock defect by shifting the runner timezone. Under TZ=Etc/GMT+6 the payroll number for a January pay period is generated as PAY-202512 instead of PAY-202601, and the leave half-day path returns 2 days where it should return 1.5.

Both are UTC-versus-local calendar-boundary errors, the same family as the attendance defect but in different code. They are invisible to CI because the runner is UTC, and invisible to the platform only for as long as every deployment stays on UTC — a payroll period attributed to the wrong month is a finance-visible error, not a test artifact.

NOT investigated in this change: whether the production handlers or only the fixtures are wrong. The reproduction is recorded here so the owner starts from evidence rather than rediscovering it; the fix is the owner's, on the deadline set.

notes: Two concurrent activate calls carrying the same valid token (e.g. a cloned SD-card image, or an attacker racing a legitimate boot who holds the installer token) both read tokenUsedAt=null, both pass validation, both enter the transaction, and both save. Result: two distinct MQTT credential sets generated for the same device identity, the second silently overwriting the first, and the single-use invariant is violated.

notes: Many industrial devices publish 32-bit floats/ints in Low-High word order. The RTU adapter exposes a wordOrder config field and schema option but the decoder ignores it, so every LOW_HIGH device yields byte-swapped garbage. The TCP adapter's swap is limited to the first register pair and silently mis-decodes float64 and register arrays. The config schema promises a behaviour the codec does not honor. Because there are no adapter tests (see test-gap finding), this drift is invisible.

title: Sensor Modbus 32-bit word-order decoding is wrong: modbus-rtu ignores wordOrder entirely; modbus-tcp only swaps the first 2 words

notes: rollbackChangeSet builds an inverse change set by swapping requestedValue↔previousValue, but coalesces a null previousValue to 0. If the original apply never captured a baseline (e.g. read-back failed, or an emergency rollback of a partially-applied set), the rollback commands 0 to registers such as max_frequency, current_limit_percent, or a control word — a hazardous value delivered under the label 'rollback'. Range validation is not re-run on the inverse set before write.
rule_violated: category=ics-safety: Never fabricate a rollback target. If item.previousValue is null, exclude that item from the inverse set and surface it as an un-rollbackable parameter requiring manual attention, rather than writing 0. Re-run validateValueInRange on every inverse item against the current parame
title: Change-set rollback writes a literal 0 to safety registers when the original previousValue is null

notes: writeParameterValue can push an arbitrary engineering value straight to a register with no bounds check; it is a public method currently unused by resolvers. Even on the change-set path, values are validated only when added, not re-clamped at the instant of write, so a definition change between submit and apply is not re-enforced. This leaves an unguarded write primitive one wiring mistake away from an unclamped hardware write.
rule_violated: category=security: Centralize a single clampAndWrite(def, value) that enforces def.minValue/maxValue (and isWritable) immediately before every register write, used by both applyChangeSet and writeParameterValue. Remove writeParameterValue if it has no caller, or gate it behind the same validation +
title: writeParameterValue is an unbounded direct-write primitive with no server-side clamp against brand-config limits

notes: Surfaced during the SENSOR-MEDIUM-066/068 reading-store convergence remediation (PR #1004), not one of the original 102 audit findings. rule_violated: category=correctness/convergence (deeper half of SENSOR-MEDIUM-066/068): the federated per-reading read surface must return device-ingested data. narrative: Reproduced against a live PostgreSQL 16 by calling the production orchestrator directly: runSchemaMigrations({ schema: 'tenant_0000000000000001', migrations: apps/sensor-service/src/database/migrations/[0-9]*, migrationsTableName: 'migrations_sensor' }) — the exact call tenant-schema-provisioner.ts makes at processJob(). Against an EMPTY sensor schema the run created every Baseline table inside `sensor` and none inside the tenant schema; applyTenantRlsToSchema then logged 'No tenant-scoped tables found in schema tenant_0000000000000001 — nothing to do'. Against a sensor schema that already held one Baseline table (the state of any real deployment, where the source schema migrates first) the same call aborted with: relation "sensor_protocols" already exists.

Mechanism: tenant provisioning is migration REPLAY. The orchestrator pins SET search_path TO "<tenant schema>", public before every migration, which routes UNQUALIFIED DDL into the tenant schema. Every Baseline is generated by TypeORM's CLI and is therefore fully schema-qualified ("sensor"."sensors", "farm"."code_sequences", "hr"."payrolls"), so the search_path pin has no effect on it and the DDL re-targets the source schema. The only escape hatch, @SourceOnlyMigration, is applied to exactly one sensor migration and to no Baseline.

Existing tenants are NOT affected: their migrations_<schema> journals were populated by the retired runtime seeder (SchemaManagerService.seedMigrationsHistory), so Baseline is already recorded as applied and replay resumes at the first genuinely-new migration. That is why incremental fan-out works today and why the breakage is invisible until someone provisions a NEW tenant. stray-tenant-journal-heal.ts documents the same coupling from the other side: dropping a tenant journal 'would make the next deploy re-run the full history against that tenant and crash on relation already exists'.

Why no test caught it: bootstrap-from-scratch.spec.ts migrates source schemas only and never provisions a tenant; tenant-schema-provisioner.contract.spec.ts is a text-grep spec with no database; tenant-clone-parity.spec.ts provisions its fixture with CREATE TABLE ... LIKE INCLUDING ALL — the retired runtime mechanism — so it validates a fan-out shape production no longer produces, and its table-set assertion is a tautology because the spec itself is the fan-out. tests/invariants/tenant-aware-migration-ddl-guard.spec.ts would catch the qualified DDL but filters Baseline out of its own file list with no stated reason.

Fix direction (needs its own PR + architectural-arbiter review): either make every tenant-aware Baseline replay-safe (unqualified DDL for per-tenant tables, @SourceOnlyMigration for the cross-tenant ones), or have the provisioner seed a new tenant's journal from the source ledger up to the Baseline head before replaying — the behaviour the retired seeder used to provide. Whichever is chosen, the gate is a live-database test that provisions a tenant through the real provisioner and asserts a non-empty, correctly-shaped tenant schema; the current countTenantTables > 0 check inside the provisioner already fails loudly, so this is broken-and-noisy rather than silently-wrong.
notes: Found while verifying that migration 1815000000000-CreateTenantSensorMetricsHypertable actually reaches tenant schemas. It does — for EXISTING tenants, whose journals already record Baseline, so the replay resumes and runs the new unqualified migration in each tenant schema as designed. New-tenant provisioning is a separate, pre-existing platform break that predates this branch and affects all seven tenant-aware services equally, so it is tracked rather than folded into the sensor PR: the fix touches eight Baselines or the provisioner's journal-seeding contract, needs architectural-arbiter sign-off on which of the two, and cannot be validated without a live provisioning run. Owner: data-expert (by-okan@live.com). Deadline: 2026-08-15.
rule_violated: category=correctness/tenant-provisioning. ADR-011 schema-per-tenant requires that every per-tenant table exist in each tenant_<uuid> schema. Provisioning delivers that by replaying each tenant-aware service's migration set with search_path pinned to the tenant schema, which only works for UNQUALIFIED DDL. Every service's Baseline is fully source-schema-qualified, so the replay lands nothing in the tenant schema and aborts on the first duplicate relation. No new tenant can be onboarded until this is fixed.
title: New-tenant provisioning cannot succeed for ANY tenant-aware service: the replayed Baseline migration is fully source-schema-qualified, so it creates zero tables in the tenant schema and aborts with 'relation already exists'

narrative: `format check-changed` resolves its base from FORMAT_BASE_SHA and falls back to `HEAD^` when that variable is unset. CI sets it to the pull request's base, so CI checks every file the branch touches; a developer running the same command locally checks only the last commit. On this branch that was 67 files locally versus 195 in CI.

The consequence is not theoretical: 35 files added by this branch were never Prettier-formatted, the local gate reported success on every run, and the drift only surfaced when CI - Full first ran on the branch. New files are the worst case, because they have no base blob and are counted as regressions outright.

The 35 files are formatted in this change. The gate itself is NOT fixed here: making the local default match CI means resolving the merge-base against the default branch, which changes behaviour for every developer and belongs to the tooling owner. Recorded with owner infra-expert and deadline 2026-09-15 rather than patched in a sensor PR.
rule_violated: A gate a developer can run locally must evaluate the same thing CI evaluates, or it provides false assurance
title: Format gate checks a different, far narrower base locally than in CI, so a branch can look clean and still fail the required check

narrative: The test mints a JWT with `exp: Math.floor(Date.now()/1000) + 1` and asserts the guard accepts it. Because `now` is floored to whole seconds, the token's real remaining life is anywhere from ~1000ms down to ~0ms, and the guard is genuinely correct to reject it once that elapses. The assertion therefore measures runner speed, not the expiry boundary.

It failed in CI - Full at 08:24 UTC with `UnauthorizedException: Invalid or expired token`; the same suite took 40.6s under coverage instrumentation. It passed on an earlier run of identical gateway-api code, so it is load-dependent rather than broken code.

Proved by controlled comparison rather than by observing it pass once: with a 1.5s delay injected between minting the token and calling the guard, the unpinned test reproduces CI's exact error, and the pinned-clock version passes. Only `Date` is faked so the guard's real asynchronous work still settles.
rule_violated: A test must not depend on how much real time elapses between its setup and its assertion
title: AuthGuard token-expiry test asserted the runner's speed rather than the guard's boundary, and failed once the suite got slower

narrative: CI - Full's build job failed on bc96b2d1a with `Running target build for 39 projects failed` and two names: router-coprocessor:build and protocol-codec-rs:build. Across the whole job log neither name appears anywhere else — no Compiling line, no rustc diagnostic, no exit status. Nx printed the summary and discarded the tasks' output.

The evidence says the code was never the problem. The commit contains zero Rust or Cargo files (33 .ts, 2 .md, 1 .tsx, 1 .jsonl, 1 .json); both crates build clean locally; the same build job passed on the parent commit minutes earlier; and on this exact SHA all eleven dedicated Rust jobs passed, including cargo test --workspace, cargo clippy -D warnings, cargo check, cross-build (musl) for two targets, and the compile + test-compile gate.

What the mechanism actually was remains unknown, and that is the finding. There is no OOM evidence in the log — the `signal` and `137` matches are crate names and version strings, not a kill signal or exit code. A task that dies without emitting a line is not a compiler rejection, but the job as configured cannot tell anyone which of the possibilities it was, so the next occurrence will cost the same investigation. Making the build job stream or retain per-task output is the fix; it belongs to the workflow's owner rather than to a sensor PR.
rule_violated: A failing CI job must surface why it failed; a task name with no captured output is not a diagnosis
title: A failing Nx task in CI Full's build job reports its name and nothing else, so every failure costs a full investigation
The finding-ID allocator cannot see the markdown orphan store, and the commit-msg resolver cannot see the registry, so ORPHAN IDs are minted onto live findings and then fail to resolve
rule_violated: Two stores that allocate from the same identifier space must be read by the allocator that hands identifiers out and by the resolver that validates references to them; an allocator blind to half the space issues duplicate identifiers, and a resolver blind to half the space rejects valid ones.
notes: Two halves of one defect, both reproduced. (1) ALLOCATOR: cmdAdd built existingIds from the hash-chained registry plus the reservation ledger only. The registry's ORPHAN maximum was 332 while docs/reviews/orphan-findings.md was already at 416, so nextFindingId returned ORPHAN-*-333 and the next eighteen after it — all of them sequences that already named live findings. Proven directly: nextFindingId('ORPHAN','HIGH', registryIds) returns ORPHAN-HIGH-333 while the same call with the markdown sequences added returns ORPHAN-HIGH-417. Eight of the nineteen collided exactly (337, 338, 340, 341, 344, 347, 349, 350), so their commit trailers resolved to unrelated findings; eleven differed only in severity, so they failed to resolve at all. (2) RESOLVER: validateCommit routed any ORPHAN-prefixed trailer to the markdown store and never consulted the registry, while the gate's own failure message told the author that 'Finding IDs live in: docs/reviews/_registry/findings.jsonl'. Eleven ledger ORPHAN IDs were already unreferenceable before this session touched anything. Also fixed: ORPHAN_HEADING_REGEX required a CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW segment and exactly three digits, so it skipped 16 real headings (ORPHAN-001..013, ORPHAN-063, ORPHAN-INFO-363, ORPHAN-LOW-337b) — every skipped heading was a sequence the allocator believed free. The pattern and its reader now live once, in finding-registry-store.ts, read by both consumers. Remaining debt tracked separately: the 8 exact-ID collisions already pushed to a branch cannot be repaired in place, and the gate's unit tests ran in no workflow and no hook until this commit wired them.

title: Corrupting the autonomous-failure ledger silently un-trips the circuit breaker, returning the kernel's own safety net to a permissive state
rule_violated: A safety-net state derivation must answer tripped whenever its failure evidence is unreadable or incomplete; lost evidence must never reduce the trip count.
notes: Reproduced at bdaf00b with threshold_24h=3: three valid failure rows return tripped; corrupting two of the three returns ok; three rows with unparseable ts return ok. Two independent row-dropping paths cause it - _read_failures reads with on_corruption=tolerant and _count_failures_24h silently skips an unparseable ts - against a sliding >= threshold decision. auto_action_gate._load_breaker_state additionally collapsed any exception to ok.

title: The scheduled producer and the agent executor share no queue, so minted agent requests can never reach the executor
rule_violated: A work queue must be reachable by its consumer; queue authority cannot live in a path excluded from the consumer's filesystem.
notes: Structural, not observational: .gitignore line 205 ignores aria-tools/agent-invocations/, and aria-agent-executor.yml checks out ref main with no artifact-restore step, so the queue directory cannot exist in the executor filesystem and agent next-pending returns empty on every run. The response envelope is uploaded as aria-response-<id> and never ingested by the producer.

title: Every cost-budget and circuit-breaker enforcement function has zero production callers, so no documented cap or threshold can fire
rule_violated: A declared budget cap or failure threshold must be invoked on the path it claims to govern; a policy function with no caller is not enforcement.
notes: assert_within_budget, record_actual_usage, reserve_cycle_budget and circuit_breaker.record_failure appear only as definitions and __all__ entries at bdaf00b. The remaining references are prose: genesis_policy.py:15 is a comment describing intent and ci_executor.py:698 is a comment stating enforcement happens separately. There is no separate enforcement.

title: All three layers of the convergence independence check are non-functional, and the one live layer compares the wrong three roles
rule_violated: A consensus-independence gate must compare the actual dispatched roles using their real revision identifiers and real agent output; placeholder inputs and positional index lookups cannot establish independence.
notes: Proven by execution at bdaf00b. Layer 3 receives three hardcoded placeholder strings whose maximum pairwise Jaccard is 0.25 against a 0.85 ceiling, so it can never fire. Layer 2 receives synthesized ids plan-r1/plan-c1/None and returns (True, []), so it can never fire. Layer 1 is fed request_ids[0..2] positionally, but the list is appended as challenger (:596), cross_review (:785), completeness_critic (:919), primary (:1082, round 2+ only) - so the mapping is wrong from round 1. The real revision ids and plan texts are already local variables at :735-767.

title: An adversarial-review request escalated to HUMAN_REQUIRED is converted into a no_gaps approval
rule_violated: A review gate must derive its verdict from a validated accepted result bound to the request; the absence of a pending row is not evidence of a successful review.
notes: next_pending_request returns non-None only for derived state PENDING or REQUEUED, so HUMAN_REQUIRED, REJECTED and claimed-without-result all make it return None. review_runner.py:251-257 treats that None as submission_observed=True and returns verdict=no_gaps. The signal meaning a human must look at this is the signal that clears the gate.

title: The specialist review gate can never complete and fails open in both standard and autonomous profiles
rule_violated: A domain-specialist gate must consume the specialists' submitted results and must fail closed in every profile that can perform writes or merges.
notes: run_specialist_review_runner never opens results.jsonl; its tail return is unconditional, always emitting specialists_unavailable with empty findings and marking every selected specialist timed_out even when it submitted. autonomy_orchestrator.py:1509-1514 blocks on specialists_unavailable only when the profile is strict, so the autonomous profile that holds real merge authority has the weakest specialist gate in the system. Specialist selection uses cycle/<id> scope rather than the real diff.

title: Four autonomy-summary counters are structurally pinned to zero and an unverified state tree is published under the canonical artifact name
rule_violated: An operator-facing health summary must be derived from the ledgers it reports on, and only a verified state snapshot may be published under the name the next run restores from.
notes: cycle.py:646 pins incomplete_lifecycle_count to 0 and runtime_artifacts.py:756 sums that per-cycle field, so the aggregate is structurally zero. runtime_artifacts.py:802 pins warning_count to 0, and :750-751 declare suppressed_count and truncated_count as locals that are never incremented before being emitted. aria-auto-cycle.yml uploads aria-tools-state with if: always() and overwrite: true, so a cycle killed mid-write republishes its partial tree as canonical. integrity._verify_cycle_lifecycle already returns the real incomplete_count.

title: The minted GitHub installation token carries full installation scope and its advertised 5-minute TTL is never applied
rule_violated: A least-privilege credential must be scoped to the repositories it needs and must carry the expiry the API actually returned, not a requested value recorded as fact.
notes: The docstring at gh_token_factory.py:304 documents repositories=[<repo>], but the POST body at :411-415 contains only a permissions object - there is no repositories key, so the token reaches every repository the App can access. ttl_seconds is spent as an HTTP socket timeout in urlopen(req, timeout=ttl_seconds) at :415, the API response expires_at is never read, and InstallationTokenLease.ttl_seconds records the requested 300 as if it were the token lifetime. Mode B copies the operator PAT verbatim into aria-debts/keys/<cycle_id>.token inside the workspace.

title: HUMAN_REQUIRED escalations wait on a human indefinitely and the reconciling sweep that makes them visible has CLI-only callers
rule_violated: An escalation must reach a decision-maker and be visible in every view that claims to show it; where independent agents adjudicate in place of a human, their independence must be verified against the claims ledger and an irreducible class must remain that agents can never self-clear.
notes: resolve_human_required documented itself as operator-only so every lease-lifecycle escalation sat until a person opened aria-tools/human-required/. Separately sweep_lease_lifecycle_for_human_required had CLI-only callers (cli.py:3457,3482), so derive_request_state could report HUMAN_REQUIRED while no operator-facing record existed - the 13 invisible escalations in the live artifact. Closed by an independent agent panel (3 distinct judge targets, quorum 2) whose principal disjointness is verified via verify_principal_disjointness, with an irreducible class agents may never clear (profile transition, credential material, governance override, merge authority, L3/blocked risk lane, and any escalation whose scope cannot be classified) plus a hard refusal on a panel supplying a ground-truth verdict.

title: The bash sandbox perimeter has no kernel caller: wrap_bash_in_sandbox and apply_resource_limits are enforced only by prose instructing the LLM
rule_violated: A containment boundary must be applied by the code that spawns the process, never by instructions addressed to the process being contained.
notes: Adversarially verified with reproduction. wrap_bash_in_sandbox (implementation_safety.py:443) returns argv unchanged when no sandbox is available and has zero kernel callers; apply_resource_limits (:497, MemoryMax=2G/CPUQuota=200%) likewise. Autonomous write means ARIA authors and then executes its own validation scripts, so kernel self-modification and network egress were demonstrated rather than theorised. Ranked the top blocker for enabling autonomous write/merge.

title: HARD_FAIL_CHECKS is a pure-data registry with no callable field and zero production iterators, so the documented pre-PR-open and pre-merge perimeter never runs
rule_violated: A safety perimeter that a policy document and a green test both describe must be executable by construction; a registry of names cannot gate anything.
notes: Adversarially verified; the refuter reported every refutation angle failed. HardFailCheck (implementation_safety.py:550) has three fields - name, description, closes_findings - and no callable, and nothing iterates the 17-entry registry at :566. Two checks credited as wired (secret_scan_diff_clean, path_escape_guard) resolve only to comments. expert_review_gate.py in its entirety has zero production callers, so Plan 031e's 'no fix PR without evidence-verified expert consensus' is unenforced. The invariant test pins the count 17 and passes green, so the absent perimeter reads as CI success. Fix is Tier-1: add a required check callable to HardFailCheck so a non-executable entry is unconstructable, and make pr_manager.open_pr_for_action / auto_merge.merge_if_green require a HardFailReport only the registry loop can produce.

title: Gate B oscillation guard has no caller while the streak it reads only ever increments, so a fix/reopen loop is unbounded and its HUMAN_REQUIRED record is never written
rule_violated: A runaway-loop bound must be consulted by the dispatcher it bounds, and any monotonic counter feeding it must have a paired reset on the resolution path.
notes: Adversarially verified with reproduction: record_reopen called five times drives streak 1..5 and is_oscillating flips True at 3, then guard_fix_dispatch raises oscillation_fix_dispatch_blocked - but guard_fix_dispatch (:170), assert_fix_dispatch_allowed (:151), is_oscillating (:139) and record_resolution (:117) all have zero production callers. The observation half IS live nightly (cycle.py update_memory -> memory.py:844 record_reopen) and the state artifact makes the streak cumulative across nights. create_dispatch_request gates only on triage_tier; the one retry cap is scoped per assignment_id so each reopen gets a fresh budget. autonomy-unlock.md:87 tells operators to look for an escalation file that can never be written. HIGH rather than CRITICAL today only because request creation is operator-invoked - enabling autonomous dispatch removes that mitigation.

title: ARIA-Watchdog goes permanently silent after its first poll because the daemon's own governance writes advance the incremental read cursor past the events it should detect
rule_violated: An observer must not consume its own output as the signal boundary; a detector that reads an incremental window needs cumulative per-subject state.
notes: Adversarially verified against the real run_aria_watchdog_daemon. The cursor (since = last_governance_ts, aria_watchdog.py:575) is advanced by the daemon's own aria_watchdog_iteration_started rows in the same ledger, so from iteration 2 the window starts at ~now. In the deployed mode (cli.py:2621, max-iterations=None, 60s poll, a stall that begins while the daemon runs) the reproduction emitted ZERO findings across 15 iterations while the same detector over the full ledger found the stall. detect_repeated_bridge_warning's 3-in-600s threshold is likewise unreachable for warnings slower than one per poll. No invariant test touches the cursor.

title: The banned-phrase HARD-reject check scans envelope keys the production submission never has, so it grades every real submission on an empty string
rule_violated: A content check must extract prose from the envelope shape production actually emits; its test fixture must be the real builder's output, not a hand-written dict.
notes: Adversarially verified by feeding the REAL _build_envelope_from_claude_output output to the real grade_response: 11 of 12 banned phrases present, body_chars 0, hits [], hard_fail_count 0, rejection False. agent_compliance.py:209 reads top-level body/rationale/summary/narrative/explanation; the production envelope carries prose in details.agent_text and plan_content.summary. This check is a member of HARD_REJECT_CHECKS on the live submit path, so the four-check hard wall is three on 100 percent of submissions. The unit test injects a synthetic body key, which is the root cause of the blindness.

title: Architecture Spine Gate drops unreadable or undecodable files from the invariant violation count, so total evidence loss reads as the repo getting cleaner
rule_violated: A measurement must distinguish 'measured zero' from 'could not measure'; a drift comparison must treat an unmeasurable scan or a drop in files scanned as a regression.
notes: Adversarially verified. architecture_spine_gate.py:154 (also :184, :220, :136) does except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError): continue. Deleting apps/ plus libs/ scored all five invariants as improvement, and the false-clean postcheck becomes the handoff snapshot's last_validation. Latent today because all 3670 scanned .ts files are valid UTF-8; needs a damaged source file or a wrong workspace_root. Fix is a sum type: Measured(count, files_scanned) versus Unmeasurable(reason).

title: The aria-tools publication integrity gate verifies only a small fraction of the declared state surfaces, so a cycle killed mid-append to an uncovered ledger still publishes as canonical
rule_violated: A fail-closed publication gate must cover every declared state surface it claims to protect, or state precisely which surfaces it does not.
