notes: FOUND BY MY OWN VIOLATION, one increment after the fact. Before committing RC-9 I ran `npm run invariants:fast` (jest) and `findings:verify`, saw green, committed and PUSHED. The first thing I ran in the NEXT increment was `npm run aria:test:unit`, and four tests were red on the commit already at origin: test_every_actions_use_is_sha_pinned (my composite action's `uses: ./...` has no SHA to pin), test_i_sbx_01_and_02_dispatching_workflows_declare_containment (the install+verify pair moved into the composite action, so neither workflow's own text declares containment any more), and both workflow-preflight contract tests (the new probe workflow was not in the contract registry). Every one of those is a CORRECT finding by a gate doing its job; the defect is that nothing local ran it. WHY THE EXISTING PARITY INVARIANT DID NOT COVER IT, stated because the near-miss matters: tests/invariants/git-hook-binding.spec.ts asserts parity for the ci-full.yml lint-and-typecheck job, and `aria:test:unit` runs in aria-operational-proof.yml. Its scope was stated honestly, so this is a gap rather than a false claim -- but its SCRIPT_GATES map keyed each gate by one path and demanded that same string appear in both a workflow and a hook, which structurally limited it to gates whose CI and local spellings are identical. The gate that mattered most is not one of those: a hook cannot mirror `npm run aria:test:unit` verbatim, because 215 unconditional seconds on every push is how a gate gets bypassed. FIX. scripts/ci/aria-suite-changed.mjs runs the suite only when the commits THIS push adds touch a surface the suite asserts on -- aria-kernel/, tools/aria-poc/, .github/workflows/ and .github/actions/. The last two are in the trigger set because RC-9 broke the suite without touching a line of Python. Scoping decides WHETHER to run, never WHICH tests: the kernel suite is all-or-nothing and a per-file selection would report green on what it skipped. SCRIPT_GATES now carries separate `ci` and `local` tokens so a gate whose mirror is deliberately a different command is still checked. Proven both ways: green with the hook line present, and with it deleted the invariant names the missing mirror.

title: The architecture spine gate has never run in production either: both its phases require a plan_id and no production caller supplies one, so the collapse turns an invisible absence into a recorded skip rather than into an execution
rule_violated: A gate that cannot fire under any production configuration is documentation, not a gate. Recording why it did not fire is the minimum honest state; leaving it there is not a fix.
notes: EXPOSED BY RC-1, NOT CAUSED BY IT, and separated from ORPHAN-CRITICAL-498 because the cause is different. 498 was 'the phases sit behind a kwarg nobody passes'. The collapse removes that: validation_matrix and pr_lifecycle now run from CYCLE_PHASES. architecture_baseline and architecture_postcheck do not, for a second and independent reason -- their precondition is PLAN_ID_PRESENT and neither production caller supplies a plan_id. `cli.py` `cycle run` has no --plan-id argument at all (cli.py ~2019), and autonomy_orchestrator's cycle_runner call passes only workspace_root, cycle_id, base_dir and defer_reflection (autonomy_orchestrator.py ~931). So every production cycle now records {'outcome': 'skipped', 'reason': 'precondition_unmet:plan_id_present'} for both phases. WHAT CHANGED AND WHAT DID NOT. The behaviour is identical -- the spine gate did not run before and does not run now. What changed is that the absence is READABLE: pre-collapse a phase that did not run produced no key, no reason and no trace, so 'this gate is not wired' and 'this gate passed' were the same observation from outside. That is an improvement and it is not a closure, which is why this is filed rather than folded into the RC-1 commit as done. WHAT THE REAL FIX NEEDS, so the next person does not have to re-derive it: a plan_id has to reach the cycle from something that knows which plan a cycle is executing. The autonomy orchestrator drains a queue of promoted plans, so the candidate source exists -- the work is deciding whether a cycle is scoped to one plan (pass it) or to many (the spine gate needs a different shape entirely, per-change rather than per-cycle). That is a design question, not a wiring one, and answering it inside a pipeline-collapse commit would be the kind of guess this branch exists to stop making.

title: Seven invariant specs are red, not merely dormant: they were written, never wired, and have rotted against the code they assert on
rule_violated: A dormant invariant that would FAIL if switched on is not paused coverage, it is a claim the repository no longer satisfies. Carrying it without a tracked owner is how it stays true forever.
notes: SPLIT OUT FROM ORPHAN-HIGH-515 deliberately: 515 is the MECHANISM (an expiry nothing enforced, an enumerated shard list, a manifest with no finding IDs) and is closed by this change. This is the DEBT the mechanism was hiding, and it is not closed. Making the expiry load-bearing expired all 25 waivers at once; running them showed 18 pass and were revived. These 7 fail: access-log-stream-shape (asserts an access-log stream shape the platform does not emit yet); audit-immutability-triggers (asserts audit-table immutability triggers absent from every migration); audited-operation-module-wired (asserts every audited operation is module-wired; several are not); auth-users-tenant-fk (reads apps/auth-service/src/migrations/1787200000000-AddAuthUsersTenantFk.ts, which does not exist); event-contract-emit-has-interface (asserts every emitted event has a declared interface; several emitters do not); legal-hold-canonical-lib (asserts legal-hold checks route through the canonical lib; some do not); no-new-adhoc-circuit-breaker (asserts no ad-hoc breaker outside the canonical lib; some remain). WHY NOT FIXED HERE, stated as required rather than implied. Each belongs to a domain lane this change does not touch -- auth, audit, billing, legal-hold -- and every one needs a real fix in that domain, not a test edit. Switching them on would make an ARIA breaker-recovery branch red for reasons wholly outside it; deleting them would discard invariants somebody wrote deliberately. They carry a 2026-09-30 expiry that now FAILS THE BUILD when it passes, which is the difference between this waiver and the ones it replaces.

title: The two aria-tools-state restore implementations had drifted: only the consumer lane carried the ORPHAN-CRITICAL-484/488 ancestry proof, so the producer lane could publish a bootstrap-empty tree over the entire accumulated state
rule_violated: Two hand-copied implementations of one safety-critical step are not two implementations of one rule; they are one rule and one thing that used to be it. A fix applied to a copy is a fix that did not land.
notes: FOUND WHILE SATISFYING RC-6's OWN PRECONDITION. The plan's requirement for the breaker-recovery dispatch was 'no second restore path: a duplicate transaction around a hash-chained ledger is how the ledger diverges'. Checking that before building on it showed the requirement was ALREADY violated, and not harmlessly. aria-agent-executor.yml and aria-auto-cycle.yml each carried its own copy of the same ~70-line Python heredoc, and a diff of the two shows the copies are NOT equal: the executor's writes `restored=true` / `bootstrap=true` to $GITHUB_OUTPUT -- ORPHAN-CRITICAL-484's positive proof that the tree descends from a restored one plus ORPHAN-CRITICAL-488's split between 'nothing to restore' and 'restore failed' -- while the producer's writes NEITHER and its restore step carries no `id:` at all, so no publish gate could read an output even in principle. CONSEQUENCE. The 484/488 fix reached the consumer and never reached the producer -- the 01:00 lane that mints the entire agent-invocation queue. Its publish gate was `state_valid == 'true'` alone. A restore that failed or was skipped there leaves a bootstrap-empty aria-tools/, which PASSES `integrity verify` (an empty tree is trivially consistent) and is then uploaded under the canonical name with `overwrite: true`. That is not a missed publish; it is the accumulated state -- queue, ledgers, breaker evidence -- overwritten by nothing, which is precisely the absorbing failure 484 was raised to stop, on the lane where it matters most. FIX, and it is the RC-9 move applied to a bigger pair: one composite action, .github/actions/restore-aria-tools-state, used by both lanes, exposing the two proof outputs; the producer's publish / quarantine / fail gates now carry the same ancestry condition the consumer's always had. tests/invariants/aria-single-restore-path.spec.ts pins it: exactly one implementation that downloads the artifact, both lanes using it, the outputs present with no negative form, and BOTH lanes' publish gated on ancestry. Proven to bite by reintroducing an inline copy in the producer -- two of its four assertions fail. A SECOND, WEAKER GATE WAS ALSO WRONG about this: test_the_publish_gate_is_strictly_stronger_than_the_producers asserted only that both conditions mention `state_valid`. That is not a comparison, and it held for the whole life of the drift for exactly that reason. It now compares every guard term.

title: Extracting a step into a local composite action moved it outside every workflows_do_not_* content gate, and RC-9 carried a continue-on-error across that boundary
rule_violated: A gate scoped to the files a rule happened to live in when it was written enforces the rule until someone refactors. Refactoring must not be a way through a gate.
notes: FOUND BY AUDITING MY OWN PREVIOUS COMMIT before building on it. listWorkflowFiles() in sens-enterprise-validation.ts reads .github/workflows/ only, and three checks scan its output for content a governed job may not run: workflows_do_not_suppress_docs_check (|| true), workflows_do_not_continue_on_error, workflows_do_not_update_baselines. That scope was complete while every step lived in a workflow file. RC-9 ended that: extracting the sandbox install/verify pair into .github/actions/ensure-sandbox-backend carried a `continue-on-error: true` out of enforcement, and the gate kept reporting compliance. A composite action's steps run inside the calling job; the runner does not distinguish them and neither should the gate. THIS IS THE FOURTH INSTANCE OF ONE CLASS ON THIS BRANCH -- 507's hardcoded roots, 509's single spelling, 510's single gate family, and now a single directory. Each one checked part of its domain while reporting full compliance. FIXED IN TWO HALVES, and the second matters as much as the first. (1) A listGovernedStepFiles() that adds LOCAL composite actions, wired into exactly those three content scans -- not into the workflow-shaped checks (`on:` triggers, top-level permissions, curated matrices), because an action.yml legitimately has none of those and a gate that fails for unrelated reasons gets deleted for being noise. Third-party `uses:` stays out: it is SHA-pinned and reviewed as a dependency, and scanning it would assert a rule over code this repo does not own. (2) The action was changed to SATISFY the rule rather than be exempted from it: the install now tolerates apt failure through a shell `if` -- exempt from `set -e`, and it prints why -- instead of the banned per-step key. No exemption list was created. Verified both ways: with the key restored the gate names the action file; without it, 6 pass / 0 fail, identical to the origin/main baseline. SIDE NOTE WORTH THE LINE: the gate is a raw text scan, so my own comment EXPLAINING the choice failed it by spelling the key. The sibling comment in aria-auto-cycle.yml documents that same trap. Prose reworded; the trap is real and now recorded in two places.

title: Every invariant dormancy waiver expired 2026-06-30 and none was enforced: the reachability spec validated the FORMAT of expires_on and never compared it to the clock
rule_violated: An expiry field exists to force a review. If nothing compares it to the date, it is documentation shaped like a control -- and checking the syntax of a date instead of the date is the same error as checking the syntax of a rule instead of the rule.
notes: FOUND BY ADDING ONE SPEC. tests/invariants/aria-single-restore-path.spec.ts was written, passed when run directly, and ran under NO command: all three jest projects used explicit testMatch file lists, and a new file matches none of them. `jest --listTests` returned 179 against 204 spec files on disk. I FIRST CONCLUDED 24 SPECS WERE SILENTLY DROPPED. THAT WAS WRONG AND THE CORRECTION IS THE FINDING. invariant-reachability.spec.ts already asserted that every spec is either listed in the config or declared in invariant-reachability.dormant.json with owner, reason and expiry -- a real tier-3 guard, and it worked: all 24 were declared, not forgotten. What did not exist was any comparison of `expires_on` to the clock. The spec asserted /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/ and stopped. Every one of the 25 entries read 2026-06-30. On 2026-07-31 all of them were a month past expiry with the suite green, and the field that exists to force a review had never forced one. FIX, three parts. (1) The date is load-bearing: a waiver past its expiry fails. (2) Shard membership is a glob, so a spec is IN the suite because it exists, and the dormancy manifest becomes the ONE exclusion list -- the jest config reads it, so a config list and a manifest can no longer disagree. (3) Every waiver must name a tracked finding: owner + reason + expiry says who, why and until when, but without an ID nothing gets worked, which is how 25 waivers reached one shared date and passed it together. MEASURED OUTCOME, and it is why this was worth doing rather than re-dating. Making the date load-bearing expired all 25 at once. Running them showed 18 need no waiver AT ALL -- they pass -- so they were REVIVED rather than re-dated: 179 -> 197 specs now run, real coverage this repository already believed it had. The remaining 7 are genuinely red for reasons owned by the auth, audit, billing and legal-hold lanes (one reads a migration file that does not exist), and they are tracked as ORPHAN-HIGH-512 with a 2026-09-30 deadline rather than switched on red or deleted. THREE OTHER SPECS PINNED THE ENUMERATION AS CONFIG TEXT and failed on the glob -- critical-infra-ssot, backup-production-secrets, and this file itself. Each asserted a spelling ('the config contains this filename') where the property was reachability. All three now assert the property, because the obvious way to make that failure go away is to put the filename back in a list, which is the wrong direction.

title: The 2026-05-18 migration squash dropped DDL that four SSoT layers still declare, and the invariants guarding it read the .archive/ directory, so one reported green off a migration the runtime never applies
rule_violated: Evidence for an invariant must come from what the runtime executes. A gate reporting compliance off a retired file is worse than no gate: it is a standing claim that something is protected when it is not.
notes: FOUND BY CHECKING RC-6's PRECONDITION, then following the thread. Four services squashed their migrations into a Baseline on 2026-05-18 and moved 55 originals to src/.../migrations/.archive/. That archive is dead by construction: every service registers migrations: ['src/.../migrations/[0-9]*...'], which neither matches a dot-directory nor descends into one. THE FALSE GREEN. tests/invariants/auth-users-tenant-fk.spec.ts guards FK_auth_users_tenantId (DBR-HIGH-002: a tenant must not be deletable while user rows still claim it) and was PASSING. It collected migrations with `git ls-files 'apps/auth-service/src/migrations/*.ts'` -- and a git pathspec `*` crosses `/`, so it returned all 32 files including the 13 archived. The constraint exists ONLY in the archive. A freshly migrated database has no such FK. Its sibling test in the SAME FILE pinned one filename and failed with an ENOENT naming a file, which is why the breakage read as a stale test rather than as a missing constraint. SECOND DROP, SAME CAUSE. shared.access_logs is created by no live migration, while AccessLogMiddleware writes a row per request (wired into gateway-api and admin-api-service), AccessLogEntity maps it, protected-tables.ts lists it, and the RLS infrastructure-ledger SSoT declares it. Its guard, access-log-stream-shape.spec.ts, read the migration by hardcoded filename and so failed to LOAD rather than reporting the table gone -- and it was dormant, so nobody saw even that. FIX, TWO PARTS. (1) MECHANISM: tests/invariants/lib/migration-corpus.ts is the one answer to 'which migrations does service X apply?', deriving each service's migrations directory from its own data-source.ts (services disagree: src/migrations for four, src/database/migrations for ten) and excluding anything not directly in it. Eight specs each answered this privately; four answered it wrongly; one had a private function literally named loadMigrationCorpus. The helper refuses rather than guessing when a service's declaration cannot be parsed. (2) THE DDL: forward-only restorations -- RestoreAuthUsersTenantFk1807300000000 (with the orphan pre-flight the original carried) and RestoreSharedAccessLogs1801600000000. Both idempotent, so an environment that still has them is unaffected. PROOF THE FIX IS REAL: with the specs on the corpus and the restorations absent, both fail; with the restorations tracked, both pass. The FK assertion in particular went from passing-on-dead-evidence to failing, which is the correct intermediate state and the thing that proves the old green was false.

title: The baseline squash hand-authored a fifth audit-immutability variant that refuses ALL deletes, breaking audit retention on three tables and dropping shared.audit_logs protection entirely
rule_violated: A stricter rule is not a safer rule. An append-only guarantee that also forbids lawful expiry converts a compliance control into an unbounded-growth defect, and it does so while looking like hardening.
notes: The pre-squash contract was TWO triggers per audit table: <schema>.<table>_prevent_update (BEFORE UPDATE, always raises) and <schema>.<table>_prevent_legal_hold_delete (BEFORE DELETE, raises ONLY when OLD."legalHold" is true, else RETURN OLD). The second is what lets audit retention expire rows while legal hold blocks it -- the retention module's own docstring names this trigger as its database-level backstop behind the application-layer legalHold = false filter. The Baseline carries a hand-authored single function per table, <schema>.<table>_prevent_update_or_delete, raising on BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE unconditionally. That is not a stricter version of the rule, it is a different rule: retention can now delete nothing, and an audit table that can only grow is its own incident. The comment on the block reads 'Faz 3.5 hand-author addition'. WORSE FOR shared.audit_logs: the live set contains no function and no trigger for it at all. The canonical cross-service audit table lost its immutability guarantee outright. WHY THE GUARD DID NOT SAY SO: audit-immutability-triggers.spec.ts asserted the pre-squash SPELLING (ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN for legalHold; specific function names) against a corpus that also included the archived pre-squash files. It was dormant, so its red was unread. FIX. libs/backend-common/src/database/audit-immutability.sql.ts generates the contract from (schema, table) -- four tables across three services, and a migration cannot be shared across services, so the SQL is generated once and each service's migration calls it. Hand-copying is exactly what produced the fifth variant. Three forward-only migrations apply it (admin covers shared + admin; auth; farm, registered in FARM_MIGRATIONS since farm uses an explicit array). Each drops the superseded consolidated trigger by name before creating the pair, and drops the orphaned function only after the trigger using it is gone. down() refuses: dropping these makes audit rows mutable and removes the legal-hold guard. The invariant now asserts the GENERATOR's output (including that DELETE is conditional on legalHold, the half the squash lost) AND that each owning service's effective migration set invokes it for that table -- a correct generator nobody calls being the ORPHAN-HIGH-455 shape.

title: aria-debts/keys signing-key surface is stageable — per-cycle ed25519 PRIVATE KEYS + scoped-token files land in a tracked directory with no gitignore rule (re-registration of PR #936's branch-local ORPHAN-HIGH-334, which never reached main's registry)
rule_violated: Runtime secret material (private signing keys, installation-token files) must be structurally unstageable; gh_token_factory.mint_signing_key/mint_installation_token write under aria-debts/keys/ while aria-debts/ is a TRACKED directory not covered by any ignore rule, so one git add -A stages live key material
notes: Salvaged from closed PR #936 (feat/aria-autonomous-mode): the fix existed there since 2026-07-11 but the PR went stale and its registry rows were branch-local. Fixed in the same commit that registers this finding: .gitignore gains aria-debts/keys/ (key material never stageable; aria-debts/ debt JSONs stay tracked). The companion workflow-contract write root (^aria-debts/keys(/.*)?$) intentionally lands with the Wave 8/9 autonomous-lane rebuild per docs/plans/2026-08-02-aria-full-autonomy-program/PLAN.md — no scheduled lane mints keys today, so the gitignore rule alone closes the exfiltration surface.

title: FAILING_CI plan source emits non-repo-verifiable evidence (gh-run-list:<id>) — the top-priority pressure source can never converge, starving the autonomous implementation phase (re-registration of PR #936's branch-local ORPHAN-HIGH-333, which never reached main's registry)
rule_violated: Every plan-source conversion must ground evidence_refs in repo-verifiable path[:line] references (the ORPHAN-312/331 contract); a synthetic gh-run-list token fails EvidencePolicy.require_repo_verified unconditionally, so any cycle driven by the FAILING_CI source stalls before convergence
notes: Salvaged from closed PR #936: diagnosed live 2026-07-06 — with a real main-CI failure present, rank_candidate_sources selects the failing_ci candidate (highest priority) and convert_candidate_to_plan_content produces evidence_refs=["gh-run-list:<run-id>"], which classify_evidence_ref can never grade repo_verified at any target_sha, so the convergence gate rejects every envelope and the plan slot is wasted whenever main is red. Fix shape (ORPHAN-312 pattern): resolve the failing run's head_sha + failed job/step files via gh api into real repo paths, keep gh-run-list:<id> as metadata only, and skip the candidate (plan_candidate_conversion_skipped) when no repo-verifiable surface can be derived so iterative fallback reaches the next source. Scheduled into Wave 9 (runtime connectors) of docs/plans/2026-08-02-aria-full-autonomy-program/PLAN.md; owner aria-acceptance-gap-fixer, deadline 2026-09-30.

title: bridge_status_ledger.replay_pending_bridges was never written — the orchestrator's _default_bridge_drainer resolves it by name, finds nothing, returns status=skipped, and every strict/autonomous cycle exits bridge_replay_required unconditionally before reaching planning
rule_violated: A consumer wired by name to a function that does not exist is the written-yet-unreachable-control defect class (ORPHAN-CRITICAL-498's sibling): the C.5 crash-recovery/retry design documented replay as the drain path, but only the ledger primitives were built — under standard the skip is silently ignored, under strict/autonomous it is an unconditional halt
notes: Found during the full-autonomy program session audit (Wave 0 discovery): grep for replay_pending_bridges returned only the four orchestrator-side mentions; _default_bridge_drainer's getattr fallback returned status=skipped every cycle, and autonomy_orchestrator breaks the cycle loop with exit_reason=bridge_replay_required whenever profile is strict/autonomous and bridge status is skipped/unknown/failed or pending_after>0 — making those profiles structurally unable to complete a cycle. Fixed in the registering commit (Wave 0 PR 0.1 of docs/plans/2026-08-02-aria-full-autonomy-program/PLAN.md): replay_pending_bridges walks accepted bridge-required result rows, replays crash-recovery pending rows and budgeted pending_retry rows through the SAME code the accepted submit path runs (the bridge invocation was extracted from submit_claim_result into _invoke_bridges_for_result so replay cannot drift), records ok/pending_retry/permanent_fail transitions, and returns the orchestrator's consumer contract; a structural ledger failure returns status=failed instead of raising. One deliberate divergence: BridgeContractViolation is caught on the replay path (governance event bridge_replay_contract_violation + error) so one poisoned row cannot wedge the whole drain.

title: burn_in.run_observe_burn_in hand-rolled a THIRD cycle loop — it imported cycle's private event factories (_started_cycle_row/_completed_event/_failed_event) plus five observe primitives and re-implemented the started/terminal ledger discipline outside the pipeline, so the burn-in lane's no-action guarantee lived in a docstring instead of the CYCLE_PHASES table
rule_violated: Single-entrance pipeline (Wave 0's whole point, ORPHAN-CRITICAL-498's family): after the collapse deleted the dead run_phases= second entrance, burn_in.py remained a live third entrance — a parallel loop calling run_discovery/run_cycle_diff/update_memory/run_pressure/triage_policy_apply directly and appending its own started/completed/failed rows to cycles.jsonl, duplicating lifecycle-ledger ownership and leaving the observe lane outside every pipeline property (phase outcome ledger, skip visibility, well-formedness assert)
notes: Found while executing Wave 0 item 0.5 of docs/plans/2026-08-02-aria-full-autonomy-program/PLAN.md (the program's discovery had already flagged the pipeline having THREE entrances, not two). Fixed in the registering commit: CYCLE_PHASES gains a closed `modes` column (CYCLE_MODES = standard|burn_in; default standard-only so a new phase can never leak into the burn-in lane by omission), run_enterprise_cycle gains mode= validated against the closed vocabulary before the started row lands, the observe set (discovery, cycle_diff, memory, pressure, triage, artifact_integrity) declares burn_in membership as table data, a burn_in-only triage phase row carries the observe lane's triage step, learning hooks are skipped by mode (mirroring the pre-collapse loop which never ran them), and run_observe_burn_in's per-cycle body becomes a run_enterprise_cycle(mode="burn_in") call with its evidence bundle derived from the returned state — public signature and failure-report behavior preserved. The failure path appends a terminal row only when the pipeline did not (double-terminal prevention). Import-level pin: burn_in.py may import only _failed_event + run_enterprise_cycle from cycle (test_cycle_burn_in_mode.py).

title: Pressure test fixtures seeded with the literal date 2026-05-05 decay past the 90-day faded threshold on 2026-08-03 and vanish from the real-clock active listing — two kernel tests fail deterministically on every branch from that midnight onward, blocking all CI
rule_violated: A test must not depend on the wall clock crossing a calendar boundary: DEFAULT_DECAY_THRESHOLDS (faded: 90d) is applied by effective_workspace_pressures with now=wall clock, and the pressure list CLI has no --now, so a fixture with a fixed detected_at is a time bomb that passes for 90 days and then fails everywhere at once — invisible in review, deterministic in production CI
notes: Found driving PR #1049 to green: CI unittest failed on test_cli_pressure_list_defaults_to_active_and_explain_shows_history (test_pressure_lifecycle) and test_pressure_list_workspace_base_isolation_and_memory_tools_isolation (test_v13_contracts) — both untouched by the branch, both reproducible at main's tip after 2026-08-03T00:00Z (2026-05-05 + 90 days). Fixed in the registering commit: the two fixtures are anchored to datetime.now(timezone.utc) wherever the read side is the real clock, so evidence age stays ~0 on any calendar date; tests that pass now= explicitly on both seed and read keep their literal dates (self-consistent, never decay unexpectedly). Class sweep: all other fixed detected_at fixtures in kernel tests (four files dated 2026-05-06) verified NOT to read back through the decay-filtering surfaces with a real clock — not members of this class.

title: Executor-lane PRs bypassed the PR perimeter: agents opened real PRs via the raw `gh pr create` allowlist row, so ARIA_PR_BASE guard, GATE_PRE_PR_OPEN, the breaker producer, and the change-id auto-merge anchor all sat on a path no production PR travelled
rule_violated: Written-yet-unreachable control (ORPHAN-CRITICAL-498/520's class): pr_manager.open_pr_for_action carries every PR-opening control, but ALLOWED_BASH_COMMANDS admitted raw `gh pr create --base main` and the implementer prompt documented it as an approved alternative — the perimeter existed while the production path went around it
notes: Wave 0 item 0.7 of docs/plans/2026-08-02-aria-full-autonomy-program/PLAN.md (verification confirmed the lane shape in-session: the executor wrappers never open PRs; the agent subprocess does, via the allowlist). Fixed in the registering commit: ALLOWED_BASH_COMMANDS swaps the raw row for `python3 -m aria_kernel pr create ...` (scoped to that one subcommand; delegates to open_pr_for_action), the legacy pattern survives only while ARIA_EXECUTOR_PR_VIA_KERNEL is unset, the scheduled executor lane sets the flag to 1 (kernel-CLI-only as of this commit), and aria-implementer.md step 9 drops the raw alternative. Tracked follow-through: after one green scheduled run under the flag, the flag and LEGACY_GH_PR_CREATE_PATTERN are deleted together (PLAN.md Wave 0 §0.7).

title: integrity_index maintenance had three disagreeing parties: the grouped refresh REPLACES ledger_hashes with its own small membership on every indexed append, while update_tools_index and integrity._index_issues both used the wider covered set - so full-rewrite entries were silently discarded by the next append and the verifier stayed green only because it always ran immediately after full rewrites
rule_violated: One authority per contract: the index's membership was defined in three places with two shapes (ledger.py hand tables for refresh; covered_tool_ledgers for full rewrite and verify), and the replace semantics of the refresh meant the writers actively destroyed each other's entries - masked before ORPHAN-HIGH-433's coverage fix because the hand-list coverage and the group tables coincided on minimal fixtures
notes: Found while implementing Wave 1 PR 2.1 (manifest-derived coverage, ORPHAN-HIGH-433): six kernel tests went red with tools_index_drift expected=null because the widened verify expectation collided with the refresh's replace semantics. Fixed in the registering commit: ledger.py's group table is promoted to the sole public authority tools_index_group_ledgers and ALL THREE parties consume it (grouped refresh, update_tools_index, integrity._index_issues); chain verification stays on the wide manifest-derived covered set; index keys unchanged on disk so no migration; the rewrite-then-append-then-verify sequence is pinned green by test_manifest_derived_integrity_coverage. Scheduled residue with owner+deadline: state_manifest's index_group column has zero runtime consumers and values disagreeing with live membership (117 surfaces claim a nonexistent runtime index group); reconciliation/retirement is scheduled into Wave-2 PR 2.2 (snapshot manifests replace integrity_index wholesale) - owner aria-acceptance-gap-fixer, deadline W2 PR 2.2 landing per docs/plans/2026-08-02-aria-full-autonomy-program/PLAN.md.

title: Shadow-run mutation detector is order/load-flaky: test_007c's no-mutation contract failed once in a full sequential kernel suite (repository_mutation_attempt true) and passes solo/module-solo/instrumented re-run; same-shape failure seen earlier on an unmodified tree under cross-suite load
rule_violated: A safety detector must not flake: repository_mutation_attempt feeds pressure, readiness, and tool_health quarantine triggers, so a false positive under load can quarantine a healthy adapter; the before/after snapshots trust two consecutive git status --porcelain calls, and git's racy-stat heuristic can make them disagree with no real change (hypothesis - instrumented run captured no spurious diff, mechanism unconfirmed)
notes: Observed while validating Wave 1 PR 2.1 (manifest-derived coverage): one failure in a full sequential run on the branch; solo, module-solo, and an instrumented full re-run (spy on _partition_mutations printing before/after deltas) all green with no spurious diff captured - so the branch's coverage change is not implicated and the mechanism is unconfirmed. Fix plan: build a load-reproduction harness (repeat full-suite or parallel-suite runs capturing porcelain output on flag flips), then either force git index refresh (git update-index --refresh) before the BEFORE snapshot or replace porcelain trust with content-hash comparison for the tracked set, whichever the reproduction implicates. Deadline set two weeks out because reproduction is the gating step; escalate to HIGH if a false positive ever quarantines a real adapter in nightly.

title: ARIA had no tree-level continuity root: per-file hash chains make each ledger tamper-evident but nothing attested that a set of surfaces is one coherent state following a prior one, so losing the whole tree (expired 30-day artifact, runner-local workspace) was indistinguishable from a fresh bootstrap - every surviving file still verified
rule_violated: A control must be able to distinguish the two states it is supposed to act differently on (ORPHAN-CRITICAL-498's class, one level above the files): with only per-file chains, 'fresh bootstrap' and 'total state loss' produce identical verification output, and the closest existing witness (the daily anchor's integrity_index_chain_root) covers only the ~9-name index-group map, not surface presence
notes: Wave 1 PR 2.2 of docs/plans/2026-08-02-aria-full-autonomy-program/PLAN.md. Fixed in the registering commit: state_snapshot.build_snapshot folds every present declared surface (path, sha256, segments, ledger row_count + tail_ledger_hash) into a manifest_root; storage policy is derived from the manifest's own state_class column (ledger/index/runtime_state carried, artifact pinned-only, lock excluded) with an unclassified class raising rather than vanishing; snapshots chain via prev_snapshot_id + prev_manifest_root INSIDE the hashed payload so a continuous history cannot be forged by re-pointing genuine snapshots; snapshot_continuity reports surfaces_lost / chain_broken / genesis; sign_snapshot + verify_snapshot_signature use the existing per-cycle ed25519 identity through ssh-keygen -Y under a dedicated namespace and REFUSE rather than degrade when the binary is absent. Reachable via `aria-kernel state snapshot` / `state verify-snapshot` and consumed by the daily anchor (new state_snapshot_id + state_manifest_root fields), which commits the root outside the store it describes. NOT claimed by this finding and tracked separately: automatic per-cycle snapshot production and publish-time ancestry enforcement land in PR 2.3 (state_store + publish_state FF-only CAS), which is where ORPHAN-CRITICAL-484 and ORPHAN-CRITICAL-513 get the positive-ancestry-proof fix this primitive supplies.

title: Workflow jobs ran aria-kernel code without provisioning aria-kernel: aria-daily-report imported the kernel 27 lines before its pip install, so every scheduled run since 2026-07-17 died on ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'yaml' and the committed daily anchor stopped being produced for 17 days; four more workflows import the kernel with no install step at all
rule_violated: A correctness coupling maintained by hand in eleven places with nothing checking it is not a coupling, it is a coincidence: 'this step runs kernel code' and 'an earlier step installed the kernel' were ordered by hand per job, so a step inserted above the install silently broke a scheduled lane, and four workflows never had an install step at all
notes: Found while checking Wave 0 §0.7's follow-through gate. Watchdog incident issue #1005 (open since 2026-07-17, updated hourly) listed 10 of 14 watched scheduled workflows failing or missing. Root cause of the failing (as opposed to queued) ones: ordering. Fixed in the registering commit: .github/actions/setup-aria-kernel installs the interpreter plus the kernel's declared dependencies from pyproject.toml and verifies importability; all eleven kernel-running jobs use it and their hand-rolled install blocks are deleted; tests/invariants/aria-kernel-workflow-setup.spec.ts fails any job that runs kernel code without an EARLIER uses of that action in the SAME job (positional, per-job, because each job gets a fresh runner) and found 30 violations on first run. Separate cause, NOT fixed by code: aria-auto-cycle and aria-agent-executor declare runs-on [self-hosted, linux, claude] and their runs queue 24h then auto-cancel because that runner is offline - operator action, and it makes Wave 0 §0.7's gate unreachable until the runner returns (PLAN.md corrected in the same commit).

title: The scheduled-workflow watchdog's verdict has no consumer inside ARIA: incident issue #1005 reported ARIA's own nightly loop as not-running every hour for 17 days while the ladder, the merge authority and the program plan all continued as if evidence were accumulating
rule_violated: A signal that no gate consumes is not a control (ORPHAN-CRITICAL-498's family): detection worked perfectly - the watchdog raised and maintained an incident hourly - but nothing in the kernel reads it, so ARIA kept planning, merging and counting readiness while aria-auto-cycle had not run since 2026-07-17
notes: Registered, NOT fixed in the registering commit, and the review file says so explicitly rather than implying otherwise. The consumer belongs with ARIA's own gates (autonomy-ladder progress must not count while a watched ARIA lane is stale; merge authority should refuse autonomous merges under an open ARIA-lane incident), and wiring it wants the durable state store from Wave 1 PR 2.3 so the freeze is recorded durably instead of being recomputed per run. Deadline set two weeks out to land with or immediately after 2.3. Detection itself is sound and must not be duplicated: a second watchdog would be the copy-drift disease, so the fix is a consumer, never another detector.

title: The tree-level continuity root had no consumer: manifest_root was computed, chained and signed, but no gate refused a publish on it, so ARIA gained the evidence for ancestry without gaining the check
rule_violated: A capability with no caller is not a control (ORPHAN-CRITICAL-498's family). PR 2.2 delivered manifest_root plus a signed, chained snapshot; nothing read it. The publish gate went on proving a STEP ('restored=true', the download exited zero) rather than the BYTES, so a tree emptied between restore and publish still satisfied it, and an empty tree passes integrity verify because an empty tree is trivially consistent. build_daily_anchor's state_snapshot_path parameter was likewise unreachable: neither emit_anchor_to_path nor the CLI forwarded to it.
notes: Closed by the registering PR, not deferred: state_store.publish_state refuses unless the snapshot's prev_manifest_root equals the tip's manifest_root, read from the COMMIT (git show HEAD:snapshot.json) rather than the working tree so a caller cannot rewrite what it is checked against; and the daily anchor now receives a derived state_snapshot_path through both levels. Distinct from ORPHAN-CRITICAL-484/488/513, which are about the artifact lane's transport and stay OPEN until the lane cutover (PR 2.4-2.6) — this finding is about the evidence KIND being unused, which is closed the moment one function enforces it and both lanes can only reach the branch through that function.

title: Ledger segment rollover was superseded by measured surface archival, and the consuming trigger does not exist yet: surface sizes are now recorded but nothing reads them, so a surface that does approach an archival threshold will cross it unnoticed
rule_violated: A measurement with no consumer is the same defect class as a capability with no caller: it makes the answer available without making anyone ask the question.
notes: PLAN §2.2b originally specified .seg-NNN rollover at 8 MB with prev_segment_tail_hash continuity rows. A blast-radius map found 42 blocking couplings across roughly 100 readers: path-keyed lock identity, _verify_jsonl_from_text's None chain seed, one-name-one-path index membership, and about 25 workspace readers that resolve a surface to exactly one file. It would also have introduced a fail-OPEN append guard — surface_for_path returns None for a path matching no declared pattern and _assert_raw_jsonl_append_allowed returns on None, which is CORRECT today (an undeclared path is not a governed surface) but becomes a hole the moment segment files hold governed state under undeclared names. Measurement: the largest real ledger on disk is 313 KB against the 8 MB trigger, a factor of 26. The replacement is surface-level archival into an artifact-class file whose sha256 the snapshot already pins, preserving one-live-file-per-surface so no reader changes. PR 2.3 landed the measurement half (size_bytes on every snapshot surface entry, free because the walk already visits each file). This finding tracks the consumer: a threshold check that raises pressure when a surface approaches the archival point. Deliberately NOT urgent — the deadline reflects 26x headroom, not indifference; closing it early with a guessed threshold would be worse than closing it with a series to look at.

title: Two of ARIA's three state roots died with the runner: the workspace surfaces lived under $HOME and aria-findings/ is gitignored and carried nowhere, so every bootstrap restarted finding IDs at F-001 and lost all workspace memory
rule_violated: State that a system reasons about across runs must outlive a run. Ten declared workspace surfaces resolved under the runner's $HOME and six declared repo surfaces under a gitignored directory, so sixteen of ARIA's declared surfaces were structurally incapable of persisting - and nothing said so, because each surviving file still verified.
notes: Named as gap 4 in the program plan but never registered. Closed by binding both roots to the durable store through ONE resolver (workspace.repo_state_root for the repo root; the pre-existing ARIA_WORKSPACE_BASE seam for the workspace root), with state_store.store_environment as the single definition of the binding so a lane cannot get two roots right and the third wrong. gh_token_factory._keys_dir is DELIBERATELY not redirected: per-cycle ed25519 private keys and scoped tokens are credentials, not state, and dying with the runner is their correct lifetime.

title: The state store staged its entire working tree, so redirecting the repo-state root into it would have committed per-cycle ed25519 private keys and scoped installation tokens to a pushed branch
rule_violated: A component that commits and pushes must stage an explicitly enumerated set, never 'everything present'. Enumerating removes the class; an ignore rule only removes the instance, and must be re-added for every future secret.
notes: Found while implementing the root redirection, BEFORE the redirection existed - so it was never exploitable in a shipped state, and this is a near-miss recorded rather than an incident. gh_token_factory writes private keys and tokens to aria-debts/keys/, immediately beside the declared aria-debts/ ledgers. The main checkout's .gitignore covers that path but does NOT reach inside a worktree whose top level is store_dir (git reads no .gitignore above a worktree root), and publish_state used `git add --all --force`, which overrides ignore rules anyway. Closed by staging exactly the snapshot's own surface paths plus the two markers: an undeclared file cannot be committed because nothing names it. Two further properties fall out - the commit is bound to the attestation by construction rather than merely consistent with it, and the previous snapshot's paths are included so a surface that VANISHED can still stage as a deletion.

title: Re-observing unchanged evidence re-raised belief confidence, so ARIA read its own repetition as corroboration: one unchanged file carried a belief from 0.605 to 0.925 in eleven cycles
rule_violated: Confidence must track evidence, not observation count. A system that re-reads the same file every cycle and treats each read as new support is measuring its own schedule, not the world.
notes: Named as gap 6 in the program plan. TWO mechanisms, and fixing either alone leaves a ratchet: support_count incremented unconditionally, AND the support term is added to previous_confidence rather than to the original, so it compounds on the already-raised value. Both are now gated on evidence_hashes differing from the stored row's; both halves are mutation-checked separately (restoring the unconditional increment fails 2 tests, restoring the unconditional term fails 1). Learning is not frozen - changed evidence still increments support and still raises confidence, with a test for that. Occurrence is retained as observation_count, in a field nothing reads into confidence. Three existing tests in test_enterprise_cycle.py asserted the old behaviour and were rewritten to their real intent rather than deleted: each gained a sharper assertion (equality instead of 'confidence rose'), because the property they actually protect holds MORE strongly once the ratchet is gone.

title: A CONVERGED plan was recorded as a 0.9-confidence convention before any outcome existed, and MIN_PATTERN_CONFIDENCE is 0.7 — so ARIA served its own untested predictions to the next planner as established knowledge
rule_violated: A prediction is not a fact. Knowledge recorded before an outcome exists must not be served at the same confidence as knowledge an outcome confirmed, or the system compounds its own guesses into its own priors.
notes: Named as gap 7 in the program plan. The convention row is written when the convergent gate resolves - before merge, before CI has run against the change, before any outcome exists - and 0.9 sits above lookup_pattern's 0.7 serving floor, so it was immediately handed to later planners as established knowledge. Convergence IS evidence (planner, challenger and cross-review agreed) but evidence about AGREEMENT, not about outcome. Closed by recording the row at CONVENTION_HYPOTHESIS_CONFIDENCE=0.5 with outcome_status='hypothesis': stored, because the observation is worth keeping, and below the floor, so it is not served. Pattern.outcome_status defaults to 'unknown' rather than 'verified' - every convention written before this field existed was also pre-outcome, and defaulting them to verified would assert something the ledger never observed. Promotion to 'verified' on a VERIFIED mission and demotion on a rolled-back one is Wave 10's half; this is the half that stops the false claim. Both halves mutation-checked.

title: A required merge gate depended on a live third-party chart registry being reachable at that instant, in two hand-copied callsites: one TCP reset from charts.bitnami.com failed pre-flight and took build-status with it on a PR that touched no infrastructure, and the workflow token cannot re-run a failed job so recovery required pushing an unrelated commit
rule_violated: A single-shot network fetch inside a merge gate is a coin flip the gate has to win every time. `charts/` is build output rather than source, so every renderer must resolve subchart archives from upstream at CI time; spelled as two hand-written `run:` lines with no retry, that put an external CDN's momentary availability on the critical path of a branch-protection-required check, and the same defect had to be fixed twice or not at all.
notes: Observed, not theorised: run 30798949933 on PR #1056. Fixed in the registering commit by one composite action used by both callsites, with bounded retry (3 attempts, 5s then 10s) and a ::warning:: per retry so flakiness stays countable rather than silent. The retry lives in resolve.sh rather than inline in the action's run: block for a testability reason that is the point of the design — inline, the only available assertion is that the words 'attempt' and 'sleep' appear in the YAML, which a loop that never increments its counter also satisfies; as a script it is run against a stub helm and the tests count invocations (1 call on first success, 2 on one transient, exactly 3 when the registry is down, exactly 5 under ATTEMPTS=5, 0 under ATTEMPTS=0 and 0 on a missing Chart.yaml). Six mutations each fail at least one test. NOT taken and named rather than left implied: vendoring the resolved .tgz archives would remove the network entirely and is structurally stronger, but it inverts the convention this chart states explicitly (Chart.yaml is the SSoT, charts/ is build output) and committed archives that drift from their pinned versions have no detector except fetching from the network - that trade is an infrastructure-ownership decision with an ADR's weight, not a side effect of unblocking a merge queue. The invariant tripped over its own documentation twice on first run (comments, then the step's name: label) and one mutation initially SURVIVED because the assertion checked for any ::warning:: while the retry notice satisfied it; both messages are now pinned by content.

title: Nothing consumed tree-level continuity before a cycle acted: a bootstrap-empty aria-tools/ and a restored one were the same observation to everything downstream, and an empty tree passes integrity verify because an empty tree is trivially consistent
rule_violated: A control must be able to distinguish the two states it is supposed to act differently on, and the evidence for that distinction cannot live inside the thing being judged: a tree that lost its history also lost any record that it had one, so no file under aria-tools/ can answer whether aria-tools/ is complete. PR 2.1 gave the tree a manifest, 2.2 a chained manifest_root, 2.3 a publish-time refusal - and none of them was read before a cycle planned, learned or counted acceptance evidence on the tree.
notes: Wave 1 PR 2.5 of docs/plans/2026-08-02-aria-full-autonomy-program/PLAN.md. Closed in the registering commit: memory_gap.assess_memory_continuity compares a snapshot of the tree the cycle opened on against a reference resolved OUTSIDE it (the aria/state branch tip first, then the daily anchors committed under aria-tools/reports/daily/), and a new preflight stage runs it before discovery. THREE verdicts, and the third is load-bearing: unknown is neither ok nor critical, returned whenever no reference exists, because guessing continuous re-opens the hole and guessing amnesiac would refuse every cycle on this repository today - every committed anchor predates state_manifest_root and the newest two are hand-written markdown with no frontmatter. Stated plainly rather than buried: on main today this gate reports unknown every night and blocks nothing; it starts refusing when either reference becomes real (the daily anchor lane resuming, or the state-store lane cutover in PR 2.6). ONE freeze mechanism: record_failure(kind='state_integrity_gap'), a new closed-taxonomy FAILURE_KINDS member, because _cycle_preflight already consults the breaker for every profile in PROFILES_WITH_ACTION_AUTHORITY - a separate frozen flag would be a second answer to how ARIA stops, which is what ORPHAN-CRITICAL-513 cost. freeze_autonomous_writes RAISES on any status but critical, so an unproven gap structurally cannot trip a breaker. TWO PLAN CORRECTIONS from reading the code the plan described: PLAN §2.5's 'delete the silent-bootstrap path' named integrity migrate-tools-bootstrap, which is not a bootstrap-only step but an idempotent contract migration carrying restored trees from v0/v1/v2 to v3 - deleting or gating it would leave older restored trees unmigrated, so it stays; and the silence was never there, since the restore action already fails hard and writes restored=true only on success - the real gap was that both lanes evaluate that transport proof at the END of the job, having already acted. No workflow edit ships: a second early check duplicating what the action enforces is the copy-drift this wave keeps treating. restore_and_replay moves to PR 2.6 with the lane that gives it a transport; equivalence_check ships here because 2.6 needs it and it is testable standalone. Two existing gates failed on first run by design and were edited as the reviewed decisions they demand: the breaker-producer allowlist gained memory_gap.py, and the pinned burn-in phase set gained state_continuity (burn-in's output IS the acceptance evidence the ladder counts, so evidence gathered on a tree that forgot its history is exactly what must not count).

title: A lost publish race left the losing lane's rows stranded: publish_state correctly refused and rolled back, but the caller was told to fetch and rebuild by hand and on the scheduled lanes there is no such caller, so the rows sat in a worktree nothing revisits
rule_violated: A correct refusal that leaves work stranded is still work stranded. publish_state is a compare-and-swap against a fast-forward-only branch, so the second of two lanes publishing from one tip is rejected by the server; PR 2.3 made that refusal safe (rollback, rows staged, nothing overwritten) but left the recovery as a manual instruction in an error message, on lanes that run unattended.
notes: Wave 1 PR 2.6 of docs/plans/2026-08-02-aria-full-autonomy-program/PLAN.md. Closed in the registering commit. The common prefix is PROVEN, not assumed: every ledger row carries a ledger_hash over the whole chain behind it and the base snapshot records each surface's row_count + tail_ledger_hash, so 'do these two files share their first N rows' is answered by requiring the row at index N-1 to carry the base tail hash in BOTH files - a match there implies the whole prefix matches. Anything else is a rewrite wearing an append's clothes and is refused; the resolution is deliberately not a git merge, because -X ours/-X theirs would silently drop one lane's rows, which is ORPHAN-CRITICAL-484's outcome by another road. The winner is checked against the base too, and that check initially had no real test: a refusal asserted with a base hash matching NEITHER tree came from the loser's check, and mutating the winner's check away left all twelve tests green - the isolating test now has the loser descending cleanly and only the winner diverging. Order is the safety property: the loser's ledgers are copied out BEFORE the worktree is reset, so rows are never only in memory across a destructive git operation. Replayed rows are re-chained rather than copied. Replay is NOT idempotent by construction and a failing test found that (a retry against a stale base duplicated every row); the guard is a tail match on logical content rather than set membership, because two lanes can legitimately emit similar rows. TWO PLAN CORRECTIONS: the advisory publish lease from PLAN 2.6 is deliberately NOT built - with replay the race is correct and cheap, and an advisory lease adds a second coordination mechanism whose stale-lease failure mode is worse than the problem, a second answer to 'who may publish' being the pattern this wave spent five PRs removing; and a store-checked-out tools root cannot be used until bound, because repo_identity.json is machine-local binding state (absolute bound_repo_root) and so is not a declared surface, leaving a fresh checkout in exactly the ambiguous_tools_root shape - the governed binding step is integrity migrate-tools-bootstrap, the same step PLAN 2.5 wanted deleted, which is the second and stronger reason it stays.

title: Adapter candidate confidence fails open to maximum certainty: tool_runner._valid_memory_candidates accepts any non-negative number and clamps it with min(float(confidence), 1.0), so an adapter emitting a count, severity grade, or milliseconds reading as confidence is silently promoted to 1.0 and flows into memory._record_belief as the belief's starting weight
rule_violated: Out-of-range input on a trust surface must be refused, not coerced toward maximum trust. instinct_candidate.py already draws the line correctly (raise GovernanceError outside [0,1]); tool_runner disagrees in the opposite direction, and the disagreement fails open: min(float(confidence), 1.0) turns a unit error into certainty. The two modules answer 'what does an out-of-range confidence mean' differently, which is the two-answers defect this program keeps removing.
notes: Found while grounding the mathematical-kernel proposal review (PLAN 4d.1) against the tree. Fix shape is tier 1 (make it impossible): a validating Confidence construction path per kind - pattern score, belief weight, judge probability, adapter score, instinct score - that refuses out-of-range input the way instinct_candidate already does. The clamp is deleted, not widened. Scheduled into Wave 2's first schema PR (mission.py PR 1.1) because the fix touches the adapter candidate contract, not one callsite; the closing commit carries Closes against this row. Related but distinct: judge_calibration's else-branch assumes the FEEDBACK_VERDICTS pair is complementary, so a third verdict added later would silently count as false_positive - scheduled as PLAN 4d.3 (Wave 4) and noted here so the two do not merge into one fix.

title: Work identity is cycle-scoped and the candidate generator has no production caller: task.py derives task_id from cycle_id, so the same defect rediscovered on a later night is a new task with no history, and generate_task_candidates - the only thing that would turn discovery into tracked work - is never called by production code
rule_violated: No plan may silently go half-done - the program's first rule - is unenforceable without a durable subject to enforce it against. _task_id(cycle_id, source, source_id) makes identity a function of WHEN the work was seen rather than WHAT it is, so nothing accumulates evidence, nothing resumes after a crash, and a mission cannot carry a retry ladder or a wake condition across the cycle boundary. The generator compounds it: machinery that exists and is never called is the defect class six of Wave 1's seven PRs closed.
notes: Wave 2 PR 1.1 of docs/plans/2026-08-02-aria-full-autonomy-program/PLAN.md. The IDENTITY half closes in the registering commit: mission_id = m-sha256(source_kind|source_id|repo_hash)[:16] with no timestamp, counter or cycle reference, so the same source re-observed in any later cycle folds into the same mission. Pinned by an AST test rather than a behavioural one because a time component would collide within one second and pass a same-run equality check - test_mission_id_source_never_reads_cycle_or_time walks the module source and refuses any mission-id function referencing cycle identity or any freshness source (clock, uuid, randomness). The NO-PRODUCTION-CALLER half stays open until PR 1.2 wires the mission_ingest phase as the first production caller of task.generate_task_candidates; this finding tracks both halves until then rather than being split, because closing it on identity alone would record the harder half as done. Vocabularies (9 mainline + 5 interim + 5 terminal states, transition edges, retry ladder, wake kinds, binding keys, event kinds) are closed tables in mission.py and nowhere else, with one stated exception: a forward mainline skip is legal only under reason_code=coarse_observation, because today's pipeline genuinely cannot distinguish every intermediate state and a skip that says so is honest where a skip wearing a precise reason would be the schema lying about its own resolution. Interim states sit outside ACTIVE_WIP_STATES on purpose so a mission waiting on a human releases its WIP slot instead of deadlocking the pipeline.

title: The ARIA kernel suite writes into the host repository when it inherits GIT_DIR: cwd= selects the work tree but GIT_DIR selects the repository, so every fixture that carefully passed cwd=<tempdir> still ran git init, git config, git add and git commit against the developer's real checkout - and the pre-push hook that runs the suite is itself launched by git, which exports GIT_DIR
rule_violated: A gate must not damage the thing it guards. git exports an absolute GIT_DIR into its own environment whenever the git dir is not the default .git in cwd, which is always true inside a linked worktree; git push therefore hands GIT_DIR=<repo>/.git/worktrees/<name> to .husky/pre-push, which hands it to scripts/ci/aria-suite-changed.mjs, which forwards process.env verbatim to the Python suite. apply_hermetic_git_env redirected GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL and GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM and claimed that made ambient leakage structurally impossible for every fixture in the process - but it never touched the variable family that decides WHICH REPOSITORY a git subprocess acts on, so the guarantee was narrower than its own docstring.
notes: Observed live, not hypothesised: a push from a linked worktree ran the pre-push suite and mutated the real repository - core.bare=true (git guesses BARE because the exported GIT_DIR ends in the worktree name rather than /.git, and for a linked worktree git_path(config) resolves through commondir to the MAIN .git/config), user.email=fixture@aria.test and user.name='Aria Fixture', gc.auto=0 / gc.autoDetach=false / maintenance.auto=false, remote.origin.url rewritten to the fixture literal at tests/test_phase3_discovery_mfe.py, about twelve stray commits (fixture: initial commit, fixture: seed N files, init, initial), files x.ts and src/a.ts staged onto the real index, branches aria/feature-test, aria/executor-fixture, aria/fixture-proposal-<id> and fixture-wt, and worktree registrations pointing into /tmp. The three keys gc.auto, gc.autoDetach and maintenance.auto are written by exactly three lines in the entire codebase (git_fixtures.py:58-60), which identifies the factory beyond doubt. Under explicit GIT_DIR with no GIT_WORK_TREE, git's setup_explicit_git_dir falls through to set_git_work_tree(cwd), so git add <rel> reads the temp file and stages it into the REAL index at that relative path. FIXED at tier 1 in the registering commit: apply_hermetic_git_env now REMOVES the nine repo-location variables (GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_COMMON_DIR, GIT_INDEX_FILE, GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY, GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES, GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES, GIT_NAMESPACE, GIT_PREFIX) rather than overriding them, because there is no value for GIT_DIR meaning 'use the directory I am standing in' - absence is the only way to say it. Scrubbed at process start via tests/__init__.py so it covers every fixture, factory-built or inline, instead of a discipline each of the ~30 inline call sites must remember. hermetic_git_env_is_active now includes absence in its definition so the predicate cannot answer 'hermetic' while GIT_DIR points at the host repo. Three new invariants I-HERM-07/08/09; I-HERM-09 reproduces the incident end to end in a child process and mutation-checking confirms it fails when the scrub is removed.

title: Four HIGH advisories in production dependencies turn security-scan red and block every merge platform-wide: brace-expansion DoS, fast-uri host confusion, ip-address SSRF/trust-boundary bypass (3 CVEs), socket.io-parser memory exhaustion - and the override that should fix brace-expansion under minimatch does not take effect
rule_violated: security-scan runs npm audit --audit-level=high --omit=dev and feeds the required build-status check, so a newly published advisory in a transitive production dependency halts every merge in the repository until it is resolved. Three of the four resolve cleanly by raising existing override floors; the fourth does not, which means the repository has no working mechanism to pin that transitive package.
notes: Diagnosed but NOT fixed - recorded so the blockage is tracked rather than rediscovered. All four are transitive (isDirect false). THREE FIX CLEANLY by raising floors that already exist in package.json overrides: fast-uri ^3.1.4 -> ^3.1.5, ip-address ^10.2.0 -> ^10.4.0 (vulnerable range is <=10.3.0, so the obvious ^10.3.1 is NOT enough), and a new socket.io-parser ^4.2.7; that combination also clears nx's brace-expansion copy. THE FOURTH RESISTS: node_modules/minimatch/node_modules/brace-expansion stays at 5.0.8. minimatch@10.2.5 requests ^5.0.5, 5.0.9 is published, and the existing override key minimatch@^10 -> brace-expansion is demonstrably the key that produced 5.0.8 from ^5.0.8 - yet raising it to ^5.0.9 leaves 5.0.8 in place, including after deleting package-lock.json and re-resolving from scratch. A version-range override key (brace-expansion@>=4.0.0 <5.0.9) does not help either, because npm matches override keys against the spec a PARENT REQUESTS, not against the resolved version. A blanket brace-expansion override is the wrong instrument: the tree carries safe 1.1.15/2.1.1/2.1.2 copies under eslint, glob and others that a 5.x override would major-bump. Likely next step is bumping minimatch itself, since 10.2.5 is what pulls a vulnerable floor. SEPARATE OBSERVATION worth its own investigation: lockfile regeneration is not idempotent with the committed state on this repo - npm 10.9.7 yields 3076 packages via --package-lock-only and 2902 from a full re-resolve, against 3407 committed. 331 of those are the @turf/* family, which is declared in no package.json and imported nowhere in source, so pruning them is CORRECT and the committed lockfile carries dead weight; the remaining delta is unexplained and points at an npm version skew. Nothing was pushed - the working tree was reverted clean.

title: A mission's recorded state is only ever what ARIA last wrote: nothing reads back what GitHub did between two cycles, so a PR merged by a human, closed unmerged, or stripped of its branch leaves the mission stuck in IMPLEMENTING forever, holding a WIP slot for work that already landed and waiting on an event that already happened
rule_violated: Persistent missions are only worth their durability if the durable record is TRUE. PR 1.1 made mission state survive the cycle and PR 1.2 made discovery write into it, but every writer in the chain records what ARIA decided and none reads back what the world did with it. A mission whose PR merged externally keeps a wake_condition for an event in the past and keeps a WIP slot the scheduler will honour, so the pipeline starves itself on work that is already on main.
notes: Wave 2 PR 1.3 of docs/plans/2026-08-02-aria-full-autonomy-program/PLAN.md, CLOSED by the registering commit. The safety rule is that ONLY a positive, recognised observation moves a mission; an unrecognised state, a None and a raising adapter are all recorded and change nothing. That is not general caution but the shape of the production lane: select_github_adapter hands observe/standard/frozen a RecordingGitHubAdapter that never calls gh, so a reconciler reading 'not merged' as 'closed unmerged' would advance the retry rung of every mission on every dry-run night and every GitHub outage until each reached justified_reject without a single real observation. PLAN specified a would_transition soak before going live and this PR ships none, deliberately: a flag is a second control surface for what the adapter table already decides, and one somebody can leave in the wrong position, whereas the profiles that must not act get an adapter that cannot answer. Three consequences of the same rule: get_pr could not carry reconciliation because it never requests state or merged (a phase built on it would classify every real PR as unobserved and never fire), so get_pr_lifecycle is purpose-built; merged is read before state and against the boolean because GitHub's REST API reports a merged PR with state closed and 'false' is truthy; branch absence goes through git ls-remote rather than gh api because 'the branch is gone' and 'I could not ask' are an exit code apart there and a stderr string apart over HTTP. Divergence table: merged before MAIN_VERIFYING fast-forwards under reconciled_external_merge; merged at or past it is steady state not divergence; closed-unmerged from IMPLEMENTING..MERGING replans one retry rung up and escalates to HUMAN_REQUIRED when the ladder is spent; a positively absent branch returns IMPLEMENTING..READY to PLANNING but is only checked when the mission binds no PR, because GitHub deletes the head branch when a PR merges. A merge outranks a closed sibling attempt and an open sibling holds the replan back. At most one transition per mission per sweep, because the snapshot is folded once. mission.py's forward-skip guard now reads a closed FORWARD_SKIP_REASONS set rather than the single coarse_observation literal: an externally-observed merge is honestly that shape (end state seen, path not) but writing coarse_observation on it would discard the only record of why the mission jumped. PR bodies are untrusted content: the ARIA-Mission trailer is anchored and strict, and adoption can only BIND an already-open mission - an unknown id is recorded and refused, pinned by an AST test over both Name and Attribute call forms because a source-text search for open_mission is satisfied by the list_open_missions this module imports. 42 tests written before the code; 17 mutations, 16 killed on the first pass and the survivor (deleting the sweep's outer handler) fixed by adding the test that makes transition_mission refuse one mission's edge and asserts the next mission still reconciles.

title: The plan state machine's entire implementation phase is unreachable: request_implementation and the four events after it have no production caller, so a promoted plan never leaves CONVERGED, the plan-coverage precondition never runs, and IMPLEMENTATION_MERGED / IMPLEMENTATION_REJECTED are terminal states nothing can reach
rule_violated: Plan ARIA-V9.0-B added five implementation-phase event writers with state preconditions, two terminal states and a coverage gate (_require_coverage_for_implementation) that only runs inside request_implementation's validator. grep for callers finds exactly one hit outside plan_convergence.py, and it is a comment. promote_converged_plan_to_dispatch writes a dispatch row and no plan event at all, so the plan stays CONVERGED - which list_active_plans treats as terminal. Every safety property the implementation phase encodes is therefore inert, and any gate built on plan state for in-flight work is structurally unable to fire.
notes: Found while verifying ORPHAN-HIGH-487's proposed data source rather than assuming it. 487 proposed gating promotion on plan_convergence.list_active_plans(); that function filters out TERMINAL_STATES, CONVERGED is in that set, and promote_converged_plan_to_dispatch refuses any plan that is not CONVERGED - so the candidate is structurally never in the active list, and neither is any previously-promoted plan, because promotion writes no plan event. The 487 gate therefore reads the DISPATCH ASSIGNMENT fold instead, which is the record the promotion path actually writes. NOT FIXED in the 487 change, deliberately: wiring five events through five points of the dispatch lifecycle (promotion -> implementation_requested, claim -> implementation_started, worker result -> implementation_outcome_recorded, merge -> implementation_merged, rejection -> implementation_rejected) is a state-machine change whose preconditions must be reconciled with the assignment fold's own transitions, and doing it inside a gate fix would have shipped it unreviewed. The consequence while it stays open is bounded and recorded: the WIP gate does not depend on plan state, and _require_coverage_for_implementation - a real safety property (ORPHAN-HIGH-310's class: convergence measures agreement, not coverage) - is inert until the phase is entered. Wave 2 PR 1.5 weaves mission ids through plans and dispatches and is the natural place to make the same lifecycle write plan events.

title: The 17-check pre-PR-open / pre-merge perimeter's verdict type could be constructed by hand, so a passing HardFailReport was forgeable in one line and ORPHAN-CRITICAL-428's stated closure - that a caller cannot assemble a passing report - was never enforced
rule_violated: A gate's verdict must be producible only by the thing that ran the checks. ORPHAN-CRITICAL-428 introduced an opaque construction token for exactly this and both producers pass it, but the field defaults to None and no code ever compared it back, so HardFailReport(results=(HardFailResult('no_force_push', True, 'ok'),)) built a report whose passed property was True and whose raise_if_blocked() returned silently. The perimeter was bypassable without a single check being defeated. PerimeterObservation carried the identical hole.
notes: CLOSED by the registering commit. Found while pinning the math-kernel document's 'no score bypasses a hard gate' invariant - the strongest form of that rule turned out to be that nothing needed to bypass the gate at all, because the verdict object itself was forgeable. Verified by running it rather than by reading the docstring, which asserted hand-assembly was 'impossible rather than merely discouraged'; that claim is load-bearing because every later reviewer of this file has been reasoning from it. FIX: _require_registry_token in __post_init__ on both HardFailReport and PerimeterObservation, comparing the sentinel by IDENTITY rather than equality so a later __eq__ on some wrapper cannot make the guard true by accident; ForgedVerdict is its own exception class rather than a ValueError so an audit can grep for it, and the message names the producer that should have built it. PerimeterObservation is guarded too even though it authorises nothing: it cannot bypass a gate but it can feed a fabricated telemetry record into the governance ledger the autonomy ladder counts. Blast radius nil - grep finds exactly two construction sites, both legitimate producers. Also pinned in the same change, from the math doc: HardFailReport.passed contains no comparison and no numeric constant, the failure set is selected by the boolean rather than by a rank, and no registered check's source reads a confidence/score/probability/likelihood/weight name to decide. Two of the doc's other three proposals were checked and found ALREADY IMPLEMENTED and better than its framing - independence_check.py's three layers (ORPHAN-HIGH-421) and INCONCLUSIVE-as-blocker in both human_required_adjudication and PerimeterVerdict.evaluable; the open residue is belief support_count in memory.py counting two refs from one file or one tool run as two supports, which #1056 did not cover.

title: The mission trailer adoption path shipped with no producer: mission_reconcile parses ARIA-Mission: from PR bodies and binds the mission, but nothing anywhere writes that trailer, so the adoption branch could never fire
rule_violated: A consumer waiting on a string no producer emits is machinery that can never fire - the defect class this programme has spent eight PRs closing, introduced by one of its own changes. PR 1.3 (#1066) added _adopt_trailered_pull_requests with a strict anchored MISSION_TRAILER_PATTERN, an AST test proving a PR body cannot mint work, and correct untrusted-input discipline; no code path wrote the trailer. Every test in that PR supplied the trailer itself, so none of them could have caught it.
notes: Self-reported: the gap was introduced by #1066, whose own review document criticised exactly this pattern. CLOSED by the registering commit. format_mission_trailer lives beside MISSION_TRAILER_PATTERN in mission_reconcile.py and VALIDATES ITS OWN OUTPUT against that pattern, so a producer that could emit a shape the consumer misses fails at write time rather than silently on a future night when a PR goes unadopted; two literals in two modules is how a producer and consumer come to disagree about a format. The trailer is a BARE LINE after ## Provenance rather than a bullet inside it, because the pattern is anchored with MULTILINE and the obvious placement would never match. The load-bearing test is not the regex round-trip but the end-to-end one: a body build_pr_body produced, handed to reconcile_missions unmodified, binds the mission. open_pr_for_action takes NO mission_id parameter - it derives one via mission_for_assignment from the assignment it already has, so the PR's mission and the dispatch row's mission cannot disagree. Promotion writes mission_id onto the dispatch row AND binds plan_ids + assignment_ids back onto the mission (one-way reference means reconciliation has nothing to reconcile against), and refuses an id naming no open mission rather than writing an unresolvable reference. NOT DONE HERE, tracked as PLAN Wave 2 PR 1.6: mission_id does not yet reach emit_change_planned or the worker envelope, and the only caller supplying one is the operator CLI (plan promote-to-dispatch --mission-id) - the scheduler that selects a mission and promotes its plan is the next phase, and a successful-promotion fixture belongs with it. 22 tests written before the code; 10 mutations, 7 killed on the first pass and 3 survivors each exposing a test that proved less than its name claimed (a signature check instead of a behaviour check, an ordering assertion with only one fault present, and a type guard nothing fed a wrong type to).

title: Wave 1's entire deliverable has no production caller: the aria/state durable store is wired into no workflow, both scheduled lanes still restore and publish the 30-day aria-tools-state artifact, and state_continuity therefore returns `unknown` every cycle because no reference outside the tree exists
rule_violated: Machinery written and never called is the defect class this programme exists to close, and Wave 1's headline deliverable is the largest instance of it. state_store.py implements checkout/build_snapshot/publish_state/verify with FF-only CAS and contention replay, and its only callers are the operator CLI and memory_gap's read side. grep across .github/workflows for ARIA_STATE_STORE, state_store or aria/state returns nothing: both scheduled lanes use ./.github/actions/restore-aria-tools-state and upload actions/upload-artifact name=aria-tools-state. Consequences: ORPHAN-CRITICAL-484/488/513 stay OPEN because the artifact transport they describe is still the live state path; restore_and_replay has no transport; and state_continuity's third verdict `unknown` - correct by design until a reference exists outside the tree - is the only verdict it can ever return.
notes: Found by re-verifying a blocker carried unchecked all session ('lane cutover blocked on the self-hosted runner'). The runner blocks EXECUTION; it never blocked WRITING the cutover, and the cutover was neither written nor tracked - it lived in a parenthetical in PROGRESS.md ('Wave 1 COMPLETE (except the lane cutover)'). PLAN 2.6 specifies it: restore_and_replay 'moves to 2.6 with the lane that gives it a transport', and state_continuity's `unknown` verdict exists 'until the state-branch lane cuts over (2.6) or the daily anchor lane resumes'. PR 2.6 landed its modules (contention replay, the deliberate no-publish-lease decision) and not its workflow half.
