rule_violated: 100-tenant readiness plan Task 8 — capacity activation must be entitlement-driven; the 60-min zero-loss promise is scoped to the 2K envelope only

title: Tenant erasure left PUBLISHED sensor_outbox rows, cached MQTT device credentials and late-message re-inserts reachable after the schema drop
rule_violated: GDPR Art 17 erasure cascade completeness — no copy of an erased tenant's data may stay reachable through outbox rows, auth caches or late device messages after the tenant schema is dropped
notes: PR #1338 commit 65753cb90 closes this id with a Closes: trailer but no row or review heading ever existed; allocated at integration (documented in the 2026-09-03 integration review) so the post-merge close ceremony can record the main-reachable commit.

title: Declared JetStream stream budgets (~7.75 GiB) exceed the droplet's 2GB max_file_store, and the deploy capacity gate still pins the pre-telemetry 1920 MiB floor
rule_violated: The JetStream account file store and the deploy capacity gate must both cover the sum of the stream budgets the code declares; a stream whose max_bytes exceeds the account store cannot be created at all
notes: Task 2 landed AQUACULTURE_TELEMETRY (6 GiB default) and AQUACULTURE_DLQ (256 MiB) on top of AQUACULTURE_EVENTS (1.5 GiB) while nats.conf stayed at max_file_store: 2GB and NATS_REQUIRED_FILE_STORE_BYTES stayed at 2013265920. The capacity script's own comment predicted exactly this half-done state. Sizing inputs are also absent: docs/perf/results/ (the Task 0.4 M/E/R artifact) does not exist and BROKER_QUEUE_BUDGET_BYTES defaults to 0. Closure needs the measurement, the derived caps, the raised store (or a recorded PENDING_CAPACITY resize decision), and a new invariant summing declared stream budgets against the configured store. Renumbered from SENSOR-CRITICAL-104 at integration: main allocated SENSOR-HIGH-104 (domain sequence 104) after the branch forked.

title: Cold telemetry archive writes columnar-JSONL while the directory, both services and the retention contract all say Parquet
rule_violated: A file, directory or service name must describe what the code actually does; the shipped artifact format must match the documented retention contract
notes: ARCHIVE_CODEC_ID is 'columnar-jsonl'; the codec header comment states the Parquet writer dependency could not be installed in the authoring environment. The deterministic-bytes, manifest+sha256 and independent re-read guarantees ARE present and codec-independent, and the codec id is stamped in both header and ledger manifest, so the pluggable seam is real. Closure is either a Parquet codec behind the same interface under format version aqua-telemetry-archive/2, or dropping Parquet from ADR-024 plus renaming the directory and both services off 'parquet'.

title: Task 5 shipped no load, resilience-drill or WAL-G restore evidence, yet Task 6 and the sidecar promotion verdict landed on its exit gate
rule_violated: A durability or capacity claim is only closed by a recorded measurement; a task's exit gate may not be consumed by downstream tasks before it is met
notes: None of Task 5's declared outputs exist in the merged tree: tools/scripts/telemetry-reconciliation.ts, tools/scripts/telemetry-failure-drill.ts, docs/runbooks/telemetry-capacity-and-recovery.md and e2e/tests/integration/telemetry-reconciliation.spec.ts are all absent, and docs/perf/baseline-2026-04.md is unchanged. Steps 5.1-5.6 (steady profile, nine-scenario resilience matrix, 15K stress, hardware verdict, RLS/compression decision, WAL-G scratch restore with RPO <= 300s) are unexecuted, so the zero-loss claim is asserted rather than measured. The operator-run drills need an external load host.

title: Telemetry capacity entitlement exists in billing but the admin provisioning path never reserves it, so a tenant still goes ACTIVE over the platform envelope
rule_violated: A capacity state machine is only load-bearing when the provisioning path that can exhaust the capacity is routed through it; partial work needs an owner, a deadline and a tracked finding, not a follow-up note
notes: The billing core (contract, entity with the two partial unique indexes, migration 1802200000000, reserve/activate/release with same-transaction outbox emit) is real and covered. apps/admin-api-service and web/ contain ZERO references to TelemetryCapacity, sustainedIngressMessagesPerSecond or sustainedMetricRowsPerMinute: no Step 8.3 calculator, no admin DTO, and the provisioning workflow never calls reserve(), so PENDING_CAPACITY cannot occur. The SENSOR_READINGS meter is not reconciled against the approved entitlement. The branch's own review lists these as follow-ups with no owner, deadline or id.

title: sanitize-html ^2.17.7 floor pulls ESM-only htmlparser2@12 nested under sanitize-html, which the Jest CJS sandbox cannot parse; messaging-service suites red
rule_violated: Never commit with red tests (CLAUDE.md CRITICAL block); a dependency floor must land with the test-runtime consequence it causes, and the Jest preset's ESM allowlist must reach nested node_modules copies
notes: Consequence of SUPPLY-HIGH-006 (commit b701cc7b3). Fix: jest.preset.js ESM_ONLY_TEST_DEPENDENCIES list + last-node_modules-segment anchored transformIgnorePatterns; htmlparser2, domhandler, domutils, dom-serializer, domelementtype, entities appended.

title: Production deploy jobs interpolate dispatch text into shell source and secret-bearing jobs do not independently prove exact protected-main authority
rule_violated: Untrusted workflow inputs must cross into shell only through environment/data channels, and every production-secret-bearing job must independently prove exact protected-main authority before checkout or secret access.
notes: A crafted bypass reason can terminate the generated assignment and inject shell syntax. The workflow-level permission block and partial job predicates do not substitute for a pre-secret exact-main assertion in every production-bearing job.
narrative: This is a deploy-lane recurrence of INFRA-CRITICAL-045. The repair must move all dispatch values into env, reduce job permissions independently, and make each protected job reject non-main or stale workflow authority before checkout and before any Environment secret is materialized.

title: The repository GITHUB_TOKEN with contents and packages write authority is transported to the production host as a general GHCR credential
rule_violated: A production host may receive only a narrowly scoped package-read credential for the shortest possible command boundary; repository contents-write and workflow orchestration authority must never cross SSH.
notes: The token is serialized into the SSH payload and remains available to remote setup until docker login. Unsetting it after login reduces lifetime but does not narrow the authority that crossed the trust boundary.
narrative: Repair requires a protected package-read-only credential or an equivalent exact-digest pull authority, job-scoped permissions, and a proof that no contents-write or id-token-capable credential appears in the host payload.

title: The Linux platform-binary installer executes downloaded native code after missing or mismatched lockfile integrity is reported only as a warning
rule_violated: Every downloaded native executable in the release producer chain must be bound to a committed integrity value and fail closed before extraction or execution on any mismatch or missing authority.
notes: The action extracts and executes the artifact even when the expected SHA-512 is absent or differs. Exact-SHA source checks cannot compensate for a fail-open native toolchain.
narrative: Repair must source the exact package integrity from the committed lockfile, reject absent or mismatched entries, clean temporary bytes on every exit, and add an executable tamper regression.

title: Production deploy accepts stale protected-main ancestors and force-moves the deployed baseline before independent post-deploy verification
rule_violated: Production state transitions must be main-tip monotonic and compare-and-swap guarded; the deployed baseline may advance only after the exact host release passes independent verification.
notes: An older main run can mutate the host after a newer run because the workflow proves only ancestry, concurrency is ref-scoped, and the baseline tag is force-pushed. Manual dispatch also omits the reusable independent post-deploy verifier.
narrative: Repair must bind one global production concurrency group, assert exact current main at every mutation edge, capture the prior deployed baseline, run post-deploy verification for automated and manual paths, and update the baseline through a non-force CAS that rejects any concurrent movement.

title: Capacity maintenance lets an operator-supplied registry prefix and historical ancestor SHA widen destructive image garbage collection authority
rule_violated: Image deletion scope must derive from the canonical deployed release, exact service catalog, rollback manifest, and unresolved DR state; workflow inputs may select a non-destructive report but cannot widen repositories or target a historical release.
notes: The script removes tags beneath IMAGE_PREFIX, while the manual workflow accepts both IMAGE_PREFIX and any main ancestor as data. This can make a validly dispatched maintenance run remove rollback or current-release references outside the intended catalog.
narrative: Repair must remove image_prefix and mutating deploy_sha inputs, resolve the exact atomically published current release on the host, restrict repositories to generated catalog entries, and prove current/rollback/DR images remain protected.

title: Protected production SSH verifies a configured fingerprint but does not require the selected host key to be ED25519
rule_violated: The protected SSH authority contract names the droplet ED25519 host key; both the exact SHA256 fingerprint and the expected key algorithm must be enforced before connection.
notes: Exact fingerprint matching prevents an arbitrary key, but the documented provisioning contract specifically selects ED25519. Requiring the algorithm removes ambiguity during multi-key ssh-keyscan output and rotation.
narrative: Repair must filter ssh-keyscan to ssh-ed25519, reject any non-ED25519 match, and cover RSA-only plus mixed-key negative tests.

title: Backup and PITR evidence publishers retain protected secret, OIDC and mirror-write authority after their workflow SHA becomes stale main
rule_violated: Every protected secret, OIDC signing and external evidence-write edge must prove its workflow revision is the authenticated exact current main at that edge; a long-running prior main revision cannot retain authority.
notes: The execution jobs are exact-main guarded, but publish-evidence can outlive that proof and still enter production-backup with id-token:write and Spaces credentials after main advances.
narrative: Authenticated current-main equality must be re-proved before protected profile materialization, immediately before Sigstore OIDC signing, and immediately before the mirror write.
Stale-run status publication, if required, must use a bounded metadata-only lane with none of those authorities.

title: Shared production concurrency replaces pending deploy and DR runs and lets non-main dispatches churn the release queue
rule_violated: Production release, backup and restore authorities must form a lossless main-only queue; monitoring must not cancel or starve a pending production operation.
notes: GitHub concurrency defaults to queue: single: a new same-group run replaces the existing pending run even when cancel-in-progress is false. The five-minute WAL watcher shares the whole-workflow release group, and workflow-level concurrency is acquired before main/environment gates, so monitor traffic or a non-main dispatch can cancel a legitimate pending deploy, backup, PITR or verification. Move freshness to a dedicated coalescing group with a shared host lock; route non-main dispatches to run-scoped rejection groups and use queue: max for the remaining production authority entrants.
narrative: The default one-pending queue makes cancel-in-progress false insufficient: it protects the running operation but not the legitimate operation waiting behind it.

A long deploy holds the workflow-level group through build and approval time, suppressing the five-minute WAL freshness signal even though the monitor only needs a short read-only host critical section.

title: An empty rollback inventory leaves a manifest without its checksum and makes cold release finalization permanently fail closed
rule_violated: Rollback release state must publish its manifest/checksum pair as one complete validated unit for every cardinality, including an empty but authoritative inventory.
notes: capture_rollback_manifest always creates rollback-images.tsv but hashes it only when non-empty; the GC state verifier correctly rejects exactly that incomplete pair.
narrative: Cold or legacy production with no healthy application rollback point must still produce a checksum for the canonical empty manifest.
Failure injection must prove no ordinary or interrupted producer path leaves exactly one member of the pair.

title: Exact-SHA source retention deletes bind-mount source bytes still owned by live containers before the incoming release commits
rule_violated: Immutable source GC may delete only a source proven unreferenced by every existing production container; the incoming release cannot revoke the still-authoritative release's bind-mount bytes before terminal commit.
notes: Selective deploys can leave live containers bound to source generations older than the current marker, so a simple incoming-plus-prior retention rule remains unsafe.
narrative: The protected set must be derived under the host lock from the incoming SHA and all existing Docker container bind sources beneath the canonical source root.
Malformed, aliased or unparseable source-root references must make pruning fail closed rather than be ignored.

title: Generic production SSH secret names silently fall back to repository-wide credentials when Environment values are absent
rule_violated: Production host credentials must be structurally addressable only through their protected Environment; an absent Environment value must fail closed and must never resolve a repository-wide credential with the same name.
notes: Live production contains only DROPLET_SSH_FINGERPRINT while DROPLET_HOST, DROPLET_USER and DROPLET_SSH_KEY remain repository secrets. GitHub's secrets context therefore supplies the repository values to Environment jobs instead of proving Environment ownership. Deploy also lacks the new package-read credentials and production-backup lacks its protected profile.
narrative: Use production-specific secret identifiers in every workflow and manifest so repository-level legacy names cannot satisfy preflight.
Closure additionally requires out-of-band Environment provisioning, repository-secret revocation and a live negative proof; no secret value belongs in Git.

title: Live production baseline and Environment controls permit mutation outside the signed compare-and-swap broker
rule_violated: The production baseline and protected Environment approvals must be enforceable only through the narrow reviewed release authority; live repository controls must match that declared fail-closed contract.
notes: Live rulesets are empty, deployed/production is unprotected, both production Environments allow admin bypass and require no reviewer, and main has required checks but no enforced pull-request approval. The workflow's atomic updateRefs CAS is correct but can be bypassed by a direct ref writer.
narrative: Closure requires a reviewed live ruleset and Environment protection change coordinated with the other active agents so the release broker is usable without granting implementation workflows merge authority.
The production stop-line remains false until the live controls, protected credentials and backup/PITR evidence are all proven together.

title: Production E2E can bypass the release stop-line and sends repository JWT and database secrets into opaque live-host scripts
rule_violated: Production observation must be read-only, exact-release-bound and subject to the production stop-line; repository-wide application and database secrets must never be injected into an opaque remote execution path.
notes: The workflow has an independent workflow_dispatch path, no stop-line or exact-current-release proof, uses appleboy SSH/SCP, installs packages on the live host, and runs suites that seed live rows while forwarding repository JWT_SECRET and DB_PASSWORD. A successful deploy trigger does not make this a read-only production observation.
narrative: Immediate containment must remove the manual live-mutation bypass and repository secret fallback without weakening the production Environment.
Closure requires staging to own destructive E2E and a narrow native-transport production smoke lane that is read-only, exact deployed-release-bound and emits independently verifiable evidence.

title: Staging can certify an operator-selected image and force-push it as the current main SHA promotion proof
rule_violated: A staging promotion proof must bind the exact protected-main source SHA, immutable image digests and observed deployment result through a non-force compare-and-swap; operator-selected tags and target-host Git cannot mint that authority.
notes: workflow_dispatch accepts image_tag_override, the remote deploy uses appleboy plus mutable target-host Git, and success force-moves deployed/staging-<github.sha>. The resulting tag names the workflow SHA even when the deployed image tag was selected independently, so production's staging gate can accept false provenance.
narrative: Remove the image-tag override and target-host Git authority, transfer an exact-SHA runner-built immutable digest manifest over fingerprint-pinned native transport, and attest the observed containers before promotion.
Advance the staging baseline and proof only through prior-OID CAS; destructive E2E may move to staging only after this authority is established.

title: Production secret environment file is accepted world-readable without inode or mode authority
rule_violated: Persistent production secrets must be read or mutated only through a root-owned, single-link, non-symlink mode-0600 inode established before the first consumer.
notes: Read-only metadata inspection confirmed the live file is root-owned but world-readable. Existing-file paths neither converge the known safe legacy 0644 shape nor reject symlink, hardlink, foreign-owner or writable-mode substitutions before reading and appending credentials.
narrative: No secret contents were read while reproducing this finding.

Repair must run under the exclusive host lock, atomically create an absent file as 0600, narrowly converge only the exact root-owned single-link legacy 0644 inode, fsync it, and fail closed on every other shape.
Read-only metadata observation on 2026-07-19 found /var/aqua-saas/.env to be a root:root, mode-0644, single-link regular file.

title: Production certificate store exposes every NATS service identity to host users and sibling containers
rule_violated: With certificate CN as NATS identity, private-key storage and delivery must prevent host-user reads and must expose exactly one service identity to each consumer container.
notes: Read-only metadata inspection confirmed traversable root-owned certificate directories and readable private keys. Compose mounts the whole NATS clients directory into each application and the whole NATS directory into the broker; generator skip paths incompletely validate existing key identities.
narrative: No key contents were read while reproducing this finding.

Repair must harden the persistent store ancestry, validate owner/type/link/mode on existing material, preserve non-root consumer readability only behind non-traversable host ancestry, and replace directory-wide mounts with exact per-consumer certificate/key mounts.
Read-only metadata observation on 2026-07-19 found the /var/aqua-saas/certs directory ancestry at mode 0755 and NATS client/server private keys at mode 0644.

title: Full production deploy force-removes every aqua-prefixed container without project or catalog authority
rule_violated: A production deploy may remove only exact container IDs proven to belong to its canonical Compose project and service catalog; a name prefix is not lifecycle ownership.
notes: The full-deploy fallback pipes every name matching aqua- into docker rm -f. It can destroy backup/PITR integration evidence, sibling-agent workloads or future unrelated containers even though they are outside the aqua-saas Compose project.
narrative: Repair must enumerate bounded exact container IDs, inspect project/service labels, require membership in the generated catalog or an explicit infrastructure allowlist, and reject malformed/duplicate/unowned rows.
No live container was stopped or removed while reproducing this finding.
Live container naming inspection on 2026-07-19 confirmed that aqua-walg-it-* integration and restore-proof workloads share the host.

title: Secret-bearing backup jobs can silently lose opaque evidence passed through GitHub job outputs
rule_violated: Bulk evidence produced inside a secret-bearing job must cross trust boundaries through immutable artifact identity, never through an opaque job output that GitHub may suppress after secret-substring matching.
notes: Backup and PITR jobs currently emit up to roughly 440 KB of random-looking gzip Base64 as four job outputs. GitHub skips outputs containing any registered secret substring; short alphanumeric production values such as region identifiers make the handoff nondeterministic even though all local invariants pass. Replace the bulk output with an exact run/name/id/digest-bound immutable artifact and retain only small server-issued metadata where unavoidable.
narrative: The defect fails closed but can indefinitely prevent three-backup and PITR closure evidence from becoming visible.
Tests must include evidence containing a configured-secret substring and prove artifact transport is unaffected.

title: Release-state growth eventually reaches the bounded scanner limit and permanently blocks every host operation
rule_violated: A bounded production state scanner must be paired with bounded, authority-aware retention so normal successful operation cannot deterministically exhaust its own safety limit.
notes: The hardened host scanner fails closed after 512 release directories, but successful releases are never retired. Normal deployment history therefore becomes a deterministic permanent outage. Add exclusive-lock retention that preserves the current marker, active/prior journal identities, rollback and DR references, retains a bounded audit window, validates every candidate directory, and deletes only exact unreferenced terminal releases.
narrative: Raising or removing the 512-row bound is not a fix; it converts a deterministic wedge into unbounded disk and traversal risk.
Retention must be restart-safe and prove protected releases cannot be collected across selective deploy and recovery states.

title: A completed markerless bootstrap epoch can prevent a later SHA from retrying the first production cutover
rule_violated: One-time markerless bootstrap authority must close after each terminal attempt yet permit a new protected-main epoch when no release marker was ever committed; it must never become reusable or permanently single-SHA.
notes: Bootstrap GC records a terminal COMPLETED claim for the incoming SHA. If the first deploy later fails before publishing current-release.json, a corrected newer main SHA cannot establish a fresh bootstrap epoch even though the markerless precondition still holds. Introduce an atomic epoch rollover allowed only from a terminal prior claim, with no marker, no unresolved release transaction, exact current-main descendant proof and preservation of all live image identities.
narrative: The same SHA must not replay a completed destructive claim and a nonterminal claim must never roll over.
Tests must cover failed first cutover, newer descendant retry, stale/replayed SHA rejection and marker-created structural unreachability.

title: The isolated PITR workflow embeds a run script larger than the GitHub Actions step limit
rule_violated: A production recovery ceremony must remain loadable by the workflow engine; executable payloads above the platform step limit must live in a versioned, testable repository script rather than an oversized inline run block.
notes: The Run isolated PITR ceremony on the droplet step is 23,589 characters while GitHub Actions accepts at most 21,000 characters for one steps[*].run value. Move the exact ceremony into a repository-owned script, transfer it through the protected runtime bundle and preserve shell/YAML/executable contract tests.

title: Evidence mirror publication fails on an empty object-store prefix
rule_violated: An immutable evidence mirror must support its first publication; an absent S3 Contents field represents an empty list and must not make the idempotent conflict check fail before the first object can be written.
notes: AWS S3 ListObjectsV2 omits Contents when the prefix is empty, so the current JMESPath length(Contents) expression evaluates length(null) and fails the initial backup or PITR mirror publication. Normalize absent Contents to zero and test first-write, exact replay and conflicting-object rejection.

title: Evidence mirror rejects valid opaque S3 version IDs outside a 256-character subset
rule_violated: An S3-compatible immutable evidence mirror must accept the provider's full documented opaque VersionId contract while preserving bounded, quoted transport.
notes: AWS documents VersionId as an opaque URL-ready UTF-8 value up to 1,024 bytes and publishes an example containing plus signs. The current 1-256 character allowlist rejects that valid contract before pinned HEAD/GET verification. Keep newline/NUL and byte bounds, but do not invent a narrower provider alphabet.

title: PITR evidence accepts producer-chosen snapshot and lock-set digests without their preimages
rule_violated: A signed restore proof must independently recompute every snapshot and lock-set digest from a closed canonical preimage; checking only SHA-256 syntax does not bind the claimed source consistency boundary.
notes: The evaluator recomputes the source/restored payload hashes and lock count, but initially accepted source_verification_snapshot_sha256 and source_verification_lock_set_sha256 after only a 64-hex format check. Carry the bounded snapshot identifier and exact sorted relation list, derive the canonical expected list independently from topology plus tenant schemas, and recompute both hashes before promotion.

title: PITR source parity can hold partial SHARE locks for the full one-hour RTO while waiting on a busy relation
rule_violated: A production verification drill must bound lock acquisition independently from restore RTO so a busy relation fails the drill quickly instead of converting evidence collection into a prolonged write outage.
notes: The source keeper is bounded by the remaining 3,600-second RTO, but the generated transaction has no local lock_timeout. Its root and full relation LOCK statements may acquire earlier SHARE locks and then wait behind a concurrent writer on a later relation, blocking new production writers on the already-held set until the outer timeout kills the session. Set a short transaction-local lock_timeout before the first LOCK and prove both contended acquisition failure and prompt lock release.

title: Production PITR requires a sentinel table that the active deployment stop-line prevented from ever reaching the live database
rule_violated: The recovery proof that unlocks a fail-closed deployment gate cannot depend on persistent database DDL that only the gated deployment path can install.
notes: Read-only live production evidence returned ABSENT for platform.pitr_drill_sentinels. Stage 011 landed after the production stop-line and is installed only by db-migrate, while the locked deploy workflow skips db-migrate. The PITR script fails before source capture when the table is absent. Remove the bootstrap edge with a self-contained, hash-pinned WAL boundary protocol (for example transactional pg_logical_emit_message records plus exact replay-LSN bracketing) or establish a separately reviewed least-privilege bootstrap authority; do not temporarily unlock the general deploy lane or grant the backup workflow arbitrary DDL.
narrative: A read-only live-production to_regclass check on 2026-07-20 returned ABSENT for platform.pitr_drill_sentinels.

title: Evidence mirror publishers expose Spaces write credentials beside GitHub Actions runtime authority
rule_violated: A static external-storage write principal must execute in a credential-minimal process that structurally excludes GitHub, OIDC, artifact-runtime, and command-file authority.
notes: Both publisher steps unset named AWS variables and then continue in the original Actions step subprocess. They do not re-exec through env -i or reject ACTIONS_RUNTIME_TOKEN, ACTIONS_RESULTS_URL, OIDC request credentials and GitHub command-file channels, so Spaces write credentials coexist with a second write-capable control plane. Use an exact-binary, sanitized AWS-only child and inject every forbidden channel in dynamic tests.

title: Evidence mirror accepts a stale singleton snapshot when object versions or bucket versioning change after pinned reads
rule_violated: Immutable mirror acceptance must revalidate the bucket and exact-key version set after every pinned HEAD/GET so concurrent replacement, deletion, or versioning suspension cannot pass on a stale pre-read snapshot.
notes: Publisher and closure verifier list a singleton version, perform pinned HEAD/GET, and return success without a final list-object-versions or get-bucket-versioning check. A racing second version/delete marker or suspension can leave a green result whose claimed singleton immutability is already false. Require a matching post-read VersionId snapshot and Enabled status.

title: A valid opaque S3 VersionId beginning with a dash is transported as a separate AWS CLI option value
rule_violated: Opaque provider identifiers must remain one unambiguous data argument even when their first byte is an option prefix.
notes: Pinned calls currently pass --version-id and the opaque identifier as two argv elements. A URL-ready value beginning '-' can be parsed as an option by the AWS CLI. Transport a single quoted --version-id=<opaque> argv element and dynamically cover leading dash plus UTF-8 byte boundaries.

title: Evidence mirror materializes an auto-paginated object-version listing before enforcing any bound
rule_violated: Every remote listing in the evidence authority must be bounded at the producer before bytes reach runner disk or memory.
notes: Every list-object-versions call allows AWS CLI auto-pagination and redirects the aggregated JSON only afterward. A polluted or heavily versioned prefix can consume unbounded runner resources before exact-count validation. Disable auto-pagination, set a small server max-keys bound, reject IsTruncated/continuation state, and test the truncated response.

title: PITR bounded capture reader races the following protocol marker on the same pipe
rule_violated: A bounded streaming protocol must own and validate a deterministic frame; correctness cannot depend on whether the operating system coalesces two adjacent lines into one read chunk.
notes: The reader exits successfully at the first LF only when that LF is the final byte of its current Node data chunk; it rejects any later bytes in the same chunk. The PostgreSQL coprocess immediately emits SOURCE_VERIFICATION_CAPTURED as the next line, and the shell later tries to read it from the same pipe. Kernel chunk coalescing therefore makes identical valid output either pass or fail, while a reader that reads ahead can also consume bytes expected by the shell. Give one reader ownership of both the bounded payload line and the exact following marker, with no producer output until the later commit command.

title: PITR closure incorrectly requires the stop-lined live database release SHA to equal the current workflow SHA
rule_violated: The current protected-main SHA authorizes the recovery tool bytes, while the independently deployed release SHA identifies live database state; a closure proof must bind both authorities without conflating them.
notes: The stop-line prevents current main db-migrate from reaching production, so platform.release_ledger correctly reports the database migration release while the protected workflow runs current main tool bytes. Schema-v2 PITR currently requires source/restored payload release.git_sha to equal evidence main_sha, making the first closure proof impossible. Preserve main_sha as exact workflow/tool authority; add source/restored database release SHA fields derived from their canonical payloads; require exact payload, release, migration-head and sentinel parity; and never accept a dispatcher-supplied release value or require a deploy-published host marker.
narrative: The database release may legitimately differ from the running application marker after forward-only migration states, failed deployments or rollback attempts; database verification must name that authority explicitly.

No workflow input may choose the database release SHA, and evidence main_sha must still equal the exact current protected workflow SHA. A current-main ancestry check may strengthen the signer boundary only when it is independently available without creating a bootstrap dependency.

title: PITR writes an evidence timestamp syntax that PostgreSQL 16 rejects as recovery_target_time
rule_violated: A recovery ceremony must translate its canonical evidence timestamp into a PostgreSQL-accepted GUC literal and independently normalize the observed setting back to the evidence representation.
notes: Production-pinned PostgreSQL 16.13 rejects the canonical evidence value 2026-07-20T08:36:32.340761Z when it is copied verbatim into recovery_target_time. The current restore script writes that exact rejected literal, so PostgreSQL exits before recovery. Preserve UTC ISO T/Z in signed evidence, derive the exact PostgreSQL config form with a space and +00 offset, and query/normalize the observed GUC back to canonical ISO before equality attestation.
narrative: The physical PostgreSQL 16 replica-recovery integration proves the WAL marker boundary with a real base backup and archived WAL.

title: PostgreSQL image uniformity invariant assumes an obsolete combined build-and-push step name
rule_violated: A workflow invariant must verify the semantic build-argument and publication authority across split steps without depending on an obsolete display name.
notes: npm run invariants:fast reproduced the false negative after the deployment workflow split image construction from registry publication. The current workflow step builds the matrix image without registry authority and still passes BUILD_MAIN_SHA, while a separate publish step owns registry credentials; the invariant searches only the obsolete combined Build and push display name. Update the assertion to bind the actual build step and exact BUILD_MAIN_SHA contract without weakening the separate publish-authority boundary.

title: Billing lifecycle tests encode calendar dates that inevitably cross the wall clock and invert active or future assertions
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Test Rules — lifecycle tests must control time or derive boundaries from an injected clock so their truth does not change with the calendar.
notes: Tests used 2025-12-31 as a future expiry or due date. Once the real clock crossed that value, subscription resume, trial expiry, tax exemption, credit stacking, coupon expiry, negotiated discount and overdue-invoice assertions inverted. Inject one fixed test clock and derive past/future values relative to it.

title: Billing unit fixtures and assertions still model Decimal entity fields as JavaScript numbers after the lossless MoneyColumn migration
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Architectural Approach and currency-safe billing contract — financial entities remain Decimal end to end; tests may not coerce exact monetary state back to IEEE-754 numbers.
notes: The production entities use Decimal through MoneyColumn, but mocks populate totals and payment amounts with number values and compare returned Decimal objects using numeric Jest matchers. Align fixtures with entity types and assert exact decimal strings without toNumber conversion.

title: RecordPaymentHandler does not validate persisted invoice monetary values before arithmetic, allowing non-finite NUMERIC state to escape as Decimal errors or propagate NaN
rule_violated: Currency-safe billing requires persisted monetary state to be finite and Decimal-typed before any comparison or write; corrupt server state must fail closed as a controlled integrity error.
notes: PostgreSQL NUMERIC can represent NaN and runtime corruption can violate TypeScript assumptions. Money.of currently accepts a Decimal NaN, while undefined produces an unclassified DecimalError. Validate amountDue, amountPaid and total at the transaction boundary and return a sanitized server-side integrity error before creating a payment.

title: Monthly auto-invoice generation persists totals beyond the currency minor-unit scale instead of applying banker's rounding at the invoice boundary
rule_violated: Currency-safe billing requires finalized invoice amounts to be quantized with the ISO 4217 currency scale and ROUND_HALF_EVEN while remaining Decimal values.
notes: The scheduler computes exact Decimal totals but writes 33.333 USD directly into invoice totals. Quantize the single canonical invoice total to the configured currency scale with ROUND_HALF_EVEN, reuse it for subtotal, total and amountDue, and preserve Decimal persistence.

title: Unbounded sanitize-html minor drift installs an ESM-only transitive parser and breaks messaging-service Jest while violating the repository Node.js support floor
rule_violated: Direct production dependencies must resolve reproducibly from the committed lock and remain compatible with the repository's declared Node.js floor and Jest module contract.
notes: Verified dependency-state drift: package.json permits sanitize-html ^2.17.4 and the committed lock resolves 2.17.5 with htmlparser2 10.1.0, but the shared mutable node_modules contains sanitize-html 2.17.6 (Node >=22.12) with nested ESM-only htmlparser2 12.0.0. Jest's CommonJS transform then rejects dist/index.js before sanitizer tests execute. Exact-pin the last lock-compatible 2.17.5 release; do not transform-ignore the ESM graph or weaken sanitization.
narrative: The repository declares Node.js >=20.11.0, so allowing a direct dependency release whose own engine begins at Node 22.12.0 is a production compatibility regression even where a developer happens to run Node 22.
The failure is reproducible from installed package metadata and module syntax; the dependency tree must be restored narrowly from the exact committed lock before focused messaging verification.

title: The eslint-plugin workspace declares an empty Jest target that deterministically fails every affected test run

notes: Nx infers the workspace test target from the package script, but the package contains no Jest suites. Jest therefore exits 1 with No tests found whenever broad affected scope reaches this project. The target must explicitly accept its governed empty-suite state or gain package-local tests.

title: AquaMobil typecheck uses Array.at outside its configured TypeScript library target

notes: Reproduced after installing AquaMobil's standalone lockfile dependency graph: Tailwind resolution was clean, then tsc rejected Array.prototype.at because this standalone PWA intentionally targets a pre-ES2022 library. Fix the assertion without widening the runtime target.

title: Production control-plane durable staging paths use banned temporary terminology
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Architectural Approach bans temporary-language fixes; durable crash-recovery staging state must be named for its actual lifecycle.
notes: The staged banned-phrase gate reproduced 31 matches introduced by the control-plane diff. These paths are durable atomic-publish or crash-recovery staging objects, not throwaway state. Rename identifiers and diagnostics to stage/staged_path without changing the fail-closed lifecycle.

title: Production-host invariant fixtures cannot find setup-node outside the system PATH
rule_violated: Hermetic CI fixtures must bind the exact active Node executable when invoking repository-local Node launchers instead of assuming node is installed in /usr/bin.
notes: The bundle producer executes the Node-based esbuild launcher while four new invariant fixtures deliberately replace PATH with /usr/bin:/bin. This passes where node is system-installed but fails on GitHub setup-node runners with exit 127. Pass process.execPath as the explicit NODE_BIN test authority, keep the remote runtime PATH contract narrow, and prove the complete fast invariant shard.

title: Power-cut invariant pins a retired staging variable identifier
rule_violated: Source-level fault-injection contracts must track the canonical durable staging identifier when that identifier changes, or verify a semantic boundary that survives local renaming.

title: Production runtime bundle workflows omit the setup-node binary from their sanitized authority
rule_violated: An exact-SHA production runtime builder must receive every executable authority explicitly inside its sanitized environment; it may not rely on setup-node remaining discoverable through an excluded ambient PATH.
notes: setup-node installs Node under /opt/hostedtoolcache, while the producer exports PATH=/usr/bin:/bin and executes the esbuild JavaScript launcher through its env shebang. The three production workflow callers likewise re-exec through env -i without carrying Node, so bundle construction exits 127 before any protected SSH/deploy action. Resolve and canonicalize the active pinned setup-node executable in each workflow, pass it as NODE_BIN, validate it fail-closed in the exact producer, and invoke esbuild through that exact binary.
narrative: GitHub Actions run 29780800607 job 88481309871

title: Production control-plane fixtures pass unproved optional values into strict APIs
rule_violated: Changed-file TypeScript checks must prove parsed workflow blocks and generated release identifiers are present before passing them to strict string APIs.
notes: The affected type-check enables strict indexed access. Two YAML-derived run blocks remain optional after callback boundaries, and releaseIds array indexes remain string-or-undefined even though loops populate them. narrative: GitHub Actions run 29780801838 job 88481805379

title: Physical PITR integration leaves its bind-mounted backup owned by the container user
rule_violated: Container integration fixtures must restore host ownership of bind-mounted scratch state before runner cleanup so successful assertions cannot be converted into teardown failures.
notes: The PostgreSQL target correctly chowns /base-backup to postgres and chmods it 0700, but the host runner later calls rmSync after the container stops. GitHub Actions cannot traverse the bind mount and reports EACCES after the physical PITR proof itself passed. Re-attest the mount path and restore the original runner uid/gid through the still-running root container before teardown.
narrative: GitHub Actions run 29780801838 job 88481805372

title: Physical PITR fixture derives its source floor from a lagging WAL writer observation
rule_violated: Physical recovery tests must establish WAL ordering with the logical insert end rather than an asynchronously lagging write position.
notes: A real PostgreSQL 16 run failed beforeFencePosition <= sourceFloorPosition even though the fence command completed before the separate capture command. pg_logical_emit_message returned an inserted fence LSN while pg_current_wal_lsn reported the asynchronously lagging WAL write position. Use pg_current_wal_insert_lsn as the deterministic source floor without weakening the BEFORE/cutover/AFTER recovery proof.
narrative: Local PostgreSQL 16 integration run 2026-07-20T22:22Z

title: Production PITR evidence records WAL write progress as the source snapshot floor
rule_violated: A PITR source snapshot floor must represent the logical end of all WAL inserted before capture completion; asynchronous WAL writer progress cannot serve as that replay lower bound.
notes: The generated production source capture stores pg_current_wal_lsn(), which PostgreSQL defines as the WAL writer position. It may lag pg_current_wal_insert_lsn(), the logical WAL end containing already-inserted marker and database records. A restore replay comparison against the lagging value weakens the claimed source boundary. Generate the insert LSN instead and prove strict marker/floor/replay ordering with PostgreSQL 16.
narrative: PostgreSQL 16 system administration functions documentation

title: PR CI findings store run prose in the canonical evidence citation field
rule_violated: Findings created after the evidence-shape cutover must keep evidence as canonical file citations and place CI run, advisory, or explanatory prose in narrative.
notes: The full fast-invariant run rejected nine prose strings across the eight new PR-CI findings. Preserve the contextual text in narrative, keep only canonical repository citations in evidence, rechain from the first affected entry, and rerun the complete invariant gate.

title: PITR integration teardown can mask the primary proof failure with unsafe diagnostics
rule_violated: Integration teardown must always execute without throwing from finally, preserve the primary test failure, and sanitize unknown cleanup diagnostics without default object stringification.
notes: The CI-equivalent ESLint run reports no-base-to-string for unknown cleanup details and no-unsafe-finally for the final teardown throw. Capture the proof failure, execute every cleanup step afterward, normalize unknown failures to safe Error objects, and report proof plus cleanup failures without allowing teardown to replace the primary cause.

title: Finding truth table header is not pinned to the canonical registry tip
rule_violated: Generated registry projections must assert their declared registry tip equals both the plan manifest and the canonical JSONL chain tip.
notes: The manifest follows the 1093-entry registry tip while the truth-table header still declares the pre-CI 1083-entry tip. Existing tests compare table rows to active critical IDs but never bind the declared header to manifest.registry_tip_hash. Update the projection and add an exact singleton header assertion.

title: Production source publication hardens a directory before its cross-parent rename
rule_violated: Immutable production publication must remain atomic and recoverable while succeeding under the owner-pinned non-root test authority used by required CI.
notes: The publisher recursively changes the payload root to 0555 and then moves that directory from the private stage parent into the sources parent. Linux denies a cross-parent directory rename to an unprivileged owner when the moved directory is not writable, while root masks the defect. Keep the root owner-writable only inside the exclusive lock, publish it, converge it through an inode-pinned 0555 transition, and recover the exact interrupted 0755 final form fail-closed.
narrative: GitHub Actions run 29800384169 job 88540150938
Reproduced locally as uid 65534 with both failing invariant suites

title: DR corruption fixture overwrites a read-only terminal artifact without restoring owner write access
rule_violated: Negative filesystem fixtures must construct corrupt evidence explicitly under ordinary runner permissions rather than depend on root bypassing canonical read-only modes.
notes: writeTerminalJournalArtifacts correctly creates result.json as mode 0400. The invalid-result scenario then calls writeFileSync on that same inode without first granting owner write permission, so the test throws EACCES on the non-root GitHub runner before exercising the fail-closed parser. Open only the fixture file to 0600, write the corrupt payload, and restore 0400 before invoking the control plane.
narrative: GitHub Actions run 29800384169 job 88540150938

title: Production-host invariant teardown cannot remove its immutable published source tree as a non-root runner
rule_violated: Filesystem integration fixtures must explicitly reverse test-owned immutable modes before teardown and must not rely on root or rm force semantics to bypass permissions.
notes: Once publication succeeds as an ordinary UID, the canonical source contains 0555 directories and 0444/0555 files. Node rmSync with recursive force still cannot unlink entries from non-writable directories, so nineteen otherwise-passing tests fail in finally. Route fixture teardown through one bounded helper that first grants the owner recursive write/traverse access on the unique mkdtemp root, checks chmod, and then removes it.
narrative: Reproduced locally as uid 65534 after repairing INFRA-HIGH-132

title: Release recovery fixture overwrites its read-only transaction journal without an explicit permission transition
rule_violated: State-transition fixtures must explicitly restore owner write access before replacing canonical read-only journals under ordinary CI runner permissions.
notes: The recovery path upgrades active-release-transaction.json and leaves it at canonical mode 0400. The fixture then overwrites that inode with a ROLLED_BACK state without first granting owner write access, so a non-root runner fails before it can prove host operations resume. Open only the fixture journal to 0600, write the next state, restore 0400, and retain the parser assertion.

title: Production host runtime invariant hardcodes a non-portable Node executable path
rule_violated: Runtime invariants must execute bundled JavaScript through an explicitly resolved absolute Node authority and must not assume the hosted runner exposes Node at /usr/bin/node.

GitHub setup-node installs Node outside /usr/bin, so the otherwise valid runtime test exits 127 after publication. Pin the fixture's child runtime authority to process.execPath and prove both probes work with PATH restricted to /usr/bin:/bin.

title: Production deploy mutates host state before proving its Node 22 runtime authority
rule_violated: A production host entrypoint that executes Node-22-targeted exact-SHA runtime artifacts must resolve, validate, and pin one compatible absolute host executable before any release, Docker, database, or secret mutation.
notes: The protected runtime bundle is compiled with esbuild target node22, yet droplet-up invokes bare node only after substantial release work and has no Node preflight; a missing or older host executable can therefore fail both the health gate and rollback after mutation. Post-deploy verification checks only command presence and also invokes the ambient PATH result. Establish one canonical host-node resolver, require major version 22, export the resolved non-symlink executable path, and invoke every bundled runtime through it.
narrative: Discovered while separating GitHub setup-node build authority from the production droplet runtime authority after PR #1022 run 29816085763

title: The NATS SSoT drift gate repairs the checkout before it judges it, and cannot tell staleness from a malformed SSoT
rule_violated: A freshness gate must evaluate the committed artifact without mutating the working tree, and must report drift through a status distinguishable from a producer error.
notes: Both drift gates ran scripts/nats/generate-nats-conf.py and then asked git whether the tree became dirty. The generator's write lands before the check, so a stale artifact is silently repaired in the runner's checkout and every later step in the same job reads the repaired file while the commit under test still carries the stale one. The generator also had no read-only mode and no drift-specific exit code, so a forgotten regeneration and a malformed services.yaml were indistinguishable to the gate. Add --check (compare only; exit 3 for drift, 64 for a usage error), move both gates onto it, and prove the detector detects.
narrative: Raised while recovering PR #1022's nats-conf --check mode onto the integration head; the branch added the flag but left both gates on the generate-then-diff form.

title: The production host control plane is committed but unreachable: no workflow or host entrypoint invokes it, so the deploy lane still mutates the host without its lock, source authority, or Node-22 proof
rule_violated: A control that exists, is tested, and is not wired where it matters enforces nothing; a landed authority must have at least one caller on the path it is meant to govern.
notes: The control plane, the exact-SHA runtime bundle producer and the SSH payload producer landed with their invariants, but deploy-digitalocean.yml still reaches the droplet through appleboy/ssh-action and runs main's droplet-up.sh directly. droplet-up.sh and post-deploy-verify.sh resolve `node` from PATH rather than through aqua_control_plane_require_node_authority, and neither takes the fixed-inode host lock. The branch wired this by rewriting droplet-up.sh, droplet-capacity.sh, deploy-paths.sh, post-deploy-verify.sh and three deploy workflows wholesale, which is excluded by owner decision; the wiring must be built additively on main's deploy shape instead. Closure criterion: the production deploy, capacity maintenance and post-deploy verification paths each enter through production-host-control-plane.sh (lock-exec / hydrate-exec / shared-exec), every bundled runtime is invoked through ${AQUA_PRODUCTION_NODE_BIN}, and deploy-isolated-checkout-ssot.spec.ts pins the ordering (node authority before lock, lock before any release/Docker/secret mutation) on main's files.
narrative: Raised while integrating PR #1022 by path slices; the control plane itself is verified by tests/invariants/production-host-control-plane-runtime.spec.ts (20 tests) but has no production caller.
Until this lands, every INFRA-CRITICAL-080..101 finding whose subject is the deploy lane remains exactly as PR #1022 left it.

title: Every NATS service private key is stored mode 0644, so any host user can read the material that IS the service's identity
rule_violated: With the certificate CN as the NATS identity, a private key is a credential; it must not be readable by any principal other than the one consumer container that presents it.
notes: The generator writes ${DEPLOY_CERTS_DIR}/nats/clients/<cn>-key.pem at 0644 and validates that mode as canonical. PR #1022 wrote the same mode, so this half of INFRA-CRITICAL-101 was never repaired by either line. The identity-store directories are now 0700, which stops a directory listing, but any process that can name a key path still reads it. The mode cannot simply be tightened to 0600 without knowing each consumer container's runtime UID: the compose bind-mounts the file into the container and the in-container reader is the service process, not root. Closure criterion: each per-service key is readable only by the UID of the container that mounts it (or delivered through a mechanism that does not place it on a shared host path), the generator validates that exact mode, and production-cert-identity-store.spec.ts asserts it.
narrative: Raised while landing the compose half of INFRA-CRITICAL-101; the broker no longer holds every service key, but the host filesystem still exposes them.

title: PR #1022's WAL-G evidence rewrite (schema v2 to v3, run-scoped PITR ceremony, sanitized mirror publisher) cannot be recovered as scripts alone and dies with the branch unless its workflow half is planned
rule_violated: A signed evidence chain has one producer and one consumer contract; half of it cannot be landed, and a landed half that nothing calls is dead code that reads as coverage.
notes: The branch's WAL-G work is five new scripts (walg-pitr-ceremony.sh, verify-walg-evidence-mirror.sh, materialize-walg-signed-transfer.sh, read-bounded-line.mjs, pitr-source-verification-locks.sql) plus roughly 2700 changed lines across evaluate-walg-evidence.mjs, walg-evidence-attestation.mjs, walg-pitr-restore.sh, verify-walg-github-evidence.sh and generate-database-verification-sql.ts, and it introduces subcommands (verify-local-run, verify-binding, --check) and a sanitized run_trusted_node re-exec that exist only inside its rewritten backup-production.yml (+1629) and pitr-restore-production.yml (+1840). Landing the scripts alone gives the new subcommands no caller while changing the behaviour of create-run and create-evidence, which the live backup lane does call — an untestable change to the production evidence chain. Its runbook text is equally unportable: the database-restore-drill diff is the v2-to-v3 evidence description plus the PRODUCTION_* secret rename, and the secret-rotation diff is the rename alone. Closure criterion: an execution plan that reconciles the branch's v3 attestation with main's #1255 DR-candidate control plane and the 2026-07-30 recovery architecture, landing producer and consumer together with the workflow half, or an explicit owner decision that main's v2 chain stands and the branch's evidence work is abandoned. Findings INFRA-CRITICAL-090, INFRA-HIGH-102/103/104/108-120 and INFRA-MEDIUM-110/116/117/128/129/131 stay OPEN until that decision.
narrative: Raised while integrating PR #1022 by path slices. The scripts-and-docs-only scope this integration was given is not satisfiable for this surface, which is the finding rather than a reason to force it.

title: Tenant session-timeout clamp is omitted on 5 of 7 token-mint paths (verifyMfaLogin the primary MFA login path, verifyStepUp, acceptInvitation, resetPassword, verifyWebAuthnLogin): an idle MFA session keeps a rememberMe refresh token up to 30 days regardless of a 5-minute tenant policy

title: A NATS subscriber that is not an IEventHandler shipped behind `as never`, alongside 23 spec doubles the compiler was told to stop checking

notes: The production half is the defect: ErasedTenantTombstoneService.attachEventBus passed an object with only `handle` to subscribeTo, which declares IEventHandler (handle + getEventType). The cast made the missing member invisible; nothing on the current dispatch path calls getEventType, so the gap was latent rather than firing. The 23 spec occurrences are the same class one layer down — doubles for NatsConnection, JetStreamManager/Client, EntityManager, DataSource, MqttAuthService, TankBatchService and TenantErasureRequestedEvent that the compiler was instructed not to compare against the types they stand in for. Fixed by typing the handler as IEventHandler<IEvent> (IEvent, not TenantErasedEvent: validateEventBySubject covers only the farm/sensor/messaging registries, so a TenantErased payload reaches the handler unvalidated and the existing runtime guards are load-bearing) and by routing every double through stub/collaborator/stubMember from libs/testing/src/doubles/typed-double.ts.

title: Platform bootstrap stage 008 runs before the service migrations, so no table created by a migration is ever owned by its schema owner or covered by the schema-wide runtime grant

OWNER TO and GRANT ... ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA. Both are point-in-time over the relations that exist when Phase 0 runs; every table a Phase 1 migration creates is outside them until some later deploy's Phase 0 sweeps it up. On a from-scratch install there is no later deploy.
notes: NOT fixed in the PR that raised it. The immediate casualty (the dry-run guard) is fixed at the guard; the class is not. Fix direction: re-run the hardening stage after the Phase 1 migration loop so 008's own invariant holds in one pass. Deliberately deferred because the bootstrap needs timescaledb and pgvector, so re-ownership of every table in every schema cannot be exercised anywhere but CI, and shipping it untested alongside a provisioning fix would risk the fix. In CI both the bootstrap and the migrations run as the same superuser, so ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES masks the grant half there; a production split between the bootstrap role and db_migrate would not be masked. title: A deploy stamps the entire source migration history into any ledger-less tenant_<uuid> schema it finds by name, so the schema a failed provision leaves behind is reported fully migrated, never repaired, and — where TimescaleDB is installed — breaks every subsequent deploy
rule_violated: category=tenant-routing. A ledger row is a claim that a migration was applied; writing it without evidence that the schema carries what the migration creates turns the ledger from a record into a fiction. listTenantSchemas discovers tenants by namespace pattern alone and consults no evidence table, and backfillTenantLedgersForSource copies the whole source ledger into any tenant ledger it finds empty — so an empty or partial schema (the shape a failed PROVISION leaves, see the sibling finding) is stamped as complete, the fan-out sees nothing pending, RECONCILE_EXISTING_SCHEMA refuses it as an empty schema, and the deploy's Phase 1.3 REVOKE on the tenant's sensor_metrics raises 'relation does not exist'.
notes: Not theoretical: the four failed provisions the live gate produced on the way to 24/24 each left exactly this shape (farm + sensor present, hr/messaging/hydroponics/ai/alert absent). The 'no tables at all' guard first considered is wrong for that shape — it would pass and stamp the five missing services. The fix is per source schema: before stamping migrations_<src>, require the tenant schema to carry every per-tenant table MODULE_SCHEMAS registers for <src> (tables + referenceDataTables, the same set the provisioning gate asserts); otherwise skip the stamp and log the missing set. With the ledger left empty, the fan-out that runs next sees every migration pending and builds the missing schemas in the same deploy — so the rule turns a bricked tenant into a self-healing one, including the phantoms that already exist in production.

title: A failed PROVISION leaves the tenant schema it created behind: CREATE SCHEMA runs autocommit, the per-migration rollback cannot undo it, and the failure path records evidence but never drops it
rule_violated: category=tenant-lifecycle. A provisioning job that did not commit must not leave a namespace that looks like a tenant. processJob issues CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS outside any transaction (the replay cannot be one transaction — CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY and TimescaleDB steps opt out), and its catch block collects failure residue and writes FAILED evidence but contains no DROP SCHEMA; the only DROP in the file is on the DELETE path. The partial schema is then discovered by name on the next deploy (sibling CRITICAL).
notes: Drop only a schema THIS run created: assertTenantSchemaIdentityAvailable checks that no OTHER tenant holds the name, not whether the schema pre-exists, and CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS hides pre-existence — so the provisioner must probe information_schema.schemata before CREATE and remember the answer. A schema left by an earlier attempt (reachable once retries work) is not dropped; the ledger-driven fan-out resumes it and the stamping guard (sibling CRITICAL) keeps a deploy from sealing it. collectFailureResidue keeps running FIRST — it is the diagnosis the live gate used four times — and the drop outcome is recorded in the same failure evidence.

title: retryOperation cannot re-issue a FAILED tenant schema job: runStep short-circuits the SUCCEEDED publish_provisioning_requested step, so the retried run meets the same FAILED job and fails again
rule_violated: category=saga-idempotency. A step's ledger row is not its postcondition. publish_provisioning_requested's postcondition is 'a PROVISION job for this operation exists and is not terminally failed', which is a fact about platform.tenant_schema_jobs, not about admin.tenant_provisioning_steps. retryOperation resets every step except SUCCEEDED ones and runStep returns early on a SUCCEEDED row, so the request is never re-issued even though platform.request_tenant_schema_provisioning is idempotent per operation_id and re-opens a FAILED/ABORTED job by design. The wait step then reads the FAILED job and throws — the retry is dead on arrival.
notes: Same class the file already documents for activate_tenant (activateTenantAfterVerification: re-verify before acting because runStep skips SUCCEEDED steps on retry). Fix direction: runStep accepts a postcondition probe; when the ledger says SUCCEEDED but the probe says the postcondition no longer holds, the step re-runs. For the publish step the probe is 'a PROVISION job exists whose status is not FAILED/ABORTED'. A first-attempt failure still fails the run — only an explicit retry re-issues — so there is no unbounded re-provision loop. COMMITTED jobs are never re-issued (the SQL leaves them untouched anyway). [RENUMBERED ADMIN-HIGH-009 -> ADMIN-HIGH-094 on 2026-09-05] Registered on the phantom-tenant branch (PR #1427) as ADMIN-HIGH-009; main had meanwhile allocated sequence 009 in the ADMIN domain to an unrelated finding, so the row is re-registered as ADMIN-HIGH-094 when the branch took main. The original id names a live ledger row and cannot be an alias; fix commit cb75f3505 carries the original id in its Closes: trailer and closes THIS finding, not main's ADMIN-HIGH-009.

title: FEFO feed allocation filtered lot expiry against the wall clock instead of the deduction's own asOf, so a retroactive record was judged against now

title: lot expiry is compared as an instant in UTC rather than the site's local calendar day, and the boundary operator excludes a lot on its own expiry date
rule_violated: Day semantics resolve in the site's zone and bind as a date; no query carrying day meaning may compare a DATE column against an instant

title: AquaMobil water-quality recording is rejected on every submission: the page sends a `parameters` field the backend contract deleted, the hand-written input type makes that field mandatory and the required equipmentId/dynamicParameters optional, and the offline lane renders an unconditional green success for a payload that can never sync
rule_violated: category=contract-drift. A client payload must match the server input contract field for field. `CreateWaterQualityInput` on the backend has no `parameters` (single-ingress: `dynamicParameters` is the sole channel) and requires `equipmentId` and `dynamicParameters`; the aquamobil mirror declares the inverse, so TypeScript forces the bad field to be sent. GraphQL variable coercion rejects the unknown input field before the resolver runs, online and on offline replay alike. Same root cause as PRODUCT-MOBILE-CRITICAL-001 (mobile-app-auditor) in the same cycle.
notes: Raised in review markdown as PRODUCT-FORM-CRITICAL-001 (form-write-auditor) and PRODUCT-MOBILE-CRITICAL-001 (mobile-app-auditor); neither prefix is a registry domain, so the finding is registered here under MOB. title: No gate can see the GraphQL INPUT/variable axis of the mobile write path: 19 hand-written *Input mirrors type the queued payload union, the registry documents are plain strings outside codegen, and graphqlRequest's DocumentNode overload accepts an untyped variables bag — so a CRITICAL-class drift is structurally unavoidable
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Architectural Approach tier 1 (make it impossible) / tier 3 (make it detectable). The document-text validator (`validate-graphql-operations.mjs`, ceiling 0) proves every document parses against the supergraph and can never see a variables object; the codegen glob covers only src/graphql so pages, hooks and the queued-operation registry get no TypedDocumentNode; `graphqlRequest`'s second overload — selected by every call that writes one explicit generic, ~65 sites — types variables as Record<string, unknown>; `OperationPayload` is an untagged union of hand-written mirrors intersected with the envelope, so `queueOperation(type, payload)` correlates nothing. Every queued OperationType carries the same latent risk the water-quality CRITICAL realised.
notes: Raised in the cycle report as MOB-HIGH-019 (mobile synthesis; opening id PRODUCT-MOBILE-SYNTH-CRITICAL-002) — that id was never allocated by the registry, which is why the number here differs. title: Mobile-shaped storage response DTOs expose domain enums as GraphQL String! (itemType, movementType, coverageStatus, stockEventsSummary.type) and serialise the lowercase TS enum VALUES, while the client narrows them to hand-written uppercase unions — StorageHubPage indexes MOVEMENT_TYPE_CONFIG with a value it never contains and crashes

title: Invitation e-mail links cannot be validated: the link carries the ActionToken row id, but validateInvitation hashes the URL segment and looks it up as a raw invitation token, so every valid invite is rejected before the password screen
rule_violated: category=contract-drift. The ActionToken indirection (CRITICAL-001/002: keep raw tokens off the event bus) was retrofitted into the two write paths — acceptInvitation resolves actionToken.id → tokenHash, resetPassword likewise — but not into the read path validateInvitation, which still assumes the URL segment is a raw token: sha256(uuid) matches nothing, the plaintext fallback matches nothing, and the form gates on that answer. No spec covers validateInvitation.
notes: Raised by an external review (2026-09-05) and confirmed against the code; the reviewer's phrasing ('looks up in a different table') is imprecise — both paths read Invitation, the missing piece is the ActionToken.id → tokenHash resolution. Fix direction (tier 1): one ActionTokenResolver.resolve(urlSegment, purpose) primitive that every consumer of an emailed link segment goes through, so a consumer that skips the indirection cannot be written; plus a validateInvitation spec. Independent of the FRONTEND_URL defect — fixing this alone still leaves every link pointing at localhost.
