title: Super-admin password recovery silently does nothing: a tenant-less user's PasswordResetRequested event carries tenantId 'system', notification-service's UUID guard drops it (and acks), and the internal action-URL resolver would also reject the tenant-less token — the user sees success and no e-mail
rule_violated: category=contract-drift. Two subsystems disagree on how 'no tenant' is represented: auth-service encodes it as the sentinel string 'system' in a UUID-typed field, notification-service enforces 'tenantId is always a UUID' as a cross-tenant-leak guard. No shared type makes the platform-scope case representable, so the sentinel fails a validator written for a world where it does not exist — the same modelling gap FARM-HIGH-083 records on the outbox publish side.
notes: Confirmed 2026-09-05. A second, independent blocker sits behind the first: even past the UUID guard, requireNotificationService rejects an identity without tenantId and the action-token lookup filters WHERE tenantId = $2 while the super-admin token was saved with tenantId NULL. Fix direction (tier 1): make tenancy scope explicit in the event contract (discriminated scope: {kind:'tenant', tenantId} | {kind:'platform'}) so consumers must handle the platform case at compile time and the UUID guard applies only where a tenant is structurally required; the internal-API identity needs the matching platform-scope audience so tenant-less action tokens resolve. [RENUMBERED SEC-HIGH-057 -> SEC-HIGH-159 on 2026-09-05] Registered on the Faz 3 branch (PR #1424, claude/mobile-graphql-contract-0jj9jg) as SEC-HIGH-057; main had meanwhile allocated that sequence in the domain to SEC-HIGH-057 (Rust edge SignatureMode), so the row is re-registered as SEC-HIGH-159 when the branch took main. The original id names a live ledger row (sequence = identity) and cannot be an alias; the review file carries a Ledger ids table.

title: notification-service's auth event handler converts every failure into a normal return — a caught SMTP error, and null-returning PII/tenant/action-URL resolvers on any auth-service non-2xx — so the NATS consumer acks the message and the bus's own nak/backoff retry never engages; a transient outage loses invitation and password-reset e-mails for good
rule_violated: category=delivery-semantics. The bus documents the invariant explicitly ('Handler failures must NOT be swallowed while the message is acked… Route failures to retry/DLQ') and naks with exponential backoff on a thrown error; the handler never throws — it logs and returns on an exception, and its resolvers collapse permanent (404) and transient (5xx/network) failures alike into null. 'Logged and returned' is spellable as success, so the failure is invisible: no DLQ entry, no metric, no user-visible error.
notes: Confirmed 2026-09-05; the auth-service-outage path is deeper than the external review's cited catch block — the null-returning resolvers would survive deleting that catch. Fix direction (tier 1): make delivery outcome a value the transport reads rather than an exception a handler may absorb — IEventHandler.handle returns Ack | Retry(reason) | DeadLetter(reason), so a handler that wants to log must still choose an outcome; resolvers distinguish permanent from transient failure instead of returning null. Compounds with the super-admin reset defect: that drop is then acked as success.

title: The default MQTT ingestion path stores the calibrated, farm/pond-scoped reading but publishes the RAW, unscoped wire payload as the SensorReading event: the alert engine's fail-closed scope filter silently excludes every farm/pond-scoped rule and evaluates a value that is not the stored one, and an unmapped channel key upcasts to an empty reading that auto-resolves live incidents
rule_violated: category=event-contract. saveReading and publishSensorReadingEvent are two independent projections of one physical event built from two different inputs (calibrated SensorMetricInput rows with scope vs the untouched wire payload); every field that would catch the drift (farmId, pondId, tankId, flat readingXxx) is optional on SensorReadingEvent and no publish-side schema gate exists, so the producer omission type-checks and the alert engine's scope filter turns it into silent rule exclusion. The Rust-sidecar bridge and the GraphQL ingestion path already carry calibrated values and scope; only the two legacy MQTT/HTTP producers — still registered unconditionally, the SENSOR_SERVICE_PROFILE gate not yet wired — are wrong.
notes: Confirmed 2026-09-05; Phase 5 (VFD apply, SENSOR-CRITICAL-007) does not touch publishSensorReadingEvent. Life-safety relevant: a farm/pond-scoped dissolved-oxygen rule on the default ingestion path does not fire, and an unmapped key ('dissolved_oxygen', 'flow_rate', 'orp') closes an open INFO/LOW incident as 'returned to normal'. Fix direction (tier 1): no producer may mint a SensorReadingEvent from anything but persisted metric rows — saveReading returns the SensorMetricInput[] it wrote and one shared buildTypedReadingEvent(metrics, sensor) (the mapper the sidecar bridge already owns) is used by all four producers, publishing v3 flat fields; the v1 nested emission is deleted. Complementary: the alert engine distinguishes 'unscoped reading' from 'reading scoped to no farm' and rejects the former. Adjacent: SENSOR-MEDIUM-066/067. [RENUMBERED SENSOR-CRITICAL-106 -> SENSOR-CRITICAL-111 on 2026-09-05] Registered on the Faz 3 branch (PR #1424, claude/mobile-graphql-contract-0jj9jg) as SENSOR-CRITICAL-106; main had meanwhile allocated that sequence in the domain to SENSOR-HIGH-106, so the row is re-registered as SENSOR-CRITICAL-111 when the branch took main. The original id names a live ledger row (sequence = identity) and cannot be an alias; the review file carries a Ledger ids table.

title: A full deploy destroys the separately-installed monitoring stack and replaces it with a silent one: droplet-up.sh force-removes every container whose name contains 'aqua-' with no Compose-project scoping, then docker-compose.droplet.yml recreates the four monitoring containers under aqua-saas with the placeholder alertmanager.yml (smtp.invalid, receiver 'null') that checkout -f keeps unrendered
rule_violated: category=ownership. Two compose files claim the same four global container names, and the deploy's clean-slate step selects containers by a name substring instead of by the Compose project label that is the actual ownership boundary (the correct idiom is already used at droplet-up.sh:224); the monitoring compose's own header defends only against --remove-orphans. The Alertmanager config is rendered by mutating a git-tracked file while the consumer is a force-checked-out worktree at a different path, so the render is discarded by construction.
notes: Confirmed 2026-09-05. Net effect of one full deploy on a droplet running aqua-monitoring: the stack is reaped, recreated under aqua-saas pointing at smtp.invalid with a null default route, the Tier-1 memory gate in monitoring-up.sh is bypassed, TSDB history is orphaned in the other volume, and the runbooks' 'docker compose -p aqua-monitoring ps' reports a false outage. Nothing pages, nothing errors. Fix direction (tier 1): one owner per container — delete the four monitoring services from docker-compose.droplet.yml (docker-compose.monitoring.yml is the documented sole activation path); every container-selection step in droplet-up.sh filters by label=com.docker.compose.project=aqua-saas; render alertmanager.yml to a persistent gitignored path symlinked into the checkout like .env/certs (deploy-paths.sh:137-139) and mount that. OBS-HIGH-002's closure notes list the separate project as delivered and never noticed the duplicate; orphan-findings.md:8529 declares the render 'one script run away', which checkout -f makes false.

title: Uploaded object bytes are outside the recovery cut: MinIO lives in a bare local minio_data volume with no backup or replication path (the repo's only mc command is a purge), and the PostgreSQL PITR/restore proof and its production stop-line never mention object storage, so a restore that reports success leaves dangling keys to photos, certificates and attachments
rule_violated: category=dr-scope. The DR programme was scoped to 'the database' rather than 'the durable state'; because object references are stored in PostgreSQL, a green PITR proof looks complete while the referenced bytes are gone with the host. The plan's own current-state table records the gap (BR-3, exit target 2026-08-28, now passed) but it is the one architectural conclusion there with no finding id, so it is invisible to the sweep, the deadline machinery and any merge gate.
notes: Confirmed 2026-09-05 (external review claim 7). Full BR-3 (versioned Spaces replica + AWS Object Lock WORM vault + version-bound references + the three-state adapter protocol) is the end state and is gated on BR-1 secrets. Smallest architecturally sound step now: an object-storage-replica capability in dr-activation.json (state not-activated, unlockPhase BR-3) with a bucket-versioning/replication probe lane, so every backup/PITR run warns 'PRODUCTION HAS NO object-storage-replica', and the restore-drill stop-line names object-version parity as a required condition — a PostgreSQL-only restore can no longer be read as a platform restore. Claim 6 of the same review (backup activation/restore proof) is already covered by INFRA-HIGH-033/034/035/073 and is an operator-evidence gap, not a code gap; note dr-activation.json cites ORPHAN-HIGH-563 which is prose-only, not a registry id.

title: the tenant localization screen that sets every tenant's feeding-day boundary shipped with no test, and the branch that claimed to cover it tested a component main had already replaced

title: seven federation configs aliased @aquaculture/shared-ui to a build artifact, so a module's vitest run passed or failed on whether web/shared-ui/dist happened to exist

title: the WAL-G signer accepted any run record that merely parsed, so an appended field, a reformat or a duplicated key passed into the signature unchallenged

title: fourteen nullable numeric column reads guarded on truthiness, so a measured zero was reported as no data — a batch that did not grow, a tank filled to the rim, feed that cost nothing

title: nine admin-api audit writes named a literal instead of the operator, so retention-policy changes, security-incident timelines, support tickets and cross-tenant database reads were attributed to an identity no account has

title: three admin analytics reports answered a failed read with a zeroed 200, and two of them cached it, so one transient outage reported zero revenue for the whole TTL

title: the system-performance report invents 45ms response time, 0.1% error rate and 99.9% uptime when nothing measured them, and analytics.service reports the same metrics as 0

title: nothing recorded a finding's closure after its PR merged, so every merge left finding-registry-closure-drift red for whoever opened the next PR

title: every Stripe webhook was discarded: the producer writes internalTenantId into metadata and all five handlers read metadata.tenantId, so no payment, past-due, cancellation or refund ever reached the ledger
rule_violated: A tenant is resolved from the local row that owns the third-party object, never from a field the third party's account holders can write
notes: Confirmed against main before the fix: stripe-api.service.ts:108,134 write internalTenantId; the five handlers read paymentIntent/stripeInvoice/stripeSubscription/charge .metadata?.tenantId and warn-and-return. payment_intent.* additionally required metadata.invoiceId, which nothing writes at all. No service-level spec existed (only stripe-webhook.controller.spec.ts, which mocks the service), which is how it survived. Headline confirmed from claude/superadmin-panel-audit-dm2t1v; the fix is re-derived, not merged.

title: the invoice scheduler billed a longer cycle without the commitment discount the quote applies, so an annual tenant was charged 15% above the agreed price every year
rule_violated: A price rule that has to hold across a service boundary is declared once, above both services, and both sides compute through it
notes: Confirmed on main. pricing-calculator.service.ts:113-123 declares BILLING_CYCLE_DISCOUNTS (5/10/15%) and applies it to the quote; billing-scheduler.service.ts:304 does basePriceMoney.multiply(cycleMonths) with no discount. Second defect in the same column: get-tenant-billing.handler.ts:calculateMonthlyPrice DIVIDED pricing.basePrice by the cycle months while the scheduler MULTIPLIES it and create-subscription publishes it as monthlyPrice on SubscriptionCreated, so an annual tenant on $99/month was reported as $8.25. Third: annualTotal applied the REQUESTED cycle's rate, overstating the annual price by 15% beside a monthly quote. Headline from claude/superadmin-panel-audit-dm2t1v (BILLING-CRITICAL-003 there); re-derived, branch not merged.

title: the months-per-billing-cycle table is declared in nine more places across two services, each a date-arithmetic copy that can drift from the commercial terms
rule_violated: A cycle's length is one fact; a service that keeps its own copy can bill a period the catalogue does not sell
notes: Raised explicitly rather than folded into the CRITICAL. BILLING_CYCLE_MONTHS now exists in backend-common and the two PRICING paths use it; the remaining copies are period-date arithmetic (calculatePeriodEnd, retention windows, analytics buckets) which have never disagreed with the commercial terms. Consolidating them touches six files across two services and is a separate reviewable change, so the single-source invariant deliberately governs only the commitment-discount table until this closes.

title: the plan catalogue states a 10/15/20 percent commitment discount per cycle while the pricing calculator applies 5/10/15, and no pricing path reads the catalogue figure
rule_violated: An operator-facing price the platform does not charge is worse than no price at all
notes: Found while re-reading my own BILLING-CRITICAL-007 fix, and it exposed a gap in that fix's invariant. plan-definition.service.ts:421-484 seeds per-tier pricing.{quarterly,semiAnnual,annual}.discountPercent of 10/15/20, with per-cycle basePrices that agree with those rates (Starter monthly 99: quarterly 267 = 10.1% off 297, annual 950 = 20.0% off 1188). pricing-calculator.service.ts applies 5/10/15. Nothing reads a plan definition's per-cycle discountPercent -- the only discountPercent readers are custom-plan.service.ts / custom-plan.entity.ts, which is a custom plan's own discount, a different concept. Which price book actually bills a given tenant is NOT yet established: plan-definition.service.ts:522 returns pricing.<cycle>.basePrice to some caller and that path was not traced. Resolving this needs a decision on whether commitment terms are per-plan (operator-editable, snapshotted at sale so an edit cannot re-price existing customers) or platform-wide, which is a commercial decision, not a refactor.

title: the closure-reconcile lane refused to finish any run that resolved a CRITICAL, because the debt-plan repin treated a removal from the active set exactly like an addition
rule_violated: A gate that refuses must distinguish the judgement it needs a human for from the arithmetic it was built to do
notes: Observed live: finding-closure-reconcile run #3 on the merge of PR #1461 resolved BILLING-CRITICAL-006 and 007, verified the chain, then refused at gates:debt-plan:repin because active_critical_ids had changed -- which is precisely what resolving a CRITICAL does. No PR was opened, main kept both findings OPEN while carrying their Closes: trailers, and finding-registry-closure-drift went red for the next contributor (PR #1462). This is PROC-MEDIUM-029's tax reappearing on the machinery built to remove it. Fixed by splitting the refusal: an ADDED active CRITICAL still refuses (it needs a human-authored truth-table row); a REMOVED one is recorded mechanically -- manifest id list rewritten from the registry, row lifted out of the active table, entry appended to Resolved Evidence with the closing commit and the bucket it left.

title: operator-provisioned tenants had no Stripe objects at all: the provisioning INSERT omitted stripe_customer_id and stripe_subscription_id from its column list, so nothing ever charged them
rule_violated: Two paths that create the same aggregate mint its external identifiers through one writer, or one of them will forget
notes: Confirmed on main before the fix. billing-admin-nats.handler.ts:669 raw-INSERTs into billing.subscriptions with a column list that omits stripe_customer_id and stripe_subscription_id entirely; the three UPDATEs in the same handler (373, 418, 457) touch status/cancellation/trial only; and the sole writer of those columns anywhere in billing-service is create-subscription.handler.ts:85-102, the GraphQL path the operator flow does not use. So the columns stayed NULL permanently. Compounding: two of the five Stripe webhook handlers fixed in BILLING-CRITICAL-006 resolve the tenant from Subscription.stripeSubscriptionId, so invoice.payment_failed and customer.subscription.deleted stay inert for these tenants -- not a regression, since Stripe cannot emit events for a subscription it never had, but it bounds that fix's reach. Headline from claude/superadmin-panel-audit-dm2t1v (e27b0fa1c); re-derived, branch not merged.

title: two SUPER_ADMIN endpoints read and terminated sessions in admin.user_sessions, a table nothing ever wrote to, so the read always said "no sessions" and the terminate always said "0 terminated" while every real session stayed live
rule_violated: A security control that reports success while doing nothing is worse than one that is absent, because the operator stops looking
notes: Confirmed on main before the fix. admin.user_sessions (security.entity.ts:990) had exactly one INSERT in the platform -- ActivityLoggingService.createSession (activity-logging.service.ts:516) -- and that method had no callers; neither did updateSessionActivity (:546) nor terminateSession (:562). The table was therefore empty for its whole life. Two SUPER_ADMIN-gated REST endpoints on the documented Swagger surface read it: GET /security/activities/sessions/user/:userId returned [] always, and POST /security/activities/sessions/user/:userId/terminate returned { terminated: 0 } always while revoking nothing. An hourly @Cron (cleanupExpiredSessions, :884) swept the empty table. SecurityMonitoringService.checkSessionHijacking (:582) queried the same table and returned false at its first lookup -- but it had ZERO callers, so it was dead code, not a live control silently disabled; stating otherwise would overclaim. Not CRITICAL: no operator UI reaches the dead endpoints. The admin panel's real path works and was untouched -- UserManagementPage.tsx:235 -> PATCH /users/:id/force-logout -> users.service.ts:631 -> NATS AUTH_ADMIN_COMMAND_SUBJECTS.FORCE_LOGOUT_USER -> auth-service adminForceLogout, which revokes auth.refresh_tokens and the Redis sessions; and GET /users/:id/sessions reads auth.refresh_tokens. The dead pair was a second implementation of both against a store nobody filled. Fixed by deleting the duplicate rather than by giving it a writer: session state is auth-service's, the same rule already applied to auth.users where admin-api's raw-SQL INSERT was replaced by a NATS delegation. Removing the endpoints turns a silent lie into a loud 404 with a working replacement one route away. Also removed: the concurrentSessionLimit / sessionHijackingDetection config pair, dead knobs duplicating a limit auth actually enforces in SessionManagerService.enforceSessionLimit.

title: session-hijacking detection does not exist: the only implementation read a table with no writer and had no callers, and was deleted with that table rather than left as a stub that looks like a control
rule_violated: A capability the codebase names but never runs is a claim, not a control; either wire it to the real store or record that it does not exist
notes: Raised explicitly rather than folded into ADMIN-HIGH-100, because that fix DELETES the stub and a deletion with no record would let the gap disappear quietly. SecurityMonitoringService.checkSessionHijacking compared a stored session IP against the request IP and raised a critical security event on a change -- correct in shape, but it read admin.user_sessions, which nothing ever wrote, and it had zero callers, so it could never fire. Deleting it removes nothing that worked. What the platform actually needs: mid-session IP/device-change detection against the store that holds real sessions -- SessionManagerService (Redis), written by token.service.ts:409 on login and already carrying SessionMetadata -- invoked from the authenticated request path rather than from an admin service that sees no traffic. Alternatively record the decision not to have this control; the gap is that neither has happened. The concurrentSessionLimit knob removed alongside it is not this finding: that limit IS enforced, in SessionManagerService.enforceSessionLimit, and the admin copy was a dead duplicate of a working control.

title: Audit actor identity is client-supplied, hardcoded or null: DTO properties such as performedBy/createdBy/invitedBy carry the actor, 273 admin mutation routes have no @AuditedOperation, and the admin audit writer swallows failures so a forged or missing actor is never rejected
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Review Finding Traceability; SOC 2 CC4; audit-log mandatory shape
notes: Fix: actor is never a DTO property (property-name ban enforced structurally), taken from @CurrentUser only; adopt the existing awaited transaction-aware AuditedOperationInterceptor across admin-api; audit.service.log becomes logOrThrow by default; delete or lock the audit-forgery endpoint. Gate: tests/invariants/admin-mutation-audit-coverage.spec.ts enumerating mutation routes via reflected metadata with a ratcheting allowlist; add admin-api to SERVICES_REQUIRED in audited-operation-module-wired.spec.ts.

title: tenantId is a transport value, never a verified identity: ~20 admin call sites attach an unvalidated tenant id to money, messages, config, exports and destructive operations; erasure targets are derived by column sniffing so tenant erasure is structurally impossible
rule_violated: ADR-013 tenant isolation; CLAUDE.md Tenant-ID sourcing; GDPR Art 17
notes: Fix: @TenantParam() resolves the id to a verified ACTIVE auth.tenants row before it can reach any handler (one resolution point); erasure becomes an explicit per-table registry entry (tenant-column | cascade-via | excluded-with-reason). Gate: every table in MODULE_SCHEMAS[].tables is classified in the erasure registry; e2e erases a tenant holding threads, invoices and audit rows. Depends on class DTOs (R9 precondition).

title: Email template preview renders operator-editable HTML in an iframe via srcDoc with no sandbox attribute, so a stored template is a same-origin XSS path to the SUPER_ADMIN token
rule_violated: OWASP A03 injection; CSP discipline (gateway-api CSP)
notes: Fix: a single SandboxedPreview component in shared-ui that structurally sets sandbox (no allow-same-origin, no allow-scripts) and is the only permitted way to render untrusted HTML; ESLint rule banning raw srcDoc/dangerouslySetInnerHTML in web/**; CSP frame-src/sandbox directives. Gate: the lint rule plus a component test asserting the sandbox attribute cannot be omitted.

title: No shared admin-panel query/mutation primitive: ~60 handlers hand-roll try/catch/close/refetch, useAsyncData is cache-first so writes read back stale, the existing useAdminQuery/useAdminMutation/adminQueryKeys are adopted by zero pages, and 34 pages compute pagination, sort and stat cards from a loaded slice
rule_violated: ADR-009 frontend data-fetch pattern; ADR-010 admin-panel styling and data discipline
notes: Fix: migrate every page onto useAdminQuery/useAdminMutation and delete useAsyncData; one AdminTable contract owning server-side pagination, sort (bound to backend allowlists), search and dataset-scoped aggregates. Gate: ESLint rule banning useState+useEffect fetching and bare apiFetch under pages/**, AST rule banning aggregates computed from a fetched array, no-console re-enabled with a shrinking allowlist, bundlesize budget.

title: Retired backend stores were left as registered 410/409/501 stubs (tenant configuration, provisioning settings, messaging personas) so live pages call routes that can never succeed, and parameterised routes registered before literal siblings shadow /scheduled and /failed
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Architectural Approach (retirement is two-sided); NestJS route registration order
notes: Fix: retirement deletes route + client in the same commit as the store; route-registration linter sorts static segments before parameterised ones. Gate: no controller method body reduces to a thrown Gone/Conflict/NotImplemented exception; smoke gate that every FE-called route returns something other than 404/410/501 on a booted app.

title: admin schema physical types are permissive: naive timestamps on 82 decorators, varchar tenantId, money in jsonb, simple-array stored as text, no CHECK on money/enum/state columns, IP addresses as unbounded varchar, and no soft-delete on operator-facing rows
rule_violated: ADR-011 schema ownership; ADR-012 schema drift; layer-1 TypeORM discipline
notes: Fix: one forward migration per class (timestamptz AT TIME ZONE 'UTC', uuid tenantId, numeric money, real arrays, inet) landed together with {type:'timestamptz'} on every decorator; SCHEMA_DRIFT_FATAL in production. Gate: invariant that no admin column is timestamp without time zone; decorator lint banning bare @CreateDateColumn()/@UpdateDateColumn(); CHECK presence invariant for money/enum/state columns.

title: Admin crons run without leader election, heartbeat or lease: ~40 @Cron/@Interval jobs execute on every replica, the impersonation expiry tick throws every minute at the DB trigger, disposal runs unbatched DELETEs, and job claiming has no FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
rule_violated: CronHeartbeat contract; CLAUDE.md Layer Rules
notes: Fix: @LeaderOnly()/pg_try_advisory_lock primitive in backend-common placed beside CronHeartbeatService so adopting one forces the other; job claiming via FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED mirroring the provisioning-run lease; shared batched-delete helper. Gate: invariant that every @Cron/@Interval in the fleet is leader-wrapped and heartbeated; CronJobNeverRan / CronJobFailingEveryRun alert rules are the runtime half.

title: Detective and monitoring stores have no producer: login_attempts, user_sessions, api_usage_logs, performance_metrics and performance_snapshots are read by dashboards and detectors that nothing writes, so the security health score is 100/100 by construction
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Architectural Approach (no false security claims); SOC 2 CC7 monitoring
notes: Fix per store: outbox-backed projection from auth-service LoginAttempted/SessionCreated events, or delete the store together with its detector and dashboard. No middle state. Gate: invariant that every entity registered in MODULE_SCHEMAS[].tables has at least one save/insert/upsert reference in the owning service.

title: Two plan catalogues: admin.plan_definitions (money as IEEE-754 floats in jsonb, Stripe ids with zero readers, plan ids that never resolve at execution) shadows billing.plans which every runtime path reads; admin.module_pricing, custom_plans and discount_codes carry the same defect class
rule_violated: ADR-037 plan limit SSoT; CLAUDE.md D14 billing is the SSoT for subscription state
notes: Arbiter R7 (reverses the apps/billing-service/CLAUDE.md ownership clause): billing.plans is the sole catalogue of record; delete the four admin tables and migrate their data into billing with numeric(12,2) + CHECK columns; admin keeps authoring, forwards commands. Gate: tests/invariants/plan-catalog-ssot.spec.ts — no money-typed field inside jsonb fleet-wide, stripe ids in exactly one entity. ADR-0013.

title: Admin billing bypasses the command model: raw UPDATE/INSERT against billing.subscriptions with no Stripe object, no outbox, no audit; Stripe metadata key asymmetry (producer writes internalTenantId, all five webhook consumers read tenantId) leaves the reconciliation loop dead; BillingAdminCommandMeta has no idempotencyKey so retried refunds mint new Stripe keys
rule_violated: ADR-007 CQRS; ADR-016 Stripe SDK adoption; SECREV-CRITICAL-001 customer lookup
notes: Arbiter R8: provisioning via CreateSubscriptionHandler (FREE is the only non-Stripe tier); delete the three raw-SQL blocks in favour of Cancel/Reactivate/ExtendTrial handlers; fix the CONSUMERS to read internalTenantId through a shared constant (producer rename rejected: it would orphan every existing Stripe object) plus a real customer-lookup fallback; BillingAdminCommandMeta gains required idempotencyKey + correlationId with receipts on all eight commands; seed billing.plans for every cycle. Gate: tests/invariants/billing-command-contract-ssot.spec.ts incl. metadata-key symmetry. ADR-0014. Depends on R7.

title: Root CLAUDE.md Migration Runners section describes apps/<svc>/src/database/migrations + createMigrationRunnerService, which matches no service; claude-md-accuracy.spec.ts skips placeholder paths so the drift is invisible to the gate
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md is Tier 4; claude-md-accuracy invariant
notes: Arbiter ARCH-LOW-012: shrink the Tier-4 text to a pointer at libs/backend-common/src/database/typeorm-config.factory.ts + apps/db-migrate and extend claude-md-accuracy.spec.ts to resolve <svc> against the real service list instead of skipping it.

title: No machine-readable FE-BE contract for the admin surface: 29 interface-typed @Body() parameters make ValidationPipe structurally inert and Swagger schemas empty; hand-written types in web/modules/admin-panel/src/services/types drift on fields, enums, nullability and the paginated envelope (two flattening heuristics); the URL-shape gate suppresses 50 endpoints via KNOWN_EXCEPTIONS with no owner
rule_violated: ADR-009 frontend data-fetch pattern; CLAUDE.md Security (ValidationPipe whitelist/forbidNonWhitelisted)
notes: Arbiter R9: class DTOs are the hard precondition (re-arms ValidationPipe across billing/modules/settings/support/messaging in one change); OpenAPI emitted from Nest DTOs via the existing SwaggerModule.createDocument into a committed apps/admin-api-service/openapi.json; openapi-typescript into src/services/generated/; delete services/types/*, contract-validation.spec.ts and KNOWN_EXCEPTIONS; one Paginated<T> and the seven enums in libs/event-contracts; AuditLogInput.action becomes AuditAction. title: Operator tenant provisioning still raw-INSERTs billing.subscriptions, and no admin billing command is idempotent: main's BILLING-CRITICAL-010 fix minted the Stripe objects but left the write path and the retry semantics untouched
rule_violated: ADR-0014: billing.subscriptions has one writer and every admin billing command carries an idempotencyKey + correlationId and executes at most once. A raw INSERT beside the CQRS handlers tells Stripe nothing, writes no outbox event, projects nothing onto auth.tenants and validates no state transition under a lock.
notes: Split out of W4 at land time. main closed BILLING-CRITICAL-010 independently (63619406e) with StripeSubscriptionProvisionerService, which fills stripe_customer_id / stripe_subscription_id but leaves the raw INSERT in provisionTenantSubscription. The audit branch closed the same finding with SubscriptionWriterService.createWithin, which REPLACES the INSERT, and built at-most-once command receipts (BillingCommandReceiptService + BillingCommandReceiptInterceptor + billing.command_receipts) on top of it. The receipt work is unbuilt on main: no command carries an idempotencyKey, so every NATS retry of a refund, an invoice or a plan change executes again. Porting it is not a cherry-pick — the writer has to be extracted against main's provisioner, and create-subscription.handler uses the repository rather than raw SQL, so 'both paths use it' needs designing rather than transplanting. The audit branch's implementation is on claude/superadmin-panel-audit-dm2t1v at c7f82ec77, with its gate (tests/invariants/billing-command-contract-ssot.spec.ts) already written and already correctly failing against main's tree.

title: the ScadaPackageService test module was wired eight times across six spec files, so a new constructor dependency had to be learned by each copy separately
rule_violated: Test wiring that exists only to satisfy a constructor is wiring that will be forgotten when the constructor changes, and the copy that forgets fails at DI resolution instead of at the behaviour under test
notes: Recovered from PR #1022's SENSOR-MEDIUM-058, one of nine IDs the 2026-09-04 integration review listed as colliding with IDs main had since given to unrelated findings. That review said the nine branch rows were preserved at scratchpad/r1022/branch-findings.jsonl; that path was never committed, so none of the nine had a registry entry, an owner or a deadline. All nine were re-verified against main on 2026-09-08 and this is the ONLY one with a live residual. CORRECTION to the branch's wording: it claimed the test modules 'omit the required lifecycle event emitter'. That half is FALSE on main -- every one of the modules provides EventEmitter2. What is true is the duplication, and it was larger than the branch recorded: eight Test.createTestingModule blocks across six spec files, not five across three. The three extra copies (deploy-archived-guard, deploy-edge-widget-boundary, pin-control-security) were found by the invariant written for this fix, not by reading. No spec asserted on the emitter -- it was pure boilerplate present because the constructor requires it. Fixed by extracting createScadaPackageHarness() and pinning single-source with tests/invariants/scada-package-harness-single-source.spec.ts. Left OPEN with a deadline rather than closed on the same commit only if the fix does not land; it closes with the commit that carries this ID.

title: the admin messaging list showed zero unread on every thread and never showed one as closed, because the page re-derived both from GraphQL field names the REST endpoint does not send
rule_violated: A response shape that the generated contract cannot describe is a shape the client will hand-declare, and a hand-declared shape drifts silently
notes: Confirmed end to end on main before the fix. GET /support/messages/threads returns MessagingService.getAllThreads's PROJECTION -- { id, tenantId, tenantName, subject, lastMessage, lastMessageAt, unreadCount, messageCount, isClosed } -- built at messaging.service.ts:154-168, where unreadCount is the row's unreadAdminCount and tenantName comes out of thread metadata. The client typed that response as MessageThread, which is the GraphQL support-thread shape (status, unreadCountAdmin, unreadCountTenant) consumed by useMessaging. apiFetch performs no transformation, so MessagingPage.tsx:87-94 spread the correct payload and then overwrote it: unreadCount: thread.unreadCountAdmin || 0 -> undefined || 0 -> 0, and isClosed: thread.status === 'closed' -> undefined === 'closed' -> false. Both correct values were already on the object from the spread. Operator effect: a tenant sends a support message, the thread's unread badge stays 0 (MessagingPage.tsx:399-401 renders it only when > 0), so nothing signals that a reply is owed. ROOT CAUSE, one layer down: ThreadSummary was an INTERFACE (support.entity.ts:523). The @nestjs/swagger plugin emits schemas for classes only, so the projection never reached openapi.json and the admin panel had no contract shape to source -- it reached for the nearest same-named type instead. Fixed at that layer: the projection is now the ThreadSummaryDto class, the controller declares Promise<PaginationResultV1<ThreadSummaryDto>>, and @ApiExtraModels registers it because the plugin resolves the generic to the envelope and stops. The frontend type is now ApiSchema<'ThreadSummaryDto'>, so a backend rename is a compile error rather than a silent zero. Verified by admin-openapi-artifact-parity.spec.ts, which regenerates both the artifact and the client and compares bytes.

title: 26 admin-panel types hand-declare a shape the generated contract already describes, and 16 of them disagree with it field-for-field
rule_violated: A contract nobody is required to source from is documentation, not a contract
notes: The systemic form of ADMIN-HIGH-110, raised separately because that fix repairs one shape and this needs a decision per shape. services/contract.ts already states the rule -- "Use ApiSchema<'CreateTenantDto'> rather than re-declaring a shape by hand" -- and 51 types follow it (billing 46, tenant 4, users 1). 142 are still hand-declared, which is mostly legitimate: view models, page state, enums, and DTOs the backend does not expose. The actionable subset is the 26 whose NAME matches a contract schema: audit.ts AuditLog; billing.ts ModuleQuantities, ModuleSelection, TierMultipliers; database.ts TenantSchema, SchemaMigration; reports.ts ReportDefinition, ReportExecution; settings.ts EmailTemplateVariable, FeatureToggle, ErrorGroup, ErrorOccurrence, BackgroundJob, JobQueue; support.ts SupportTicket, TicketComment, MessageThread, Announcement, Message; tenant.ts TenantLimits, TenantSettings, TenantContact, Tenant, TenantStats, TenantNote, TenantProvisioningStep. A field-set comparison shows 16 of them disagree with their counterpart. Some are severe: database.ts SchemaMigration declares name/sql/error where the contract has migrationName/downScript/errorMessage, and tenant.ts Tenant declares tier/limits/farmCount/sensorCount where the contract has plan/maxUsers/subscriptionEndsAt. Others are benign: a client view model that legitimately adds a derived field, or a payload the endpoint really does narrow. NOT resolvable by mechanically aliasing all 26 -- each needs the same check ADMIN-HIGH-110 got (which endpoint actually returns it, and is the contract shape the response shape), and MessageThread specifically must stay hand-declared because it is the GraphQL thread, not a REST DTO. NO GATE SHIPPED ON PURPOSE: a shadowing rule today would need a 26-entry allowlist, which is longer than the enforcement and would read as compliance rather than provide it. The gate lands with the last conversion.

title: platform MRR divides a monthly rate by the cycle's months, so every non-monthly tenant is under-counted by exactly its cycle length
rule_violated: A revenue figure an operator makes decisions on must mean what its label says
notes: AnalyticsService.calculateMonthlyPrice returned basePrice/3, /6, /12 for quarterly, semi-annual and annual subscriptions. billing.subscriptions.pricing.basePrice IS the monthly rate -- CreateSubscriptionHandler publishes it as monthlyPrice on SubscriptionCreated and BillingSchedulerService MULTIPLIES it by the cycle months to price a period -- so the division under-counted an annual tenant on $49/month as $4.08 in both mrr and revenueByPlan. Identical to the defect BILLING-CRITICAL-007 fixed in billing-service's GetTenantBillingHandler, which documents the same reasoning at the callsite; it survived in admin-api because that service reads the same column through its own read-only projection and carried its own cycle-months switch to divide by. Found while consolidating BILLING-HIGH-008: the copy was only visible once every cycle-months restatement was enumerated, which is the argument for the consolidation itself. Fixed in the same change.

title: updateHarvestRecord edits quantityHarvested/totalBiomass/averageWeight but moves no stock: batch aggregates, tank composition, tank biomass, the tank_operations mirror and the farm-stock projection all keep the original harvest's numbers
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Layer Rules 6 (single writer); FARM-HIGH-104 single-count-writer discipline (TankBatchService.applyBatchDelta)
notes: Surfaced while implementing FARM-HIGH-198. The handler imports no Batch/Tank/TankBatch/TankBatchService/FarmStockProjectionService — it saves the record and enqueues the event, nothing else. Reachable by TENANT_ADMIN/MODULE_MANAGER on the GraphQL wire. Fix is tier 1 removal of the three quantity fields from UPDATABLE_FIELDS and from UpdateHarvestRecordInput (corrections go through cancel + re-create, whose reversal and forward paths are already correct and tested), not a third stock-write path. No hand-written client selects the fields; only generated types under web/ reference them. BREAKING CHANGE on the SDL.

title: the audit log severity filter offers Low/Medium/High, three values the column has never held, so filtering for high-severity events returns an empty list
rule_violated: A filter that silently matches nothing tells an auditor there are no such events
notes: AuditSeverity (apps/admin-api-service/src/audit/audit.entity.ts:55) is info|warning|critical. The admin panel hand-declared AuditLog.severity as low|medium|high|critical and its SEVERITY_LEVELS dropdown offers Low, Medium, High, Critical. Three of the four filter values match no row that can exist, so an auditor filtering for High sees an empty list and reads it as 'no high-severity events'. getSeverityBadgeVariant maps low/medium/high/critical, so real info and warning rows both miss the map and fall through || 'default' to render grey -- a warning-severity audit entry is visually identical to a routine one. Only critical works, by coincidence of appearing in both vocabularies. The same hand-written type also declares `metadata`, where the column is `details` (audit.entity.ts:124), so the detail drawer's Metadata block never renders. Root cause is ADMIN-MEDIUM-111's: a hand-declared frontend type shadowing a contract schema, undetectable because the hand copy also carried an index signature that swallowed the mismatch.

title: saving a feature-toggle edit sends two fields the update DTO forbids, so every edit is rejected with 400
rule_violated: A request typed from the response shape is not a request contract
notes: FeatureTogglesPage.handleUpdate PUTs { name, description, scope, category, rolloutPercentage, isExperimental }. UpdateFeatureToggleDto declares none of scope or isExperimental -- scope is fixed at creation by design, and the platform ValidationPipe runs forbidNonWhitelisted: true (create-service-app.ts:467), so the request is rejected 400 and the toggle is never updated. The client could not see it because settings.ts typed the call as Partial<FeatureToggle> -- the RESPONSE type -- rather than the request DTO the endpoint validates, and typed create as Omit<FeatureToggle, 'id'|'createdAt'|'updatedAt'> while a real CreateFeatureToggleDto exists. Same root cause as ADMIN-MEDIUM-111: a hand-derived type standing in for a contract schema. Found while sourcing FeatureToggle from the contract; the scope union was also missing 'environment', so an environment-scoped toggle rendered with the fallback badge and its edit form offered no matching option.

title: the ticket-comments endpoint has no declared return type, so the contract requires a `ticket` relation the response never carries
rule_violated: A contract that overstates a response is as unusable as one that understates it
notes: TicketController.getComments (ticket.controller.ts:250) declares no return type, so the swagger plugin resolved it through TicketService.getComments to PaginationResultV1<TicketComment> and emitted the ENTITY: the contract's TicketComment requires `ticket: SupportTicket`. TicketService.getComments calls findAndCount with no `relations`, so no ticket is ever loaded and that property is never in the response. This is the inverse of the rest of ADMIN-MEDIUM-111 -- the contract overstates rather than understates -- so support.ts's TicketComment is deliberately left hand-written rather than aliased to a schema that would demand a field the API does not send. Closing it means an explicit TicketCommentDto on the endpoint, which is a response-shape change with its own review. Two adjacent items to fold in when it is done: getTicketComments in api/support.ts declares a FOURTH inline copy of the shape, and TicketsPage.fetchComments hand-remaps it field by field with `as string` casts plus fileName||filename and fileSize||size fallbacks -- all of which the typed response removes.

title: only notification-service binds a durable dead-letter sink, so farm and alert dead-letters exist only as log lines while the code beside term() claims the envelope is durably stored
rule_violated: A comment that states a guarantee the wiring does not provide is worse than no comment
notes: NatsEventBus falls back to LoggingDeadLetterSink when no EVENT_DEAD_LETTER_SINK is bound, so a dead-letter is never silent: a structured event_bus_dead_letter line carrying eventId, tenantId, disposition, reason and deliveryCount, plus deliveryMetrics.observeDeadLetter and the NATS MSG_TERMINATED advisory. What is missing is a durable, QUERYABLE record. Only notification-service binds a sink (NotificationLogDeadLetterSink -> NotificationLog with status DEAD_LETTER, PII-redacted, which the admin panel already reads). farm-service and alert-engine bind none, so recovering a terminated message there means log scraping. The comment beside msg.term() in nats-event-bus.ts:1467 reads 'The envelope is durably stored, so redelivery must stop' -- true only for a service that bound a sink, and stated unconditionally. Found while verifying PR #1031's content against main: the PR carried per-service event_dlq tables for farm, alert and notification. Main superseded the notification one with a better design (reuse the row the panel already queries) but the farm and alert ones did not land and nothing replaced them. Either bind a durable sink in both services or narrow the comment to what the wiring guarantees; the comment is the part that is wrong today.

title: the GDPR data-request status filter offers two values the API cannot return and omits the one it can, so an operator filtering by them sees an empty list
rule_violated: A filter that silently matches nothing tells a compliance officer there are no such requests
notes: CompliancePage declares its own DataRequestStatus as pending|in_progress|identity_verification|processing|completed|rejected. The contract's DataRequest.status is pending|in_progress|completed|rejected|expired, and services/types/security.ts matches it. The page's status dropdown offers Identity Verification and Processing, and statusFilter is sent to the API (line 613 -> apiParams.status) AND applied client-side (line 715), so selecting either yields an empty list from both paths -- a compliance officer reads that as 'no requests in that state'. The reverse gap: expired is a status the API CAN return, and the page has it in neither the dropdown nor getStatusColor's cases, so an expired request cannot be filtered for and renders grey through the default branch, indistinguishable from pending. The erasure<->deletion translation at lines 138 and 177 is DELIBERATE and correct -- the UI presents GDPR's own vocabulary -- and is not this finding; `objection` in the type union is unreachable from the UI and is dead rather than wrong. Root cause is ADMIN-MEDIUM-111's one level out: the page re-declares a union services/types already owns, and the shadowing gate shipped with ADMIN-MEDIUM-111 scans only services/types/*.ts.

title: 106 recursive fixture-tree teardowns across the gate suites pass no maxRetries, so any of them can redden an unrelated PR with ENOTEMPTY
rule_violated: A gate that fails on someone else's diff teaches the team to re-run it, which is how a real failure gets waved through
notes: invariants-fast went red on PR #1491 (admin-panel TypeScript + one Markdown file) with ENOTEMPTY: directory not empty, rmdir '/tmp/aqua-runtime-bundle-repo-2kLgwL/.git' raised from backup-restore-verification-contract.spec.ts:424 -- the spec's own finally block. All assertions passed; only teardown failed. Recursive removal is not atomic: Node walks readdir+unlink then rmdir, so any entry appearing in that window surfaces as ENOTEMPTY. Two writers open it. (1) git commit ends by running `git maintenance run --auto --quiet` -- confirmed under GIT_TRACE=1 on git 2.43 -- and gc.autoDetach defaults true, so the gc task daemonises and keeps writing under .git after spawnSync returned. That is why the failure landed on .git and nothing else. (2) CI runners use overlayfs, where deletion writes a whiteout and rmdir can transiently see a directory as non-empty. force:true does NOT cover this -- it suppresses ENOENT only. maxRetries is the option Node documents for exactly EBUSY/EMFILE/ENFILE/ENOTEMPTY/EPERM, and is ignored unless recursive is set. Measured: 87 recursive removals in tests/invariants and 19 in tools/gates, 106 total, zero passing maxRetries. Fixed at three tiers: the fixture git env now sets gc.auto=0 and maintenance.auto=false via GIT_CONFIG_COUNT so the background writer does not exist (verified -- GIT_TRACE shows no maintenance invocation); tools/gates/fixture-tree.ts owns removeFixtureTree/removeExistingFixtureTree with the retry budget and all 106 callsites route through it; fixture-tree-removal-ssot.spec.ts fails on any recursive rm outside the owner and on the owner losing its retry budget. Both negative controls verified. Full invariants suite 290/293 -- the 3 production-host failures reproduce identically with the change stashed and are pre-existing local-env failures that pass in CI.

title: eleven of the twelve specs that build fixture git repos inherit the invoking user's global git config, so they fail on developer machines CI cannot reproduce
rule_violated: A fixture whose result depends on ambient host configuration is not a fixture
notes: Twelve files run git commit inside a throwaway repo. Exactly one -- backup-restore-verification-contract.spec.ts -- builds a hermetic environment (GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null, pinned HOME and LC_ALL). The other eleven are markdownlint-event-range, production-host-control-plane-runtime, production-host-ssh-payload, production-host-runtime-bundle, affected-development-pipeline, tools/gates/banned-phrase.ts, git-reachability.spec.ts, aria-authority-hash.spec.ts, finding-registry-store.spec.ts, finding-traceability.spec.ts and commit-msg-validator.ts. A developer with commit.gpgsign=true, a commit.template, a core.hooksPath or a non-C locale gets failures the runner cannot reproduce; the reverse also holds, since a config-dependent bug stays invisible where the config is empty. The git auto-maintenance detach that INFRA-HIGH-172 closes in the one hermetic fixture is still open in these eleven. Deliberately NOT folded into INFRA-HIGH-172: that is a teardown race, this is config bleed, and closing it means one shared hermetic runFixtureGit adopted across eleven files with eleven different invocation shapes.

title: the analytics time-series response types are interfaces, so the whole contract is absent from openapi.json and the dashboard page must hand-declare it
rule_violated: A response shape the contract cannot describe is a shape the frontend is forced to guess
notes: Surfaced while closing PR #1035. That PR's premise -- 'admin-api bootstraps no SwaggerModule' -- is false on today's main (generate-openapi.ts calls SwaggerModule.createDocument, openapi is an Nx target, openapi.json and the generated panel client are both committed). Its concrete bug example was re-checked and REFUTED: it reported AnalyticsDashboardPage declaring value:number against a backend number|null, but both sides declare value:number on main today, so the zero-plotting bug it described does not exist. What IS live: TimeSeriesPoint, TimeSeriesData and TimeSeriesResponse are declared as `interface` in analytics-snapshot.entity.ts, and the @nestjs/swagger plugin emits schemas for CLASSES ONLY, so all three are absent from openapi.json (225 schemas, none of them). They sit on a live response path -- analytics.controller.ts:135 returns toTimeSeriesResponse(...) -- so the analytics time-series contract crosses the wire with no generated counterpart and the page has nothing to source from. The two declarations agree only by coincidence. Unlike ADMIN-MEDIUM-111 and ADMIN-HIGH-115, their gate cannot catch this: the type is not contract-derived because there is nothing to derive from. Fifth occurrence of this root cause after ADMIN-HIGH-110, 112, 113 and the tenant detail pair. Fix is to convert the three interfaces to classes with @ApiProperty, regenerate both artifacts, and point the page at ApiSchema<'TimeSeriesResponse'> -- after which the ADMIN-HIGH-115 gate covers it automatically.

title: Every @SubscribeTo method-level subscriber dead-letters every message on its first delivery: the methods return void against a Promise<HandlerOutcome> contract, and the registrar binds them through an untyped Function so nothing catches it
rule_violated: PLAT-HIGH-902: a handler reports its delivery outcome as a VALUE. foldHandlerOutcomes treats a non-HandlerOutcome return as a contract violation and terminates the message. The class-level path is compiler-checked because a handler implements IEventHandler; the method-level path is not, because the registrar casts through `Function`.
notes: Found landing W5. The two registration paths converge on one registry: subscribeTo pushes the handler into this.handlers, and every delivery does `outcomes.push(await handler.handle(event))` then folds. HandlerOutcome.is(undefined) is false, so the fold yields terminate with 'handler returned no HandlerOutcome (contract violation)' — a dead-letter on delivery 1, with no retry. Every @SubscribeTo method in the repository returns Promise<void>, including admin-api's TenantOnboardingAck / TenantOnboardingFailed subscribers, so the tenant-provisioning acknowledgement path is dead-lettering. It compiles on main only because nats.module.ts binds via `(instance[methodKey] as Function).bind(instance)`, whose `any` return satisfies the IEventHandler shape structurally. Typing that bind is what surfaced it. Same class as CONTRACT-MEDIUM-005, one layer down.

title: Actor columns hold either a user uuid or a service name in one varchar, so no type can constrain them: performedBy takes 'admin-api-service' and createdBy takes 'system' alongside real user ids
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Architectural Approach tier 1 (make it impossible) — a column whose domain is a union needs a type that says so
notes: Split out of ADMIN-HIGH-012 during W6. The uuid conversion covered 14 tenantId/userId/assignedTo/resolvedBy columns and deliberately stopped at the actor family (audit_logs.performedBy, tenant_activities.performedBy, security_incidents.createdBy, plus the createdBy/updatedBy config columns). Both non-uuid writers are CORRECT: an audit actor may be a service, and a detector-raised incident has no human author. So this is not a uuid problem, it is a missing sum type - an actor is {kind: 'user' | 'service', id}. Forcing the column to uuid would mean minting a fake uuid for 'system', replacing an honest string with a dishonest identifier, and converting one member of the family while leaving its twin would be worse. Fix: an `actor_kind` enum column beside the id (or a composite domain type), a CHECK that binds kind to the id's shape, and one helper that writes the pair so no callsite decides for itself. Carried in tests/invariants/admin-physical-types.spec.ts ACTOR_COLUMNS, which fails when an entry names a column that no longer exists.

title: The billing read-only mirrors widen money through parseFloat: InvoiceReadOnly's four numeric(12,2) columns use DecimalTransformer, so every amount admin reads from billing.invoices arrives as an IEEE-754 double before anything sums it

40 admin-panel pages reach the network outside the data layer: each imports an admin API client directly, so a write cannot invalidate the reads it affected and the results land in a second cache instead of the shell's QueryClient
rule_violated: web/CLAUDE.md Data fetch: the cross-module pattern is TanStack Query; ADR-009's useAsyncData is admin-panel-scoped legacy
notes: Split out of ADMIN-HIGH-105 when W8a closed that finding's stated subject — the missing shared primitive. The primitive now exists, fits the REST transport its 44 pages actually use, is exported from hooks/index.ts, and is gated. ADOPTION is a separate, larger piece of work and gets its own id rather than holding the primitive's finding open indefinitely. Governed by .claude/allowlists/admin-panel-unmigrated-reads.yaml, whose ceiling only decreases; the file is deleted at 0 and this finding resolves with it. Gate: tests/invariants/admin-panel-data-layer.spec.ts fails both on an unlisted unmigrated page and on a listed page that has already migrated, so the number cannot be padded and cannot go stale.

title: The GDPR compliance page displayed four fabricated zeros: pending, in-progress, completed and OVERDUE data-subject request counts were hardcoded 0 in the frontend because /security/compliance/data-requests returns only a page of rows and a total
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Working Style: report faithfully — a constant rendered as a measurement is a false statement about regulated state
notes: Found while migrating CompliancePage to the data layer in W8d. `fetchDataRequests` built a ComplianceStats whose only real field was totalRequests; the other four were literal 0. On this page that is the platform telling an operator there are no OVERDUE GDPR data-subject requests, which is a regulated claim it has no basis for. W8d stops the lie — the fields are `number | null` and the cards render an em dash — but the aggregate itself is missing and needs a server-side GROUP BY over admin data-subject requests, plus the resolution-time average. Belongs to W9 (real backends behind the fake surfaces).

title: The performance dashboard reported perfect health from no measurements and ran every time range against the same hour: the page read currentSnapshot.overallHealthScore ?? 100, calculateHealthScore returned 100 minus alert deductions with no snapshot to score, and the five-entry range selector sent start/end to an endpoint whose parameters are startDate/endDate
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Working Style: report faithfully — a default rendered as a measurement, and a control that changes nothing, are both false statements about platform state
notes: Found while migrating PerformanceDashboardPage to the data layer in W8f, and fixed in the same commit. Three claims made without evidence: (1) the health score defaulted to 100 in BOTH layers, so a platform with no snapshot reported perfect health — calculateHealthScore now returns number | null and takes the metrics it scores rather than a persisted row, which also fixes createPerformanceSnapshot storing a score computed from no measurements; (2) the time-range selector sent start/end, which the server ignores, so all five options returned the default last hour — the query object is now typed through ApiQuery<> from the generated contract, making the drift a compile error; (3) statfs failure, an unprobed fleet and the absent Kubernetes API all reported 0 — diskUsage, diskTotal, networkLatency, containerCount, healthyContainers and podRestarts are number | null, and containerCount counts endpoints PROBED so an unreachable fleet reads 0 of 10 rather than 0 of 0.

title: The SUPER_ADMIN landing page reported zero tenants, zero users and zero API calls when its reads failed: AdminDashboard mapped every Promise.allSettled rejection to a zero-filled platform object, and its only setError call sat in a catch allSettled can never reach
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Working Style: report faithfully — a fallback constant rendered as a measurement is a false statement about platform state
notes: Found while migrating AdminDashboard to the data layer in W8g, and fixed in the same commit. `const platformMetrics = metrics?.platform || { totalTenants: 0, activeTenants: 0, totalUsers: 0, eventsLast24h: 0, apiCallsLast24h: 0 }` sat under a comment reading 'Calculate metrics with fallbacks'; because the fetch used Promise.allSettled and the only setError was in an unreachable catch, a rejected /system/metrics rendered the platform's first screen as a platform with nothing in it, silently. The cards render an em dash now and QueryFailureNotice names the failed read. Two smaller defects went with it: the 'Active Tenants' guard printed a dash whenever both counts were 0, hiding a genuine zero as if it were a failure; and the page built an AbortController it handed to no request, because systemApi.getMetrics/getServicesHealth/getCircuitBreakers and usersApi.getStats took no signal.

title: The analytics dashboard rendered a complete platform of zeros when its reads failed: getDefaultData() supplied ~40 zero fields including MRR, ARR, LTV, churn rate and uptime, and the page displayed them with no failure banner; the server degrades the same way, substituting getDefaultFinancialMetrics() zeros for a section it lists only in unavailable[]
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Working Style: report faithfully — a zero substituted for an unavailable measurement is a false statement, and on a revenue surface it is a false financial statement
notes: Found while migrating AnalyticsDashboardPage in W8h. The FRONTEND half is fixed in the same commit: getDefaultData() is deleted, a failed summary renders QueryFailureNotice instead of a dashboard, every formatter returns an em dash for an absent value, a KPI trend arrow only renders when there is a change behind it, and a section named in the server's unavailable[] is treated as unknown rather than rendering the zeros the server put there. The BACKEND half remains: analytics.service.ts substitutes getDefaultTenantMetrics/getDefaultUserMetrics/getDefaultFinancialMetrics/getDefaultSystemMetrics/getDefaultUsageMetrics — all zeros — for any source that throws, and those same interfaces feed reports.service.ts snapshot aggregation, so widening them to number | null changes report averaging math. title: analytics.service.ts substitutes zero-filled metric objects for any dashboard source that throws (getDefaultTenantMetrics / getDefaultUserMetrics / getDefaultFinancialMetrics / getDefaultSystemMetrics / getDefaultUsageMetrics), so an unreachable billing source is served to every consumer as $0 MRR rather than as unknown
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Working Style: report faithfully — a zero substituted for an unavailable measurement is a false statement, and on a revenue surface a false financial statement
notes: The server half of ADMIN-HIGH-125, split out so it is tracked by an OPEN row rather than by the notes of a resolved finding. W8h fixed the frontend: the admin panel now treats a section named in the response's unavailable[] as unknown and renders an em dash for it, so no operator sees these zeros on the analytics dashboard. They are still served to every OTHER consumer of GET /analytics/dashboard and of the per-section endpoints. title: The job queue page reported zero failed jobs today for a dashboard that had not loaded, patched job and queue rows into local state instead of re-reading the server after a write, and rendered a progress bar through a contract field the generator emitted as an object with no keys
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Working Style: report faithfully — a zero substituted for an unread measurement is a false statement, and a row showing a status the server never confirmed is another
notes: Found while migrating JobQueuePage in W8i and fixed in the same commit. Three defects. (1) `defaultDashboard` was six zeros installed by the catch whenever /system/jobs/dashboard failed; on a job-queue screen 'Failed Today: 0' is the number an operator reads to decide nothing is wrong. It is deleted; a failed read renders QueryFailureNotice. (2) Every write patched local state — setJobs(jobs.map(...)) after a retry, setDashboard({...queues: map(...)}) after a pause — so the row showed a status the server had not confirmed while the counters beside it stayed pre-action; all four writes go through useAdminMutation with invalidateKeys now, and a rejected action is reported next to the table rather than in a fixed-position toast in the corner. (3) `JobProgress` was an interface, and the OpenAPI generator's swagger plugin can only describe classes, so BackgroundJob.progress reached the frontend as `Record<string, never>` and the page read `job.progress.percentage` through a type saying the property cannot exist. It is a class now; the contract carries the four fields and the artifact plus the generated client were regenerated. No DDL: the column is jsonb and its stored shape is unchanged.

title: The error tracking page reported zero unresolved and zero critical errors when its dashboard read failed, and its resolve/ignore handlers decremented that server-computed count by hand so the card drifted further from the truth with every click
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Working Style: report faithfully — a zero substituted for an unread count is a false statement, and client-side arithmetic on a server aggregate manufactures a second one
notes: Found while migrating ErrorTrackingPage in W8j and fixed in the same commit. The stats object was seeded with four zeros and reset to four zeros by the catch, so a failed /system/errors/dashboard displayed '0 unresolved' and '0 critical' on the screen an operator opens to find out whether anything is broken — with the failure itself in a fixed toast in the bottom-right corner. The counts are `number | null` now, render an em dash, and QueryFailureNotice names the read. `todayErrors` likewise: it was the last trend point `|| 0`, so an empty series read as 'no errors today' about a window nobody had measured. The three write handlers spliced the updated group into local state and then did `unresolvedErrors: prev.unresolvedErrors - 1`; all three go through useAdminMutation with invalidateKeys and the counts come back from the server. Five console.error calls went with them.

title: The maintenance page wrote the platform's operational record from the operator's browser clock: start, end, extend and cancel each discarded the updated window the endpoint returns and patched status, actualStart, actualEnd, scheduledEnd and estimatedDurationMinutes into local state
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Working Style: report faithfully — a timestamp invented by the client and displayed as the moment maintenance began is a fabricated operational record
notes: Found while migrating MaintenancePage in W8l and fixed in the same commit. Each of the five write handlers threw away the MaintenanceWindow the endpoint returns and wrote its own row: start set status 'in_progress' with actualStart = new Date(), end set status 'completed' with actualEnd = new Date(), extend recomputed scheduledEnd and ADDED to estimatedDurationMinutes locally, cancel set status 'cancelled', and create unshifted its own optimistic row. actualStart and actualEnd are the record of when the platform went into maintenance and came out — filled in from the operator's browser for a transition the server may have performed at a different moment, or, on a 200 that did not change the status, not performed at all. All five go through useAdminMutation with invalidateKeys now, so the row is the server's. Five console.error calls and the corner toast went with them.

title: Deactivating an email template flipped the row locally and swallowed a refusal into the console, so an operator could believe a customer-facing message was stopped while the server still had it enabled and sending
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Working Style: report faithfully — a write that fails while the screen reports success is a false statement about what the platform is doing
notes: Found while migrating EmailTemplatesPage in W8m and fixed in the same commit. handleToggleActive awaited the PUT, flipped isActive in the local array, and on failure logged to the console and did nothing else — no banner, no revert — so the row read 'inactive' for a template the server still had active. On this page that is a message customers keep receiving after an admin believes it was stopped. The toggle and the save both go through useAdminMutation with invalidateKeys now, so the list is the server's, and a refusal is reported on the page. The save's success banner also moved behind the awaited mutation: it used to be announced beside a loadTemplates() call the handler did not await.

title: Four admin-panel CSV exports build their rows by joining raw values with commas, so an audit action, activity label or tenant name containing a comma or a quote shifts every later column in the exported row
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Working Style: report faithfully — an export that silently misaligns its own columns is a false record of what the platform holds
notes: Found in W8p while giving the seven blob downloads one saveBlob authority; NOT fixed there, because escaping is a different defect class from the download mechanics and needs its own toCsv authority plus a per-page conversion and tests. Six pages spell the escape rule six ways: AuditLogPage and InvoicesPage have a correct escapeCsvCell (quote-wrap when the value contains a comma, quote or newline, doubling inner quotes); QueryEditor has a third correct copy; MessagingAuditPage quote-wraps only `details`; ActivityLogPage quote-wraps only `action`; AuditTrailPage and BillingReportsPage escape nothing at all. On AuditTrailPage the unescaped columns include `action` and `userName`, so an audit row for an action recorded as "deleted pond, tank 4" moves severity, user and IP one column right in the file an auditor reads. The fix is one `toCsv(headers, rows)` next to `saveBlob` in services/blob-client.ts, adopted at all six sites, with the four hand-rolled escapers deleted; QueryEditor is exempt because it is on the W10 kill list.

title: The database management page printed four platform totals — schemas, active schemas, total size, total tables — that it computed by reducing over the first 100 rows it listed, so past a hundred tenants every one of them was a subtotal rendered under the word Total
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Working Style: report faithfully — a subtotal labelled Total is a false statement about the size of the platform's estate
notes: Found while migrating DatabaseManagementPage in W8q and fixed in the same commit. The four cards read schemas.length, schemas.filter(active).length and two reduce()s over getSchemas({page:1,limit:100}).data. The server has owned the aggregate all along at GET /database/schemas/summary, but three things kept it unreachable: the admin-panel's hand-written type named four fields the server never returns ({total, active, suspended, deleted} vs {totalSchemas, activeSchemas, suspendedSchemas, totalSizeBytes, avgSizeBytes}), the route's inline return-type annotation left "200": {} in openapi.json so nothing could catch that drift, and the summary carried no table count so the fourth card had no server owner. Fixed at the root: SchemaSummaryDto class + @ApiOkResponse so the contract describes the route, totalTableCount added, the handler rewritten as one COUNT/FILTER/SUM aggregate instead of find() plus four passes in Node, the FE type sourced through ApiSchema<'SchemaSummaryDto'>, and the cards render an em dash when the aggregate has not loaded. The list header now says 'showing N of M' so the page never implies the table is the estate.

title: The SUPER_ADMIN user surface rejected every platform role but TENANT_ADMIN: four hand-typed role lists in admin-api validated create, update, invite and the list filter against MANAGER/OPERATOR/VIEWER, which are not roles, while rejecting MODULE_MANAGER and MODULE_USER, which are — and the invite body carried an invitedBy field the whitelist pipe refuses outright
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Architectural Approach: if the upstream were correct, would this code need to exist — four copies of one vocabulary, each drifted, is the definition of a missing single source
notes: Found in W8r while migrating the tenant batch, and fixed in the same commit. The platform defines four roles in Role (backend-common/decorators/roles.decorator.ts): SUPER_ADMIN, TENANT_ADMIN, MODULE_MANAGER, MODULE_USER — the same four auth-service assertRoleHierarchy ranks. admin-api's users.dto.ts retyped that list four times (CreateUserDto, UpdateUserDto, InviteUserRequestDto, ListUsersQueryDto) as ['SUPER_ADMIN','TENANT_ADMIN','MANAGER','OPERATOR','VIEWER']. Consequences, all 400: creating a user at the New User form's default role MODULE_USER; changing any user to a module role; inviting anyone below TENANT_ADMIN; and filtering the user list by a module role. Separately the role-template catalogue published six templates including SUPERVISOR and OPERATOR — the only two marked isSystem:false, neither a Role — and the admin-panel invite form renders whatever that catalogue returns, so both appeared as choices that could only fail. Separately again, the frontend InviteUserDto declared invitedBy as REQUIRED, so the one caller sent invitedBy:'system'; the server's InviteUserRequestDto does not declare it and admin-api runs ValidationPipe({forbidNonWhitelisted:true}), so every invitation was rejected before reaching a handler — and the server had always taken the inviter from req.user.id anyway. Fixed at the root: PLATFORM_ROLES and INVITABLE_ROLES are derived from the Role enum with Object.values, all four DTO enums consume them and their role fields are typed Role, RoleTemplate.code is typed Role so a template for a non-role is a compile error (which deleted SUPERVISOR and OPERATOR), the frontend derives PlatformRole from a runtime list proved equal to the generated contract in both directions by a type-level assertion, isPlatformRole narrows the two <select> handlers instead of asserting, and invitedBy is typed never so it cannot be sent. Gate: apps/admin-api-service/src/users/__tests__/role-vocabulary.spec.ts (18 cases) holds both directions — every catalogue role is assignable, every legacy code is refused, and SUPER_ADMIN is not invitable.

title: The onboarding dashboard's Stalled card counted a field the server has never returned, its status filter offered a value no row can hold, and it recomputed a total the server was already sending — while every skipped tenant arrived as a status the frontend type did not admit
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Working Style: report faithfully — a card wired to a field the endpoint does not return can only ever display a fabricated number
notes: Found in W8t while migrating OnboardingPage, and fixed in the same commit. The server's OnboardingStatus is 'not_started' | 'in_progress' | 'completed' | 'skipped'; the admin-panel's TenantOnboarding.status said 'not_started' | 'in_progress' | 'completed' | 'stalled'. Two independent consequences. First, getOnboardingStats returns {total, notStarted, inProgress, completed, skipped, avgCompletionPercent, avgCompletionDays, completionByStep} while the client type declared {notStarted, inProgress, completed, stalled, avgCompletionDays} — so the Stalled card read undefined on every load and the page's zero-filled default rendered 0 forever, on the card an operator reads to find tenants that are stuck; and totalTenants was computed as notStarted+inProgress+completed+stalled while the server was already sending `total`, a subset sum that could never include skipped tenants. Second, the status filter offered a 'stalled' option the service never sets, so filtering by it always returned empty, and every tenant whose onboarding was skipped arrived carrying a status the FE union did not admit and no badge handled. The spec type gate caught it: a fixture using the real 'skipped' status failed to compile against the FE type. Fixed by aligning both the status union and the stats shape to the server's, renaming the card to Skipped, reading totalTenants from stats.total, and taking the filter option from the corrected union.

title: the oscillation guard is half-wired: memory.py increments the reopen counter in production and nothing reads it, while three comments claim an active consumer
rule_violated: A comment asserting a consumer that does not exist is how a reader concludes a control is in place
notes: Found while auditing ARIA autonomy design health at the owner's request. The dormancy waivers for assert_fix_dispatch_allowed and guard_fix_dispatch say 'there is no live caller to attach it to'. True of the DECIDER; false of the RECORDER. memory.py:1004 calls record_reopen() on every belief whose evidence changed, disappeared or stopped matching its glob -- a live production write path. The only two functions that read that counter, assert_fix_dispatch_allowed and guard_fix_dispatch, have zero production callsites (verified by grep across aria-kernel and tools: only their own definitions, __all__ entries and tests). So the system accumulates oscillation evidence no control consumes. The waste is not the defect; the false assurance is. memory.py:1001-1002 states 'the fix dispatcher's guard_fix_dispatch decides' -- there is no fix dispatcher and nothing decides. Two more modules shape data for the same absent reader: capability_gap.py:465 ('for oscillation guard use. Nights are UTC dates, not rows, so two cycles on...') and observation_coverage.py:199 ('the oscillation guard uses to tell a loop from a revision'). Three comments across three modules assert an active consumer that does not exist -- the ORPHAN-HIGH-455 shape, where a reader concludes the control is in place because the code says so. Not a safety hole today because the lane the guard would refuse is not dispatching. Fix by making the comments true (state that the counter is accumulated for a consumer not yet wired) or by wiring the pair; do not leave as-is.

title: Eighteen npm advisories at or above moderate sat unfixed in root-production dependencies, thirteen of them attributed to @nestjs packages whose only real defect was a transitive multer and js-yaml, so npm's suggested remedy was a set of breaking NestJS downgrades rather than two leaf bumps
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Architectural Approach: if the upstream were correct, would this code need to exist — thirteen breaking downgrades to fix two leaf packages is the symptom being treated instead of the cause
notes: Surfaced when an unrelated package.json script rename tripped dependency_audit_required. Root advisories: multer, js-yaml, hono, nodemailer, sharp. All five patched inside their current majors.

title: The dependency audit gate runs only when package.json changes, not when package-lock.json does, so newly published advisories against an unchanged lockfile accumulate on main unobserved until some unrelated edit to package.json happens to trip the trigger
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Test Rules: a gate that does not run is not a gate
notes: Eighteen advisories were live on main and no PR reported them; a two-line script rename is what finally surfaced them. Advisories are published against a FIXED lockfile, so the trigger must not key on manifest edits alone.

title: The ARIA acceptance lane's truth check reported PASS on a sample of zero — validate_drift_output collapsed evidence-integrity and sample-size into one flag, so an empty drift set printed [PASS] checked=0 TP=0 FP=0, and three of the four signals poc.py actually emits were never examined at all
