notes: Found while adversarially re-validating an operator claim about ARIA maturity.

title: The acceptance harness could never return ACCEPT: its fixture workspace was not a git repository, so experiment_night failed with experiment_night_head_sha_unavailable and the cycle check demanded a 'completed' status the fixture made unreachable
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Architectural Approach: root-cause only — the fixture was the wrong artifact, not the assertion
notes: Proven by a two-arm test: identical fixture, git absent -> failed, git present -> completed.

title: tools/aria-acceptance/test_harness.py raised NameError at import for three days, so zero of its nine tests ran — two assertions sat dedented at module scope and unittest.main() sat mid-file above a class it therefore hid
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Test Rules: a test target nothing invokes is not a gate
notes: CycleAcceptanceTests is exactly the test that would have caught the sibling finding on the day it was written.

title: The ARIA acceptance lane was invoked by no workflow: the script was named aria:acceptance, and the CI-reachability invariant only collects root scripts named test or test:*, so a test entrypoint outside that namespace is invisible to the gate that enforces test entrypoints
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Test Rules: every test* target must be reachable from CI
notes: Rename closes this lane; widening the prefix scan itself is tracked as ARIA-MEDIUM-043-R1.

title: Three open CRITICAL findings carry neither owner_user nor deadline and are therefore unreachable by any governance timer: planSweep exempts CRITICALs from auto-staleness while the past-deadline BLOCKED branch cannot fire without a deadline, and the registry add path lets a CRITICAL be created without one
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Architectural Approach: tracked debt requires an explicit owner + deadline + finding ID
notes: Not fixed by the harness repair. Tier-1 fix: buildFinding must REFUSE a CRITICAL stub with no deadline. Affects ARIA-CRITICAL-007, -009, -015.

title: The architecture spine gate's baseline comparator compares violation COUNTS with no identity, so a change that removes one tenant-isolation violation and introduces a different one reports no drift, and a fix-two-break-one change reports an improvement that absorbs the new defect
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Architectural Approach: make it detectable — a gate that cannot see a swapped violation green-lights plan advancement carrying a new defect
notes: Proven by calling detect_drift directly: (3->3 identity swap) = NO DRIFT; (3->2 after introducing one) = improvement. Tier-1 fix: measurements must carry the violation SET, and detect_drift must report introduced/removed as distinct facts.

title: The Closes: trailer gate admits a trailer that can never close the finding it names: the registry lane checks only that the id exists while the closure derivation also binds the review file, and any commit type that does not require a trailer had its trailer skipped unread
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Review Finding Traceability (MANDATORY); admission must not be looser than derivation
notes: Proven against merged history: 793dbfd34 (skipped entirely - refactor type) and 77d164947 (validated and passed) both shipped 'Closes: docs/reviews/orchestrator/2026-09-05-production-readiness-gaps.md#SEC-HIGH-056', where SEC-HIGH-056 is an unrelated RESOLVED admin-api SQL-injection finding whose review_file is docs/reviews/security/2026-08-23-vuln-scan-findings.md. Result: SEC-HIGH-158 and SEC-HIGH-159 sit OPEN with no closers although their fixes are on main. Fix reuses commitMessageClosesFindingExactly so admission and derivation cannot drift; bare un-anchored trailers stay admissible. Measured blast radius: 0 mis-bound trailers in the last 200 main commits.

title: A finding's review_file is a single mutable pointer while its merged Closes: trailers are immutable, so when the document that raised a finding and the document that records its fix differ, the exact matcher refuses the real closer forever and the ledger reports fixed work as OPEN
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Review Finding Traceability (MANDATORY): a merged fix must be recordable against the finding it closed
notes: Measured over all Closes: trailers on origin/main against OPEN/IN-PROGRESS rows: 23 active findings are named by a merged trailer; 3 bind correctly (INFRA-HIGH-147 and PLAT-MEDIUM-901 carry rejected_closing_commits - deliberate reopens; INFRA-MEDIUM-168 has an empty review_file) and 20 do not. Two distinct sub-classes. A = right path, wrong id (SEC-HIGH-158/159, from the #1420 renumbering) - the id-alias sidecar cannot help because the cited id is a live ledger row and finding-id-aliases.spec.ts refuses an alias that shadows one. B = right id, different path, and it is usually not staleness but two legitimate documents: SENSOR-HIGH-105 was RAISED in docs/reviews/zcode/2026-09-03-100-tenant-readiness-integration.md:52 and CLOSED by 1f94881db citing docs/reviews/zcode/2026-09-04-telemetry-readiness-v4-port.md:92, and both files carry a heading for the id. The id has finding-id-aliases.yaml for exactly this shape of problem; the path has no equivalent, so close and reconcile refuse the commit permanently. Tested and DISPROVED: the append-only chain does not retain a prior review_file (each id has exactly one row), so there is no mechanical repair from history. Fix direction (tier 1, one mechanism not two): extend the SAME sidecar with declared closure anchors folded into FindingTrailerTarget by withFindingAliases and matched only in the anchored branch, loaded by the backward-looking derivation and NOT by the forward-looking commit-msg gate, so a NEW commit must still cite the current review_file and PROC-HIGH-031 is not reopened; guarded by the mirror invariants the alias sidecar already carries (declared path exists, carries a heading for that id, and at least one named merged commit really cites it). SENSOR-HIGH-097 needs more than the mechanism: its trailer cites docs/reviews/zcode/2026-08-24-100-tenant-readiness.md, which has never carried a SENSOR-HIGH-097 heading - the 2026-09-03 integration review records that at :162.

title: Payroll seeds and stamps a hardcoded USD literal instead of the tenant currency the same service already resolves, so a non-USD tenant can get USD-denominated payroll rows and a USD-stamped PayrollProcessed event crossing into the finance ledger
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Architectural Approach: tenant currency has an SSoT (PayrollCostSettingsService.getDefaultCurrencyInTx) and a write path must not re-derive it from a literal
notes: Found by the FARM-HIGH-151 verification, not by a report: finance-currency-ssot.spec.ts guards FINANCE_HANDLER_ROOTS recursively plus a hardcoded NAMED_GUARDED_FILES list, so handlers outside those roots are unguarded. Scanning every apps/**/*.handler.ts for the spec's own CURRENCY_FALLBACK pattern found 7 unguarded writers: these 2 hr payroll handlers and 5 billing handlers (the billing ones are a separate finding - platform vs tenant currency is undeclared there, not obviously wrong). create-employee.handler.ts:67 resolves the tenant default through payrollCostSettings.getDefaultCurrencyInTx in the same service, so employee.currency is normally set and the || 'USD' fires only for employees seeded by another path or created before FARM-HIGH-151; approve-payroll.handler.ts:72 has no such upstream and stamps savedPayroll.currency || 'USD' onto the cross-service PayrollProcessed event.

title: Five billing handlers default currency to a bare 'USD' literal with no declared platform-currency SSoT, so nothing in the code says whether billing is denominated in the platform's currency or the tenant's and neither reading can be enforced
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Architectural Approach tier 4 is a last resort: an undeclared currency policy cannot be gated at build time
notes: NOT asserted to be a defect - the honest defect is that the code does not say which reading is intended, so a reviewer cannot tell a bug from a policy. Stripe-facing platform billing in USD is a defensible policy; per-tenant invoicing in the tenant's currency is equally defensible, and billing.subscriptions is keyed by tenantId. Fix direction: declare it. If it is the platform currency, name it (PLATFORM_BILLING_CURRENCY) so the literal disappears and the currency guard can exempt it by rule rather than by omission; if it is the tenant's, route it through the settings SSoT like every farm and hr create-handler. Until then the currency guard carries billing as an explicitly declared exemption citing this id, so the exemption is visible instead of being the absence of a list entry.

title: The platform-scope event seam has no cross-service integration test: every hop of a super-admin password reset is proven in isolation and the producer and consumer are joined only by a shared constant
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Test Rules: a trust-boundary crossing needs cover at the boundary, not only on each side of it
notes: Recorded while closing SEC-HIGH-159 rather than papered over. A composed producer/consumer assertion inside libs/event-contracts was written and then DISCARDED after mutation testing: drifting eventTenantScope off PLATFORM_EVENT_TENANT_ID onto its own literal is already caught by two existing assertions in tenant-scope.spec.ts, so the composed one caught nothing new and would have been decoration. The real gap is a level up and needs the e2e lane: one super-admin reset carried from initiatePasswordReset through the outbox worker into AuthEventHandler, so the seam is exercised rather than asserted twice against the same constant. Belongs with the other live-stack lanes (INFRA-MEDIUM-153).

title: Sixteen entity currency columns still carry hardcoded DDL defaults that disagree with each other inside one service, so any insert path that omits the column books in a currency chosen by which table it touched
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Architectural Approach: the tenant default currency has one SSoT; a column default cannot know the tenant, so every literal default contradicts it
notes: FARM-MEDIUM-145 and FARM-HIGH-151 migrated the HANDLERS to FinanceSettingsService/PayrollCostSettingsService; the DDL layer they write into was never touched. Measured across apps/**/*.entity.ts: 16 currency columns carry a literal default, and farm-service disagrees with ITSELF - chemical 'TRY', consumable 'NOK', worker 'USD', purchase-order 'NOK', spare-part 'TRY', feed 'TRY', equipment 'TRY'. That is the same drift FARM-MEDIUM-145 was raised for, one layer down. The handlers always supply a currency today so no live write reaches the default, but it is a loaded trap for a backfill, an admin tool, a data migration or the next handler, and nothing detects it. Precedent for the fix is in this same branch: HR-HIGH-008 dropped payrolls.currency's DEFAULT 'USD' (migration 1802200000000) rather than swapping the literal, because a column default cannot know the tenant and the column is NOT NULL, so removing it makes a currency-less row impossible instead of silently mis-denominated. Doing that for the remaining 16 is 16 migrations across 4 services plus a NOT NULL audit on each column, which is why it is registered rather than done here. Until then finance-currency-ssot.spec.ts carries them as declared, finding-linked exemptions with a staleness test, so the set can only shrink.

title: An alert rule's condition.parameter is an unvalidated free-text column while the platform has a canonical reading vocabulary, so a rule spelled any other way silently never matches instead of being rejected at creation
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Architectural Approach: a vocabulary with an SSoT must be enforced where rows are written, not assumed where they are read
notes: Found while fixing SENSOR-CRITICAL-111, and deliberately NOT asserted to be a live break. checkConditions does a plain readings[condition.parameter] lookup; the handler builds that map from PARAMETER_BY_READING_FIELD, whose keys are the canonical camelCase parameter names, and alert-rule.entity.ts:57 documents exactly that vocabulary ('temperature', 'ph', 'dissolvedOxygen'). Producer and consumer therefore agree today. The defect is that nothing ENFORCES it: `parameter!: string` is a free column with no enum, no IsIn validator and no FK to SENSOR_READING_PARAMETERS, so a rule created with the device-facing snake_case spelling ('dissolved_oxygen') is accepted and then never matches any reading - a life-safety rule that exists, looks configured in the UI, and cannot fire. That spelling is not hypothetical: the service's own alert-evaluation.service.spec.ts:70 fixture uses it, and it passes only because it calls evaluateSensorReading directly with a self-consistent readings object, bypassing the handler that would have produced camelCase. Fix direction (tier 1): bind the column to SENSOR_READING_PARAMETERS at the write path so an unknown parameter is rejected at rule creation rather than at 3am; the same SSoT already backs the producers, the NATS consumer and the handler.

title: VFD automation rules are configurable, persisted and evaluated by nothing: onSensorReading carries no @OnEvent and has zero callers, so no reading has ever triggered a rule
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Architectural Approach: a surface the product offers must be reachable; a handler nothing subscribes is a feature that cannot run
notes: VfdAutomationRuleService.onSensorReading(event: SensorReadingEvent) is a complete implementation - it finds matching rules, evaluates conditions and creates change sets - reached by nothing. The method carries no @OnEvent, no @EventPattern and no bus subscription, and a tree-wide grep finds zero callers outside its own file. A tenant can therefore create an automation rule ('when dissolved oxygen drops below X, raise the aerator to Y Hz'), see it listed as ACTIVE, and it will never fire. This is not the same defect as SENSOR-HIGH-067 (no telemetry poller): that one is about reading FROM drives, this is about reacting to sensor readings by writing TO them. Both are reachability holes on the same surface, which is why the VFD module looks complete and does nothing. Fix direction: subscribe the handler on the sensor-reading subject the alert engine already consumes and return a HandlerOutcome (PLAT-HIGH-902 contract), rather than adding a second private dispatch path. Deliberately out of scope of the VFD reachability PR that registered it: that PR fixes the surfaces a human operates (activation, device selection, panel mounting, channel CRUD); wiring an autonomous write path to live sensor readings is a separate blast radius that needs its own review and its own tests.

title: The SCADA VFD drive widget binds its device by free-text id and its start/stop/program buttons are dropped by the node's command dispatcher, so the widget renders controls that do nothing at runtime
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Architectural Approach: a control that cannot perform its action must not be rendered as if it can
notes: Two independent halves. (1) VfdDriveWidgetConfig asks for the VFD device by a plain <input type="text"> labelled 'VFD Device ID' with placeholder 'Enter VFD device ID...', so binding a widget requires a human to paste a UUID copied from elsewhere; a typo binds the widget to nothing and reads as an empty drive. Every other device-bound surface in the module selects from a device list. (2) VfdDriveWidget's start/stop/program buttons call onCommand('vfd:start'|'vfd:stop'|'vfd:program') and are enabled only when !isEditing - that is, only at runtime - but ScadaWidgetNode.handleCommand branches on 'navigate' and, in simulation mode only, 'toggle'/'press'/'writeTag'. The three vfd: commands match no branch, there is no else and no warning: the click is swallowed. An operator on a SCADA screen presses Stop on a running drive and gets no error and no effect. Registered rather than fixed in the VFD reachability PR because a real fix issues a VFD command from a SCADA runtime surface, which needs the command authorization and audit path reviewed on its own - a silent no-op is safer than an unaudited write, but it must not stay silent: the minimum correct interim behaviour is to disable the buttons, which is itself part of the fix and not a workaround.

title: A data channel's operationalMin/operationalMax gate every reading through validateValue but no GraphQL type reads or writes them, so a manually created channel has no operational band and no way to get one
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Architectural Approach: a column that changes runtime behaviour must have a defined way to be set, or it is state nothing can reach
notes: Surfaced while fixing SENSOR-HIGH-063 and NOT asserted to be a live break - it may well be the intended design. operationalMin/operationalMax are distinct from minValue/maxValue: the latter is the physical range, the former the operational band SensorDataChannel.validateValue rejects readings against (:408-411) with a reason string (:433). They are populated in exactly one place, sensor-type.service.ts:347-348, from a sensor-type template's channel definitions. Neither CreateDataChannelInput, UpdateDataChannelInput nor the DataChannelType output object mentions them, so a channel created through the channel manager - the only manual path - is born with no operational band and can never be given one; its readings skip that validation entirely while a template-provisioned channel's do not. Two readings of this are possible and the finding does not pick one: either the operational band is deliberately template-owned (in which case the gap is that nothing says so, and a manual channel silently opts out of a safety check), or it is user config that was never wired (in which case the input types are missing three fields). Deciding needs product intent, which is why this is registered rather than fixed inside a CRUD repair. The FE had been sending the editor's PHYSICAL range under these names, so nothing was ever written to them from the UI even before the request started failing.

title: The VFD change-set Apply button re-sent approveVfdChangeSet on an already-APPROVED set, so every click reported an error for an apply that was already happening
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Architectural Approach: a control must not exist for an operation the contract has no mutation for
notes: Registered AFTER its fix, to correct a mis-attribution rather than hide it: commit 9e420e0d4 removed the button but its Closes: trailer named SENSOR-HIGH-062, which is the hardcoded mock device selector and was already closed by 661d2de24. The trailer was structurally valid - a real id whose review_file matched the cited path - so the commit-msg gate PROC-HIGH-031 hardened accepted it. That is the gate's known limit: it proves a trailer CAN close the finding it names, not that the diff is about that finding. The defect itself: useVfdChangeSets.applyChangeSet was a byte-for-byte copy of approveChangeSet because no applyVfdChangeSet mutation exists. Approval is the trigger - VfdChangeSetSchedulerService applies on vfd.changeset.approved with a 30s sweep as the crash-durable backstop - so a second approve on an APPROVED set hits assertStatus(changeSet, PENDING_APPROVAL, 'approve') and is rejected. The operator saw an error about a change set that was already on its way to the drive.

title: The autonomy CLI wrote ARIA_JOB_DEADLINE_EPOCH with no restore, so one command's deadline outlived it and every later cycle, drain and burn-in in the same interpreter raised PhaseDeadlineExceeded before doing any work
rule_violated: A process-global environment mutation that exists to serve child processes must be scoped to the run that sets it; a deadline that outlives its command silently disqualifies every later run in the same interpreter
notes: Introduced by ef4238fec (merged in #1397, the ARIA-HIGH-034 in-phase deadline interrupt). Symptom: two full local kernel-suite runs failed with an unstable set (27 then 17) drawn from four modules that all pass in isolation; CI aria-kernel red twice (33663053914, 33688751606) then green. Mechanism: test_cli_autonomy_subcommand invokes cli_main(['autonomy',...]) six times, pinning a deadline over the remaining ~250 modules; once wall-clock passed it, _run_phase_with_deadline raised before invoking any phase — 30 burn-in cycles dead in one second each, drain_done stop=job_deadline_reached. Proof after fix: same five modules in one interpreter, drain_done stop=queue_empty, Ran 71 tests OK. Re-registered 2026-09-11: the original fix e927eac3f (branch fix/aria-job-deadline-scope, id ARIA-HIGH-038 reserved in that worktree only) never reached main; Codex publication push on 8ec2536b hit the same leak and masked it with a test-level patch.dict(os.environ).

title: The kernel test suite inherits the operator's ARIA state-root environment: a fixed ARIA_REPO_STATE_ROOT makes every fixture share one finding history (41 false F-901 errors on a green commit), and an unset ARIA_WORKSPACE_BASE writes 4,927 fixture workspaces under the operator's home
rule_violated: A test suite's isolation must be established by the suite itself, not by whoever invokes it; a shared state root across fixture repositories cannot be a valid configuration, and operator state must not be the suite's default write target
notes: Found while taking over the Codex publication lane: the push of 8ec2536b ran the pre-push kernel suite with ARIA_REPO_STATE_ROOT/ARIA_WORKSPACE_BASE/ARIA_TOOLS_DIR/ARIA_STATE_STORE_ROOT fixed to gate directories and failed 2849 tests / 8 failures / 38 errors. Reproduced on clean main 53d3e82d: the ordered pair test_change_outcome.VerdictTests.test_no_gain_when_the_finding_reproduces_after_the_merge -> test_experiment_finding_bridge.ExperimentFindingBridgeTests.test_certainty_vocabulary_is_producer_backed passes with the variable unset and raises GovernanceError F-901-before-emitted with it set. The Codex repair bound a fixture-local root in two of the hundreds of finding-emitting fixtures; the suite bootstrap is the owner. The remaining 5 failures (adjudication sweep, burn-in) are ARIA-HIGH-064's deadline leak.

title: validation.py runs validation commands with the whole inherited process environment, so an in-cycle self-validation that runs the kernel suite executes it under the durable store's ARIA_TOOLS_DIR/ARIA_WORKSPACE_BASE binding and fixture state lands in the store
rule_violated: A validation command that exercises test fixtures must not inherit the runtime's durable-state binding; the runner that launches it owns that boundary
notes: Residual of ARIA-HIGH-065. The test package now unbinds ARIA_REPO_STATE_ROOT itself (cross-fixture finding replay is closed), but ARIA_TOOLS_DIR and ARIA_WORKSPACE_BASE are honoured when inherited, and restore-aria-state exports both into the job. validation.py line ~386 builds the child env as {**os.environ, **env_updates}; parse_allowed_command only admits PYTHONPATH as an explicit override. Owner: the validation command environment. Deadline: the validation stage of the end-to-end chain being connected in this handoff.

title: Liveness guards were used as performance budgets across the state lock, the evidence probes and the executor children: every governed state writer waited file_lock's 5 s default behind a healthy publish replay, a git probe that could not answer was graded as the agent's worktree_candidate, and the executor killed its submit child at 120 s while the kernel bound was minutes
rule_violated: A bound on a wait is sized to the longest legitimate live hold it can be behind and is derived from the arcs that hold it; an observation that could not be made is undecided, never a verdict against the party that did not make it
notes: Found by push #4 of fix/aria-suite-hermeticity (33,754 s pre-push suite, 3 failures): test_publish_contention writers raised with_exclusive_lock_timeout at 5 s during a replay that legitimately holds the state-group locks across capped git steps; test_seed_evidence_concrete graded a committed glob worktree_candidate because _git_blob_matches returned False on TimeoutExpired. Five verified rounds: STATE_LOCK_LIVENESS_SECONDS derived from the transaction-held arcs (state_store_lifecycle_arcs.py: pending recovery fetch/ff/probe = 900 s) with one deadline across the ordered locks and a runtime guard refusing an unpriced heavy git step under a transaction; the lifecycle lock waits the whole holder arc (publish 5400 s / checkout 2700 s) with every heavy git call under it a registered step (11 steps, AST-walked and runtime-traced); GitProbeSession (30 s attempts x3, backoff, one 300 s clock per decision, baseline resolved once) grades verification_unavailable — never resolvable, never worktree_candidate — with rejection_codes on the submit response and a harness-class executor release evidence_verification_unavailable; a pre-claim git gate; the executor submit/record/claim/release children priced from the kernel bounds (child worst case 6333 s, drain window 7200 s, job reserve 9000 s, job 280 min) with a visible kernel-import fallback; claim/reaper timestamps under the lock; evidence_target_sha and the anchor probe on the session (undecided is not unreachable); worktree add/remove bounded; the acceptance harness reports host_unavailable apart from ARIA's fp_rate; notify senders under one wall clock. Verified by wf_5229dba4-11e, wf_c02ed913-698, wf_6a5e9dd8-e28, wf_cf0825d5-602, wf_afce3d0e-768, wf_883d4922-940 (round 5 accepted: 878 + 142 tests, gates clean).

title: notify() evaluates its per-signature dedup across channels inside one call: with two configured channels the second is recorded deduped by the first channel's sent row of the same call, so a multi-channel operator gets one delivery per signature instead of one per channel
rule_violated: Dedup keys are per (signature, channel); one call delivers to every configured channel once
notes: Observed while pinning the notify wall clock (ARIA-HIGH-109 round 4): test_notify_bound pins the current rows ['sent','deduped'] as observed so the behaviour is visible, not fixed. Owner claude; the fix is the dedup key including the channel, with the pin inverted.

title: About thirty governed append sites (notify, tool_registry, agent_invocations, worker_dispatch, ...) write through transaction.append_declared_jsonl directly and bypass ledger.append_declared_jsonl's ENOSPC-to-environment_failure translation, so a full disk surfaces as a raw OSError instead of the named environment refusal promised for every governed append
rule_violated: One governed append primitive every site uses; a full disk is one named refusal everywhere
notes: Observed by the ARIA-HIGH-109 round-4 re-verifier on notify's outbox append and confirmed as the prevalent pattern. Also on the executor: ci_executor.py's model-refusal exit runs an in-process append_tools_governance('model_refusal_unresolved') — an unpriced state-lock wait before the priced record child. Owner claude; the right shape is the transaction API routing every append through the ENOSPC translation, pinned by an AST invariant over direct callers.

title: The finding-registry allocator concatenated every active worktree's registry ids with a spread call (`claimed.push(...ids)`), so once the sweep grew past V8's argument ceiling (98 worktrees x ~1,600 rows on 2026-09-13) every registry mutation — add, add-explicit, close, sweep — failed closed as 'Maximum call stack size exceeded'
rule_violated: A gate scales with the repository it governs; an unbounded collection is never spread into a call
notes: Reproduced on this host while registering ARIA-HIGH-109: `add-explicit` died in claimedIdsForDomain (finding-registry.ts:708) under the authority's catch. Fix: appendAll loops; idsFromActiveRegistries takes an injectable ActiveRegistryReader so the sweep is pinned at 100 registries x 2,000 ids without touching disk (finding-registry-allocation-scale.spec.ts; the spread variant fails it with RangeError). The 98 worktrees themselves are leftovers of workflow agents and old sessions and are pruned separately.

title: nx dev toolchain exposed to GHSA-7w5x-hrqm-74c2 (high); remediation is a breaking 22.6.4 workspace-wide bump
rule_violated: npm-audit root-full gate (scripts/ci/npm-audit-gate.mjs)

title: Z.ai was reachable only by pointing the claude binary at api.z.ai with the Z.ai key in the child's environment, which the 2026-09-11 operator policy forbids; the native admission could not admit Z.ai at all, and a native run on any request role outside a hand-copied seven-name cost vocabulary completed at the vendor and then failed at cost attribution
rule_violated: A provider's credential is used only by that provider's own transport; the fleet is the one binding of a model to its provider; any request role the kernel can mint must be attributable at cost recording
notes: Operator policy (handoff 2026-09-11): Codex/Claude only through managed subscription CLI sessions; Z.ai alone through its distinct subscription API; never inject Z.ai credentials into Codex/Claude children. The existing ORPHAN-HIGH-763/764 route did exactly that (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL + ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN per spawn). model_fleet listed zai with runtime_hint='claude', so native admission required a claude binary and returned status unknown. budget.COST_INVOCATION_ROLES was a hand-copied subset of agent_surface.INVOCATION_ROLES; an evidence_judgment request on the native lane reached the vendor, then raised 'agent_role MUST be in COST_INVOCATION_ROLES'.

title: ARIA agents have not yet been exercised against the real Z.ai subscription API: the transport is proven only against a local stand-in vendor, the operator's key is not provisioned to the runtime, and the Coding-Plan endpoint entitlement is documented but unmeasured
rule_violated: A provider route is admitted on the vendor's own answer, not on a fixture's; success against a stand-in is transport evidence, not live evidence
notes: Explicit backlog acceptance from the 2026-09-11 handoff: exercise ARIA agents with REAL Z.ai API access using the user-provided subscription key. Closure requires: the key placed by the operator at a 0600 file named by ARIA_ZAI_API_KEY_FILE (never pasted into chat, argv, Git, logs or evidence); probe_zai_status recorded against api.z.ai with the HTTP status and vendor code/message; one native request accepted through _invoke_native_zai with the vendor's usage block recorded; the vendor dashboard confirming which quota the call drew. Owner: claude (this session). Deadline: 2026-09-18.

title: The agent-response contract validated roles against REQUEST_ROLES, a strict subset of what the request writer mints, so the one role the expert producer mints (specialist_domain_review) could be requested, claimed and answered but never admitted; with no consumer for the panel, the fifth pre-merge predicate (expert_consensus_evidence_verified) stayed check_not_implemented
rule_violated: A contract validator obeys the vocabulary its writer obeys; a mintable role must be answerable; a declared perimeter predicate with a live producer and evaluator must have its consumer
notes: Reported by the Codex memory lane as its first consumer failure (expert-consumer-first-red: 'response_schema: agent-response.role unknown: specialist_domain_review', test 796) with the instruction to trace role admission ownership rather than weaken the schema. Ownership traced: agent_invocations.ROLES is INVOCATION_ROLES (REQUEST_ROLES + specialist_domain_review) and surface_reachability already records that binding the narrower vocabulary makes a surface describe a rule its writer does not obey; agent_contract now validates both envelopes against INVOCATION_ROLES. The consumer joins the panel by the implementation binding the producer embeds and evaluates it with the existing evaluate_expert_consensus at the implementation head.

title: The rendered request told the model to answer 'per your agent contract' and no route delivered the contract: the Claude route sent the prompt on stdin without --agent, and the Codex/Z.ai routes have no file reader, so the first completed native planner attempt (Codex, 297 s, 69,945 tokens) returned a plan under `plan` and was refused as plan_content:absent_or_not_object
rule_violated: A model is shown every input it is told to obey; a contract the runtime cannot deliver is a refusal waiting to be paid for
notes: Found on the first completed native planner attempt (trial five, dispatch one, request AIR-aria-challenger-planner-bf0c69ea80c0): the Codex answer self-reported 'the exposed tools provide no text-file reader' and 'status: partial'. The delivery module strips the agent frontmatter, inlines every @.claude/knowledge citation (bounded, omissions listed) and hashes the text; every route prepends it (Codex prompt prefix, Z.ai system turn, Claude stdin prefix) and records agent_contract_hash on the envelope and the finished row. With the contract delivered and the Z.ai output budget widened, the same task produced the first ACCEPTED native planner result (trial six, AIR-aria-challenger-planner-b82f89291809, glm-5.3, state CHALLENGER_DRAFTED).

title: The managed Anthropic session could not be admitted on the native lane (status 'unknown', no context, no invoker), the legacy Claude dispatch still applied a nominal-dollar reservation under the managed-subscription policy, and both of its refusal branches passed a string where the summary writer reads .failure_class
rule_violated: Every provider the fleet lists is admitted on the vendor's own status answer and executed with the same attempt/finished evidence; a policy decided once at admission is not re-decided as dollars at spawn; a refusal is a typed failure
notes: `claude auth status --json` (loggedIn / authMethod claude.ai / subscriptionType) is the non-model status the CLI itself reports and the mirror of `codex login status`; the executor's observe_status returned 'supported_auth_status_unavailable' for the anthropic row. The legacy invoke_claude_cli's ARIA-AUDIT-021 reservation refused with failure=<str> (AttributeError on .failure_class) — a latent crash on every refusal — and applied the dollar ceiling regardless of the managed-subscription policy that ORPHAN-HIGH-472 had already retired for ci_executor's dispatch budget.

title: Native admission handed the whole fleet a single probe's recheck budget as its deadline, so one stalled first probe left the providers behind it 'status_deadline_elapsed' without ever being asked
rule_violated: A per-probe budget is offered to every fleet member; the admission's wall-clock bound is the fleet's own arithmetic, not a caller's guess
notes: Measured on trial four (AIR-aria-challenger-planner-1809efa4dcb9, dispatch two, 2026-09-11T21:24Z): host at 96% swap, the Anthropic probe hit its 20 s limit (status_timeout, honest) and the Codex row was recorded status_deadline_elapsed with an empty status command — the executor had set deadline = now + recheck_timeout_seconds for all three providers. The fleet now computes its own deadline (recheck × fleet size) and offers each member the full recheck; an overrun costs only the members behind it.

title: The Claude spawn's resource limiter was selected by a probe in the executor's environment and launched in the agent's built environment, which carries no user-bus plumbing, so `systemd-run --user` failed with 'Failed to connect to bus' on the managed route's first live attempt
rule_violated: A limiter is probed in the environment it will be launched with; the user-bus plumbing reaches the limiter alone and never the agent it limits
notes: Trial six cross-review (AIR-aria-cross-reviewer-1da71e60e0ee, dispatch two, 2026-09-11T21:57Z): the managed Anthropic route was admitted natively for the first time (runtime_attempt_started provider anthropic/claude/subscription) and the spawn exited 1 with claude_stderr_tail 'Failed to connect to bus: No medium found'. claude_runtime called apply_resource_limits with no environment, so the cached host probe ran in the executor's environment (which had DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS from the operator session) while the spawn ran with the built agent env (allowlist; no bus). The Codex lane already probed in its launch environment and fed the bus to the limiter by hand; the kernel helper now owns both halves for every lane: probe in the launch environment, `env NAME=VALUE systemd-run ... env -u NAME <command>`.

title: Inside the write-containment sandbox the Claude spawn ran a different CLI installation than the one the executor had probed (PATH re-resolved under /usr/local), could not see the settings and MCP documents written for it under the host /tmp, and was handed the operator's whole login directory read-only, on which the CLI stalls writing its own state
rule_violated: What the attempt names is what runs: the resolved executable, the documents written for this spawn and one credential file are bound into the sandbox explicitly; the operator's session state and identity never enter the agent
notes: Trial six cross-review dispatch three (2026-09-11T22:22Z): the limiter now launched, and the spawn failed after 164 s with 'Settings file not found: /tmp/aria-spawn-settings/aria-settings-AIR-aria-cross-reviewer-1da71e60e0ee.json' although the file existed on the host (0600, written 22:22:37). The sandbox mounts a fresh tmpfs on /tmp; the spawn wrote its settings and MCP documents there. The binary was named 'claude' and PATH inside the sandbox (which binds /usr but not ~/.local) resolved /usr/local/bin/claude = 2.1.233 while the executor had probed ~/.local/bin/claude = 2.1.269. Measured in the same sandbox with the real CLI: whole login dir ro-bound = 37 s for a one-turn haiku run; one credential file into a private home = 2.7 s. Also observed: the operator session's own child exports (CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION, CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET, …) reached the executor and passed the CLAUDE_CODE_ prefix filter into the agent; they are excluded by name now (CLAUDE_INSTANCE_ENV_NAMES).

title: The cross-reviewer's contract told the model the kernel reads `id` + `verdict` only, the canonical-envelope SSoT skeleton showed no `note`, and the validator then rejected a substantive live cross-review for the missing `note` on `contradicted`; the executor's unconditional release after that rejection failed on the kernel's own terminal rule and reported a claim leak that did not exist
rule_violated: The rules a validator enforces are delivered to the model from the validator itself, never restated by hand; a kernel-recorded rejection is the claim's terminal effect and is not released again
notes: First live managed-Claude native run (trial six cross-review, AIR-aria-cross-reviewer-1da71e60e0ee, dispatch four, 2026-09-11T22:39Z): opus, 334 s, claude_returned_exit=0, usage row ledgered, pre_submit_validation_passed, then submit rejected with 'response_schema: satisfaction_matrix[0].note required when verdict=contradicted'. The 23.6 KB answer carried three matrix entries with the reason under `evidence` (as its contract's anchor 3 instructed) and a grounded details.cross_review with two blocking risks. The executor then called release_claim(reason=submit_rejected) → GovernanceError 'result already terminal' and printed 'The request stays CLAIMED and no later run can pick it up' — false: derive_request_state returns REJECTED from the result row. Fix: agent_contract.render_response_validator_contract() renders the validator's rules from its constants and agent_contract_delivery appends it to every delivered contract; the prose in aria-cross-reviewer.md, aria-primary-planner.md and the layer-2 SSoT skeleton is corrected; ci_executor releases only when the submit refused BEFORE a result row (_rejected_result_recorded). The lifecycle-leak invariant, red since the main→_main split, follows _main and scopes to the held-claim window.

title: The pre-spawn cost-budget gate refused a managed-subscription spawn on notional dollars, reading the DEFAULT policy because it took the tools store's parent directory for the workspace while the store was bound elsewhere
rule_violated: Under the managed-subscription policy notional dollars are telemetry, never admission; operator policy is read from the workspace a tools store is bound to, not from a directory-layout assumption
notes: Trial eight cross-review (AIR-aria-cross-reviewer-f7ddfbedc372, 2026-09-12T00:46Z): admission chose the managed Anthropic route, then claude_runtime._assert_budget_before_spawn raised cost_budget_daily_cap_exceeded projected=6.227328 cap=5.0 — two attempts, control_or_transport_unavailable, no model reached. The workspace's aria-config/genesis_policy.json declares monetary_admission=managed_subscription; cost_budget._load_caps computed repo_root = Path(base_dir).parent (= trial/store) and read the shipped defaults ($5 daily). tool_registry.bound_workspace_root now resolves the bound workspace (bound_repo_root in repo_identity.json; parent for a legacy store) and cost_budget, circuit_breaker and the agent-request anchor policy read through it; assert_within_budget returns status=telemetry_only under managed_subscription instead of refusing or tripping the breaker.

title: The plan-convergence bridge honoured an agent-supplied revision `round` and `parent_revision_hash` against its own contract, so a round-2 primary that echoed the request's round_number was refused by the reducer and the accepted envelope was declared dead (HUMAN_REQUIRED)
rule_violated: Kernel-state facts (the critique round, the parent revision) are read from kernel state, never from the agent that cannot read it
notes: Trial eight round 2 (AIR-aria-primary-planner-f3c9a608e939, managed Claude fable, 1,133 s, ACCEPTED at the request layer, 2026-09-12T01:38Z): details.revision.round=2 echoed the envelope's round_number; fold_plan_state said current_round=1; _canonicalize_revision_payload passed the supplied round through; _validate_revision refused 'revision round must match current critique round' (agent_bridge_warning); the drainer found no live primary_plan envelope for round 2, raised _EnvelopeDead and forced HUMAN_REQUIRED (verdict split, branch defensive_default). round and parent_revision_hash now come from kernel state only; the agent's revision_id label is kept.

title: The round-2+ primary revision envelope asked the planner to address cross-review findings it never carried; a tool-less route or a sandboxed spawn with the store outside the workspace revised blind
rule_violated: An envelope carries everything its role needs to answer, inside untrusted-content tags; no route may depend on reading the store
notes: The same trial-eight revision answered: 'The expected output directory for flow-… does not exist on this host, so no round-1 primary plan, challenger plan or cross-review envelope was readable' (details.revision.note, prior_round_artifacts_found=false). issue_primary_envelope's default suggested_prompt was one sentence. It now builds the prompt from the plan state it already folds: latest primary body, challenger body and the last round's cross_review_risks_by_round inside <untrusted_*> tags, mirroring the cross-review envelope.

title: The twin's self-feature qualification runs under a hardcoded 2-second scoped-source budget, and three PlannerTwinContext fixtures assert 'available' — on a loaded host the budget expires (qualification_deadline) and the fixtures fail without any code change
rule_violated: A production time budget is policy, not a literal; a fixture may not assume host speed
notes: Measured 2026-09-12T02:0xZ on the candidate beside the pre-push suite (load 5): test_cross_review_controller_forwards_current_body_and_explicit_root, test_cross_review_drainer_preserves_current_source_context_and_both_proposals, test_later_primary_drainer_uses_reviewed_body_and_current_cycle failed with implemented.status 'unknown' != 'available'; re-run alone at load 3.9 the same fixture reported available/selected_source_definition. _ScopedSourceBudget() defaults deadline_monotonic = now + 2 (snapshot.py); _self_feature_projection builds it with defaults and returns qualification_deadline when it expires — honest at runtime, host-dependent in a fixture. Owner: the qualification budget as a policy value with a fixture seam.

title: The Claude runtime read only the last assistant frame as the agent's final message; an answer resumed after the CLI's synthetic 'output token limit hit' turn lost its first 38,681 characters and a complete, valid challenger plan was refused as plan_content:absent
rule_violated: The final message is the whole final turn: every assistant text frame after the last real user event, joined across synthetic continuations
notes: Trial nine challenger (AIR-aria-challenger-planner-4e66e9b99256, managed Claude fable, 1,230 s, 80,522 output tokens, 2026-09-12T02:58Z): the answer streamed as assistant text frames of 38,681 and 3,795 chars separated by a `user` event with isSynthetic=true ('Output token limit hit. Resume directly — no apology…'); the CLI's result.result carried the second frame only; extract_final_message preferred it; _extract_envelope_json found no object; the executor projected a fallback envelope (verdict 'unverified', evidence = a 4 KB tail) and pre-submit refused plan_content:absent_or_not_object — a request-fault requeue for a plan that parses to a full 8-key plan_content when the frames are joined. extract_final_message now joins the frames of the final turn and treats a synthetic user event as a continuation, not a turn boundary; result.result wins only when it is not that turn's suffix.

title: The Codex route passed the whole prompt as one argv element, so a request that carries its round's plans and risks plus the agent contract (≈133 KB) exceeded MAX_ARG_STRLEN and the spawn died before the model with OSError (argument list too long)
rule_violated: A prompt of unbounded size rides a transport with no size limit — the child's stdin — never an argument
notes: Trial nine round-3 primary revision (AIR-aria-primary-planner-7c5f3102c977, 2026-09-12T05:18Z): request prompt 97,705 bytes + agent contract 35,273 bytes as the last argv element of `codex exec` → codex_native_execution_unavailable:OSError, control_or_transport_unavailable, no model reached. Reproduced: /bin/true with a 135,000-byte argument raises OSError [Errno 7]; 131,000 passes (Linux MAX_ARG_STRLEN = 131072). `codex exec` reads its instructions from stdin when no [PROMPT] is given; build_codex_argv no longer takes a prompt, run_codex_exec passes input=prompt and the managed path passes input_text=prompt through the existing spawn seam.

title: The planner dispatch hook handed the executor its fused claim metadata as the VALUE of one environment variable, so a round-3 cross-review envelope carrying both plans exceeded MAX_ARG_STRLEN and execve refused the executor before it started
rule_violated: Unbounded payloads cross process boundaries through files or stdin; an environment string is bounded like an argument
notes: Trial nine round-3 cross-review (AIR-aria-cross-reviewer-d56ccafa2f21, 2026-09-12T07:1xZ): planner_dispatch_hook.dispatch_one_pending_planner_request → subprocess.run(python3 ci_executor.py …, env={…, ARIA_CLAIM_METADATA: <fused envelope JSON>}) → OSError [Errno 7] Argument list too long: 'python3' (subprocess.py _execute_child). The fused envelope of a round-3 cross-review carries both plans and the surfaced risks; its JSON exceeded 131,072 bytes. The metadata now crosses as a 0600 file under <tools>/runtime/claim-metadata/<claim_id>.json named by ARIA_CLAIM_METADATA_FILE and removed once the child exits; the payload schema, forbidden-key checks and ledger-hash integrity verification are unchanged; the lease token still transits only via ARIA_LEASE_TOKEN.

title: The convergence drainer declared a step's envelope dead while its claim was merely STALE (lease expired, reaper not yet run) and forced the plan to HUMAN_REQUIRED for a harness fault the reaper would have requeued
rule_violated: A request whose fate the reaper has not yet decided is live; only a terminal request layer state ends a step
notes: Trial nine round 3 (2026-09-12T07:44Z): the hook claimed AIR-aria-cross-reviewer-d56ccafa2f21, its spawn died before the executor started (ARIA-HIGH-085), the lease expired at 07:23; the next drainer step at 07:44 saw derive_request_state == STALE, _live_request_id returned None, _ensure_envelope raised _EnvelopeDead('cross_review') and force_plan_human_required recorded convergence_envelope_dead with verdict split — after three accepted rounds. reap_stale_claims would have requeued it (a lease expiry counts one request-fault requeue; two are allowed). _live_request_id now counts STALE as live; the reaper decides.

title: The operator policy file the kernel obeys (aria-config/genesis_policy.json: monetary admission, cost caps, breaker thresholds, anchor age) was inside a write-capable spawn's write scope — not in READONLY_PATHS, so neither the sandbox ro-bind nor the write hook protected it
rule_violated: The policy that governs an agent is not the agent's to author: every file the kernel reads as policy sits under a read-only prefix for the spawn
notes: Raised by the adversarial review of tonight's commits (workflow wf_a685b12c-d36, review:tonight): bound_workspace_root (ARIA-HIGH-079) routes cost_budget, circuit_breaker and the agent-request anchor policy to <workspace>/aria-config/genesis_policy.json; native admission (_adaptive_runtime_policy) read it before tonight too. READONLY_PATHS had no aria-config entry; hooks.py denies writes on READONLY_PATHS only; implementer/worker profiles carry write_scope **. A spawn could set monetary_admission=managed_subscription or raise failure_threshold in its tree and the next dispatch of the same store would obey. aria-config/ joins READONLY_PATHS (sandbox ro-bind + hook deny + scope subtraction) and an invariant pins that every path genesis_policy loads from the workspace sits under a read-only prefix.

title: The seventh pre-merge predicate (cycle_and_turn_budget_cap, policy §14) was a placeholder: nothing bounded an implementer's Edit/Write/Bash turns, and the cycle half was declared in dollars that ORPHAN-HIGH-472 and ARIA-HIGH-074/079 had already made telemetry
rule_violated: A declared pre-merge control is a control only when the run it governs produces native evidence that it held; a placeholder that refuses every merge by name bounds nothing
notes: Raised by the parallel closeout workflow (wf_a685b12c-d36, cycle_and_turn_budget_cap lane). The cycle cap is the run-scoped job deadline (cycle.job_deadline_epoch; turn_budget.job_deadline_reached with the 120 s close-out margin the phase loop already used); the turn cap is turn_budget.IMPLEMENTER_TURN_BUDGET = 10 budgeted turns, compiled by claude_settings.build_settings as --turn-budget on the PreToolUse hook of write-scope profiles (implementer, worker); hooks.admit_budgeted_turn counts the request's admitted turns from hooks/decisions.jsonl and appends its verdict inside one state transaction so parallel tool calls cannot both be admitted as the tenth; every budgeted verdict carries a turn_budget observation; merge_authority captures hooks/decisions.jsonl and the predicate refuses on absent/malformed evidence, another cap, either refusal class, or more admitted turns than the cap. ARIA-CRITICAL-009 (seven placeholders) is closed in code by this and ARIA-CRITICAL-007; its closure mode is task_commit_and_live, so it stays open until a native merge observes all seven predicates.

title: Three ORPHAN-CRITICAL-805 artifact-index tests in tests/test_state_compact.py sat below a mid-file `if __name__ == '__main__'` guard and were never collected (14 collected, 20 declared); their fixtures carried fixed 2026-09-04/08-10 cycle stamps the 7-day sweep removes and a hash without the sha256: prefix verify_artifacts compares
rule_violated: A test that is declared but never collected is a green gate that does not exist (tests/invariants/test-target-ci-reachability class)
notes: Found while extending test_state_compact.py for ARIA-HIGH-089: pytest collected 14 tests on bd74c801c and 20 once the guard moved to the end of the file; the three revived tests needed clock-relative, writer-shaped fixtures to pass. Fixed in the same commit as ARIA-HIGH-089.

title: Two publishers wrote aria/state with different staging contracts: the maintenance lane's shell `git add -A` admitted 16 file_lock side-cars, repo_identity.json, integrity_index.json and a stale snapshot.json into the live tip, and the kernel's bounded-pathspec publish, which can neither add nor remove them, has been refused by its own tree contract and soft-reset on every attempt since 2026-09-04
rule_violated: One publisher per state branch: every commit on aria/state is built by the kernel's publish primitive from a bounded pathspec, a fresh snapshot.json and its own verification; a lane that bypasses it writes what the kernel cannot read back
notes: External audit item B2, verified live 2026-09-12 (workflow wf_171bf59b-f6a): git ls-tree origin/aria/state lists 16 zero-byte .lock blobs; the candidate's tree-contract gate run against the live tip refuses with state_snapshot_unclaimed_tree_entry:tools/cycles.jsonl.lock and passes only when the 16 lock paths are claimed; no chore(aria-state) publish since 00d97a0a9 (2026-09-04); all 8 later commits are maintenance-lane compactions, and the full verifier refuses the tip earlier still with state_snapshot_surface_mismatch:memory_beliefs because compaction rewrote ledgers without rebuilding snapshot.json. Fix: the maintenance lane publishes through `aria_kernel state publish`; a Jest invariant forbids any workflow pushing aria/state with git or adding the whole tree; publish is self-healing (prepare_publishable_snapshot classifies the parent tree against the manifest, records state_publish_inherited_entries_dropped inside the healing commit and drops the unclaimable entries index-only); compaction attests its prune (state_compacted.pruned_paths) so the continuity gate accepts only attested losses, chain_broken is refused by name regardless of ack, and an ack-accepted loss leaves a governance row. The live tip heals on the first kernel publish from any lane after this lands.

title: The implementer turn cap was a kernel literal (turn_budget.IMPLEMENTER_TURN_BUDGET = 10) that every reader hard-coded: a real root-cause implementation spends 20-40 Edit/Bash turns, so the cap was a wall rather than a runaway guard, and the operator had no policy seam to size it for the store being governed
rule_violated: A cap the operator owns is policy, resolved for the workspace the store is bound to (ARIA-HIGH-079 / ARIA-MEDIUM-082 shape), never a literal three readers retype
notes: Operator decision 2026-09-12 (delegated to the supervising session): the cap is policy with kernel default 60 budgeted turns and a derived ceiling 2 x plan_convergence.MAX_AFFECTED_PATHS = 400; a wrong-shaped or unknown-key block refuses by name rather than yielding the default; every reader resolves through tool_registry.bound_workspace_root with the store REQUIRED (an explicit None is refused); the sandboxed hook trusts argv only; the merge capture compares the recorded cap to the merged store's policy cap and the predicate refuses native_turn_budget_cap_mismatch / native_turn_budget_policy_invalid. Verified by wf_284f4dbe-940 and re-verified after fixes by wf_5be8bcb2-3ca.

title: The self-improvement lane (Plan 032 Faz 032i) was disconnected at three points: no self_improve schedule was ever seeded (add_schedule is CLI-only), the gateway daemon that would run it is disabled and dead since 2026-09-08 with no doctor organ reading its heartbeat, and propose_self_change has no kernel caller — a mission's next_action was forwarded as prompt prose, never dispatched
rule_violated: A lane exists when something runs it: schedules exist by construction, every *_NEXT_ACTION pointer has a non-CLI dispatcher, and a dead daemon is a doctor fault (ORPHAN-694 false-close class)
notes: External audit item B6, verified live 2026-09-12: live store has no gateway/schedules.jsonl and 0 gateway_schedule_changed rows; aria-gateway.service last beat 2026-09-08T09:41Z, unit disabled/inactive; open_self_improvement_missions reachable only from the scheduler's self_improve action and the CLI; the orchestrator's mission branch forwarded next_action as recommended_action prompt text. Fix: DEFAULT_SCHEDULES (doctor */30, self_improve 05:45Z, economy 05:50Z, deliver 06:30Z) ensured once per daemon start with OPERATOR_ONLY_ACTIONS carrying reasons and an invariant over SCHEDULE_ACTIONS; mission_dispatch NEXT_ACTION_CONTRACTS + GENERIC_PROJECTION_POINTERS (reason + named consumer) with an AST invariant that every pointer is compared against outside the CLI and the table; self_change_bridge mints aria/self-change-request/v1 and on acceptance calls propose_self_change, which refuses at the authority boundary (terminal, operator-held, moved-on, adjudication already open) before any write; per-mission in-flight de-dup in the drain; self_improvement in SOURCE_RANK; doctor organ gateway_heartbeat_fresh fails on a stale or absent heartbeat while schedules exist. aria-gateway.service stays parked until the operator re-enables it. Verified by wf_284f4dbe-940, fixed and re-verified by wf_f4cb3a2b-f0a.

title: test_every_executor_release_reason_is_classified scanned ci_executor.py with a text regex for any reason="..." literal, so the native fleet's admission observations (control_reason=native_readonly_runtime_prepared, sandbox_unavailable, supported_auth_status_unavailable, ...) counted as release reasons and the invariant has been red on the candidate since the fleet landed
rule_violated: An invariant reads the seam it guards (the _release_claim call sites), not every string in the module that happens to share a keyword name
notes: Reported as a pre-existing red by four independent verifiers (opus-leaf, B6, B8 and B7 lanes, identical six-entry list on a7bc52db9). The scan now walks the AST for _release_claim(..., reason=...) and collects the literal (or each branch of a conditional) — twelve release reasons, all classified; parameterised f-string reasons stay owned by the prefix tables; the six observation strings are not release reasons and no longer count.

title: Credit exhaustion downgraded work to a weaker tier: the fallback ladder (fable→opus→sonnet→glm-5.3→opus) retried an exhausted opus on sonnet for every role including the write-scope implementer, the executor really spawned sonnet on the legacy lane, and provider_cooldown_seconds had no reader anywhere, so nothing cooled a provider or requeued the request
rule_violated: Opus-only policy (2026-09-12): a decision or an implementation is never downgraded; credit exhaustion is a provider-level fact answered by a cooldown and a requeue, and read-only vendors never run write-scope roles
notes: Operator decision delegated 2026-09-12. MODEL_FALLBACK_TIER and CREDIT_FALLBACK_EFFORT are gone; the one map left is AUTH_FAILOVER_TIER (opus<->glm-5.3), used only for auth failures and only for read-only roles (model_fleet.Provider.admits_writes; a write-capable profile is never failed over to Codex/Z.ai, which also closes a gap where a writer could be admitted natively on Z.ai). Exhaustion raises ClaudeCreditExhausted carrying provider/model; the executor records provider_quota_cooldown (new provider_cooldown module, the first reader of provider_cooldown_seconds) and releases the claim REQUEUED under provider_quota_unavailable:<provider>; native admission refuses a cooled provider without a probe and refuses read-only runtimes for write-capable profiles; the worker lane records the same cooldown, honours it before claiming and backs off. Verified by wf_284f4dbe-940 (the executor spawned sonnet on the base: ['opus','sonnet'] != ['opus']); fixed and re-verified by wf_5be8bcb2-3ca.

title: The executor admission chain refused every live dispatch on 2026-09-04 and hid it: no policy file declared executor.adaptive_runtime (the native fleet never engaged; the metered gate priced raw aliases as unknown = deny), a refusal crashed before the lease was released (7 claims leaked), and a runner offline since 2026-09-08 left every scheduled run cancelled silently
rule_violated: Admission prices one alias from one function; a lease is released on any exit; the operator's stated policy is declared where the kernel reads it; a lane that cannot get a runner fails loudly
notes: External audit item B8, verified live 2026-09-12: 82 requests minted 2026-09-04 got 0 results; the ARIA-AUDIT-021 cost-reservation gate refused opus/fable as pricing_unknown and glm-5.3 by the 0.5 per_run cap; the str->DispatchFailure crash leaked 7 claims (ci-executor:gha-33920896040); the runner suderra-droplet-claude offline since 2026-09-08 09:48Z. Fix: budget.price_spawn_reservation is the one road for the gate and the fleet's admission row (AST pin over aria_kernel and tools/aria-poc); a HeldClaim ExitStack guard releases on any unwind under executor_uncaught_exit:<class>; aria-config/genesis_policy.json declares executor.adaptive_runtime managed_subscription and worktree_per_request true (each request drained in a worktree at its own target_sha inside the checkout, node_modules resolved from the parent) with an invariant that a metered cap admitting no profile model is red; a task-binding refusal is a named refused summary and the drain never counts a summary-less exit-0 child as drained; every self-hosted lane (executor, auto-cycle, daily-report, dataflow watchdog) gains the require-self-hosted-runner preflight (administration:read token) that fails by name when no online runner carries the labels. Verified by wf_00c868e8-647, fixed and re-verified by wf_5e9b9dbd-471.

title: Mission candidate admission starved and mis-explained itself: the ranked list was cut to ten before the adopter saw blocked_by, so permanently panel-blocked candidates held 5-7 of 10 slots nightly while admissible work below the cut was never offered; a retired producer minted a constant panel token with no route; refusals named no owner; no doctor organ for a dying orchestrator
rule_violated: A budget is spent on admissible work only; a refusal names its owner and the operator action from a closed vocabulary; a producer whose every output is refused by design is retired, not re-routed; a store whose last N runs all failed the same way is a doctor fault
notes: External audit item B3 re-diagnosed against origin/aria/state: the 71 mission_candidate_refused rows (43 genesis_adjudication_required + 15 operator_feedback_required + 13 unverifiable) did NOT kill the cycles (every run went on to mission_schedule_decided); the four cycle_failed exits had recorded causes (product_fitness NameError / declared-surface rejection; integrity_failed from 158 run_artifact_missing rows; test-gap-adapter budget_exceeded) already fixed on the candidate. notes: live store: tools/agent-invocations/outputs/general/round-na-human_required_adjudication-*.md (102 envelopes, 0 with a top-level verdict); tools/governance.jsonl 215/215 human_required_adjudication_folded still_escalated. rule_violated: A seam catches the faults its callee declares, never Exception; a caller and its callee are pinned to each other; a funnel counter is recorded where its fact becomes true, so its absence can be judged
notes: External audit items B1 (fixed on the candidate by 4f4918c88, pinned here) and B4-adjacent (the funnel organ was blind).
