title: Two candidate-only tests contradicted their own contracts: the memory hook's replay test demanded a LedgerIntegrityError on a torn governance tail that ORPHAN-CRITICAL-561 tolerates and heals, and the convention-history test demanded a schema refusal the reader never performed while the conventions writer let the ledger stamp a Pattern row's absent schema_version as the ledger's own format version
rule_violated: A test pins the owner's contract; a reader that decides over a history validates every row it reads; a writer states its own schema before a lower layer stamps a different one
notes: Both reds arrived with the Codex integration (4f4918c88) and were reported as pre-existing by four independent verifiers. (1) test_pending_selection_rejects_truncated_governance_snapshot expected complete_pending_observations to refuse a torn trailing governance record; the ledger's contract (ORPHAN-CRITICAL-561) is that a torn tail was never acknowledged to any caller, is tolerated on read and healed by the next append — refusing would strand every pending observation behind one interrupted write. The test now pins that contract. (2) test_recorded_convention_lookup_verifies_entire_history_before_match[schema] expected _has_recorded_convention to refuse a row under an unknown schema_version; _observation_rows verified both chains and no row schema, so a v2 row could hide a conflicting observation. _pattern_from_row is the one projection every reader uses (chain verification, then schema per row); and because the ledger stamps a silent row with its format version 2, the conventions writer now states KNOWLEDGE_GRAPH_SCHEMA_VERSION on every Pattern row before the ledger sees it, so the mixed native/declared history the historical-defaults test exercises stays readable while an explicit unknown schema is refused.

title: The first native CONVERGED plan could not be staged: staging demanded architectural_tier and validation commands from the canonical suite or a registered recipe, and no planning contract, envelope or validator ever told the planners either rule — the same contract-vs-gate class as ARIA-HIGH-078, discovered only after the plan was CONVERGED and immutable
rule_violated: A gate's rule is stated where the author reads it and enforced where the author can still act; a plan cannot converge carrying what staging will refuse
notes: Proven 2026-09-12 by running apply_engine.stage_converged_plan_for_pr on a copy of trial ten's store under the strict profile: stage_validation_command_not_declared (npx nx run shell:test) and, behind it, stage_requires_architectural_tier (body keys carried no tier). Fix: plan_contract.py is the one owner of both rules with a closed refusal vocabulary; every planning envelope carries a store-rendered plan_contract block (tiers with meanings, the canonical suite, this store's recipes) rendered as a Plan contract section, the response-validator contract states the same rules, and the three planner agent files, the layer-2 skeleton and CONTRACTS.md §12.15 mirror them (pinned by a test); submit_claim_result rejects a planner envelope that breaks the contract (claim released for retry), the executor's pre-submit gate reads the same check, submit_challenger_plan/record_revision refuse in the command path only so historical folds replay; evaluate_plan records a plan_contract_complete gate row that turns CONVERGED into NEXT_ROUND_REQUIRED and the drainer carries every refused entry into the primary revision as escaped data under one obligation per reason; staging resolves declared commands through the same resolver. Five further implementer-seam gaps found on the way are ARIA-HIGH-104. Verified by wf_6dbb11ea-0ba (its replay of the real trial-ten ledger names the eight violations that killed staging).

title: Five implementer-to-merge seam gaps no contract states: the required validation_commands request field is never written; auto_merge demands a format:check run outside the canonical suite; the implementer contract reads key_changes[].file while the skeleton emits strings; its mandated Closes: trailer does not fit a plan-originated change; minted must_satisfy rows drift from the request schema
rule_violated: Every field or command a later gate demands is stated by the contract the agent reads (ARIA-HIGH-078 / ARIA-HIGH-103 class)
notes: Found by the plan-contract lane (wf_6dbb11ea-0ba) reading the implementation envelope and the gates behind it: (1) aria/agent-request/v1 lists validation_commands as REQUIRED and render_invocation_prompt prints a Validation commands section, but create_agent_invocation_request never writes the field; (2) auto_merge._HYGIENE_DIMENSIONS demands a verified exit-0 run containing format:check, which is not in CANONICAL_VALIDATION_COMMANDS and is named by no must_satisfy obligation; (3) aria-implementer.md step 2 reads key_changes[].file while the layer-2 skeleton defines strings and plan_synthesizer emits paths (apply_engine._intended_files_from_plan accepts both); (4) step 7 mandates a Closes: aria-findings/F-V9-NN trailer while a converged plan's change chain is keyed plan:<plan_id> and no gate checks the trailer; (5) kernel-minted must_satisfy items carry {id, kind, description, source} while agent_contract._ensure_must_satisfy requires {id, statement}. Three sibling gaps in the same seam were fixed by ARIA-HIGH-103's commit (completed_at stamped by the bridge; details.implementation shape; the content_hash-on-disk wording). NOT done in this batch; owner claude; the first native implementer trial will hit whichever of these is reached first.

title: The kernel lanes checked the code repository out shallow (actions/checkout default fetch-depth 1): the twin saw one commit and published an empty history layer as a healthy map, the incremental refresh never ran, and the anchor gate had been taught to tolerate the condition (a workaround by its own docstring) instead of the checkout being whole and a partial clone being refused by name
rule_violated: A kernel workspace is a whole clone; a reader whose history is unavailable refuses by name rather than publishing an empty layer or guessing a terminal fact
notes: External audit item B5, verified live 2026-09-12: the runner log of the run that wrote the live map shows --depth=1; twin._history_layers counted one commit; refresh.reason=unknown_anchor on every run; agent_invocations._repo_is_shallow softened the anchor check ('neither ARIA lane overrides it'). Fix: fetch-depth: 0 on every kernel lane (auto-cycle, executor, eval, readiness-claim, capability-probe, kernel, kernel-fast; the state-branch checkout is the kernel's own depth-less fetch and needed no change), an invariant that derives the governed set from every workflow that provisions the kernel (15 lanes, watchdog excluded by construction); git_probe.is_shallow_checkout is the one probe; twin refuses a shallow checkout at both publishers' entry and a failed git log by name (twin_history_unavailable) instead of writing an empty layer; the anchor gate raises anchor_history_unavailable_shallow before any ANCHOR_STALE row is written on a shallow clone, and the softening is deleted; cycle fixtures are committed repositories. First run after merge on the persistent workspace fetches --unshallow once. Verified by wf_00c868e8-647, fixed and re-verified by wf_5be8bcb2-3ca.

title: The post-CONVERGED memory hook was handed signer_key_fp=None on every profile and the only knowledge signer lived inside the V9 runner behind pr_create, so every live (standard) cycle disclosed needs_signing and nothing completed it — knowledge-graph/conventions.jsonl was never created; the cycle key's git signing config was restorable only while its key file still existed
rule_violated: A pillar the cycle claims to activate must be reachable in the profile the cycle runs under; a snapshot the recovery depends on lives where the lane's pre-clean cannot reach it, and is consumed only by a decision
notes: External audit item B7, verified live 2026-09-12: no conventions.jsonl in the live store; every memory_hook row status=needs_signing; the V9 runner's on_signer_ready callback (the only completion path) fired only under pr_create. Fix: cycle_phases.knowledge_signer mints one ephemeral ed25519 identity per converged cycle for every profile holding the new knowledge_record cell of ACTION_PERMISSIONS (standard/strict/autonomous), registers the public half in knowledge-graph/signers.jsonl (kg_signers) before handing out the fingerprint, signs the hypothesis row in the converging cycle, replays every earlier needs_signing disclosure (reasons cycle_signer_unavailable / cycle_append_failed) under the cycle signer, and revokes before the cycle proceeds; the V9 runner re-mints the same identity idempotently and no longer receives on_signer_ready. The mint/revoke pair is a transaction on the checkout's local git signing config: the snapshot lives in .git/aria-signing-config-snapshots/ (the lane's git clean -ffdx wipes aria-debts/keys but never .git/), the startup prune unwinds every key-less snapshot with no age gate and inherits across crashed cycles, the workspace root is resolved once so relative and absolute callers name the same key, and the restore returns a four-valued decision (SigningConfigRestore) — an undecided restore (git timeout, unreadable snapshot) keeps its snapshot for the next prune, with user.signingkey released by the last git call so the retry is sound. Integrated on the candidate after ARIA-HIGH-105; the integration also found the c2 memory-hook suite red since ARIA-HIGH-103 (a private copy of the converging plan body) and replaced it with the shared converging_plan_content fixture. Verified by wf lanes reverify-b7-before/edges/qdzyf1gk; the pass-2 residual the re-verifier raised is the SigningConfigRestore change, proved by I-B7-GIT-10/11 (mutation-checked).

title: open_state_store assumed the state branch instead of reading it from the store's own lineage, so a store materialised for any other branch was judged against aria/state's published tip (its own genesis 'not at tip', every production surface 'lost'); and a workspace with committed daily anchors but no state-store worktree reported 'chain broken: got_prev=None' instead of naming the missing restore
rule_violated: A store's identity comes from the store, never from a caller's default; a refusal names the actionable fact, not a symptom of it
notes: Found live in trial eleven (2026-09-12 21:23Z and 21:49Z) while running the kernel's own `autonomy run` against the converged trial store on a FULL checkout. Run 1: no state-store worktree -> the committed daily anchors became the reference and the fresh probe was refused as state_continuity_chain_broken:expected_prev=<anchor> got_prev=None (trial ten's subset workspace carried no anchors, so this never showed). Run 2: a store bootstrapped with `state checkout --branch aria/state-trial-eleven-20260912` was opened by resolve_continuity_reference/store_is_at_published_tip through open_state_store(repo_root) with the DEFAULT branch, so _publication_anchor read refs/remotes/origin/aria/state and the verdict was state_continuity_store_not_at_tip:head=<trial genesis> tip=<production tip> plus every production surface as lost. Fix: store_lineage_branch reads the branch from the GENESIS record at the lineage's single root commit (the worktree is detached by design, so HEAD cannot say; the genesis record is hash-chained under every publish); open_state_store derives it, checks a caller-named branch against it (state_store_branch_mismatch) and refuses a lineage without a genesis record (state_store_branch_unresolvable); the CLI's --branch is the checkout target and an open-time check; assess_memory_continuity names a fresh probe against a committed anchor state_continuity_store_not_restored:anchor=<root> (run `state checkout`) and keeps chain_broken for a probe naming another predecessor. Also fixed in this commit: the capability roster missed mission_dispatch.py as an observational reader of agent_invocation_results (test_capability_specs_cover_discovered_surface_writers_and_consumers had been red since ARIA-HIGH-092's commit bd6e6191b).

title: The native fleet admission treated a status probe that did not answer (a 20 s `claude auth status` timeout under load) like a vendor refusal and handed a read-only role to the next vendor — trial eleven's primary plan ran on openai after two dispatches had admitted anthropic; conversely a logged-out CLI's exit 1 with a readable document would have read as a stall and blocked failover
rule_violated: An undecided observation is retried within a liveness bound and never laundered into a decision; the fleet fails over only on what the vendor or the ledger actually said
notes: Live evidence: trial eleven dispatch-03 (2026-09-12 20:42-20:51Z, load ~7): anthropic row status_reason=status_timeout, auth_observation=unknown, controls unknown; admission eligible_routes=[openai/gpt-6-astra]; the primary plan was authored by Codex although the operator decision (opus is a leaf; cross-vendor failover for read-only roles on AUTH reasons only) forbids it. Fix: StatusDecision (AVAILABLE/UNAVAILABLE/UNDECIDED) is a required, contradiction-checked field of every _RuntimeStatusObservation; status_probe.observe_until_decided retries only UNDECIDED probes (3 attempts, 2/5 s backoff, one AdmissionClock per admission; the policy's recheck_timeout_seconds stays the per-attempt cap; native_admission_budget_seconds derives from it); native_admission.py owns the ladder: a provider is passed only on a DECIDED unavailable observation or a cooldown; the first provider in contention that stays undecided halts the admission as PROVIDER_UNDECIDED (no route, request stays PENDING, no attempt burned, harness-class release native_runtime_provider_undecided; the planner hook backs off one tick); a host that cannot bind its controls after a decided-available auth halts as PROVIDER_CONTROL_UNAVAILABLE by name; tools/aria-poc/status_answers.py classifies the vendor's DOCUMENT/LINE before the exit code (Claude Code 2.1.269 prints {loggedIn:false} and exits 1; Codex prints 'Not logged in' and exits 1) so a logged-out session is DECIDED unavailable and fails over; every candidate row carries decision and probe {attempts, undecided_reasons, backoff_seconds}. Integration: the two release-site invariants (v12 RELEASE_02 and test_requeue_fault_ownership) now share one reading (tests/_helpers/release_sites.py) after the second scanner refused the refusal record's attribute; a Z.ai transport that does not answer is pinned through the ladder as provider_undecided(zai), never a control gap or an openai fail-over. Verified by wf_9eb2e54f-ec1 (verify must_fix -> fix -> reverify must_fix on the scanner regression, closed at integration).

title: The connected candidate carried 23 red tests since the Codex integration: Prettier rewrote byte-pinned capture fixtures under their manifests, verify_convention_signer had no production caller, nx requirements were matched by substring, four suites hand-loaded ci_executor, and two planner prompts lacked their pedagogy pairs
rule_violated: A red test is a defect in the tree until proven otherwise; a capture fixture is immutable bytes, a dormant control is a control that does not exist, and a requirement is matched by identity
notes: Roots, each closed in the tree: (1) prompt_render_legacy/*.input.json, prompt_render_issued_v4/*.request.json+*.fused.json and five runtime_archive_legacy files were reformatted by Prettier at integration while their capture manifests / SHA256SUMS still named the captured bytes; the captured bytes are restored (json.dumps indent-2 sorted / compact shapes reproduce every recorded sha256) and aria-kernel/tests/fixtures/ is an archive_immutable formatter exclusion. (2) knowledge_graph.verify_convention_signer was dormant (test_control_reachability); reconcile_convention_promotion now verifies the hypothesis signer and answers signer_unverified. (3) validation_matrix_gate matched required nx commands by substring so `nx test P` never satisfied `run-many --target=test --projects=P`; required_test_cmd_satisfied_by compares nx run identity. (4) Four suites loaded ci_executor by hand under divergent module names; tests/_helpers/executor_module.py is the one loader. (5) v31 d2/d3 pins read ci_executor.main after main split it into _main. (6) The kg public-API pin lacked the B7 signer surface. (7) Two hermetic socket tests lacked the allowlist marker. (8) aria-primary-planner.md / aria-cross-reviewer.md imperatives lacked pedagogy pairs; added inside the tier-2 token budget.

title: gh_token_factory wired git commit signing only when <workspace>/.git was a directory, so in every linked worktree — the executor's per-request worktrees, a trial's task-source — the mint silently skipped the config, every commit went unsigned, and a --local write there would have signed the whole shared checkout
rule_violated: The checkout a transaction runs on is what git says it is; a per-cycle identity is scoped to the worktree that uses it, and a wiring that did not happen is refused by name, never skipped silently
notes: Evidence: trial eleven's task-source .git is a 50-byte gitdir file (linked worktree of /var/aqua-saas); _configure_git_commit_signing returned at `if not git_dir.is_dir()` and _restore_git_commit_signing answered ABSENT, so no allowed-signers file, no snapshot, no config — and had the test been dropped, `git config --local` in a linked worktree writes the COMMON config shared by every worktree (the operator's checkout, every other lane). Fix: SigningCheckout resolves `git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir --git-common-dir`; the allowed-signers file and snapshots live in the private git dir (.git/ or .git/worktrees/<name>/); config scope is --local on a main checkout and --worktree on a linked one, with extensions.worktreeConfig enabled once in the common config (refused by name when core.worktree or a true core.bare is present); a git that does not answer is UNDECIDED in restore and prune, never ABSENT; the mint returns GitSigningWiring (configured/scope/reason) on SigningKey.git_signing and the V9 runner refuses IMPLEMENTATION_REQUEST_REFUSED/git_signing_unconfigured (governance implementation_git_signing_unconfigured) before an implementer turn is spent. Proof: test_phase_v31_p_linked_worktree_signing (6; all fail on the pre-change factory), test_implementer_merge_seam refusal test, the 46 existing B7 tests unchanged. Sibling registered separately: ARIA-HIGH-115 (the executor lane never mints a signing identity at all — the V9 runner revokes its key before the implementer exists).

title: The implementer's signing identity does not survive to the lane that commits: the V9 runner mints and revokes the cycle key inside its own run, the executor lane mints nothing in the request worktree, and the outcome validator requires a signer_key_fp the agent cannot know — so every executor-lane implementation result is refused (empty fp) or refused (fabricated fp fails verify-commit)
rule_violated: The identity a gate verifies against is minted where the commits are made and stamped by the kernel that holds it, never by the agent
notes: Trace: AutonomousV9ImplementationRunner.run mints the key, stages, issues the envelope and REVOKES the key in `finally` — the implementer is claimed later by tools/aria-poc/ci_executor.py in a per-request worktree (_add_request_worktree) where no signing config, key or fingerprint exists; the prompt says 'commit with the per-cycle signing key' and demands details.implementation.signer_key_fp; plan_convergence.record_implementation_outcome requires it non-empty and plan_convergence_bridge verifies branch_tip_sha against it with `git verify-commit --raw` in the process cwd (repo=None). Cost attribution reads ARIA_CYCLE_SIGNER_KEY_FP which nothing exports (SHA256:no-key). Design: for role=implementation the executor mints the cycle key INSIDE the request worktree at claim (worktree-scoped config, ARIA-HIGH-114), registers the public half in kg_signers, stamps signer_key_fp on the submitted response itself (kernel-owned, overriding the agent), exports the fingerprint to the cost record, and revokes on release/submit; the bridge verifies against the registered public key (an allowed-signers file built from kg_signers via `-c gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile`, run in the request worktree) so verification does not depend on the process cwd. Pin: an executor-lane implementation run whose commit is signed by the key the executor minted lands the IMPL row; the same run with the fingerprint removed or another key is refused commit_signature_unverified. Blocks halka 4→5 of the live chain.

title: The kernel test suite left one scratch directory pair per pytest process (tests/__init__.py mkdtemp for ARIA_TOOLS_DIR and ARIA_WORKSPACE_BASE) plus per-test mkdtemp leftovers in three modules, so a day of batteries under TMPDIR=/dev/shm accumulated ~1100 directories in RAM on the shared host
rule_violated: A fixture owns the lifetime of what it creates: a scratch directory is removed by the process or the test that minted it
notes: Observed 2026-09-13 17:00Z on the droplet: /dev/shm held 2173 entries, 1110 of them aria-* test directories older than 12 h (aria-test-tools-/aria-test-workspaces- 319 each, aria-codex-bin*/aria-codex-home* ~45, aria-fleet-empty-path- 28, signer-registry- 39), 1.5 GB of tmpfs. Fix: tests/__init__.py mints the two process-lifetime roots through _process_scratch_dir (atexit rmtree); test_model_fleet_and_codex uses one module-level empty PATH dir removed at exit and addCleanup for the codex home/bin dirs; test_knowledge_signer's SignerRegistryTests addCleanup its root. Proof: a pytest run of the three modules adds no /dev/shm entries (1033 before and after).

title: The daily state-maintenance compaction strips hot artifacts older than 7 days and drops their index rows, but the 3825 thin raw-finding rows that point into those artifacts stay, so the executor lane's integrity gate reads every one as raw_pointer_corrupt and has refused to publish the live aria/state store since 2026-09-12 (3898 issues; runs 34745606502, 34762798856)
rule_violated: Compaction is one transaction over every surface that references an artifact, and a verifier tells an artifact the kernel's own maintenance stripped (attested) apart from one that is corrupt
notes: Live evidence (quarantine-evidence-34762798856, artifact 10320819613): all 93 ledgers valid; runtime_artifacts status failed with 3898 issues = 3825 raw_pointer_corrupt (every raw-findings.jsonl row; all thin — json_pointer into the run artifact, no inline finding; cycles cyc-20260904T093220Z-auto 1773 + cyc-20260904T194353Z-auto 2052) + 36 artifact_ref_missing + 36 artifact_index_ref_missing + artifact_index_empty_with_run_refs; artifact-index.jsonl 0 rows, run-artifacts/hot empty, .archive/runtime empty, no retention/events.jsonl (retention_apply never ran on the live store); archives/artifact_index-compact-20260905/0911/0912 present; governance carries nine state_compacted rows (retain_days 7); aria-state-maintenance.yml runs daily and published each compacted store green (its publish verifies the snapshot, not the runtime pointers). Both the main (43f0aa3bf6) and candidate (88f64f7e6e) verifiers refuse the tree identically. Root: _strip_hot_artifacts + _compact_artifact_index (ORPHAN-CRITICAL-805) strip the artifact and its index row but leave raw-findings rows and runs.jsonl refs that name it, and verify_runtime_artifacts has no notion of a compacted artifact. Fix shape (tier 1): compaction records what it stripped on a declared ledger (runtime_artifact_compactions: artifact_id, uri, cycle, compacted_at, archive path) in the same transaction, archives and drops the raw-findings rows that point into stripped artifacts (nothing is lost: they ride the compact archive), and verify_runtime_artifacts classifies a run/raw pointer whose artifact is on that ledger as compacted (valid, counted separately) rather than missing/corrupt; the next maintenance run then heals the live store by construction (presence predicate, as index compaction already heals a stranded index) with no manual repair of aria/state. Pin: a store compacted past the window verifies ok with compacted counts, and a store with a truly missing artifact (not on the ledger) still fails; the maintenance lane's publish verifies runtime pointers too. Deadline moved 2026-09-16 -> 2026-09-22 on 2026-09-16: the fix is the aria/state restore that follows PR #1553's merge (2026-09-15 restart plan, 9.2); the row was branch-only, so no sweep had seen it.

title: An adapter could be registered without a fixture-backed evidence contract: agent-harness-security-adapter shipped findings the validator could not read (evidence_error, quarantined on the spot in trial eleven), capped read_paths at 200 and carried an unknown ref field, and nothing at the manifest-sync door required a fixture case the validator accepts
rule_violated: Every registered adapter proves against a fixture that the validator accepts its output before the registry accepts the adapter; the PR lane that pins it fires on the adapter directory
notes: Integrated from lane/aria-high-098 (wf_21487a46-bd7 rounds 1-2, wf_4a4fb60b-126 round 3). The contract refuses at cycle._phase_tool_manifest_sync (fixture_cases_missing / fixture_case_expects_non_ok_run / fixture_case_malformed); expected_run_status is the one reader shared with fixture_runner.evaluate_fixture_expectation; both kernel PR lanes fire on tools/aria-adapters/** and the suite selector maps the directory; the PR-time pin runs every shipped manifest through the real fixture runner (budget_exceeded reported as unverified by name; the two heaviest adapters are observed only in CI).

title: The fixture path guard walked up from the tools root accepting only a .git DIRECTORY, so a workspace that is itself a linked worktree (trial eleven, every executor per-request worktree) was stepped past, discovery fell back to the state store and nine of ten registry fixture paths were judged fixture_path_escape_outside_repo
rule_violated: A checkout root is the directory holding .git whether a directory or a gitdir: pointer; one parser answers every walker, and the state store is told apart by its GENESIS record, not by the shape of its .git
notes: Integrated from lane/aria-high-098. checkout_root.py owns read_gitdir_pointer / resolve_git_directory / resolve_git_common_directory / is_git_worktree_marker / discover_checkout_root; fixture_runner._discover_git_root delegates, the guard consults the store's declared bound_repo_root first, latest_fixture_status takes workspace_root; agent_invocations' anchor gate and gh_token_factory's SigningCheckout (ARIA-HIGH-114) read the same parser.

title: Event-schema identity regressions do not reach the native cycle failure decision
rule_violated: Detected native architecture regressions must change cycle progression; counts must not hide introduced event-schema identities
notes: Bounded event-schema identity and registered postcheck-to-terminal fix. Wider ARIA-HIGH-045 remains OPEN. Outer repair/resume is the services specialist next core phase; native model/merge/learning evidence remains separate. Genuine RED and unchanged GREEN were reviewed by a different agent; clean-main publication uses its own selected run. Re-registered 2026-09-11 on the Claude-stacked branch: ARIA-HIGH-063 stayed reserved in the Codex publication worktree registry that never pushed. Registered on the connected candidate at integration (2026-09-13): the code, tests and ARCHITECTURE.md section from 67709d1e03 (fix/aria-event-regression-progression-20260911-v2) are already in the candidate body; this row and the review file carry the finding.

title: integrity.verify_integrity builds an issues list it never returns, so doctor._check_integrity reports integrity_drift:0_issues when only the runtime artifacts fail — the doctor undercounted the very verdict that kept the executor lane from publishing
rule_violated: A verdict's issues are returned to every reader that reports on it; a count of zero must mean zero
notes: Observed by the ARIA-HIGH-117 implementer and verifier independently (wf_a4e68c08-436): verify_integrity computes the runtime_artifacts issues but the returned dict carries only the tools-ledger issues, so the doctor's integrity organ prints integrity_drift:0_issues on the quarantined live store whose runtime pointers fail with 3898 issues. Fix: return the full issue list (tools + workspace + runtime_artifacts) from verify_integrity, have doctor read the same count the executor's integrity verify step prints, and pin with the quarantined-store shape (doctor FAIL naming the runtime-artifact issue count).

title: The ARIA-HIGH-104 integration landed two source-marker assertions (assertIn of a literal in aria_kernel source read by the test) that the Plan 026R §H.1 invariant refuses, so tests/test_source_marker_invariant.py was red on the candidate
rule_violated: A test proves behaviour or a node shape, never that a substring exists in the kernel's source
notes: Found by the ARIA-HIGH-117 fix agent as a pre-existing red on the base tree (f21c142f62): test_must_satisfy_shape.py lines 323 and 359 read cross_review_bridge.py / autonomy_orchestrator.py / human_required_adjudication.py and assertIn'd call-site substrings. Both now parse the module AST: every must_satisfy_item(description=<Name>) is refused by shape and the producers call key_change_obligation; the re-mint's must_satisfy keyword is the upcast_sealed_items(...) assignment, proven by mutation (a verbatim list(dead.get(...)) copy fails the pin). test_source_marker_invariant green.

title: ARIA copes with a changed condition (failover, retry, backfill, quarantine) and names what it refused, but its own refusals and HUMAN_REQUIRED records are not a mission source, so a changed environment (CLI output format, provider quota, adapter drift, lapsed waivers) waits for an operator instead of becoming a plan the kernel-self-change lane can carry
rule_violated: A condition the kernel can name is a condition the kernel can plan against; adaptation to the environment is a mission, not an operator chore
notes: Operator direction 2026-09-14: 'aria koşulların değişmesine de kendini adapte edebilmeli'. Today: self_improvement.scan_signals feeds missions from capability gaps, funnel stalls, delivery gaps, MCP quarantine and doctor FAIL only; named refusals (provider_undecided, state_publish_runtime_artifacts_unverified, native_task_binding refusals, tool-degraded escalations, lapsed dormant-surface waivers) and HUMAN_REQUIRED kinds are not signals; kernel-path changes are refused for self-merge (implementation_safety kernel self-mod = Plan 009 operator lane) with no automatic path from a refusal to a drafted kernel PR. Design: (1) every named refusal / escalation class becomes a Signal with its evidence rows; (2) an adaptation surface split — self-merge for tools/aria-adapters/**, fixtures, policy JSON and waiver re-dating with measured evidence; operator-approved PR drafted by ARIA for aria-kernel/** core, identity and security; notify-only for credentials/subscriptions/prod infra; (3) every adaptation carries a before/after proof the way the lane discipline does. Operator decides the exact self-merge set. Sequenced after ARIA-HIGH-115 and ARIA-HIGH-097 and the first live end-to-end merge.

title: The write-capable implementer spawn is bwrap-contained with only the workspace bound and .git/ read-only, so inside a linked per-request worktree git fails 'not a git repository: <checkout>/.git/worktrees/<name>' and in a main checkout 'git add' cannot create .git/index.lock — the agent's git commit the identity contract relies on cannot run in the real sandbox in either lane
rule_violated: A containment that a role's own contract cannot execute inside is a refusal by accident; the write-capable implementer's sandbox binds exactly what its commit needs (the worktree, its private git dir and the common object store, writable) and nothing more
notes: Found by the ARIA-HIGH-115 reverifier (wf_85686100-726) and reproduced on this host with the production bind shape: bwrap --ro-bind /usr ... --bind <worktree> <worktree> --chdir <worktree> -- git status in a linked worktree → fatal: not a git repository: <checkout>/.git/worktrees/req-1 (the common dir and the worktree's private git dir are outside the bound workspace); in a main checkout git add → Unable to create .git/index.lock: Read-only file system (.git/ and aria-debts/ are in READONLY_PATHS, pinned by test_phase_v31_p_preconditions). The HIGH-115 e2e proves the identity chain through a pass-through bwrap and says so in its docstring. Fix shape (tier 1): the sandbox profile for a write-capable implementer derives its binds from the checkout (checkout_root: worktree + resolve_git_directory + resolve_git_common_directory, writable) and keeps aria-debts/keys/ unreadable to the agent (the key is used by git, not read by the agent — bind the private key path read-only for git only, or run the commit through a kernel-owned helper outside the sandbox that the agent invokes); pin with a real bwrap child committing in a linked worktree. Blocks halka 4 in production regardless of HIGH-115.

title: ARIA has no nightly fitness measure of its own precision/recall: the goldset curator exists but the live store holds one proposal, judge calibration is reported but never scored against ground truth, so every promotion decision the RSI ladder (ARIA-HIGH-122, ORPHAN-HIGH-689) would make has no measured 'better' to rest on
rule_violated: A system that promotes itself measures itself first: a nightly goldset run yields precision/recall per adapter and per judge, and promotion reads that number, never a self-report
notes: Post-chain plan item 1. Design: a versioned goldset (operator-confirmed TP/FP findings, sampled from raw findings + operator feedback) replayed every night through the judges and adapters; fitness-reports.jsonl gains precision/recall/ECE per role; promotion_veto and genesis EVAL_WINDOW read it.

title: ARIA's 'did I break something' answer is only as good as the target repository's tests, and ~16 platform projects sit in CI unit-test quarantine, so a change ARIA lands in a quarantined project is verified by nothing the kernel can see
rule_violated: The impact closure a plan is judged against includes the test floor of every closure node; a node with no live tests is a coverage gap the plan must answer, and lifting the quarantine is a standing mission
notes: Post-chain plan item 2. Design: plan_coverage marks closure nodes whose project is quarantined as untested_node obligations (waivable only by the critic with a reason); a standing operator mission 'lift the CI quarantine' seeded from the quarantine list, one project per night, with the kernel's own PR chain.

title: Every human decision ARIA asks for (HUMAN_REQUIRED records, waiver renewals, mission opening, adjudication outcomes) lives in ledgers and CLI flags; the operator is the throughput bottleneck (73 adjudications, 215 folded rows on the live store) with no single surface to see and answer them
rule_violated: A system that escalates to a human owns the human's queue: one inbox, one action per item, every answer a ledger row
notes: Post-chain plan item 3. Design: an operator inbox (MCP read view + one CLI verb per answer kind, or a minimal web page over the same ledgers) listing open HUMAN_REQUIRED records, lapsing waivers, pending missions and adjudication outcomes with one-line decisions; every decision is a governance row.

title: Deadlines the kernel itself enforces (dormant-surface waivers, load-sensitive budgets, signing-key grace windows, retention windows) fire at the gate with no early warning; the eight waivers that lapsed on 2026-09-13 turned every kernel lane red on main the next morning
rule_violated: A deadline the kernel will enforce is a deadline the kernel announces first: the doctor names every clock-bound rule due within seven days
notes: Post-chain plan item 4. Design: a deadlines doctor organ reading every clock-bound rule (waiver expires_on, budget deadlines, retention cutoffs, key grace windows) and WARNing seven days ahead, FAIL on lapse; the daily report carries the list.

title: The knowledge graph records that a convention entered a prompt (context-usage) but never whether it helped: no correlation from convention use to plan outcome exists, so 'ARIA learns' cannot be shown or refuted
rule_violated: A memory whose value is claimed is a memory whose value is measured: usage joined to outcome, per convention
notes: Post-chain plan item 5. Design: join context-usage rows to plan outcomes (converged/refused/merged/regressed) per convention; conventions whose presence correlates with worse outcomes decay faster; the fitness report carries the per-convention lift.

title: The containment contract (ARIA-HIGH-123) is proven only on this host: GitHub-hosted runners cannot run the real-bwrap pins (no provisioning step; 24.04 AppArmor restricts unprivileged userns), so CI skips every sandbox pin and the containment probe alone is the canary
rule_violated: A security property CI cannot exercise is a property CI cannot defend; the kernel lane provisions the containment it proves
notes: Post-chain plan item 6. Design: aria-kernel.yml installs bubblewrap and enables unprivileged userns (or runs the containment pins on the self-hosted lane by name), and a pin refuses a run where the real-bwrap tests skipped silently.

title: The hook broker (ARIA-HIGH-123) is the one privileged interface from the sandbox to the kernel; it was verified inside its own lane but has had no independent adversarial review as an attack surface (verb vocabulary, request forgery, socket ownership, denial of service by a hostile agent)
rule_violated: A privileged boundary gets its own adversarial review, separate from the lane that built it
notes: Post-chain plan item 7. A dedicated adversarial lane over the broker: verb allowlist, per-request authorization, rate/size bounds, socket permissions, replay, and the client's failure modes.

title: When main goes red after a change ARIA merged, the path back is a finding folded into the next cycle's plan; there is no fast, evidence-bound revert candidate, so a broken main waits a night
rule_violated: A regression the kernel attributes to its own merge yields a revert candidate within the same run it was observed, under the same gates
notes: Post-chain plan item 8. Design: change_outcome's regression attribution mints a revert-candidate proposal (git revert of the merged commit) through the normal apply gate and PR path, flagged for operator approval; no autonomous revert on main.

title: The kernel lives inside the repository it operates on: pointing ARIA at a second repository or a customer's codebase is not a supported shape (adapters, policy and state layout assume this monorepo), which blocks the Legal/finance product line the operator is pursuing
rule_violated: A product kernel is separable from any one target: workspace, policy and adapters are inputs, the kernel is a package
notes: Post-chain plan item 9. Design: package the kernel as an installable unit with a target-repo manifest (workspace root, policy, adapter set, state branch), prove it on a second small repository end to end, then on the Legal MVP corpus.

title: The kernel suite was green on one host only: three fixtures symlinked the operator checkout's /var/aqua-saas/node_modules and eleven sandbox-proving tests need a bwrap the hosted kernel CI lane never provisioned, so the candidate's first hosted run (34853938794) failed fourteen tests the droplet passes
rule_violated: A test's dependencies come from the checkout under test and the lane that runs it provisions what the tests prove; a suite that passes on one machine is not a gate
notes: PR #1553 aria-kernel job 104008882051 (2026-09-14): 4 failures from Path('/var/aqua-saas/node_modules') (Codex-era hardcode, 4f4918c88c), 11 from SandboxUnavailable (bwrap absent or unusable on ubuntu-latest). Fix: tests._helpers.node_modules.installed_node_modules (the checkout's own install, missing package named) + an AST pin refusing host-bound literals in the suite; the kernel lane runs ensure-sandbox-backend (one definition with the executor/nightly lanes) and the action names bwrap presence and the AppArmor userns knob when it refuses. Whether the hosted image can confine at all is decided by the run, not assumed.

title: aria-kernel-fast.yml runs the identical full kernel suite as aria-kernel.yml with less provisioning (no npm ci, no sandbox backend) under a 60-minute budget the 48-minute suite plus setup cannot meet on a hosted runner, so every kernel PR now carries a duplicate lane that ends cancelled
rule_violated: One definition per gate: a second lane that runs the same suite is drift with a CI bill, and a lane whose budget cannot contain its work is a cancellation, not a signal
notes: PR #1553 run 34853938795 (aria-kernel-fast/unittest): cancelled at 60m15s by its own timeout while aria-kernel (run 34853938794) finished the same suite (Ran 6484 tests in 2901 s) inside its 75-minute budget. aria-suite-run.sh takes no mode; both lanes invoke it without arguments, so fast has been the full suite since 2026-08-27 when its 15-minute budget was raised to 60 rather than its scope narrowed (ARIA-MEDIUM-020). ORPHAN-MEDIUM-769 already deleted aria-kernel-full.yml for the same reason. Fix: delete the fast lane; aria-kernel.yml is the one kernel lane on PR and on main push, and inherits the fast lane's docs/adr/** PR path so a SPEC/ADR amendment still fires it; every pin that named the fast lane pins its absence.

title: The kernel suite costs three hours per pre-push on the shared host and 48 minutes hosted (6,484 tests; the affected selector picks most of it), so one HIGH costs a day and the adaptation loop and measured promotions cannot validate a self-change inside a night
rule_violated: A validation loop the system cannot afford is not a loop; the suite runs in parallel and in risk tiers so the fast answer arrives in minutes
notes: Push #7 pre-push: Ran 2512 tests in 11298 s (171 modules); push #8: 231 modules; hosted lane 2901 s. Fix: xdist/process pools with per-process scratch dirs, concurrent affected run, seam-proving slow tier separated; targets pinned over the timing ledger (pre-push < 30 min droplet, hosted < 25 min).

title: The chain has only ever carried changes to ARIA itself; no task in apps/ has met the executor lane, the apply gate or the merge predicates, so 'ARIA works' cannot be said and the post-chain measurement plan would measure the kernel's own repairs
rule_violated: A system is proven on the work it exists for; external task zero runs the full chain on one small real apps/ task with no manual repair before fitness is built on top
notes: Milestone 0 of the revised plan. Operator picks the task; every refusal it meets becomes a finding before HIGH-125/126 start; the section records plan id, PR number and merge outcome.

title: Every seam the live chain touched failed under tests that mocked the very process that failed (HIGH-117 compaction, HIGH-123 git in the sandbox, HIGH-124 kernel authority and package import inside the sandbox, MEDIUM-134 the suite off the droplet); nothing requires a seam to be proven by a real process
rule_violated: A seam is proven by a real process, not by a mock of it: a closed seam registry, one real-process test per seam, and a pin that refuses a seam without one or a spawn site outside the registry
notes: The ORPHAN-694 false-close class made structural. Tier 3: registry of seam modules + marked real-process tests (real bwrap, linked worktree, unix socket, ssh-agent, executor child) + AST walk over spawn primitives; runs on the lane ARIA-MEDIUM-139 provides.

title: The only host that confines the kernel's sandbox is the production droplet (Suderra), and the hosted CI image keeps unprivileged user namespaces under AppArmor, so the kernel lane and the executor lane either cannot prove containment or run beside the tenants
rule_violated: A lane that proves containment runs on a host that confines and that production does not share
notes: Operator decision (owner okan): a small dedicated runner VM with bubblewrap and the managed CLIs, labelled for the kernel lane and the executor lane; the droplet keeps only tenant services. Until decided, hosted CI's verdict is whatever ensure-sandbox-backend names, and PR-3 does not merge on a red kernel lane. Wiring (labels, workflow runs-on, capability probe) is claude's once decided.

title: A cycle cut by its deadline inside a work phase skipped its own close-out, reported the store it never verified as integrity_failed (the one verdict the orchestrator fails closed on), persisted no phase ledger, and fixture_refresh began suites with no runway left — two trial-eleven cycles on 2026-09-15
rule_violated: integrity_failed is reserved for a store that failed verification; a cycle's close-out phases run whatever the deadline did to its work; every phase outcome reaches the store
notes: Ring 3 reruns cyc-20260914T231106Z-auto (5400 s) and cyc-20260915T004952Z-auto (10800 s): tool phase 64 and 150 min under host load (three to four adapters at their budgets), fixture_refresh 3.5 min per adapter, the deadline alarm inside it, every later phase skipped by job_deadline_reached, artifact_integrity {} -> integrity_valid False -> integrity_failed over an index that verified 9/9; the phases dict lived only in memory. Fix: CyclePhase.closeout (artifact_integrity, metrics) runs past the deadline and outside the alarm; runtime_status takes a tri-state integrity verdict and a phase_interrupted fact (-> failed, phase named); the orchestrator's bounded summary carries the phase ledger; fixture_refresh asks the remaining wall-clock between suites and records what it skipped.

title: The replica containment binds the shared git common dir read-only as a whole, so under a current git (2.55 on the hosted 22.04 lane) a ref update inside the sandbox cannot create packed-refs.lock beside it and a signed commit cannot land - the design was proven against the droplet's git 2.43, which never takes that lock on a loose-ref update
rule_violated: A containment property proven under one git must hold under a current one: the sandbox keeps landing signed commits through its replica while every shared entry stays EROFS - the packed-refs.lock sibling a current git creates is part of what the design must permit, and the probe pins the property under the host's own git
notes: Hosted 22.04 kernel lane, run 34910051620, git 2.55.0: test_git_containment.UnderRealBwrapTests and test_containment_probe fail 'Unable to create <checkout>/.git/packed-refs.lock: Read-only file system' - the lock is created beside packed-refs in the shared common dir the containment binds read-only as a whole; the droplet's git 2.43 never takes it on a loose-ref update, so the ARIA-HIGH-123 fix was proven against one git and is refused by a newer one. Fix shape (tier 1, after ARIA-HIGH-124 - same module): the common dir becomes a tmpfs at its own path with every shared entry bound back read-only one by one (config, hooks, info, objects, refs/tags, refs/remotes, packed-refs, worktrees), so a lock sibling can exist while every entry stays EROFS; publication keeps reading the quarantine's loose refs/heads only; the containment probe pins the property under the host's git and names a git below the proven floor. Until it lands the hosted kernel lane carries these failures by name (PR-3 run 34910051620: 20 failures + 3 errors, the larger part this class).

title: The in-sandbox kernel clients (the hook client run on every event, the MCP relay the aria server renders as) were served from <workspace>/aria-kernel, not the running kernel, so a workspace checked out at a commit without them (trial eleven's task source) gave every hook and the relay a path absent inside the sandbox and both died silently on the first real implementation request
rule_violated: A client the kernel runs inside the sandbox is the kernel's own code, served from the kernel's own root and bound read-only where the sandbox can reach it; the workspace is the implementer's subject, never the source of the machinery that judges it - and a client that cannot be found is refused by name before a spawn, not discovered as a silent execvp failure inside one (ARIA-HIGH-133's class: a live seam with no live input)
notes: Found while preparing ring 4 on trial eleven (2026-09-15 restart plan, Blok 5): claude_runtime derived hook_context.kernel_root as <workspace>/aria-kernel (:948, :1044) and the MCP relay followed it; the trial task source predates hook_client.py, mcp_relay.py, git_containment.py and hook_broker.py, so nothing the sandbox needed existed at the path the settings document named. ci_executor._REPO_ROOT falls back to the module's own checkout when ARIA_WORKSPACE_ROOT is unset, which is the kernel's tree and not the request's. Fix: claude_settings.kernel_code_root() is the SSOT (the running kernel's aria-kernel/), claude_runtime._hook_context names it for any workspace and refuses kernel_client_missing:<path> before a settings document is written, implementation_safety.kernel_root_ro_binds binds that root read-only on every sandbox route when it lies outside the workspace and under no system root, and the executor writes a provenance note (REPO_ROOT_FROM_MODULE_MARKER) whenever its root came from its own module. Pinned by tests/test_kernel_clients_from_code_root.py, red on the tree before the fix.

title: The implementer sandbox shares the host network namespace so the CLI can reach its provider, .env is a visible read-only bind and resolv.conf is bound in, so a prompt-injected agent needed one allowed test runner and one test file it wrote to exfiltrate a secret; the policy refuses curl/wget by name but pytest and nx test run whatever the tree holds, the only brake the model's judgement
rule_violated: A sandbox that must reach exactly one network destination (the model provider) is confined to that destination by construction, not by the confined process's own good behaviour; the egress boundary is an allowlist the host enforces, and a spawn without one is refused a claim rather than run on trust
notes: Verified (Fable review, confirmed against origin/main and the candidate): the managed spawn already has --unshare-pid (implementation_safety.py:1122); the real open gap is MANAGED_SPAWN_ALLOW_NETWORK = True plus a bound resolv.conf, and this sandbox has never run on a real implementation request, so closing it before the first live run (Blok 6) is cheap where closing it after is 'after the first exfiltration'. Fix: aria_kernel/egress_proxy.py is an allowlist CONNECT proxy (stdlib, ~180 lines) run by infrastructure/aria/aria-egress-proxy.service on the host (loopback :3128 + a unix socket), passed to the spawn via HTTPS_PROXY (agent_env BASELINE_ENV_NAMES already carries the proxy vars); the kernel adds the three free namespace flags --unshare-ipc/--unshare-uts/--new-session to MANAGED_SPAWN_ISOLATION_FLAGS and the probe mirrors them (ORPHAN-MEDIUM-452); ci_executor._pre_claim_environment_gate gains egress_boundary_probe, refusing egress_boundary_unavailable when no allowlist proxy answers an off-allowlist CONNECT with a refusal by name. Rejected as over-engineering (same as Fable): a seccomp profile, gVisor/microVM, a separate worker VM (ARIA-MEDIUM-139 already records that), hiding .env with /dev/null. Pinned by tests/test_egress_proxy.py and the gate/isolation pins in test_environment_contract.py, test_managed_claude_sandbox.py, test_sandbox_and_perimeter_hardening.py.

title: The implementer's kernel-authority commands (apply gate, pr create) and the aria MCP server run inside the agent's sandbox where the durable store is not mounted, so none of them has ever worked in production and an executor-lane implementation cannot open a PR; kernel authority inside the agent's sandbox is unsound regardless of the mount
rule_violated: Kernel authority is exercised by the kernel outside the agent's containment; the agent produces evidence, the executor records it and opens the PR
notes: Rounds 1-6 (2026-09-14 to 09-15). r1-2 moved kernel authority out of the agent sandbox (request broker: apply gate validation contained INSIDE, the store mutation and pr create OUTSIDE with the executor authority; the aria MCP server served outside over a bound socket, mcp_relay a thin client inside). r3 priced the implementation child into the drain window and contained the validation commands. r4 verified the committed tip identity and moved the kernel delivery sum. r5 put the signing key in a private dir outside the workspace, retired before delivery, and contained the validation sandbox with the keys dir masked. r6 minted the delivery token where it is consumed (revoked in its finally) and ran the executor git with hooks off. Reverify under real bwrap 20/20 on the droplet. Ported from lane aria-lane-124 (r6 tip 5072864525) to the candidate as C3, patch /root/aria-lab/lane124-c3.patch. Pinned across test_implementation_delivery, test_mcp_broker, test_executor_pr_via_kernel, test_executor_implementation_identity, test_git_containment, test_containment_probe, test_state_lock_liveness_bound and the executor lanes.

title: The implementation envelope mint never passed target_sha and the executor's native task binding read nothing else, so under the adaptive runtime policy (B8) every implementation request was refused target_revision_unavailable before a claim; the drain had added the worktree at implementation_ids.base_sha (ARIA-HIGH-124) and the child refused the tree it stood in
rule_violated: The commit a request is about is derived once, by the kernel, and every reader of it — the mint that writes the row, the anchor gate, the drain that adds the worktree, the executor's task binding — reads that one derivation; a row's fact is not re-derived differently at each seam
notes: Found by the first live ring-4 run on trial eleven (executor log: runtime_task_binding_unavailable reason=target_revision_unavailable target_sha=null observed_head=6652139901, request AIR-aria-implementer-b7a519f5be58 left PENDING). Fix: agent_invocations.request_anchor_sha (target_sha, else implementation_ids.base_sha, else None) is the one derivation; ci_executor._native_task_binding_refusal and ci_executor_drain.request_worktree_target read it (the governance row names anchor_source); the anchor gate reads it; issue_implementation_envelope passes target_sha=base_sha so new rows are self-describing. Pinned by test_ci_executor_live_path_smoke (a legacy row without target_sha is bound at its staged base under the B8 policy — red before the fix — and a moved tree is target_revision_mismatch naming the anchor's source), test_agent_request_anchor (the derivation), test_must_satisfy_shape (the minted row carries target_sha == base_sha).

title: The implementation rollback treated every journaled files_touched as an edit, reads included, and unlinked an untracked file the agent had only read; on trial eleven the timed-out implementer had read the store's plan ledger through the workspace it lay in and the rollback deleted the CONVERGED plan's event ledger
rule_violated: A rollback puts back what the agent changed and touches nothing else; a file the agent read is not the agent's edit, and a file no checkpoint holds is never removed unless a journaled write created it
notes: Found by the first live ring-4 spawn (2026-09-16 16:38-17:08Z, cli exit 124): checkpoints/index.jsonl 'restored' seq 2 removed=['.aria-state-store/tools/plans/events.jsonl'] restored=[implementation_safety.py, command_policy.py, plan_convergence.py, package.json] while the work journal shows only Read rows for all five (the one Write was refused path_escape). Fix: restore_checkpoint follows command_family=file_write rows only (JOURNAL_WRITE_FAMILY); the pre-write hook adds the write's own target to the checkpoint and never folds a checkpoint whose target the latest one does not hold (latest_checkpoint_holds). Pinned in tests/invariants/v12/test_phase_v12_c_checkpoint.py (I-V12-CKPT-03b: an untracked read survives, reads restore nothing; CKPT-05: an untracked first-touch write is restored, not removed) — both red before. The trial's ledger is restored from the 2026-09-15 capture and re-minted through the kernel; the trial layout (store nested in the workspace) is also what let the agent read a ledger at all — production's store is outside the checkout.

title: The executor rendered the agent's contract and runtime profile from the workspace at the request's target_sha, not from the kernel that grades the response; a workspace at an older commit ran that commit's contract — trial eleven's implementer got the 2026-09-12 contract twice while the running kernel carried the 124-round one
rule_violated: The contract an agent runs under is the one the kernel validates its response against; it is served from the running kernel's checkout, like every other kernel-owned artefact the sandbox receives (ARIA-HIGH-142), never from the tree the agent is changing
notes: Found by the two live ring-4 spawns of 2026-09-16 (16:38Z cli exit 124, 17:26Z agent refusal implementer_turn_budget_exhausted): the prompt's contract prefix was task-source's .claude/agents/aria-implementer.md at 6652139901. Fix: ci_executor._kernel_checkout_root() (= claude_settings.kernel_code_root().parent) is the root _deliver_agent_contract and every read_agent_runtime_profile in the executor use. Pinned in test_kernel_clients_from_code_root.TheContractIsTheKernels (a workspace carrying a different aria-implementer.md still yields the kernel's contract hash and profile; the three executor readers name the root in source).

title: The implementer contract's first obligation — recompute the CONVERGED plan's content_hash by hand — is not executable under the sandbox's command policy (no python3 -c, base64, grep; scratch writes refused), so both live spawns spent their entire budgets on it and never reached an edit: 1800 s to cli exit 124, then the kernel's own 60-turn cap and an honest refusal
rule_violated: An obligation the contract places on the agent is one the agent's admitted tools can discharge; what the kernel can answer from its own ledger, the kernel answers, and the agent cites the answer rather than re-deriving it under a policy built to refuse exactly that
notes: Transcripts of AIR-aria-implementer-b7a519f5be58 (16:38Z) and AIR-aria-implementer-ff499d2321eb (17:26Z): the agent read implementation_safety/command_policy/plan_convergence to find an admitted way to hash, tried python3 -c (refused), a /tmp scratch (path_escape), ts-node one-liners, and ran out. Fix: mcp_server READ tool plan_verify {plan_id, content_hash} recomputes from converged_plan_body (hash-verified) and returns verdict + revision + the full plan body; the envelope prompt and the contract's step 1 send the obligation there and forbid hand recomputation. Pinned in test_phase_v12_g_mcp (verified/mismatch/unknown-plan), test_must_satisfy_shape (the prompt names the tool) and test_kernel_clients_from_code_root (the kernel's contract carries step 1).

title: The implementer's git ran the repository's own hooks inside the sandbox (core.hooksPath=.husky bound read-only): the pre-commit gate suite writes a fixture under aria-debts/, a READONLY path, so `git commit` exited 1 on a clean index and no implementation could ever be committed from the sandbox — found by the third live spawn, which probed the commit path before editing and refused
rule_violated: The gates that judge the agent's work are the kernel's (the apply gate, the PR's CI); the developer's local commit hooks are neither the agent's to run nor its to satisfy, and a sandbox that lets them run lets an unrelated gate decide whether an implementation exists
notes: AIR-aria-implementer-62bd314dcd65 (2026-09-16 19:22Z, the first spawn under the kernel's contract with plan_verify): step 1 verified in one MCP call, branch/HEAD confirmed, then `git commit -m probe` on the clean index exited 1 inside .husky/pre-commit (tools/gates/commit-msg-validator.spec.ts mkdirSync aria-debts/.test-fixtures → ENOENT under the READONLY bind); the agent refused honestly. Fix: git_containment binds an EMPTY read-only tmpfs at the effective hooks dir whether or not the repository has one (the missing-hooks branch became the only branch); the agent's git runs no hooks and can plant none; the executor's own git already ran with hooks off (KERNEL_GIT_NO_HOOKS_ARGS). Pinned in test_git_containment (a failing repository hook blocks the commit on the host and neither runs nor blocks inside; the hooks dir is empty and unwritable inside; the commit publishes). Named, not closed: the plan's new spec files make tools/quality/format-scope.json stale for the PR's quality-gates CI and that manifest is outside allowed_scope — a delivery-side regeneration the kernel does not yet do.

title: The canonical validation suite named `npm run format:check` — prettier over every ts/tsx/js/jsx/json/md file in the tree, which fails on main itself (4,957 unmanaged files) and is enforced by no workflow — so under require_worktree_ok every delivery was candidate_validation_not_green; the first implementation ARIA committed was refused at the apply gate on that line
rule_violated: A canonical gate command is one the repository itself passes on its base and one its CI enforces; a command that fails on main is not a gate on the change, it is a wall in front of every change
notes: Run #9 (AIR-aria-implementer-184834167f7f, 2026-09-16 20:59-22:08Z): the agent committed bf197ada7c (7 files, its own suites 59/59 green, lint and type-check ok); the apply gate's canonical run recorded `npm run format:check` exit 1 (4,957 files, identical on the baseline) and blocked. Fix: CANONICAL_VALIDATION_COMMANDS' format entry is `node tools/quality/quality.mjs format check-changed` (what ci-full.yml runs against the PR base; HEAD^ when unset = the staged base for a one-commit branch); validation.parse_allowed_command admits the quality runner for its two read-only verbs only (ALLOWED_QUALITY_RUNNER_ARGV: format check-changed, format-scope check); impact's low-risk suite, the shared safety contract, CONTRACTS.md and the SSOT/battery/perimeter/e2e pins follow (fixtures answer `node` like npx/npm). Not closed here: the invariants project's environmental reds inside the validation sandbox (ARIA-HIGH-150).

title: The validation sandbox does not carry the toolchain the repository's invariants need (no cargo on its PATH, no docker), and a workspace behind main fails finding-registry-closure-drift by construction, so `nx affected --target=test` selecting the invariants project can never be green inside the gate — trial eleven's apply gate saw 4 environmental suites red beside 59 green product tests
rule_violated: The environment the gate validates in is the environment CI validates in, or the gate names by test which reds are its own and which are the room's; a green-only gate over a room that cannot run the suite refuses every change for reasons that are not the change's
notes: Run #9 gate log trial-eleven-ring4-mint-000: invariants suites red inside the sandbox — backup-ssh-broker-contract (rustc not on the sandbox PATH; /root/.cargo/bin is not bound), deploy-ssot-contract and production-host-control-plane-runtime (environment), finding-registry-closure-drift (the 2026-09-12 registry against origin/main's Closes trailers: environmental for any worktree behind main). The baseline at base_sha fails identically (regression_status no_regression) and require_worktree_ok still blocks. Fix shape (not decided here): (a) the validation sandbox binds the toolchains CI has (cargo, the docker socket is NOT one of them) and the invariants that need a service refuse by name inside the sandbox instead of failing; (b) the gate compares per-test failing sets against the baseline so a red that is the room's, present identically at base_sha, is named as baseline debt rather than as the change's — with require_worktree_ok kept for every command the baseline passed. Decision is the operator's (ORPHAN-717 asked for green).

title: The runner provision script verified the sandbox backend as root, the one user bwrap works for on Ubuntu 24.04: apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1 denies user namespaces to an unprofiled bwrap for gharunner, the lanes' user, so the rebuilt runner reported a verified backend and the capability probe reported sandbox_backend=none
rule_violated: A capability is verified as the user who needs it; root's verdict on a namespace check is the trap, not the proof
notes: Capability-probe run 35321850013 (2026-09-18 07:56Z): envelope holds, sandbox_backend=none. As gharunner: _bwrap_probe_argv rc=1 'loopback: Failed RTM_NEWADDR: Operation not permitted'; git containment 'setting up uid map: Permission denied'; as root both pass (every ring-4 run in this review). Host: Ubuntu 24.04, kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1, no AppArmor profile for /usr/bin/bwrap. Fix: /etc/apparmor.d/bwrap in Ubuntu's own shape (unconfined + userns), kept in the repo at scripts/aria/apparmor/bwrap; provision_runner.sh reads the knob, installs the profile in apply mode, checks the namespace capability unprivileged via setpriv and runs sandbox_backend() as $RUNNER_USER (deferring by name when the user is absent or cannot read the checkout); the runbook carries the step and expects the accessor's spelling (bwrap, not bubblewrap). Verified on the droplet: sandbox_backend() as gharunner = bwrap, git containment reason None.

title: The batch request-state derivation called ensure_tools_dir twice per request (directly and through the control fold); ensure_tools_dir rewrites integrity_index.json under a whole-group store transaction, so one queue selection over the 828-row backlog of 2026-09-18 was ~1,650 index rewrites and the planner drain ran 44+ minutes after the cycle had completed
rule_violated: A derivation is a read; a read resolves a path and never creates, writes or re-indexes to answer — what the batch ensured once, the fold it feeds must not ensure again
notes: Production run 35322803000 / cyc-20260918T081405Z-auto: cycle completed 09:27:17Z (73 min, 47 phases, 0 failed); process then at 86% of one core in run_planner_dispatch_daemon with no child and every ledger mtime touched every few seconds. py-spy: derive_request_state → ensure_tools_dir → update_tools_index → write_index → state_transaction, and derive_request_state → effective_control → _rows → commands_path → ensure_tools_dir. strace 4 s: 23 index-group transactions, repo_identity.json opened 720 times. Fix: with injected ledgers derive_request_state resolves tools_dir and writes nothing; the batch folds effective_control once and injects _control; control._rows resolves via tools_dir. Pins: batch ensures once (was 3 for two requests), folds control once, fold never calls ensure_tools_dir. Related: HIGH-136 (cycle cost); a separate finding follows for cycle-metrics recording a single 'cycle' duration with no per-phase breakdown.

title: The publish continuity gate read only governance pruned_paths, not the run-artifacts/compacted.jsonl attestation ARIA-HIGH-117's heal writes, so the maintenance lane's first healing run (176 artifacts backfilled) was refused as 18 lost hot surfaces and the nightly kept restoring the unhealed store: no lane could publish aria/state (tip still executor-33920896040-1 of 2026-09-04)
rule_violated: A guard reads every attestation the kernel writes for the loss it judges; a heal the publish cannot carry is not a heal
notes: Run 35322803000 (first production cycle since 09-04) completed, integrity verify refused: 3825 raw_pointer_corrupt + 36 artifact_ref_missing + 36 artifact_index_ref_missing, compacted_artifact_count 0 (quarantine-evidence-35322803000) — the store never carried compacted.jsonl. Maintenance run 35262206853 (09-17 18:59Z, first with the 117 fix, merged via #1553 03:08Z): compacted_artifacts_attested 176, hot_artifacts_removed 0, pruned_paths [] → state_publish_continuity_surfaces_lost with 18 runtime_artifact_hot surfaces of cyc-20260904T093220Z/194353Z. Tip snapshot executor-33920896040-1 (09-04); 09-05/11/12 compactions predate pruned_paths; 09-14..16 maintenance ran pre-fix code. Fix: losses_not_attested_by_compaction also reads compacted.jsonl rows whose archive is present (_compacted_artifact_paths); broken chain → state_publish_compaction_ledger_unreadable. Pin: live shape publishes with compaction_attested_surfaces naming the loss (red before); hand-deleted artifact still refused. Expected sequence after merge: maintenance lane publishes the healed store → nightly restores it → verify ok → first published cycle.

title: state checkout judged a hollow store worktree (registered, .git link removed by the job's git clean, tools/ re-created) by running git inside it, which resolves to the enclosing workspace repository — so the executor lane read main as 6450 unpushed store commits and refused (state_store_unpushed_commits, run 35339272100) before its first claim
rule_violated: A tree without .git holds no commit; bytes found there are preserved aside and disclosed, never judged as unpublished work and never silently deleted
notes: Executor run 35339272100 (workflow_run after cycle 35322803000): state_store_unpushed_commits '.aria-state-store is 6450 commit(s) ahead of origin/aria/state (HEAD=4335bd5be118)' — 4335bd5be1 is main. The executor job's first step git clean -ffdx removed the worktree's .git link; a later step re-created tools/; git worktree list still registered the path (prunable). _is_worktree_of checked registration only; git run inside a directory without .git resolves to the parent repo. Fix: _worktree_is_hollow → set the directory aside (.aria-state-store.hollow-<utc>), git worktree prune, fresh checkout, disclosure row names hollow_set_aside. Pins: hollow shape checks out + sets aside + discloses (red before with the production refusal); a real worktree with an unpushed commit is still refused. Same sweep as ORPHAN-712 (directory gone entirely), other shape.

title: The managed spawn bound the login file read-only, so the first sandboxed run that refreshed the OAuth session rotated the refresh token without persisting it: the run failed auth, the host's copy was left retired, every later run failed until a manual login, and the cross-provider rung's 'zai credential not configured' replaced the primary verdict in every ledger (executor run 35369756222)
rule_violated: What the runtime must write to stay authenticated is bound where it can write it; a failover rung that cannot even start never replaces the primary's verdict
notes: Executor run 35369756222 (first production drain): admission managed_session_logged_in; attempt 1 (challenger-planner, anthropic/opus) ~2 min → control_or_transport_unavailable; drain line 'zai_credential_not_configured'; requeued native_runtime_execution_unavailable; breaker tripped → drain_circuit_skip for the rest (run cancelled). Host smoke as runner user: 'OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed' (had answered OK at 07:56Z). Cause: wrap_managed_claude_in_sandbox --ro-bind of the login file; in-sandbox refresh rotated the provider-side refresh token, persist failed. Fix: --bind (writable) for that one file; run_with_model_fallback raises claude_auth_failure naming primary marker + remedy when the cross rung raises ClaudeAuthUnavailable. Pins: sandbox test (writable, one file, base binds unchanged), auth classification test (primary verdict survives). Operator: one more manual login before the next drain; ORPHAN-CRITICAL-591's 'sessions expire' was this.

title: After two failures opened the anthropic/opus circuit, the executor drain skipped the remaining ~800 requests one queue selection at a time (~30 s each, a kernel subprocess over the whole request ledger per skip), holding the single-slot runner for hours with nothing dispatched until the run was cancelled by hand (run 35369756222)
rule_violated: A route that is open is a fact about the route, not about the next request; a drain that learns it stops by name and leaves the queue pending, instead of spending the runner proving it once per row
notes: Run 35369756222: after 2 failed attempts (HIGH-157) the circuit opened; drain_circuit_skip every ~30 s (each skip re-runs agent next-pending over 828 rows + anchor probes, then excludes one id); ~800 rows × 30 s vs 21000 s budget; cancelled at 17:20Z. Fix: CIRCUIT_SKIP_STREAK_STOP=5 consecutive skips with no dispatch → stop_reason circuit_open_streak + stage line naming open routes; a dispatch resets the streak. Pins: streak stops after one dispatch with ≤7 selections; interleaved healthy route keeps draining. Related: HIGH-153 (selection cost), HIGH-157 (the failures that opened the route).

title: Production PostgreSQL restarts with an entrypoint and container configuration from different release contracts
rule_violated: Root-cause-only fixes and verified completion; credential/session consistency and supported deployment contract.
notes: Read-only runtime evidence on 2026-09-05: the live aqua-postgres container was created July 14, uses the base TimescaleDB image and User=postgres, and bind-mounts the deployment checkout entrypoint. Current entrypoint requires root staging; the declared release uses a custom image, root bootstrap, exact certificate mounts and runtime tmpfs. At approximately 15:24 UTC logs contained the root-staging FATAL; at 15:31 UTC metadata still showed exit 126 and 25 restarts. Auth logs contained EAI_AGAIN postgres and an unauthenticated GET to the public GraphQL endpoint returned HTTP 502. Later log reads differed, so the earlier FATAL is time-bounded evidence, not an assertion about every subsequent restart. Required work: Reconcile the complete PostgreSQL image and service configuration through the supported release/rollback workflow, preserving the existing volume and compatible database version. Validate all declared staging inputs and health checks; changing only the runtime user does not satisfy the new mounts/helper contract. Live account/password verification is currently blocked by availability.

title: Credential-version draft breaks token issuance after invitation acceptance and password reset
rule_violated: Root-cause-only fixes and verified completion; credential/session consistency and supported deployment contract.
notes: Both flows load User, change its password, commit the password/action-token changes, then pass the same entity to generateTokens (invitation:861; reset:1773). The new trigger advances the stored credentialVersion, while the ordinary update:false column is absent from TypeORM UPDATE RETURNING (installed ReturningResultsEntityUpdator.js:155-160). The caller therefore retains the old version and the new predicate rejects legitimate completion after consuming the one-time action. This is static code and installed-ORM evidence; no security reproduction was executed. Required work: Capture the database-owned version corresponding to the authorized credential write within that write transaction/lock, and carry that immutable snapshot into issuance. Do not indiscriminately reload at mint time, which would erase the original credential proof. Verify legitimate invitation/reset completion using the actual ORM entity and migrated PostgreSQL.

title: Login full-entity saves can overwrite newer account fields; post-mint rehash also splits login persistence
rule_violated: Root-cause-only fixes and verified completion; credential/session consistency and supported deployment contract.
notes: Bookkeeping calls save(user) on the complete earlier snapshot. Installed TypeORM loads the current database entity, compares all defined properties and updates differences by identity (SubjectDatabaseEntityLoader.js:80-105; SubjectChangedColumnsComputer.js:47-57,137-157; SubjectExecutor.js:348-374). Consequently an intervening account change can be overwritten before the new fence rejects the stale version. The draft additionally saves a legacy password upgrade after the token transaction commits; that independent save can fail after refresh/session persistence. The full-entity pattern predates this draft; moving rehash after mint adds the transaction-boundary problem. Required work: Use explicit bookkeeping-only persistence and retain an immutable authenticated snapshot. Serialize any legacy password upgrade under the credential version/row lock and define one coherent persistence boundary for upgrade and issuance. Cover normal and legacy login with actual ORM integration checks.

title: Login success audit and event are emitted before token issuance succeeds
rule_violated: Root-cause-only fixes and verified completion; credential/session consistency and supported deployment contract.
notes: LOGIN_SUCCESS and UserLoggedIn execute before generateTokens. The catch path does not retract or reclassify these signals when issuance or the draft post-mint rehash throws. This existing behavior is code-confirmed and was mentioned in the prior session; current production audit contents were not reread because PostgreSQL is unavailable. Required work: Tie successful-login observability to successful completion of the credential/session operation. Verify rejection produces no success audit/event and completed login produces them once.

title: Credential-version PostgreSQL contract is absent from ordinary affected CI and ORM flow coverage
rule_violated: Root-cause-only fixes and verified completion; credential/session consistency and supported deployment contract.
notes: Normal auth tests exclude postgres.spec.ts; the dedicated integration target selects it, but inspected workflow/CI scripts have no invocation of test:integration. The new test uses raw SQL and inserts users only after migration, so it does not validate ORM version hydration on credential writes or existing-row upgrade. E2E fallback setup fabricates the column without installing its owning trigger. These are verified coverage gaps, not evidence that the correctly executed production migration omits its trigger. Required work: Include the relevant real-PostgreSQL contract in auth/migration CI, exercise populated-table upgrades and actual User persistence/legitimate minting flows, and build E2E schema from the authoritative migration. Existing raw-SQL trigger checks remain useful.
