title: In-process migration runner ignores migration.instance.transaction = false: CONCURRENTLY migrations fail in dev/E2E while the db-migrate orchestrator applies them (ORPHAN-CRITICAL-058 regressed in the second runner)
rule_violated: One migration contract, both runners: TypeORM's instance-level `transaction = false` opt-out is the documented way to run CONCURRENTLY DDL (CLAUDE.md Migration Runners; ORPHAN-CRITICAL-058). The e2e-messaging workflow claims the platform runner has 'the same transaction semantics production gates require' — it did not.
notes: Found by PR #1586's E2E lane: the Faz 1.1 post-condition barrier rewrote the in-process runner around executor.executeMigration() with an unconditional startTransaction(), so AddMessagesContentSearchGinIndex1802300000000 (transaction = false, per-partition CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY) threw its runner-contract guard against the E2E harness's three bootstrap partitions — every messaging E2E suite failed at boot. The migration's own docblock assumed E2E databases have zero partitions. Fix: the runner honours migration.instance.transaction !== false exactly as the orchestrator does (start/commit/rollback only when wrapped); migration-runner.transaction-opt-out.spec.ts drives the real MigrationExecutor and proves up() sees no open transaction for the opt-out and a wrapped one otherwise.

title: nats.conf max_file_store (2 GiB) is smaller than the JetStream streams' summed max_bytes reservations (7.75 GiB): the production NATS cannot recover AQUACULTURE_TELEMETRY after a restart, stays unhealthy, and every deploy aborts at the ACL reload
rule_violated: A server-side limit and the application reservations it bounds are one contract; JetStream refuses a stream whose max_bytes exceeds the unreserved store (error 10047). ARCH-010/ARCH-031 explicit stream limits; the telemetry stream (SENSOR-HIGH-092, 2026-08-25) raised the reservation without the conf.
notes: Observed on the droplet after the 2026-09-19 17:35 UTC auto-deploy (release ba4366830…): nats-server logged `Error recreating stream "AQUACULTURE_TELEMETRY": insufficient storage resources available (10047)` on start, `Healthcheck failed: JetStream stream '$G > AQUACULTURE_TELEMETRY' could not be recovered` every 10 s, and the deploy step `Reloading NATS certificate identities and ACL` failed with `NATS did not become healthy after ACL reload`. /jsz: max_storage 2147483648, reserved 1879048192 (EVENTS 1.5 GiB + DLQ 256 MiB), used 5.4 MB — the 6 GiB telemetry reservation cannot fit. Fix: max_file_store 10 GiB (disk has 47 GB free) and tests/invariants/nats-jetstream-store-budget.spec.ts pins the conf against the three source defaults.

title: Adaptive admission walked the fleet in its fixed preference order: a judge declaring glm-5.3 was admitted on anthropic/opus whenever Claude was logged in, the claude wrapper ran the Z.ai transport as a failover rung and released the finished verdict as usage_unavailable at requeue budget zero, misnamed control_or_transport_unavailable; the adversarial judge never folded
rule_violated: A profile's declared provider leads its admission ladder; the fleet's preference order is the failover behind it. A run that finished with usage on its result seals an envelope the wrapper accepts, and a cause the wrapper named is the cause the attempt row carries
notes: Measured on the first production executor after the chain restart (run 35444645590, 2026-09-19 13:20-13:30Z, request AIR-aria-adversarial-judge-8281c4e19fd1): admission candidates anthropic available + zai available, route anthropic/opus taken (eligible_routes[0]), the profile's glm-5.3 re-resolved inside invoke_claude_cli and run through _run_zai_as_claude_result, envelope sealed with agent_dispatch_model glm-5.3 and a sound false_positive at 0.6, then released native_runtime_execution_unavailable with result_admission control_or_transport_unavailable and usage_ledger_hash null. Historically 2 of 11 adversarial verdicts folded with model claude-opus-5. Fix: fleet_ladder_for(declared_provider) leads the ladder with the profile's own provider (halting semantics unchanged); the envelope builder and the cost recorder take the run result's usage with the stream parse as fallback; _result_admission_for keeps a name the wrapper already gave. The dispatch-model stamp still comes from the profile, not from the rung that ran (ARIA typed-judgment plan F10).

title: judges spawn with --dangerously-skip-permissions despite read-only profiles
rule_violated: a profile that cannot write spawns in a read shape: a positive tool allowlist, prompts denied by name, user settings ignored, the workspace bound read-only, no commit containment — and the row says so.
notes: Evidence: invoke_claude_cli never passes skip_permissions=False or a permission_mode to run_claude_exec (tools/aria-poc/ci_executor.py, the call site under "Plan 032 Faz 032b"), so _is_write_capable reads True for judge_opus, judge_glm and arbiter (tools Read, Grep, Glob, write_scope: [], data/runtime_profiles.json) and every judge takes wrap_managed_claude_in_sandbox with the write-capable binds, the hook broker and the commit containment derivation. The read-only argv shape exists (claude_runtime.py, "A read-only / preview turn passes skip_permissions=False") and has no caller. Removing containment instead is worse: the spawn env derives CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR from the real HOME (agent_env.py), and the host's settings.json sets permissions.defaultMode: auto. Plan: Phase 3.

title: every process-less Z.ai judgment is one admission, one probe and one call
rule_violated: work that shares a route, an agent and an anchor shares one admission and one call; every request keeps its own claim, attempt, envelope, summary and cost share.
notes: Evidence: _invoke_native_zai makes one chat completion per claimed request with no process, no sandbox and no hook broker, yet the fleet probe (probe_zai_status, one max_tokens=1 completion), the admission row and the request-ledger load repeat per request; the drain's summary channel and _settle are keyed one summary per launched child. 322 adversarial judgments are pending against a measured ~9 per night. Plan: Phase 4b.

title: observer_identity_missing is outside the closed vocabulary and never escalates
rule_violated: every reason a consensus can end in is in one closed vocabulary that the severity map, the recorder and the sweep all read; the test that pins it walks the call sites.
notes: Evidence: generate_ai_consensus emits it through _consensus_uncertainty (no vocabulary check) for an anchor-grade group whose observer has no model; it is absent from CONSENSUS_UNCERTAINTY_REASONS (feedback_store.py) and from human_required.CONSENSUS_UNCERTAINTY_SEVERITY, so the sweep records benign_not_escalated, and record_consensus_uncertainty would refuse it. Plan: Phase 6.

title: operator batch labels never join the judge groups they label
rule_violated: a human label lands on the exact group the judges voted on; the queue that asks for labels writes the sample it asks against.
notes: Evidence: record_operator_feedback_batch writes judgment_group_id = verdict.get( "judgment_group_id") or sample_id; judge_fanout._group_id is judge:{tool_id}:{fingerprint}; judge_calibration._group_key joins on (run_id, finding_id, judgment_group_id). A human row written through the documented batch lane therefore calibrates no judge. The sampler (_sampleable_raw_findings) also never re-samples a (run_id, finding_id) that carries any feedback row, and the batch lane refuses a verdict outside the sample's items — a judged finding has no sample a label can bind to. The sample's status is never persisted (stored_sample is built and dropped; 125 pending / 65 empty samples live). Plan: Phase 6.

title: the consensus arbiter is not pre-submit gated
rule_violated: every judge role's output contract is checked before the claim is sealed.
notes: Evidence: _pre_submit_validate_envelope runs judgment_bridge.validate_judge_response for evidence_judgment and adversarial_judgment only; a consensus_arbitration envelope that cannot fold is sealed, accepted and fails in the bridge (the live agent_bridge_warning rows for one arbiter claim, retried again on 2026-09-18). Plan: Phase 2.

title: judge confidence has no Brier or ECE and no calibrated status
rule_violated: a confidence that closes findings is measured against ground truth with a scoring rule and a reliability estimate that state their sample size; until then it is a suggestion.
notes: Evidence: judge_calibration.score_judges reports precision, recall, accuracy and mean_confidence_correct / wrong; no Brier or ECE exists in the kernel; generate_ai_consensus closes a group when the mean self-reported confidence is ≥ 0.80 (CONSENSUS_MIN_CONFIDENCE); the live distribution (0.72–0.90, TP mean 0.845 vs FP mean 0.861) shows no separation. The confidence semantics are undefined in the judge contracts ("confidence: 0.0 to 1.0"), and confidence_in_unit_interval accepts 0.0–0.49 for a binary verdict. Plan: Phases 1 (contract) and 5 (measurement).

title: 40 accepted judge results never folded, three causes
rule_violated: a claim whose fold is refused by a contract that will not change stops retrying by name; a result row's bridge status is the fold's status.
notes: Evidence: 59 accepted judge results on origin/aria/state, 19 ai_judge rows. 27 came from runs gha-31562321582 and gha-31711634581 (2026-08-12/13), before operator-feedback.jsonl joined the state manifest (first on aria/state 2026-08-17): written runner-locally and dropped by the publish. 12 carried the flat verdict shape refused before ORPHAN-HIGH-629. 1 arbiter uncertainty was refused before ORPHAN-CRITICAL-735 and its claim is still retried by the replay lane (agent_bridge_warning rows dated 2026-09-18). 5 are duplicates re-minted under the finding-keyed group. bridge_status on the result row is a mint-time constant and never updates. Plan: the replay-lane stop and the bridge_status update are their own small lane after Phase 2; the first two causes are closed by history and recorded here.

title: human labels are counted, not verified; a missing source_type counts as human
rule_violated: a row that changes what closes or what calibrates is verified before it counts, and an absent provenance is not the strongest provenance.
notes: Evidence: load_feedback reads operator-feedback.jsonl through load_jsonl with no verify_operator_feedback_row; verification runs only in operator_feedback_ingestion.py. is_ground_truth_row and judge_calibration._build_ground_truth default source_type or "human". The HMAC key lives under the store and is readable by every executor process, and it attests "the kernel wrote this row", not "an operator did". Plan: Phase 6.

title: a ref inside the request box passes the fabrication detector by construction
rule_violated: a citation proves the judge read the bytes: a verbatim quote checked against the pinned excerpt, and rows record how the evidence was selected.
notes: Evidence: validate_agent_response_evidence checks response.evidence_refs and the satisfaction matrix against request.evidence_refs ∪ allowed_scope; details.verdict.evidence_refs are graded only by _has_unverifiable_evidence (missing | invalid). A judge that copies the request's own refs — or, in the typed layer, returns an index — is "evidence-backed" for every verdict; two judges citing the same request refs read as independent corroboration. Plan: Phases 1 and 2.

title: the dispatch-model stamp names the profile, not the rung that ran
rule_violated: the stamp names the model that answered, from the result, unconditionally.
notes: Evidence: _build_envelope_from_claude_output stamps details["agent_dispatch_model"] = dispatch_model under if dispatch_model: with agent_profile.model; run_with_model_fallback may have run the cross-vendor rung (AUTH_FAILOVER_TIER), and ClaudeRunResult carries no model. ARIA-HIGH-161's live envelope reads glm-5.3 for an attempt whose row says claude_session_id. The anchor grade's distinct-model count reads this stamp. Plan: Phase 2.

title: the replay lane retries a claim whose fold is refused permanently
rule_violated: a bridge refusal that names a contract, not a transient, ends the retries by name.
notes: Evidence: one arbiter claim refused with judge_verdict.verdict:invalid:None before ORPHAN-CRITICAL-735 carries three agent_bridge_warning{kind: judge_bridge} rows, two dated 2026-09-18 — the replay lane re-runs the bridge on a payload the current contract accepts only when re-minted, and the accepted row never reaches permanent_fail. Plan: with ARIA-MEDIUM-168.

title: anchor ground truth is tautological for the judges that formed it
rule_violated: a judge is scored against evidence it did not produce; an unmeasured judge weighs the prior; a floor is a floor over what was right.
notes: Evidence: is_ground_truth_row requires judges_voted == judge_count (no dissenter); score_judges scores every ai_judge row in the group against the group's own consensus, so a judge in an anchor group is "correct" at whatever confidence it wrote. The live fleet is exactly the three judges an anchor needs; with 0 human labels a judge can reach calibrated on its own anchors. judge_weights_from_calibration uses tp/fp regardless of status, so three human FP labels give a judge weight 0.5 and its partner alone (0.8/1.3 = 0.615 > 0.6) closes a two-judge split with judge_count = 1. The conformal floor (cycle.py:1793–1799) is taken over every ai_consensus confidence, not the correct ones. Plan: Phase 5.

title: enforce on a row count floods HUMAN_REQUIRED at the switch
rule_violated: enforcement waits for what it needs — two calibrated judges of distinct models — and labelling work goes to the label queue, not the escalation ledger.
notes: Evidence: a gate keyed on a global count of human rows (the first draft's 30) leaves every judge below its own per-judge minimum when the rows spread over three judges and two tools; every two-judge group then escalates, and sweep_consensus_uncertainties_for_human_required mints one record per group (322 judge groups live). Plan: Phase 6.

title: A judgment is prose in an envelope: every judge role is minted as a prose prompt and answered as free text whose verdict is scraped in three spellings; no schema states what a question or an answer is, what confidence means, how a malformed reply is refused by name, or how N judgments could share one call
rule_violated: A judgment is a typed question with a typed answer — a closed primitive, a schema, a stated confidence semantics, a checkable citation and a failure vocabulary — before it is a prompt
notes: Phase 1 of the typed-judgment plan: aria_kernel/typed_judgment.py — choice/score/noul questions, JudgmentBatch, hand-checked schemas, the two rendered turns, a parser with a closed reason vocabulary that never drops an item, index+quote citations checked against pinned excerpts, confidence := P(value correct). CONTRACTS.md §8.6.

title: The planner dispatch hook ran the executor child in the cycle's shared checkout while managed_subscription admission binds request.target_sha to that checkout's HEAD; on a main that moves hourly the challenger-plan request minted at 09-18's main was refused target_revision_mismatch forty times on 2026-09-19 and never ran: zero convergences, zero implementations
rule_violated: A request is served from a tree at its own anchor, by every caller that starts an executor child; the drain's per-request worktree is the one spelling, not the drain's private one
notes: Fix: aria_kernel/request_worktree.py holds the drain's add/remove bracket (bounded git, leftover reconcile, refused vs unanswered); ci_executor_drain delegates to it; the hook adds aria-worktrees/req-<id> at request_anchor_sha before the child, runs the child with cwd and ARIA_WORKSPACE_ROOT there, removes it after; a git that refuses falls back to the shared checkout, a git that does not answer starts no child, releases the lease native_runtime_control_unavailable and returns provider_control_unavailable so the daemon backs off.

title: The executor drain exited 1 on any failed child, so the nightly job read the harness's health and the agents' output quality as one colour: the first live drain after the chain restart (run 35444645590) dispatched thirty, folded twenty-seven and was red for one judge whose result the kernel rejected by name
rule_violated: A run's exit code reports whose failure it is: the harness's condition is red; a request's own rejected output is counted, detailed and warned by name, and reddens the run only when such failures dominate it
notes: Fix: drain_exit_code over the two halves of failed (harness_failed: harness_unavailable, timeout, auth_failed, credit_exhausted, process_exit, child_without_summary, selection and worktree unanswered; request_failed: policy_violation, response_schema_rejected) — 1 on any harness failure, on request failures at or above REQUEST_FAULT_RED_SHARE (0.5) of the attempted, or as the only outcome; both halves on the executor_drain_completed governance row and GITHUB_OUTPUT; a ::warning annotation per request-class failure.

title: A resumed Claude session never finds its transcript: the managed sandbox gives every spawn a tmpfs HOME holding CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, so the previous spawn's conversation is gone, --resume fails in zero turns (No conversation found with session ID), the claim is released native_runtime_execution_unavailable and the next dispatch resumes the same session again
rule_violated: A session is resumed only where its transcript will be found: the transcript outlives the spawn in a durable store the sandbox binds at the private config dir, and the resume decision reads that store
notes: Observed in executor run 35471772861: AIR-aria-challenger-planner-2d16fdbb749e, session 10c31c16-…, transcript = one `result` row `error_during_execution`, errors ['No conversation found with session ID: …'], num_turns 0, exit 1 → provider_nonzero → native_runtime_execution_unavailable, requeue_count 1. Fix: session_continuity.session_store_dir (ARIA_SESSION_STORE_DIR or ~/.config/aria/sessions), transcript_present, decide_session(store_dir=) resumes only with the transcript present; wrap_managed_claude_in_sandbox(session_store_dir=) binds <store>/projects writable at <private config>/projects after the tmpfs; both containment shapes and the executor pass the store.

title: NATS reply inbox scoped by the caller's label, not the certificate identity: the event bus passed `aquaculture-<service>` and the gateway bridges their bridge names, so their inboxes (`_INBOXAQUACULTURE_AUTH_SERVICE.`, `_INBOXGATEWAY_API_WEBSOCKET_BRIDGE.`) never matched the SSoT grants (`_INBOXAUTH_SERVICE.>`, `_INBOXGATEWAY_SERVICE.>`)
rule_violated: ADR-015: the certificate CN is the NATS identity; SEC-HIGH-098 scoped reply inboxes per identity. A prefix derived from an arbitrary caller string is a second identity source that the broker never sees.
notes: Live since 0afecd4f3 (2026-08-27) but masked: production ran a hand-edited nats.conf that still granted `_INBOX.>` until the 2026-09-19 17:35 UTC deploy reloaded the SSoT ACL, after which aqua-nats logged `Subscription Violation - User "CN=auth_service", Subject "_INBOXAQUACULTURE_AUTH_SERVICE.<nuid>.*"` every few seconds. Fix: under mTLS the factory reads the CN out of NATS_TLS_CERT (node:crypto X509Certificate) and sets inboxPrefix from it; the caller's name only labels the connection. Unit spec drives the factory with a test certificate (CN=sensor_service) and a product-prefixed caller label.

title: Scoped NATS reply-inbox prefix carried a trailing dot (`_INBOX<ID>.`): nats-core's createInbox joins prefix and nuid with its own dot, so every reply subject became `_INBOX<ID>..<nuid>` — an empty token no `_INBOX<ID>.>` grant matches — and every fresh service was refused at connect
rule_violated: SEC-HIGH-098 scoped inboxes: the prefix contract is dot-less (`_INBOXBILLINGCFG`, e2e note 'createInbox appends .<nuid>'); the factory's `_INBOX<ID>.` form (2026-08-27) and its CN-based successor both broke it.
notes: Seen on the droplet after the 750db0409f deploy: config-service `Bootstrap failed: Permissions Violation for Subscription to "_INBOXCONFIG_SERVICE..CP4LF3z8bkmc9GvNm1q55w.*"`. Verified with the installed nats-core: createInbox('_INBOXX.') → `_INBOXX..<nuid>`, createInbox('_INBOXX') → `_INBOXX.<nuid>`. Fix: scopedInboxPrefix returns `_INBOX<ID>` with no dot; the spec now asserts the createInbox-derived subject sits under the grant and contains no `..`.

title: services.yaml enumerates JetStream STREAM/CONSUMER rights but not `$JS.API.INFO`, which @nats-io/jetstream's jetstreamManager() publishes at construction (checkAPI) — every JetStream user is refused at connect under the SSoT ACL
rule_violated: SENSOR-HIGH-092 (Task 2) enumerated JetStream rights per service so the bare `$JS.API.>` root could go; the enumeration missed the one subject the client library requires before any stream call.
notes: aqua-nats after the 750db0409f deploy: `Publish Violation - User "CN=admin_api_service", Subject "$JS.API.INFO"` and the same for event_store, observability, messaging, config, notification, hydroponics, alert_engine, ai, hr (10–21 each within four minutes). Masked until 2026-09-19 by the hand-edited production nats.conf. Fix: `$JS.API.INFO` publish for every identity holding a `$JS.API.*` grant (17 services incl. dlq_replayer), nats.conf regenerated, and a nats-invariants case that fails when a JetStream user lacks it.

title: Twelve modules in farm-service and admin-api-service re-provide a class another module of the same app already provides and exports (ProtocolRateService ×5, DayPlanRecalcService ×4, BatchDomainService, BiomassGrowthApplierService, AuthTenantProvisioningClientService): each is a second instance resolved in the copying module, the shape that left sensor-service unbootable
rule_violated: NestJS module boundaries: import the exporting module; a re-provided class is a fork of its instance and of its dependency resolution.
notes: Carried as the KNOWN_DUPLICATES baseline of the new invariant; the list only shrinks. Each removal replaces the provider entry with an import of the exporting module (watch for cycles between BatchModule and FeedingProtocolModule, which re-provide each other's services).

title: SensorErasureModule re-provides MqttAuthService instead of importing EdgeDeviceModule, which exports it: Nest builds a second instance whose EdgeDevice repository is unresolvable there — sensor-service has failed to boot on every deploy of main since 65753cb90 (2026-08-26), and the erasure hook would have invalidated a cache no request reads
rule_violated: NestJS module boundaries: a class another module provides and exports is obtained by importing that module; re-providing it forks the instance and re-resolves its dependencies where the copy lives.
notes: Live error on the 750db0409 image: Nest can't resolve dependencies of the MqttAuthService (ConfigService, ?, DataSource, DeviceDirectoryService) … EdgeDeviceRepository at index [1] is not available in SensorErasureModule. Fix: imports: [EdgeDeviceModule], provider entry removed; tests/invariants/nest-module-provider-duplication.spec.ts bans the pattern (pre-existing farm/admin duplicates baselined under ORPHAN-MEDIUM-833).

title: ModulePricingService imports DiscountCodeService as a type only, so emitDecoratorMetadata records `Function` for that constructor parameter and Nest cannot resolve it — billing-service has failed to boot on every deploy of main since 3352ceda6 (2026-09-07)
rule_violated: NestJS constructor injection resolves through design:paramtypes; a type-only import is erased and leaves no token. Compiler, linter and hand-built unit tests cannot see it.
notes: Live error on the 750db0409 image: Nest can't resolve dependencies of the ModulePricingService (ModulePriceRepository, DataSource, ?) … argument Function at index [2]. Fix: value import; tests/invariants/nest-injected-type-only-import.spec.ts bans the shape repo-wide (the only other hit, ClaudeApiBudgetService, was a hand-built class wearing a decorative @Injectable, now removed).

title: No gate compiles any service's NestJS dependency graph before deploy: billing-service (13 days) and sensor-service (25 days) sat unbootable on main behind green CI, and the production container was the first thing to resolve their modules
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md architectural hierarchy tier 3 (make it detectable): a defect class that only the production container reveals has no gate. The two shape-specific invariants landed with this cycle catch the two shapes seen; an unresolvable token of any other origin (missing import, wrong scope, circular forwardRef) still reaches production first.
notes: Shape of the fix: a per-service DI-graph check that builds the container from AppModule metadata without instantiating providers (Nest's DependenciesScanner + a resolvability pass over every constructor token against the module's providers, imported exports and global modules), run by ci-affected for each affected app. Runs without a database or broker.

title: farm-service cannot boot: FeedingModule's re-provided copy of DayPlanRecalcService has no ProtocolResolutionService to resolve, and TenantOnboardingEventHandler types its readiness checker as `Pick<…,'check'>`, which leaves `Object` in the metadata — found by the new DI-graph gate, never by CI
rule_violated: NestJS module boundaries and constructor injection: a re-provided class resolves its dependencies where the copy lives; a constructor parameter must be annotated with a value-level class or carry an explicit token.
notes: Live error on the 750db0409 image once auth was healthy enough for farm to start: Nest can't resolve dependencies of the DayPlanRecalcService (OutboxPublisher, ?) … ProtocolResolutionService at index [1] … in FeedingModule; behind it, TenantOnboardingEventHandler (…, ?, …). Fix: FeedingProtocolCoreModule (leaf) provides the four shared protocol services once and every consumer imports it; the handler's parameter is the class, the spec uses a typed collaborator double.

title: gateway-api cannot boot: TenantConnectionLimiter is registered with useClass although its constructor takes a plain options object, and WsTokenRevalidator's factory injects TOKEN_BLACKLIST_STORE, a provider of the root module that WebSocketModule cannot see — both live since a77b0f74f (2026-08-27)
rule_violated: NestJS constructor injection and module scope: a hand-built class is registered by useFactory; a token a child module needs is exported by the module that owns it, not declared on the root.
notes: Live errors on the 750db0409 image: Nest can't resolve dependencies of the TenantConnectionLimiter (?) … index [0]; then WsTokenRevalidator (?) … Symbol(TOKEN_BLACKLIST_STORE) … in WebSocketModule. Fix: useFactory for the limiter (decorative @Injectable removed from both guards); TokenBlacklistModule owns and exports the store, imported by AppModule and WebSocketModule.

title: The Z.ai and Codex native paths passed request.convergence_id (None for every fan-out judge request) to the cost ledger, whose refusal the attempt caught as control_or_transport_unavailable after the verdict was written: the first Z.ai adversarial judgment after the declared-provider fix was paid, parsed, written and then released as a harness fault to be judged and discarded again
rule_violated: A cost row's identity is derived once, the same way on every runtime path; a request the fan-out minted without a convergence is attributed to plan-<request tail> as the Claude path always did, and a paid verdict is never released over bookkeeping it cannot fail
notes: Observed in executor run 35485712865 (main 0239eecc8): AIR-aria-adversarial-judge-8281c4e19fd1 routed zai/glm-5.3 (161 works), runtime_attempt_finished exit_code 200 result_admission control_or_transport_unavailable, envelope written with the verdict, claim requeued native_runtime_execution_unavailable requeue_count 0; the request row carries convergence_id null. Fix: ci_executor._cost_identity(request, request_id) — the Claude path's derivation extracted — used by the Z.ai, Codex and batch paths.

title: gateway-api cannot boot since 3d609b9c0: resolveErrorCapturePublisher wraps app.get('EVENT_BUS') in a try/catch that never runs — NestFactory's ExceptionsZone (abortOnError default) logs the UnknownElementException and process.exit(1)s first; gateway registers no event bus by design
rule_violated: Root-cause hierarchy tier 3 (make it detectable): the optional-provider fallback was tested nowhere that boots through NestFactory.create — Test.createTestingModule has no ExceptionsZone, so the only place the code path exists is production.
notes: Production deploy of ab0f8b203a (run 35504545888): aqua-gateway restarted 16 times in 4 minutes, every boot ending at `Nest could not find EVENT_BUS element` from resolveErrorCapturePublisher (create-service-app.js:189) — nginx 502 for the whole platform even after the ACL, DI and consumer blockers were cleared. Fix: resolveOptionalProvider() looks the token up through ModuleRef (same container, no ExceptionsZone) and answers undefined on UnknownElementException; spec boots NoEventBusModule through NestFactory.create and pins both the fallback and the exit the old code caused.

title: NatsEventBus registers durable consumers with @nats-io/jetstream's create-only action: nats-server refuses `consumers.add()` with "consumer already exists" (10148) whenever the durable exists with a previous release's configuration, so every subscriber dies at onModuleInit on the first deploy after any consumer field changes (max_deliver 3 → -1)
rule_violated: ARCH-020: a durable consumer is created or updated in place, never recreated; the v3 client migration (A3) changed the server action the bus sends from create-or-update to create without a test that holds a previous release's consumer.
notes: Release ab0f8b203@20260920T111748Z: twelve services logged 'Bootstrap failed: consumer already exists' once the DI and ACL fixes let them reach JetStream; config/event-store/observability (no changed durables) came up healthy. Stored consumer aquaculture-auth-service-events---TenantSubscriptionChanged has max_deliver 3; the code sends -1. Verified on nats:2.10.24: create with a differing config → 10148; consumers.update() → OK and the ack position survives; identical create is idempotent; a non-updatable change (deliver_policy) → 10012, still loud. The library cannot send the empty create-or-update action (opts.action || 'create'), so the bus creates, and on 10148 updates by durable name.

title: No test boots NatsEventBus against a broker that already holds a previous release's durable consumers: the unit suite mocks the JetStream manager and CI's broker starts empty, so a change in consumer-create semantics (or any consumer field) is first exercised by production
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md architectural hierarchy tier 3 (make it detectable): the boot-path smoke proves the ACL and the JetStream API path per identity but starts from an empty store; the durable-consumer path is only pinned against a mock.
notes: Shape of the fix: extend the boot-path harness (a real broker via docker, one cert per identity) with a durable that a 'previous release' created with a differing updatable field, then drive the bus's real subscription path (NatsEventBus in a Nest testing context against NATS_URL) and assert the durable is updated in place and its ack position kept; a non-updatable change must fail loudly.

title: farm-service cannot boot: three source-schema tables recorded as migrated (feeding_record_attribution_quarantine template, tenant_localization, feeding_job_runs) no longer exist, so the SchemaDriftValidator refuses the cold start; the migration ledger and the schema disagree and no migration re-aligns them
rule_violated: ADR-012 schema drift: the DB is aligned to the entities by a migration (docs/runbooks/schema-drift-response.md path a); a recorded migration whose objects are gone is drift the ledger cannot see.
notes: Release e9fd27bf3: 15/16 services healthy, aqua-farm fatal on schema.drift.detected (3 violations). db-migrate had logged 'absentTables: [feeding_record_attribution_quarantine]' every run and proceeded. Cause (mechanism verified in schema-manager.service.ts): SourceSchemaBootstrapService in strict mode DROP…CASCADEs source tables its own image's MODULE_SCHEMAS does not list; 2026-09-17 locally built farm images from an older branch reaped the three newest farm tables as orphans (tenant clones untouched). Fix: two new migrations recreate them IF NOT EXISTS (per-tenant template unqualified + fan-out; infrastructure ledgers schema-qualified + @SourceOnlyMigration), proven on a throwaway Postgres shaped like production: all three restored, tenant clone and rows untouched, template columns identical to the clone, idempotent.

title: SourceSchemaBootstrapService (strict mode) DROP…CASCADEs every source-schema table absent from the RUNNING image's MODULE_SCHEMAS: starting any older image against a newer database destroys the tables the newer migrations created, while their migration rows stay recorded — the mechanism that removed farm's three feeding ledgers on 2026-09-17
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md tier 1 (make it impossible): a runtime that destroys data the migration authority created is a second, unversioned writer of the schema; db-migrate is the DDL authority (ADR-011/012). Orphan handling must be non-destructive (quarantine/rename or refuse to boot), and a table created by a migration the ledger records must never count as an orphan.
notes: Shape of the fix: the bootstrap consults the schema's migration ledger (a table whose creating migration is recorded is never an orphan) and, for genuine orphans, renames into a quarantine namespace or fails closed with a drift alert instead of dropping; db-migrate treats absentTables for recorded migrations as a hard failure rather than a log line, so the ledger/schema disagreement stops the deploy before a service refuses to boot.

title: Three farm source-schema tables are missing although their creating migrations (1808700000000, 1809100000000) are recorded with passing postConditions — cause not established — and nothing between db-migrate and service health detects a database that no longer matches the entities: the deploy fails at the service's cold start twenty minutes after the migration step said it was done
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md tier 3 (make it detectable) and ADR-012: schema drift is validated at each service's cold start, but the migration authority that could stop the deploy runs no drift check itself; a ledger/schema disagreement therefore surfaces as a health failure, not as a failed migration step.
notes: Supersedes DATA-HIGH-017, which attributed the loss to SourceSchemaBootstrapService dropping unregistered source tables; on main that service throws (assertNoOrphanTables) and the DROP…CASCADE was removed in 42695736f (2026-06-08), before either migration existed — the schema-manager.service.ts docblock describing the drop is stale text. Established: ledger rows exist, the quarantine table exists only in the tenant clone, the two clock ledgers exist nowhere, no db-migrate run since 2026-09-17 logged a drop, and the applying run's container is gone. Candidates: the source pass executed under a tenant-first search_path, or a manual drop. Detectable fix: db-migrate runs the SchemaDriftValidator for every service after its migrations and fails the run — and the deploy — when the database is unlike the entities; plus absentTables for a recorded migration becomes a hard failure rather than a log line. Restoration itself: FARM-CRITICAL-332.

title: gateway_service subscribes `telemetry.*.SensorReading` (WebSocket bridge, since SENSOR-HIGH-092 moved SensorReading to the telemetry root) but services.yaml grants it only `events.>` — 2 Subscription Violations at every gateway boot, live readings never reach the dashboards
rule_violated: ADR-015: every subject a service subscribes needs an explicit grant in services.yaml; the RPC-coverage invariant read only @MessagePattern/@EventPattern, so a raw core `connection.subscribe()` literal was invisible to the gate.
notes: aqua-nats after the b5e04c65 deploy: `Subscription Violation - User "CN=gateway_service", Subject "telemetry.*.SensorReading"` twice at gateway boot (16:32Z); non-fatal — the gateway stays healthy, the bridge simply never receives a reading. Fix: `telemetry.*.SensorReading` subscribe grant for gateway_service, nats.conf regenerated, and extractRpcUsage now treats `.subscribe('<literal>')` as a handled subject with `telemetry.` added to the recognised roots — the negative run reproduces the drift as `handled patterns with NO subscribe grant: telemetry.*.SensorReading`.

title: The droplet deploy contract is unsatisfiable: sensor-ingestion is catalogued `required` while the deploy never ships its image (rust-sidecar excluded from the image matrix, compose pins it to the deploy's ${TAG}, droplet-up neither pulls nor starts it) — every release ledger since 2026-08-28 reads failed/required_health and promotion is blocked
rule_violated: A criticality level is a promise the post-deploy health gate enforces; it may only be made for a service the deploy can place on the host. No invariant related the catalog's criticality to the image matrix, so the 2026-08-28 'honesty flip' to required went green in CI and red on every droplet run.
notes: Runs 35514785422 and 35520382281 (2026-09-20): `[required] sensor-ingestion — container not found` → `Required service health check failed. Promotion blocked without automatic rollback`, `status=failed phase=required_health` — with 16/16 real services healthy and login working. Fix: criticality 'warning' (the truthful deploy promise today) and `deployShipsImage()` in the catalog with a parity invariant that fails any critical/required active droplet entry whose image the deploy does not build or pull; the sidecar pin now expects 'warning'. Actually shipping the sidecar (own SENSOR_INGESTION_TAG, pull + start in droplet-up, health) is the tracked follow-up that lifts it back to 'required'.

title: required-signals.yaml asserts a boot signal for sensor-ingestion, a service the deploy never ships — the same unsatisfiable promise DEPLOY-HIGH-024 removed from the health gate, through the boot-signal gate: run 35529464872 passed health, failed `phase=boot_signal` on `[sensor-ingestion] nats_auth_mode_mtls` and rolled back
rule_violated: A deploy gate may only assert what the deploy can observe; the required-signals artifact was derived from `requiredSignals` alone, ignoring whether the service's image ever reaches the host. DEPLOY-HIGH-024 introduced `deployShipsImage()` for the criticality contract but did not apply it to the sibling contract.
notes: Deploy 8c9795f3 (2026-09-20 19:30Z): `all critical/required services satisfied`, then `Missing boot signals: [sensor-ingestion] nats_auth_mode_mtls` → `Boot signal assertion failed. Initiating rollback` → ledger `rolled_back phase=boot_signal`; the droplet stayed on 8c9795f3 and healthy (login OK). Fix: the generator derives the manifest only from entries `deployShipsImage()` accepts, and the parity invariant asserts an un-shipped service is absent from it (sensor-ingestion pinned absent).

title: NatsV3Client.publish() builds the reply inbox from the registration option alone (`createInbox(this.options.inboxPrefix)`), so every ClientProxy without an explicit prefix subscribes the default `_INBOX.<nuid>` — refused under the identity-scoped grants (INFRA-HIGH-179) — and no platform request/reply through the proxy receives its answer
rule_violated: ADR-015: the reply inbox is a property of the identity on the wire (cert CN), decided by the connection factory; a second, registration-time decision that can disagree with it must not exist. INFRA-HIGH-179 scoped the factory and the grants but left the proxy's own createInbox() on the registration option — the unit spec covered the factory, no test drove publish().
notes: aqua-nats after the 8c9795f3 deploy, 19:37:00–01Z: ten `Subscription Violation - User "CN=gateway_service", Subject "_INBOX.XqtwFWfJUUH15AE22mf…"` in one second — the gateway's WebSocket RPCs (verifyMembership, verifyDeviceOwnership, request.ai.chat) subscribing the ungranted default root; the same path serves admin-api (6 clients), messaging (5), ai, hr, sensor. Latent since #1637 replaced `_INBOX.>` with `_INBOX<IDENTITY>.>`; HTTP/GraphQL login was unaffected, so it survived every probe today. Fix: the client captures the prefix the factory put on the connection at connect() (registration override kept for the separately granted `_INBOXBILLINGCFG` / `_INBOXFARMMARINECFG` channels) and publish() creates every inbox under it; a spec drives the real publish() through a stubbed transport and fails on the `_INBOX.` root.

title: The reply leg of every request/reply is refused under the scoped inbox grants: a requester's inbox is `_INBOX<ITS CN>.<nuid>` but no responder holds a publish grant for another identity's inbox root (only `_INBOX.>`), so the broker logs `Publish Violation` at the responder and the caller times out — proven on nats:2.10.24 with main's conf
rule_violated: ADR-015: the generated authorization block must let an identity complete the protocols its grants imply; scoping the requester's inbox (INFRA-HIGH-179) without a reply mechanism for responders left request/reply half-granted. Nothing exercised a two-identity round trip against the generated conf.
notes: Found by aqua-saas-0a's live-broker probe after #1654 (publish to `_INBOXGATEWAY_SERVICE.probe` as auth_service → Publish Violation) and reproduced on a throwaway nats:2.10.24 with main's nats.conf: gateway_service → messaging_service `request.messaging.verifyMembership` times out with one `Publish Violation - User "CN=messaging_service", Subject "_INBOXGATEWAY_SERVICE.<nuid>.<n>"`. Only the two config-reply prefixes worked because config_service holds explicit `_INBOXBILLINGCFG.>`/`_INBOXFARMMARINECFG.>` publish grants. Fix: the generator emits `allow_responses: { max: 64, expires: "5m" }` for every user — a responder may publish only to the reply subject of a request it received; same probe on the new conf: reply lands, zero violations. Invariant: every generated user block carries exactly one allow_responses. The blanket `_INBOX.>` publish grants are now inert (no one subscribes that root) and stay until a separate tightening.
