title: The tenant-creation wizard answered a failed module price-sheet read by offering the same modules priced from a hard-coded guess, and answered a second failure by telling the operator to go define modules that already exist
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Working Style: report faithfully — a catalogue that did not load must not be rendered as a catalogue that is empty, and quantities the operator provisions against must come from the price sheet, not from a constant
notes: Found in W8v while migrating CreateTenantPage, and fixed in the same commit. The module catalogue loaded in a useEffect with a silent double fallback. getModulePricingWithModules() failing wrote console.warn and fell through to modulesApi.list(), whose module rows carry no pricing metrics at all — so every module was offered with a hard-coded seed of {users: 1, farms: 1, storageGb: 1} instead of each metric's includedQuantity, and an operator could walk the whole wizard and provision a tenant whose subscribed quantities were a constant nobody chose. A second failure wrote another console.warn and left the list empty, which the page rendered as "No modules found — Please define modules in Billing > Module Pricing page first": an instruction to create data that very likely already exists, for a request that did not return. Nothing on screen ever said the price sheet had not loaded. The page already states the correct principle one step later for the quote (ADR-0013) — the number comes from billing or the page says it could not price the selection — so offering unpriceable modules is that same defect one step earlier. Fixed by moving the read to useAdminQuery on adminKeys.billing.modulePricing() with the abort signal threaded through billingApi.getModulePricingWithModules, deleting the modulesApi.list fallback and its hard-coded quantities, seeding each quantity from the sheet's includedQuantity, and rendering QueryFailureNotice with the failed read named and a Retry rather than the empty-catalogue copy. Re-registered on 2026-09-27: the branch had minted ADMIN-HIGH-135 for this finding on 2026-09-09, and on 2026-09-19 main minted the same id for an unrelated finding (Copernicus credential operator surface, commit e959f5811). main is merged and immutable, so main keeps 135 and this finding takes the next free id; the branch commit ac780802d still names 135 in its Closes: trailer, which is recorded in the commit-msg validator allowlist with this reason.

title: The billing overview reported an unreachable invoice service as "no recent transactions", swapped in a different endpoint's MRR whenever the real one was zero, and rendered six of the eight invoice states — overdue and refunded among them — as "failed"
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Working Style: report faithfully — on a money surface a failed read must not be rendered as an absence of money, a real zero must not be replaced by another question's answer, and a receivable's state must not be restated as a failure
notes: Found in W9a while migrating BillingDashboardPage to the admin data layer, and fixed in the same commit. Three independent misstatements, all on the platform's money overview. First, the Recent Transactions feed loaded behind a bare `catch { return [] }`, so billing being unreachable rendered as "No recent transactions" — a claim that the platform took no money, produced by a request that never answered. Second, the metric composition used `||` rather than `??` for mrr, arr and averageRevenuePerUser: `subs.mrr || revenue.mrr` treats a genuine 0 as absent, so a tenant base that really bills nothing silently displayed the analytics endpoint's figure under the subscriptions heading — not a stale number but a different question's answer. Third, billing.invoices.status holds eight states (draft, pending, sent, paid, partially_paid, overdue, void, refunded) and the feed collapsed them into three, mapping paid and pending and calling EVERYTHING ELSE "failed", so a sent invoice, an overdue receivable, a draft, a partial payment, a void and a refund all rendered with a red Failed badge; an overdue invoice is money still owed, not money that failed to move. Fixed by moving all three reads to useAdminQuery on adminKeys.billing.dashboardMetrics/revenueTrend/recentInvoices with abort signals threaded through getRevenueAnalytics, getSubscriptionStats, getInvoiceStats, getPaymentStats and getInvoices; replacing the fallbacks with `??`; rendering QueryFailureNotice for each failed read instead of an empty state; and giving each of the eight invoice states its own label and badge.

title: The invoice list asserted "Overdue: $0" from a useState seeded with zeros before billing had answered and forever after a failed read, restated five of the contract's eleven stat fields in a page-local type, and offered five of the eight invoice states as filters
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Working Style: report faithfully — a money total that has not loaded must render as absent, not as zero, and a filter vocabulary the server owns must not be restated as a subset
notes: Found in W9b while migrating InvoicesPage to the admin data layer, and fixed in the same commit. Three defects. First, the five money totals above the table lived in `useState<InvoiceStats>({totalInvoices: 0, totalAmount: 0, totalPaid: 0, totalPending: 0, totalOverdue: 0})`, so before billing answered — and permanently if getInvoiceStats failed, since the catch only set an error string and left the zeros standing — the page asserted $0 owed, $0 overdue and 0 invoices. A zero owed is a specific, reassuring claim about receivables and an unanswered request is no basis for it. Second, a page-local `InvoiceStats` interface restated five of the contract type's eleven fields, so the page was structurally blind to byStatus, byCurrency, avgPaymentTime, overdueRate, paidThisMonth and pendingThisMonth and could drift from the server shape without the compiler noticing. Third, the status filter row offered ['all','paid','pending','overdue','void'] while billing.invoices.status holds eight values, so a draft, a sent invoice, a partially_paid one and a refunded one could not be filtered for at all and were reachable only by scrolling an unfiltered list. Fixed by moving both reads to useAdminQuery on adminKeys.billing.invoices(filters) and invoiceStats() with abort signals, deleting the shadow type in favour of the contract's, rendering an em dash wherever a total has not loaded, surfacing either failed read through QueryFailureNotice, taking the filter options from the server's full vocabulary, and replacing the three writes' hand-rolled Promise.all refetch with a single reload of both queries.

title: The payments page computed "Net Revenue" in the browser from the 50 rows it had loaded and the active status filter, so filtering to failed showed $0 net, and the endpoint it should have read instead returned a shape the OpenAPI artifact described only as {"type": "object"}
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Working Style: report faithfully — a platform total may not be a subtotal of whatever rows are on screen; and CONTRACT-CRITICAL-003: a response typed by an interface is undescribed in the generated contract, which is what invites the frontend to hand-write its own copy
notes: Found in W9c while migrating PaymentsPage to the admin data layer, and fixed in the same commit. The three money cards — Succeeded Amount, Refunded, Net Revenue — were summed in the browser from `payments`, one page of at most 50 rows, narrowed further by whatever status filter was active. Two consequences on the platform's revenue figure: filtering to `failed` made Net Revenue read $0, because no succeeded row was in the array being summed; and any platform with more than 50 payments saw the net of its first page presented as its net revenue. The aggregate belongs to the server, which already ran the GROUP BY that produced the counts, so summarizePaymentStatusCounts now also returns succeededAmount and refundedAmount and both SQL windows select COALESCE(SUM(p.refunded_amount), 0). refundedAmount sums refunded_amount rather than the amount of rows whose status is refunded, because a partially refunded payment returned only part of itself and still captured in full — the distinction the client-side sum could not make. Surfacing those fields exposed a second defect: GET /billing/payments/stats was typed by an INTERFACE, and the @nestjs/swagger plugin describes classes only, so the generated artifact carried "schema": {"type": "object"} for an endpoint the admin-panel reads its money cards from — which is precisely what invited the frontend to hand-write its own PaymentStats beside the contract. A PaymentStatsResponseDto class now types the response, the artifact carries a $ref, and the frontend type is an ApiSchema alias. Also removed from the page: an `as unknown as string` cast inside a typeof-narrowed branch (banned by CLAUDE.md and type-checking nothing), a floating fetchPayments() in a useEffect and after two writes, and `data.total || 0`.

title: The subscription page's Retry button could never clear the error it offered to retry, because nothing ever assigned the error state back to null, and three lifecycle writes passed a literal 'admin' actor under a TODO describing a gap the server had already closed
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Working Style: report faithfully — a page that offers a Retry must be able to leave the failed state; and CLAUDE.md Code Quality: floating promises are forbidden
notes: Found in W9d while migrating SubscriptionManagementPage to the admin data layer, and fixed in the same commit. The page's render returned a full-page error whenever `error` was set; `loadData` assigned it in its catch and NOTHING anywhere assigned null again — grep for setError(null) returned zero hits. So after one transient failure the Retry button fetched successfully and the page went on showing the error permanently, until a browser reload. Moving both reads to useAdminQuery fixes this by construction: a query's error is derived from its last outcome, so a successful refetch clears it. The four loadData() call sites were also floating promises, which CLAUDE.md bans. Separately, the three lifecycle writes — cancel, extend trial, reactivate — passed a literal 'admin' as an actor under a `// TODO: get from auth context` comment. That comment was wrong and dangerous: the client functions took the argument as `_cancelledBy`/`_reactivatedBy`/`_extendedBy` and never put it on the wire, and the server derives the actor from the authenticated request via getAuthUserId(req), refusing with 401 when absent, under @AuditedOperation and @RequiresCapability('billing-ops'). The audit trail was therefore correct all along; the TODO invited a future contributor to 'fix' it by sending a client-supplied actor, which is what would have opened a real accountability hole. The dead arguments and the comment are gone. Write failures now have their own state, kept apart from the reads' so a failed cancel no longer blanks the list the operator is working on. What this page already got right is left alone: the stat cards are guarded by `{stats && …}`, so unlike its siblings in this batch it never invented a zero.

title: On the metered-billing dashboard three of four reads discarded their errors, so an unanswered request rendered as "No usage data" — zero consumption on the surface invoices are built from — and the Refresh Data button refreshed one read of the four
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Working Style: report faithfully — on a metered-billing surface a failed read must not be rendered as zero consumption, and a control labelled "Refresh Data" must refresh the data
notes: Found in W9e while migrating UsageDashboardPage to the admin data layer, and fixed in the same commit. The page ran four useAsyncData reads — summary, all-tenants usage, trends, top-tenants — and only the summary destructured an `error`. The other three discarded theirs entirely, and each rendered its failure as an empty result: 'No usage data for this period' for a failed trends read, 'No tenant usage data for this meter type' for a failed top-tenants read, and 'No tenant usage data available' for a failed tenants read. On a metered-billing dashboard those are claims about consumption, and consumption is exactly what the invoice is computed from; an unanswered request is not zero usage. Second defect on the same page: the button labelled 'Refresh Data' called refreshSummary, so it refreshed one of the four reads and left the other three showing whatever they already held — an operator pressing it to get current numbers got one current number and three stale ones, with nothing to distinguish them. Fixed by moving all four reads to useAdminQuery on adminKeys.billing.usageSummary/usageTenants/usageTrends/usageTopTenants — each keyed by its own discriminators so a trend for one period cannot overwrite another's, nor a top-tenants list for one meter another meter's — threading an abort signal through all four client functions, surfacing every failed read through QueryFailureNotice, and pointing both refresh controls at all four queries.

title: The module pricing page caught both its read and its save, wrote console.error, and replaced the server's own refusal with "Please try again" — so an operator whose multiplier the server rejected with a reason retried the same rejected value forever
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Working Style: report faithfully — a refusal that names what is wrong must not be replaced by a sentence that names nothing; and CLAUDE.md Code Quality: console.* is forbidden
notes: Found in W9f while migrating ModulePricingPage to the admin data layer, and fixed in the same commit. Both the read and the save caught their error, wrote console.error (banned by CLAUDE.md), and set a fixed string: 'Failed to load module pricings. Please try again.' and 'Failed to save pricing. Please try again.' The server's own message went nowhere. On the save that is the worse of the two, because the server does not fail vaguely: the contract takes an exact decimal tier multiplier in (0, 10] and REFUSES anything outside it with a reason rather than coercing — a rule this very page already records in a comment on handleTierMultiplierChange, added by an earlier wave. Replacing that refusal with 'Please try again' means the operator retries the same rejected value, receives the same generic sentence, and never learns which field is wrong; the one piece of information that could end the loop is the one thing discarded. The same applies to the read, where a capability refusal and a network outage were rendered identically. Fixed by moving the read to useAdminQuery on adminKeys.billing.modulePricing() with an abort signal, the save to useAdminMutation invalidating that key instead of hand-reloading, and surfacing both errors verbatim through QueryFailureNotice. Also fixed alongside: `parseInt(value) || 0` on the included-quantity field, which silently turned '1OO' into 1 and 'abc' into 0 on a field that decides what a tenant is charged for — an unparseable entry now leaves the quantity alone, which is the same reasoning the earlier wave applied to the multiplier one function below and had not applied here.

title: The plan catalogue page held two standards of honesty at once — its deprecate write surfaced the server's real message while its read wrote console.error and replaced the reason with "Failed to load plans. Please try again."
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Working Style: report faithfully — a page may not tell the operator exactly what went wrong on one path and nothing at all on another; and CLAUDE.md Code Quality: console.* is forbidden, floating promises are forbidden
notes: Found in W9g while migrating PlanManagementPage to the admin data layer, and fixed in the same commit. loadPlans caught its error, wrote console.error (banned), and set the fixed string 'Failed to load plans. Please try again.', which the render then showed as a full-page takeover with a Retry. One function below, handleDeprecatePlan set (err as Error).message — the server's actual reason. The same page therefore told an operator precisely what was wrong when a write failed and nothing whatsoever when a read did, which also means the read's failure could not be distinguished from a capability refusal, an outage, or a bad gateway. Severity is MEDIUM rather than HIGH because unlike its siblings in this batch the page never rendered a fabricated number: it failed loudly, just uninformatively. Fixed by moving the read to useAdminQuery on adminKeys.billing.plans(true) with an abort signal, the deprecate write to useAdminMutation invalidating that key rather than calling loadPlans() as a floating promise, and surfacing both errors verbatim through QueryFailureNotice — inline rather than as a full-page takeover, because a refused deprecate is a message about that action and not a reason to remove the catalogue the operator is reading. The plans key now carries includeInactive as a discriminator so an inactive-inclusive listing cannot overwrite a public one in a single cache entry.

title: A discount code's redemption cap was built with `parseInt(value, 10) || undefined`, and undefined means unlimited — so a typo, and the number 0, both produced a discount code that could be redeemed without limit
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Working Style: report faithfully — a cap field whose only purpose is to bound redemption must not silently remove the bound; `||` treats 0 as absent and 0 is the clearest way to say "none"
notes: Found in W9h while migrating DiscountCodePage to the admin data layer, and fixed in the same commit. discount-rules.ts:104-106 and 112-114 enforce a redemption cap ONLY when it is neither null nor undefined, so undefined means unlimited. The create form built both caps with `parseInt(e.target.value, 10) || undefined`, which produces undefined from three different operator inputs: any unparseable entry ('abc', or a stray letter in '1OO') gives NaN and therefore undefined; an empty field gives undefined, which is correct and is what the placeholder promises; and the literal 0 gives `0 || undefined` — undefined. That last case is the sharpest, because 0 is the clearest way an operator can say 'this code may not be redeemed', and it produced a code with no cap at all, on a field whose only purpose is to bound how much revenue a discount can give away. The display was the same defect in reverse: `value={newCode.maxRedemptions || ''}` blanked a stored 0, so the box could not show the value it held. Fixed with a parseRedemptionCap helper — empty still means unlimited, a real number is kept including 0, and an unparseable entry leaves the previous value alone rather than silently removing the limit — and `?? ''` for display. Also fixed alongside: `isActive: showActive || undefined` sent NO filter when the Active box was unticked, so clearing it widened the listing to every code rather than narrowing it to the inactive ones the label implies. Both reads moved to useAdminQuery on adminKeys.billing.discountCodes(filters)/discountStats() with abort signals; the three write handlers, whose error surfacing was already honest, keep their own error block and now refresh through the cache rather than a floating loadData().

title: The custom-plan builder zeroed a priced quantity on any typo, announced a failed approval submission through the green success box with its reason discarded by a bare catch, and replaced the price sheet's own load failure with "Please try again"
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Working Style: report faithfully — a quantity a price is computed from must not be zeroed by a typo, and a failure must not be announced as a success with its reason thrown away
notes: Found in W9j while migrating CustomPlanBuilderPage to the admin data layer, and fixed in the same commit. Three defects on the page that prices a negotiated plan. First, `parseInt(e.target.value) || 0` on each module quantity turned any unparseable entry — a stray letter in '1OO', for instance — into 0, silently, on a field this plan's PRICE is computed from; the quote then returned lower and the plan could be created at it. Clearing the box still means 0, which is what the operator asked for, but a typo now leaves the previous quantity alone. Second, after createCustomPlan succeeds the page auto-submits for approval, and that step sat behind a bare `catch {}` which announced its failure through setSuccess — in the GREEN success box, with the server's reason discarded entirely. The plan really is created either way, so it is a partial success; but an operator could not tell a capability refusal from a validation rejection, and had nothing to act on. The creation is still reported as the success it is, and the submit's failure is now reported as a failure carrying the server's own words. Third, the catalogue load wrote console.error (banned) and set 'Failed to load module pricing. Please try again.' — the same endpoint and the same words ModulePricingPage used before ADMIN-HIGH-141, so a capability refusal and an outage looked identical and retrying only hit the same wall. Fixed by moving the read to useAdminQuery on adminKeys.billing.modulePricing() with an abort signal and surfacing it through QueryFailureNotice, a parseQuantity helper for the quantity fields, and splitting the partial-success reporting into its true halves.

title: The announcements page failed silently on all four of its writes, rendered a failed acknowledgment roster as "No activity yet", dropped its header strip on a failed stats read, opened the statistics modal from the Edit pencil, deleted a platform announcement with no confirmation, and crashed on Schedule with no date — over three reads that carried no response schema at all
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Working Style: report faithfully — a refused broadcast must not be indistinguishable from a delivered one, and an unread answer must not be rendered as a measurement; CONTRACT-CRITICAL-003: a response the panel renders must have a described schema
notes: Found in W9k while migrating AnnouncementsPage to the admin data layer, and fixed in the same commit. This page broadcasts to every tenant and was the quietest page in the panel about whether it had. (1) Publish, cancel, delete and create each caught their error into console.error (banned) and told the operator NOTHING, then refetched — so a REFUSED publish of a global `critical` maintenance notice looked exactly like a successful one: same click, same repaint, no message, and the operator's belief that every tenant had been notified was the only thing that changed. (2) The acknowledgment modal read `data.acknowledgments || []` behind a console.error, so an unreachable endpoint and a genuinely unseen announcement drew the same sentence, 'No activity yet', on the one screen that answers who has read a notice they were REQUIRED to read. (3) A failed stats read left `stats` null and the header strip simply vanished, unannounced. (4) The Edit pencil on a draft opened the STATISTICS modal; the form modal already titles itself 'Edit Announcement' and accepts an existing announcement, but nothing ever passed it one, so the audited PUT route had no caller in the panel. (5) The trash icon destroyed an announcement on a single click, on a route the backend marks @Destructive(), while the plan page confirms a mere deprecate. (6) 'Schedule' with an empty date picker called new Date('').toISOString(), which throws a RangeError rather than refusing. (7) The list asks for one capped page of 100 and showed it under a header whose 'Total' counts the whole table, with no indication the two measure different things and that the search box filters only what loaded. Underneath all of it, three of the page's reads — GET /support/announcements, /stats and /:id/acknowledgments — returned anonymous inline types, so the @nestjs/swagger plugin described NO schema for any of them; the client hand-typed all three, and both hand-typed shapes were wrong: the create payload was derived as Omit<Announcement, ... 'acknowledgedCount' ...> against a key the read shape does not have (it is acknowledgmentCount), so the subtraction removed nothing there and the create type went on demanding status, acknowledgmentCount and a full acknowledgments roster the DTO rejects — held together by a cast in the page; and the list filter declared isPublished, a query parameter this controller has never accepted, while omitting status, the only filter the page sends. Fixed by AnnouncementPageDto / AnnouncementStatsResponseDto / AnnouncementAcknowledgmentStatusDto in announcement-response.dto.ts, @ApiHideProperty on the two relation properties no read path loads (they were listed as REQUIRED fields of every announcement the API returns), client types derived through ApiSchema and ApiQuery, and the page moved onto useAdminQuery / useAdminMutation with QueryFailureNotice carrying every read and write error.

title: The billing report stamped every money card and CSV row with a hardcoded USD symbol over a cross-currency SUM, and counted "Payments With Refunds" from one page of 100 succeeded payments beside a true total, excluding every fully refunded payment
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Working Style: report faithfully — a figure must not be stated in a currency it does not have, and a subtotal must not be presented as a platform total
notes: Found in W9l while migrating BillingReportsPage to the admin data layer — the last page of the billing batch — and fixed in the same commit. Four defects. First and sharpest: the page's local formatCurrency hardcoded currency: 'USD', and InvoiceStats.totalAmount / totalPaid / totalPending / totalOverdue are all COALESCE(SUM(total), 0) FROM billing.invoices with NO GROUP BY currency (invoice-management.service.ts:308). The same response carries a byCurrency breakdown built by GROUP BY currency — the endpoint stating outright that the table is multi-currency. So on any platform with a single EUR invoice, four cards and an exported CSV read '$1,234,567.89' for a figure that is not an amount of dollars, or of anything else. The page now derives the currency from byCurrency: with exactly one it formats in THAT currency through formatCurrencyAmount; with more than one the cross-currency sums are rendered as an em dash and the real per-currency figures are listed instead, which are the numbers an operator can act on. Second: 'Payments With Refunds' fetched getPayments({status:'succeeded', limit:100}) and counted the rows whose refundedAmount exceeded zero, presenting that count beside 'Successful Payments' which was the endpoint's true total — a subtotal over at most a hundred rows next to a platform figure. The status:'succeeded' filter additionally excluded every FULLY refunded payment, whose status is 'refunded', so the card counted partial refunds only and labelled them refunds. Both numbers have been computed exactly on the server since ADMIN-HIGH-138 (PaymentStats.refunded and .succeeded), so the read moves to /billing/payments/stats and the hundred-row fetch is deleted. Third: five `?? 0` fallbacks on InvoiceStats fields the client type declares required — dead defensive code, and had one ever been absent it would have printed a fabricated zero into a billing report. Fourth: the CSV named no currency and no scope, so an exported 'Total amount,1234567.89' was unattributable; it now carries a Currency column, per-currency rows, and the header says the totals are all-time.

title: The messaging compliance dashboard sent both of its reads without the tenant id the routes require, so every load 400'd and the page rendered a placeholder reporting Compliance Score 100%, zero messages under legal hold, and a green tick over "No legal holds"
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Working Style: report faithfully — a regulatory surface must never assert the absence of legal holds from a request that failed; CLAUDE.md Architectural Approach Tier 1: make the wrong call impossible
notes: Found in W9m while migrating MessagingCompliancePage to the admin data layer, and fixed in the same commit. The page called messagingApi.getComplianceStats() and getLegalHolds() with NO argument. Both client methods declared tenantId as optional and their docblocks promised that omitting it returned 'platform-wide stats' and 'all tenants' — a mode neither route has ever had: MessagingAdminController.getComplianceStats and .getLegalHolds each declare @TenantParam('query') tenantId: string with the decorator's default optional: false, and VerifiedTenantPipe answers a request whose raw value is undefined with BadRequestException('tenantId is required') (verified-tenant.pipe.ts:79-81). So every load of this page 400'd on both reads. The page then evaluated `stats = statsQuery.data ?? EMPTY_STATS` and rendered its placeholder: Compliance Score 100% in GREEN, Under Legal Hold 0 messages, Active Holds 0, Pending Cleanup 0, Retention Policies 0, Active Exports 0, and a legal-holds table showing a green check icon over 'No legal holds'. An error banner sat above it, but six stat cards and a table stated numbers, and on a litigation-hold surface those numbers asserted that a platform under preservation order had no holds and perfect compliance. This is the getHealthScore()-returns-100-from-an-empty-table pattern (audit correction C2) on a regulatory surface, which is why it is CRITICAL rather than HIGH. Fixed at Tier 1 first: getComplianceStats and getLegalHolds now REQUIRE tenantId, so the call the page made cannot be written, and adminKeys.messaging.complianceStats/legalHolds take the tenant id too (a key without it would have served one tenant's holds under another tenant's view). EMPTY_STATS is deleted — a placeholder object is indistinguishable from an answer once it reaches a stat card — and every card renders an em dash for a figure the page does not have, with a neutral colour so an unknown score cannot be graded green. The page asks which tenant it reports on through TenantSelect and reads nothing until it knows. Releasing a legal hold, which makes held messages eligible for retention cleanup again, now asks for confirmation and goes through useAdminMutation invalidating the whole compliance subtree. Note for W10: TenantSelect / useTenants were on the kill list as fully dead; this page is now a real consumer, so that verdict changes for those two entries, and useActiveTenants / useTenantSearch moved off useAsyncData onto useAdminQuery in the same commit.

title: Three sections of the messaging compliance dashboard have no producing endpoint: export-job listing, retention distribution across tenants, and audit operations per day
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Architectural Approach: a fix that cannot land this session becomes a tracked finding with owner, deadline and ID — never a silent empty state
notes: Registered in W9m as the tracked half of ADMIN-CRITICAL-147. The compliance page built three empty arrays in the browser — exports: [], four zero-count retention buckets, and dailyAudit: [] — behind a `// WHY:` comment saying no endpoint served them. The comment was honest; the UI was not: it rendered 'No export jobs found.', 'No retention data available' and 'No audit data available', so a GDPR auditor reading the page concluded the platform had no export jobs and no audit activity. W9m removes those arrays and their renderers and states the gap on screen instead, naming this finding. What must still be BUILT, in messaging-service with an admin-api route in front of it: (1) a listing of the export jobs POST /messaging/tenants/:id/export creates — the endpoint creates them and nothing can enumerate them, so a completed GDPR Art 20 export cannot be found again or downloaded; (2) a retention-bucket aggregation counting tenants per retention window; (3) a per-day audit-operation count for the last 14 days. Item (1) is the compliance-relevant one and should be built first: an export a regulator asked for that the operator cannot locate is the same failure class as a report nobody produces.

title: Every @TenantParam('query') route documented no tenant parameter while refusing any request that omitted it, so a client generated from the contract could not know the one parameter it had to send
rule_violated: CONTRACT-CRITICAL-003: the OpenAPI artifact is the SSoT for what an endpoint accepts; CLAUDE.md Architectural Approach Tier 2 — make the correct behaviour the zero-effort default
notes: Found in W9n while fixing MessagingAuditPage, and fixed at the decorator in the same commit. TenantParam was only a parameter decorator, and the @nestjs/swagger plugin reads @Query() and nothing else — so all 32 query-sourced call sites in admin-api (of 132 TenantParam call sites overall) documented NO tenant parameter in openapi.json, while VerifiedTenantPipe refused any request omitting it with BadRequestException('tenantId is required'). The artifact therefore described an endpoint that could never be called successfully from it. Two admin pages proved the consequence: MessagingCompliancePage (ADMIN-CRITICAL-147) and MessagingAuditPage (ADMIN-CRITICAL-150) each shipped calls that could only ever 400, and each rendered a placeholder in place of the answer. Fixed at Tier 2: TenantParam now applies ApiQuery to the owning method for the 'query' source, so the parameter appears with the right name, its required flag, uuid format and a description saying whether the request is refused without it — for all 32 call sites and every route added after this. 'param' contributes nothing because the route path already declares it and the plugin derives a path parameter from the template; 'body' contributes nothing because TenantIdCarrier declares it on the DTO. A parameter decorator cannot be composed with a method decorator through applyDecorators, so ApiQuery is applied to the method descriptor directly — the documented way to have a parameter decorator contribute route-level metadata. Gate: libs/backend-common/src/decorators/__tests__/tenant-param-openapi.spec.ts reads the same metadata key the swagger module reads, across all three sources, the custom-key form, the optional form and two ids on one handler, so a refactor back to a bare createParamDecorator fails the build. The artifact now documents 32 tenantId query parameters where it documented none.

title: The messaging audit log could not display a correct row in any state: its default read 400'd and drew "entries will appear once messaging activity begins", a valid tenant crashed the page on an offset-vs-cursor mismatch, five row fields were invented, and none of the seven action filter values is a member of ComplianceAction
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Working Style: report faithfully — an audit trail must not explain an absence it has not established; CONTRACT-CRITICAL-003: a client type must come from the contract, not from invention
notes: Found in W9n while migrating MessagingAuditPage to the admin data layer, and fixed in the same commit. Seven compounding defects on the platform's forensic record of messaging operations. (1) GET /messaging/audit declares @TenantParam('query') tenantId: string; the page's tenant box was an optional free-text filter defaulting to '' and sent as undefined, so the DEFAULT state of the page refused at VerifiedTenantPipe with BadRequestException('tenantId is required') and the table then drew 'No audit entries found. Audit entries will appear once messaging activity begins.' — a sentence explaining an absence the page had not established. (2) With a valid tenant it crashed: the route answers {items, hasMore, cursor, totalCount} and the client declared PaginatedResult<T>, an offset page with a data array, so result.data was undefined, entries became undefined, and the next render threw on entries.length. (3) The row type was fiction. messaging.compliance_audit_logs holds {id, tenantId, userId, action, resourceType, resourceId, details, ipAddress, userAgent, createdAt}; the client declared timestamp (so new Date(entry.timestamp) was Invalid Date), tenantName and userName (absent — two blank columns), channelId and messageId (absent; the row names its subject with resourceType + resourceId), and details as a string when it is jsonb | null — so the cell rendered [object Object] and handleExportCsv called .replace on an object and THREW. (4) ipAddress and userAgent, the two fields that say where an action came from, were never shown. (5) The pager sent page and pageSize; the route takes limit and cursor, so every page returned the same first rows and Previous/Next moved nothing. (6) The seven action filter values — send, edit, delete, create_channel, join_channel, leave_channel, upload_file — are not members of ComplianceAction, so every action filter returned nothing permanently, ACTION_COLORS keyed on the same seven so every real row rendered grey, and the four an auditor comes for (message_export, data_anonymize, retention_set, legal_hold_toggle) were not offered at all. (7) The CSV quoted only the details field, so a comma in any other value silently shifted every column, and it exported one page of 25 under a filename claiming to be the audit log. Fixed by retyping the client to the row and the cursor page the route actually returns, requiring tenantId, correcting admin-api's own under-declared AuditLogRow interface, moving the page to useAdminQuery keyed by the request (cursor included), replacing page numbers with a cursor trail so Previous works, rendering resourceType/resourceId/ipAddress and jsonb details, quoting every CSV field and writing the scope and the page number into the file, and taking the action vocabulary from the entity. Gate: tests/invariants/messaging-compliance-action-parity.spec.ts pins the frontend list to enum ComplianceAction in both directions and requires every member to have a label and a badge — the highest tier available, since the enum belongs to messaging-service, reaches admin-api only as a NATS reply, and admin-api may not import another service's source.

title: The retention page's "+ Override" button discarded its arguments and closed the modal, reporting success for a data-deletion window it never wrote; its Edit could never save, its list could never load, and "Indefinite" was offered but forbidden by the DTO
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Working Style: report faithfully — a write that did not happen must never be reported as success, least of all on a setting that decides when data is deleted
notes: Found in W9o while migrating MessagingRetentionPage to the admin data layer, and fixed in the same commit. This page sets how long a tenant's messages survive, and all three of its paths were broken — two silently. (1) '+ Override' was a no-op that looked like a success: the modal collected a channel id and a window, and handleAddOverride discarded all three arguments (_tenantId, _channelId, _retentionDays), refetched the list and closed the modal. The operator set a channel's deletion window and the UI behaved exactly as if it had been written. Its comment claimed the endpoint was 'not yet available in admin gateway'; UpdateRetentionPolicyDto has taken {channelId, retentionDays} all along, with channelId documented 'null means the policy applies to every channel of the tenant'. The capability existed — only the wiring did not. (2) 'Edit' could never save: it sent {defaultRetention: '1y', applyToAll: true}, neither key on the DTO, under the platform's forbidNonWhitelisted: true, with no retentionDays — refused twice over. It also addressed the route with the POLICY id where the path parameter is the TENANT id (@TenantParam('param', {key: 'id'})), so a well-formed body would still have answered 'Tenant <policy-uuid> not found'. (3) The list could never load — GET /messaging/retention/policies requires tenantId and the client sent none, the third instance of ADMIN-HIGH-149's consequence — and the table then drew 'No tenant retention policies configured. Retention policies will appear once tenants enable messaging.' It would also have crashed had it loaded: the row type declared nine fields, seven invented (tenantName, channelOverridesCount, lastCleanup, nextCleanup, messagesCount, expiredCount, and defaultRetention as one of four labels where the wire carries a NUMBER OF DAYS), three of them rendered through .toLocaleString(). (4) 'Indefinite' was offered and could not be sent: RetentionPolicy.retentionDays documents -1 as indefinite and executeRetentionCleanup skips those policies (retention-policy.service.ts:221), but the DTO's @Min(1) refused it — the one window an operator picks for a legal-preservation channel was the one the API rejected. Fixed in the DTO (@Min(-1) @NotEquals(0) @Max(3650)), not by removing the option, because the state is real and the nightly job honours it. Zero stays refused: zero days would ask the cleanup to delete everything the moment it runs. Also fixed: admin-api's RetentionPolicyResponse named four of the seven fields the reply carries; the page now takes a tenant through TenantSelect, reads through useAdminQuery keyed per tenant, writes through useAdminMutation invalidating that key, warns only when a window is actually SHORTENED, validates the channel UUID at the field the DTO validates, and says 'Not set' where no policy row exists rather than showing a number it did not read. Gates: apps/admin-api-service/src/messaging/__tests__/update-retention-policy.dto.spec.ts (9 tests, both directions of the window contract) and the page spec (11 tests).

title: The messaging monitoring aggregates were typed by controller interfaces the swagger plugin cannot describe, so both routes carried no schema and the panel hand-wrote five shapes; the tenant chart's empty state also asserted no activity on a failed read
rule_violated: CONTRACT-CRITICAL-003: a response the panel renders must have a described schema and the client type must derive from it
notes: Found in W9p while migrating MessagingMonitoringPage to the admin data layer, and fixed in the same commit. Registered as MEDIUM, not HIGH, and the reason is on the record: this page was NOT lying. Every KPI already rendered an em dash until the aggregate arrived, the outbox panel rendered only when it had one, oldestPendingAgeSeconds === null already showed a dash rather than '0s', the error banner already carried the server's own message with a retry, and the freshness note already said the numbers were the aggregation's rather than the request's. ADMIN-HIGH-009 wrote both sides of this contract together and they still agreed field for field. Registering a HIGH here would inflate the ledger this audit exists to keep honest. What is real and now fixed: (1) GET /messaging/monitoring/stats and GET /messaging/tenants were typed by INTERFACES declared inside the controller, and the @nestjs/swagger plugin describes classes only, so both carried '{"type": "object"}' in openapi.json and the panel had nothing to derive from — it hand-wrote five shapes (TenantMessagingOverviewRow, MessagingOutboxHealth, MessagingMonitoringTotals, MessagingMonitoringStats, MessagingTenantsOverview). They are DTO classes now and the frontend aliases them through ApiSchema, which closes the drift BEFORE it happened rather than after; every other page in this audit that hand-wrote a response type had already drifted from it (ADMIN-HIGH-110, ADMIN-MEDIUM-111, ADMIN-CRITICAL-150, ADMIN-CRITICAL-151). (2) The tenant bar chart's empty state read 'No tenant messaging activity recorded yet.' on a FAILED read as well as an empty one — the one sentence on the page that asserted something it had not established. (3) The read sat in a second module-scoped cache with no abort signal, so leaving the page could not cancel it and logoutCleanup() had one more store to remember; it is on useAdminQuery now with staleTime matching messaging-service's own 60-second cache, so the page does not re-request a number that cannot have changed. (4) ErrorBanner was a fourth local copy of QueryFailureNotice and is gone.

title: The tenant data export ran, shipped its whole payload to the browser, and the page discarded it — so an operator answering a GDPR portability request saw a record count and got no file
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Working Style: report faithfully — an operation that produced a deliverable must hand it over, not report a count and drop it; CONTRACT-CRITICAL-003: the declared response must be the response
notes: Found in W9q while migrating MessagingTenantsPage to the admin data layer, and fixed in the same commit. POST /messaging/tenants/:id/export performs the export INSIDE the request — DataExportService.exportTenant serialises the rows to JSON or CSV and returns them as `data` alongside {jobId, status: 'completed', format, recordCount, isUnderLegalHold, exportedAt}. Nothing stores that payload server-side and there is no second endpoint to fetch it from, so the response is the only copy that will ever exist. admin-api declared the reply as `{exportId: string; status: string}` — `exportId` is a field the reply does not have (it is `jobId`) and five fields were missing, `data` above all. The panel's own hand-written type listed six of the seven and also omitted `data`. So the page rendered 'Export job accepted / Records: 12,431' and threw the export away: an operator answering an Art 20 portability request ran it, watched it succeed, and had no file. This is also why ADMIN-HIGH-148 found nothing to list — nothing was ever kept. Three smaller defects went with it. (1) The route answered 202 Accepted for work already finished, which is why the page's own copy told the operator the job 'runs asynchronously'; it is 200 now and both the DTO and the copy say the export happens in the request. (2) The tenant was typed by hand into a free-text UUID box: a valid-but-wrong id exports a DIFFERENT tenant's entire messaging history, on an endpoint that returns the whole of it. TenantSelect removes the class. (3) The overview read sat in a second module-scoped cache with no abort signal, and its response shapes were hand-written (closed with ADMIN-MEDIUM-152). The page now downloads the file through saveBlob with the right MIME type and extension, states the record count and the legal-hold flag the export came back with, and points at the compliance log entry — the export is audited as MESSAGE_EXPORT, one of the four actions MessagingAuditPage's filter could never match before ADMIN-CRITICAL-150.

title: The AI personas page told operators that a hardcoded glossary was the tenant's live PLC actuation policy, on the surface that governs autonomous control of physical equipment — admin-api has no path to TenantAgentConfig
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Working Style: report faithfully — a life-safety surface must not present documentation as a reading of live configuration; the page's own docblock states the rule it broke (LIFE-SAFETY C9: it MUST show real backend state, not hardcoded defaults)
notes: Found in W9r while migrating MessagingAiPersonasPage to the admin data layer, and the claim removed in the same commit. The page's docblock stated the rule it broke — 'LIFE-SAFETY (C9): This page reflects autonomous PLC actuation policy. It MUST show real backend state, not hardcoded defaults' — and its red banner told the operator: 'The actuation policy and autonomous safety limits shown below are loaded from the real backend TenantAgentConfig entity. These are not display-only values -- they directly control what the AI can do to physical infrastructure. Always verify actuation policies match your operational requirements.' NOTHING on the page was ever read from TenantAgentConfig. The two sections headed '(from TenantAgentConfig)' were a static glossary typed into the file: ACTUATION_POLICY_INFO describes what the three policy VALUES mean, and the safety-limits table lists FIELD NAMES with their descriptions. GET /messaging/personas returns {id, name, description, icon, color, capabilities} — no policy, no limits — and admin-api has no route, no NATS call and no reference to TenantAgentConfig, actuationPolicy or autonomousSafetyLimits anywhere in the service (verified by grep across apps/admin-api-service/src). So an operator who came here to verify that a tenant's SCADA AI cannot autonomously dose reagent was shown a glossary, told it was that tenant's live configuration, and instructed to verify against it. This is a fabricated PROVENANCE rather than a fabricated number, on the surface that governs autonomous control of physical equipment, which is why it outranks every other finding in this audit. Fixed by removing the claim: the banner now states that the page does NOT show a tenant's actuation policy and that admin-api cannot read the entity; both reference sections are relabelled as what they are ('What each actuation policy value means', 'The fields that make up an autonomous safety limit') with the body copy saying nothing in them is read from anywhere; capability labels are headed 'descriptive, not permissions'; and a panel where an operator looks for the effective policy states the gap and names ADMIN-HIGH-155, deliberately empty rather than filled with a default because a default there reads as a policy. Building the read path is ADMIN-HIGH-155 and was NOT done in this commit: it crosses into ai-service, needs a NATS responder plus an admin-api route and DTO, and a life-safety read path deserves its own review rather than being bundled into a page migration. Also fixed: admin-api's PersonaResponse declared id: string where the reply sends string | null, invented an isActive, and omitted icon, color and capabilities — the panel's hand-written type was the more accurate of the two; the table declared four headers and rendered three cells so the Scope column was empty; and the tenant was an unvalidated free-text UUID box, replaced by TenantSelect.

title: A SUPER_ADMIN cannot read any tenant's effective AI actuation policy or autonomous safety limits: admin-api has no path to ai-service's TenantAgentConfig
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Architectural Approach: a fix that cannot land this session becomes a tracked finding with owner, deadline and ID; the platform-admin boundary must be able to read the configuration it is accountable for
notes: Registered in W9r as the tracked half of ADMIN-CRITICAL-154. TenantAgentConfig (apps/ai-service/src/tenant-config/agent-config.entity.ts) holds actuationPolicy, autonomousSafetyLimits, autonomousActionsEnabled and proactiveMonitoringEnabled — the settings that decide what a tenant's AI may do to physical equipment through PLC actuation. admin-api has NO route, NO NATS call and NO reference to that entity: ai-service exposes exactly one admin-reachable responder, request.ai.isEnabled, and admin-api does not call even that. So a SUPER_ADMIN cannot see, from the platform-admin boundary, whether any tenant's AI is permitted to actuate — and MessagingAiPersonasPage filled the gap with a glossary presented as the answer (ADMIN-CRITICAL-154, fixed: the page now states the gap). What must be BUILT: (1) a read-only NATS responder in ai-service returning the effective per-tenant agent config, resolved the way AgentProfileService resolves it at runtime — most-restrictive-wins between the persona base policy and the tenant override, so the panel shows the EFFECTIVE policy and not the raw row, which would be a third thing to misread; (2) an admin-api route in front of it with a response DTO class, so the artifact describes it and the panel derives its type; (3) the panel's empty 'Effective actuation policy for this tenant' panel filled from it, with an explicit em dash where a field is null. NOT done in this commit deliberately: it crosses into ai-service, which this wave has not otherwise touched, and a life-safety read path deserves its own review rather than being bundled into a page migration. Owner okan, deadline 2026-12-31. Until it lands the panel says so and names this finding, which is the honest state — but it is not the finished state.

title: Every support ticket's comment thread rendered empty and silent — the client declared a flat array where the route returns a page and the TypeError went to console.error; the stats type invented ten fields, which is where a fabricated 100% SLA compliance came from
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Working Style: report faithfully — a support thread must not render empty when the read failed, and an SLA compliance figure must not be invented; CONTRACT-CRITICAL-003: a client type must come from the contract
notes: Found in W9s while migrating TicketsPage to the admin data layer, and fixed in the same commit; it also closes ADMIN-MEDIUM-114, which had tracked the missing comments DTO. Six defects. (1) THE SHARPEST: GET /support/tickets/:id/comments returns createStandardPaginatedResult, and the client declared a flat array — so `(data || []).map(...)` called .map on the decoded PAGE OBJECT, threw a TypeError, and fetchComments's catch wrote it to console.error. Every ticket's comment thread rendered 'No comments yet', silently, on every ticket. An admin opened a ticket, saw no messages, and replied to a customer whose messages were in the database. (2) The stats client type declared TWENTY fields where the endpoint sends ten: half were optional aliases the server has never sent (avgResponseTime, avgResolutionTime, satisfactionScore, byCategory, byPriority — the last two are separate endpoints) and the four real averages were marked optional. That is where the page's `a || b || 0` chains came from and where `slaBreachCount ? ... : 100` came from — a fabricated 100% SLA compliance for when the field was 'missing'. (3) getTicketStats returned 0 when there was nothing to average, so a platform that had answered no ticket showed 'Avg Response: 0m' — instant — and one nobody had rated showed a 0-star satisfaction card. The three averages are null on the wire now and an em dash in the page. (4) Every queue row carried `commentCount: 0, // Not provided by API` — a count the endpoint does not return, rendered on every ticket. The badge is gone from the list; the detail pane shows the count it actually loaded. (5) All four writes (assign, status, priority, comment) caught into console.error and then refetched, so a refused transition looked identical to an applied one. (6) slaComplianceRate rendered its float tail: three breaches over seven tickets printed 57.142857142857146%. Also fixed: SupportTicket.comments and TicketComment.ticket are hidden from the contract with @ApiHideProperty — no read path loads either, yet the generated schema listed comments among the REQUIRED fields of every ticket, each comment carrying a whole SupportTicket back, so a client typed from the artifact had to fabricate the field to compile (this is what had blocked ADMIN-MEDIUM-114); the SLA resolution deadline now prefers the server's own dueAt and only derives from createdAt + slaResolutionMinutes when there is none, where the previous order was inverted; the attachment button in the reply box had no onClick at all and is removed per ADMIN-HIGH-011; and the two action selects gained accessible names.

title: MessagingPage: the internal-note toggle was never put on the wire, so every note an admin wrote ABOUT a customer was delivered INTO that customer's thread; the Bulk Message dialog sent no audience at all, so every broadcast answered 400 under a preview promising 'all active tenants'; and the page keyed alignment, colour and the read receipt on a senderType this service has never written
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Working Style: report faithfully — a control that claims to keep a note internal must keep it internal, a dialog must not promise an audience it does not send, and a refused write must not be swallowed; CONTRACT-CRITICAL-003: a client type must come from the contract
notes: Found in W9t while migrating MessagingPage — the LAST page of ADMIN-HIGH-121's ratchet — and fixed in the same commit. Eight defects, seven of them invisible to the operator. (1) THE SHARPEST: the composer's Internal Note / Public Message toggle set local state, styled the draft yellow, and posted `{content, senderName}` — no `isInternal`. AddMessageDto accepts the field and the column defaults to false, so every internal note an admin has ever written about a customer was posted into that customer's own support thread as an ordinary message, visible to them. (2) Every broadcast answered 400. The Bulk Message dialog previewed 'This message will be sent to all active tenants' and sent neither tenantIds nor targetCriteria — the one body sendBulkMessage refuses ('No target tenants specified') — and the refusal went to console.error, so the dialog just sat there. The reply it never received carries {sent, failed} and was typed `void`, so a broadcast reaching 3 of 400 tenants would have closed exactly like one reaching 400. (3) The platform's own replies rendered as the tenant's: the page keyed alignment, bubble colour and the read receipt on `senderType === 'super_admin'`. admin-api writes 'admin'; 'super_admin' is auth-service's GraphQL messaging subgraph (SenderType.SUPER_ADMIN), a DIFFERENT support stack whose union the panel's hand-written type had adopted. The test was false for every message ever written. (4) 'failed' was missing from the panel's status union, so a message that never left drew as one awaiting a read. (5) Attachments read `filename` and `size` against a wire sending `fileName` and `fileSize`: every attachment was a nameless link reading 'NaN MB'. (6) Every message was signed with the literal 'Admin' the page sent beside a `// TODO: Use actual admin name`, and both handlers preferred `dto.senderName` over the authenticated user — the same class ADMIN-CRITICAL-102 fixed for ticket creation. (7) getMessages took page/limit, defaulted limit to 50 and returned a BARE ARRAY, so a thread past 50 messages handed over its OLDEST 50 with nothing to say so, under a header printing the real messageCount from another query. (8) Six writes (send, close, reopen, archive, create thread, broadcast) and two reads (stats, mark-as-read) were swallowed into console.error; mark-as-read shared one try with the message read, so a refused acknowledgement was indistinguishable from a failed load. Also: calculateAvgResponseTime returned Math.round(avg || 0), so a platform that had never answered a tenant reported an average response time of 0 minutes; and the new-conversation dialog took the tenant as a free-text UUID, where a valid-but-wrong id opens a support conversation against a tenant nobody meant to contact (the ADMIN-HIGH-153 class). FIX: senderName removed from both request DTOs so the wrong attribution is unrepresentable; targetCriteria made the single REQUIRED audience field with a BulkMessageAudienceDto class describing it (the AnnouncementTarget interface generated Record<string, never>); getMessages returns createStandardPaginatedResult; avgResponseTimeMinutes nullable; SupportMessageResponseDto / SupportMessagePageDto / MessagingStatsResponseDto / BulkMessageResultDto / CreatedMessageThreadDto declared so the panel aliases the contract instead of hand-writing it; page migrated to useAdminQuery/useAdminMutation with QueryFailureNotice and TenantSelect. This closes ADMIN-HIGH-121's ratchet at 0 and deletes .claude/allowlists/admin-panel-unmigrated-reads.yaml; the gate now fails the build on any unmigrated page rather than accepting an allowlist row.

title: The deploy capacity gate has no reclaim pass for Docker's build cache, so a droplet whose space sits there refuses every development deploy: 34.6 GB of build cache (19.4 GB reclaimable) held free space at 13% against a 20% floor, and no image has reached the development server since 2026-09-21
rule_violated: A capacity gate that blocks a deploy must be able to reclaim every regenerable store that fills the disk; a store it cannot reclaim turns a cache into a permanent outage.

title: policy_subscriber_applies_live_change_event waits only for the in-memory apply and then reads the disk snapshot, racing the subscriber's persist step that runs after it; losing the race failed main's CI on f2778c904 and skipped the development image build

title: The raw-findings collapse (ARIA-HIGH-185) removed every raw row of a run whose findings recur in a newer run, so after retention pruned its hot artifact the compacted tree failed the kernel's own verify (raw_pointer_missing): every aria-state-maintenance run since 2026-09-21 was refused, and publish-time compaction would refuse every cycle publish
rule_violated: A compaction must not produce a tree its own verifier refuses: every run that reports raw findings keeps a pointer to them after the collapse.
notes: aria-state-maintenance runs 35648185798 (09-21) .. 36263043814 (09-26) all failed at 'compacted aria/state tree did not pass integrity verification'; last success 35528250156 (09-20). First bad change 8028bbb005 (09-21 14:31Z); e93280b187 removed the shared-fingerprint fixture that would have caught it; no test covered raw_pointer_missing. Reproduced on origin/aria/state 1939ce19b with the #1676 head e22bbe9f9 kernel: integrity verify valid before `state compact --retain-days 7`, valid=false with 55 raw_pointer_missing after. Fix: the collapse keeps each run's newest row when it would otherwise empty the run (state_compact._collapse_survivors); same data after the fix: verify valid, 0 issues, raw-findings 66.9 MB/40,361 rows -> 13.4 MB/8,259 rows (8,199 fingerprints + 60 per-run floor rows, 80 runs).

title: A sensor that publishes MQTT directly has no broker identity: field devices are handed the sensor_service account, which can read and write every tenant's sensor, device, alert and command topics, and a free-text topic resolved first-match across tenants lets one tenant capture another's stream
rule_violated: Identity is the authenticated principal (ADR-014/015); a topic identifies its publisher only when the ACL binds it to one principal
notes: Implementation of ADR-047 (operator decision 2026-10-06). Prerequisite: #1805 (edge directory pattern, go-auth auth-cache verdict). Scope includes the tenant-erasure hook for sensor_mqtt_directory and edge_device_directory, the mqtt-acl CI gate, and the legacy-publisher list with its reserved client IDs.

title: Edge MQTT auth (CONNECT, ACL) and public provisioning resolve devices with unscoped reads of the FORCE-RLS edge_device_directory and tenant edge_devices, so every edge gateway is refused and auto-provisioning / activation cannot write
rule_violated: Tenant reads outside a request context go through runInTenantRead/runInTenantTransaction; cross-tenant source reads through runInSourceRead
narrative: Prod, as sensor_service: SELECT count(*) FROM sensor.edge_device_directory -> 0 (1 row exists); tenant edge_devices -> 0 without app.current_tenant, 1 with it.
Provisioning wrote through dataSource.transaction + SET LOCAL search_path with no tenant GUC: INSERT fails the WITH CHECK, UPDATE matches zero rows.

title: MQTT auth does not bind a device's client ID to its username, so any authenticated device can connect as aqua-sensor-service-main and evict the ingestion listener, or evict another gateway
rule_violated: A principal cannot assume another principal's session
narrative: Raised by the edge-expert review of ADR-047; becomes reachable once SENSOR-CRITICAL-143 lets devices authenticate again.

title: The MQTT auth endpoints' shared secret is never transported: mosquitto-go-auth (3.0.0, latest) has no custom-header option, so auth_opt_http_headers X-Mosquitto-Auth is inert and /mqtt/{auth,acl,superuser} rest on network isolation alone while the production bootstrap gate accepts MQTT_AUTH_SECRET as if it protected them
rule_violated: A trust-boundary control must be enforceable by the component that is supposed to carry it; a configured but inert control is not a control
notes: Independent security review of PR #1805 asked to require the header; doing so would refuse every CONNECT and ACL check in production because the broker cannot send it. Fix options: a dedicated internal-only listener for /mqtt/* (network-enforced), or a broker-side auth plugin/transport that can carry a credential (e.g. mTLS); then make an absent header a denial.
narrative: go-auth 3.0.0 backends/http.go sets only Content-Type and User-Agent; no http_headers option is parsed (source tag 3.0.0 and the shipped go-auth.so carry no 'http_headers' string).
mqtt-auth.controller.ts admits an absent header; a present header is compared in constant time on equal-length buffers.

title: Tenant provisioning-key lookup (self-register, tenant installer) reads every tenant's tenant_provisioning_keys through one pooled UNION with no tenant GUC, so under FORCE RLS no key is ever found and auto-provisioning still fails
rule_violated: Tenant reads outside a request context go through runInTenantRead/runInTenantTransaction; cross-tenant routing goes through a sanctioned index, not an unscoped UNION
notes: Same defect class as SENSOR-CRITICAL-143; found by the edge-device grep requested in the #1805 follow-up. Fix direction: a cross-tenant key route (key_token_hash -> tenant_id) written with the key, like edge_device_directory, then read the key inside the tenant's runInTenantRead.
narrative: findKeyAcrossSchemas: dataSource.query over information_schema tenant schemas + UNION ALL of tenant_provisioning_keys; the pool is deny-by-default outside a request.

title: A suspended or archived tenant's edge devices still authenticate and publish: the MQTT CONNECT/ACL path resolves the tenant from the device directory and never checks the tenant's lifecycle
rule_violated: A suspended tenant has no runtime access
notes: Fix direction: admit a directory hit only for a tenant listActiveTenantSchemaIdentities reports active (or a tenant-status column on the route kept in sync by the lifecycle events), applied in findSessionDevice.
narrative: Noted by the independent security review of PR #1805; not fixed there.

title: Concurrent device activations with one provisioning token can both succeed: activateDevice checks token_used_at in memory and its UPDATE has no token_used_at IS NULL guard, so two agents can each receive MQTT credentials
rule_violated: A single-use credential is consumed atomically
notes: Fix direction: claim the token with a conditional UPDATE ... WHERE id = $1 AND token_used_at IS NULL RETURNING (or SELECT ... FOR UPDATE inside the tenant transaction) and refuse when no row is claimed.
narrative: Noted by the independent security review of PR #1805 (provisioning.service.ts activateDevice).

title: With the go-auth cache off every MQTT PUBLISH costs two database transactions on sensor-service (~7.9 ms serial, ~200 ACL checks/s ceiling per instance measured), so ACL throughput caps fleet telemetry
rule_violated: Hot-path authorization must scale with message rate without trading away correctness
notes: Measured on the edge-mqtt-auth.rls.postgres.spec harness (testcontainers Postgres, default pool): 500 serial checks 3939 ms (7.88 ms each, 2 transactions: runInSourceRead + runInTenantRead, ~15 round trips); 500 concurrent 2510 ms (~199/s). Fix direction: an in-process ACL cache keyed on (clientid, username, topic, acc) with explicit invalidation on every lifecycle/credential change (approve, decommission, reset, revoke, erasure) broadcast to all replicas, or a broker-side cache keyed on client ID; the go-auth cache cannot be re-enabled while it keys auth on username+password.
narrative: Consequence of PR #1805 turning off auth_opt_cache (client-ID binding bypass) and dropping the positive tenant cache (stale state).

title: Directory lookup by device_code is ambiguous: device codes are unique per tenant only (registerDevice accepts operator-chosen codes) and lookupTenantId takes LIMIT 1, so a public installer/status lookup by code resolves an arbitrary tenant's device
rule_violated: A public identifier must resolve to exactly one principal or none
notes: Fails closed today (the provisioning-token check then fails for the other tenant's device), but a legitimate install of the second device is refused. Fix direction: resolve every route for the code and match the presented token, or make public flows address devices by UUID.
narrative: Raised while fixing PR #1805; MQTT auth is unaffected (mqtt_client_id embeds the tenant prefix).

title: Tenant erasure is a no-op under pool RLS: TenantErasureTargetExecutor opens its transactions with no tenant bound, so in every pool-RLS service (FORCE RLS, NOBYPASSRLS role, checkout GUC tenant '') every erasure DELETE, hook purge, proof read and outbox write matches zero rows while the proof attests the erasure
rule_violated: GDPR Art. 17: an erasure proof must attest rows actually removed; tenant writes outside a request bind the tenant RLS context
notes: Raised by the final security review of PR #1805, which made it reachable for sensor routes. Fix: every executor transaction binds the erased tenant (bindTenantRlsContext) before anything else; hook affected counts are folded into the proof hash. Covered for both modes by real-Postgres specs (sensor tenant-schema-module, config source-schema-tenant-column).
narrative: All 11 erasure targets run RlsModule.forPoolService and share this executor path.

title: No per-username failure limiter before async PBKDF2 on MQTT CONNECT: a flood of wrong-password CONNECTs naming a real device runs a 600k-iteration PBKDF2 per attempt and can saturate the libuv thread pool
rule_violated: Unauthenticated, expensive verification must be rate-limited per principal
notes: Fix direction: a bounded per-username (and per-source) failure counter with backoff checked before verifyPassword, shared across replicas or enforced at the broker.
narrative: Raised by the final security review of PR #1805.

title: Tenant provisioning-key claim (incrementUsedCount) re-checks only max_devices, so a key revoked or expired between validation and registration still registers a device
rule_violated: A credential check and its consumption are one atomic decision
notes: Fix in PR #1805: one conditional UPDATE re-checks is_active, expires_at and max_devices and requires exactly one claimed row.
narrative: Raised by the final security review of PR #1805.
